### General Ledger
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 16*

Introduction to the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

General Ledger 

Use the General Ledger application to create and manage accounts and account groups; create 

journals and journal entries, and more.  

Use the Company application to subscribe to the General ledger application. 

Configure the General ledger and its features with the General ledger Setup tab’s Configuration 

command. 

The General Ledger is where you create and maintain accounts, journals, and financial reports. 

• 
You use the General Ledger to post journal entries, design, and run reports, create budgets, 

and more. 

• 
Other applications automatically post transactions to the General Ledger in real time.

#### Key Features
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Introduction to the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Key Features 

Use the General Ledger application to: 

• 
Create and maintain any number of journals and adjusting journals, including statistical 

journals and their adjusting counterparts. 

• 
Add, modify, reverse, delete, and post transactions to a journal. 

• 
Import data from spreadsheets and other accounting applications, so you can quickly 

upload data for journals, beginning account balances, journal entries, and budgets. 

• 
Create financial reports and graphs. 

• 
Fine tune standard financial reports and navigate from financial statement line items to 

individual transactions. 

• 
Create innumerable variations of reports, including income statements, balance sheets, 

budget variance reports, departmental expense reports, gross margin, statement of 

cash flows, and so on. 

• 
Create normal G/L accounts and statistical accounts. Statistical accounts enable you to 

generate metrics such as revenue per employee. 

• 
Create account groups to use in financial reports and graphs and in the General Ledger to 

roll up and organize individual accounts into larger categories. 

• 
Create templates for non-accounting users to enter G/L transactions without having to deal 

with the intricacies of account numbers, departments, and locations. 

• 
Create and fine-tune budgets and present performance versus budget in financial reports. 

Budgets can be very general (by account with all departments/locations), or by any 

account-department-location combination. 

This is a multi-ledger system. Transactions posted to subledgers, such as accounts receivable, 

accounts payable, and cash management, are posted to the general ledger in real time. 

• 
The automated real-time posting is completely transparent to you as a user. 

• 
Transaction details are recorded in the subledgers, and summary transactions are recorded 

in the General Ledger. 

• 
Summary transactions in the general ledger have links back to the detailed subledger 

transactions to enable navigation from reports. 

Other features of the General Ledger application include GAAP-compliant double-entry 

accounting, true closing of the books, and flexible tracking of GAAP, tax, and other adjusting 

entries. 

The General Ledger comes with several standard reports that you can run right away. See the 

summary of standard G/L reports for details in online help or download (on page 718) the 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.

### About the General Ledger Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*

General Ledger Workbench 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About the General Ledger Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Application > General Ledger > All > Workbench`


The General Ledger workbench is a central location where you can view and work with data in 

General Ledger accounts. Use the General Ledger workbench to work with journal entries and 

statistical journal entries.  

From the workbench, you can: 

• 
View the journal entries in the General Ledger. 

• 
Add journal entries. 

• 
Add statistical journal entries. 

• 
Filter and sort journal entries. 

• 
Open and close books. 

• 
Export the list of journal entries. 

When you select the Reports option, you can: 

• 
Choose between Trial Balance, Income Statement, Cash Flow Statement, and Balance Sheet 

reports. 

• 
Set up filters for the desired report. 

• 
View the report results in the workbench. 

• 
Click any blue link to see the details behind a figure.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

7.

account groups for each report. 

8. 
Click Save.

#### Creating Statistical Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 30*

General Ledger Workbench 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Creating Statistical Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Statistical Journal Entry`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Workbench`


You enter statistical transactions in the same way that you enter G/L transactions. The only 

difference is that statistical transactions do not need to balance. Instead, you increase or decrease 

a value. 

After you have entered statistical transactions, you can use statistical accounts in your financial 

reports. 

Adding a Statistical Journal Entry 

You can add a statistical journal entry directly, or add it from the General Ledger Workbench. 

To add a statistical Journal entry from the General Ledger workbench: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Workbench. 

3. 
Click the Add button, and then select the Statistical Journal Entry option. 

To add a new statistical journal entry directly: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Create Statistical Journal Entry. 

Creating the Statistical Journal Entry 

1. 
In the Journal field, select the journal to which you want to post this transaction. 

This field does not appear when you add a statistical journal entry from within a statistical 

journal, as the journal is already determined. 

2. 
In the Posting date field, type the date you want to post this transaction to the Statistical 

journal or click the 
 Calendar button to select a date. 

3. 
In the Automatic reversal date field, type the date you want to reverse the transaction. 

Enter a date only if you want to post a reverse transaction to this transaction. The reverse 

transaction is identical, except it is the inverse and therefore zeros out the transaction. You 

can enter any date of today or later. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description of this transaction. 

5. 
Optionally, add a comment about the transaction in the Comment field. 

6. 
In the Reference number field, type your own number by which you can reference this 

transaction. (optional) 

7. 
In the Attachment drop-down list, select an attachment to add to this transaction.

Attaching a Document to the Journal Entry 

The Documents section appears on a journal entry when scanning is enabled for your system. If 

scanning is not enabled, use the Attachments field in the top section of the Journal entries page.

scanned image, spreadsheet, or word processor document as an attachment. 

To attach a document:

Click the Choose file button, and then find the file that you want to attach. 

2. 
Double-click the desired file to select it. If you accidentally select the wrong file, you can 

detach it by clicking the Choose File button again. 

3. 
Click the Attach button.

attach the file to this record. See Attachments (on page 708 ).

Filling In the Entries List 

You can fill in the Entries list with default values by clicking the Show defaults link, or by adding 

values directly to each line item.  

Using Defaults to Fill In the Entries List 

In the Entries section, click the Show defaults link to display a list of fields and drop-down 

lists that you can have the system complete. The system completes the fields with the values 

that you select in each existing and new line item in the Entries list. You can override any 

default value that the system inserts.  

To set up the default values: 

• 
In a field, type the desired value.  

• 
In a drop-down list, choose the desired option. 

For example, you can set up a dimension and click the Apply Defaults button so that the 

system completes the dimension in each line item. This example shows the system 

completing the Location column. 

Filling In the Entries List Manually 

1. 
In the Location field, select the location associated with the statistical journal entry. 

2. 
Skip the Doc field. The system assigns this document number when you save the 

transaction. 

3. 
In the Statistical Account field, type the name of an account, or click the drop-down list and 

then select the Find link to look up the account. If you need to create an account, click the 

Add link in the drop-down list.

Finishing the Journal Entry 

When you finish entering or editing the journal entry: 

• 
If journal entry approvals are disabled, you can either save the transaction as a draft or post 

it. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the entry without posting it. Later, 

you or another user can review the entry and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the journal entry. 

• 
You can also click the More actions button and then select Post and Print to post the 

journal entry and then print the record. 

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled, submit the journal entry for approval. 

• 
Click Submit to send the journal entry to the approval queue.  

• 
Click Submit & new to submit the journal entry to the approval queue, and then open 

a new journal entry. 

• 
After a journal entry transaction has been approved and posted, editing the entry is not 

allowed and the Edit link isn’t available. To make any changes, reverse the transaction or 

delete it and resubmit it. After the period is closed, no changes are allowed to the entry, 

including reversal and deletion.

To reverse a transaction that you have previously posted, select the check box next to the 
journal transaction that you want to reverse, and then click the Reverse button. 

8.

description, the system adds the text in the Description field to the Memo fields of the line 

items. You can change this text. 

9.

write a comment to indicate what the change was or why it was made. Comments appear 

on the History tab after you save the record. 

Each time you edit the journal entry, you can add another comment. The system adds the 

comment to the transaction history with the date. The original comment won’t appear in the 

Comment field but appears on the History tab. 

10.

Turning This Journal Entry into a Recurring Journal Entry 

1. 
Select the Make recurring check box to turn this journal entry into a recurring journal entry. 

When selected, the system shows the Schedules section for you to fill in the recurrence 

schedule. When you submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a recurring A/P invoice 

based on the current invoice.  

2. 
In the Schedules section, fill in the Journal entry start date field with the date that you want 

the system to start creating the recurring journal entries. 

3. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select: 

• 
Never: To keep the journal entry perpetually running, select Never.  

• 
Number of occurrences: The End after field appears. To have the journal entry run for 

a limited number of times, type the number of times you want the journal entry to 

recur in the End after field.  

• 
End date: To have the journal entry recur until a specific date, select End date and 

then, in the End on field, type the date on which the last journal entry is to recur.  

4. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, select the frequency that you want the system to 

generate the recurring journal entries. The options are: 

• 
None 

• 
Days 

• 
Weeks 

• 
Months 

• 
Years 

5. 
In the Every field, type the number of time frames to repeat by. For example, if you selected 

Months, then type the number of months to repeat by, such as 6 to have the system create 

a journal entry every 6 months. 

6. 
If you selected Months, then you can select the End of month check box to have the system 

create the journal entry at the end of the month.

Type the email address of the person to whom to send notifications about the recurring 

journal entry in the Email field. 

8. 
Select the Automatically reverse this journal entry check box as needed. If you select it, 

then select one of the related options: Link reversing entry to original journal entry or 

Create independent reversal schedule. 

9.

reverse the journal entry after the original entry in the Reverse by field, and then select the 

time frame: None, Days, Weeks, Months, or Years.

Entering Job Cost Line Item Entries 

If you have the Job Cost application installed, then you may see the Job Cost entries list in the 

journal entry record. Enter the line item information in the Job cost entries list. 

1. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location of the job that you are entering a journal 

entry for.  

• 
For Job Cost line items, the location that you select must have at least one job that is 

not in the Closed status.  

• 
If you selected a source entity in the Transaction information section, then the location 

is the target entity. 

• 
This automatically updates the Base currency field to show the base currency of the 

location. 

2. 
In the Job name drop-down list, select the job for which you are creating a journal entry.  

3. 
In the Cost code drop-down list, select the cost code of the line item.  

When you save the journal entry, this line item applies to the WIP account selected for the 
cost code record . 

4. 
In the Job unit drop-down list, select the unit of the line item.  

The selected cost code must allow segment -level tracking. 

5. 
Use the Txn currency drop-down list to select the currency of the line item.  

This column shows only if your company has multi-currency enabled. 

6. 
In the Debit (or Transaction debit) field, enter the amount that this line item is debiting.  

• 
If you enter a debit amount, you cannot enter a credit amount for the same line item. 

• 
The total of all entered debit amounts shows at the bottom of the section. If the 

journal entry is the Both type, debits and credits are separated between standard and 

Job Cost line items. 

• 
This automatically updates the Base debit field to show the same amount expressed in 

the base currency. 

7. 
In the Credit (or Transaction credit) field, enter the amount that this line item is crediting.  

• 
If you enter a credit amount, you cannot enter a debit amount for the same line item. 

• 
The total of all entered credit amounts shows at the bottom of the section. If the 

journal entry is the Both type, debits and credits are separated between standard and 

Job Cost line items. 

• 
This automatically updates the Base credit field to show the same amount expressed 

in the base currency.

Finishing the Journal Entry 

When you finish entering or editing the journal entry: 

• 
If journal entry approvals are disabled, you can either save the transaction as a draft or post 

it. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the entry without posting it. Later, 

you or another user can review the entry and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the journal entry. 

• 
You can also click the More actions button and then select Post and Print to post the 

journal entry and then print the record. 

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled, submit the journal entry for approval. 

• 
Click Submit to send the journal entry to the approval queue.  

• 
Click Submit & new to submit the journal entry to the approval queue, and then open 

a new journal entry. 

After a journal entry transaction has been approved and posted, editing the entry is not 
allowed and the Edit link isn’t available. To make any changes, reverse the transaction or 
delete it and resubmit it. After the period is closed, no changes are allowed to the entry, 
including reversal and deletion.

Viewing the Trial Balance Report in the Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Workbench > Reports > Trial Balance`


The summary version of the Trial balance report includes all of the G/L Accounts in the system for 

all locations. When you run the Trial Balance report, you can add journal entries when necessary.  

To run the Trial Balance report from the G/L workbench: 

1. 
On the G/L workbench, click the Reports option. 

2. 
In the Report drop-down list, select Trial Balance. The page changes to display the Trial 

Balance report’s filters. 

Setting Up the Filters 

1. 
In the Time Period drop-down list, select reporting period or date. 

If you select Reporting Periods, then the Reporting period drop-down list appears.  

• 
Select the desired reporting period to define the scope of the report.  

• 
In the As of date field, type the date or click the 
 Calendar button, and then select 

the date from the pop-up calendar to have the system add the date to the field. 

If you selected Date, then the Start Date and End date fields appear.  

• 
Type the start and end dates to define the scope of the report.  

2. 
Select the reporting book in the Reporting Book drop-down list. 

3. 
Click the Select button in the Other Books section, and then select the desired adjustment or 

user-defined book to include in the report. 

4. 
If you want the report to cover both the reporting book and the selected other books, then 

select the Combine Reporting Book with Other Books check box. 

5. 
If you want to include accounts that have zero balances in the report, then in Show zero 

balance accounts drop-down list, select All. If you want to show accounts only if they are 

active, select Only with activity. To exclude accounts with zero balances, select Do not 

show. 

6. 
If you want to show accumulated balances for income statement accounts that close into 

retained earnings at year-end, select the Retain YTD balances check box. 

7. 
In the Account multi-select drop-down list, select one or more accounts to include in the 

report. 

8. 
In the Location/Location group drop-down list, select the location or location group to 

include in the report.

9. 
Select the Include subs check box to include subdimensions (child locations) when filtering.

dimension when filtering. 

10. 
If you want to limit the report to one unit, select the unit in the Unit drop-down list. 

11. 
In the Department/Department group drop-down list, select the department or 

department group to include in the report.

Select the Include subs check box to include subdimensions (child departments) when

Opening Books from the G/L Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Workbench > Books > Open`


1.

After an entity’s books are opened, you can post transactions from the top level or entity. In 

other words, opening the books at the top level for a specific entity opens the books at the 

top and entity level but only for the entity you specified. For example, suppose you select a 

period to open, but you do not select an entity. The system opens the books and the 

subledger for all entities. Alternatively, if you select an entity or entity group, then the 

system opens the books and subledger only for the selected entity/entities. 

5.

want to open. The drop-down list defaults to the most recent period, and includes two 

months into the future and up to seven years in the past.

You can scroll through the list by typing the first letter of an option to move quickly through 

the list. Options include:

• 
F: Move from first quarter to fourth quarter to the next. 

• 
S: Move from second quarter to the next. 

• 
T: Move from third quarter to the next. 

• 
M: Move from month ended to the next.  

If you have a custom-named period, then you can use the first letter of your custom period 

to move to it.

Exporting from a Workbench

export the data.

You can use files that you save in the CSV format with any spreadsheet program. After 

selecting this option, the system exports the list as a CSV file.

native format.

format. 

The location of the exported file depends on your browser’s default download functionality. 

All three of these export formats export the entire list, including these links: 

• 
Actions: Exports the HTML code for editing, viewing, approving, and declining the 

transaction. 

• 
Add approver: Click to add another approver for the transaction. 

• 
Send back: Send the transaction back to the requester. 

• 
Status: Click to view the transaction’s approval history.

data into a text file or another application. 

• 
Select Copy with headers to copy the data in the selected cell and the cell’s column header 

to the clipboard.

## Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 73*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Accounting Methods 

RealPage Accounting lets you choose your accounting method—accrual, cash, or both. If you choose both Accrual 

and cash, the system records transactions in separate journals behind the scenes so you can later report on either 

basis. For example, you can run a balance sheet report on accrual basis and then run the same report on cash 

basis. 

The following topics compare your choices for accounting method and provide an overview of the impact of 

choosing both Accrual and cash. 

In This Chapter 

Selecting an Accounting Method ...................................................................................................... 60 

Dual-method: Accrual and Cash ........................................................................................................ 61 

Setting Up Accounting Methods ....................................................................................................... 62 

Changing Accounting Methods ......................................................................................................... 64 

About Periods ............................................................................................................................................ 69 

C H A P T E R 3 

---



### Selecting an Accounting Method
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 74*

Accounting Methods 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Selecting an Accounting Method 

Your administrator can select your accounting method as part of the General Ledger setup. See 

the Accounting Settings Section. 

Accrual 
All transactions are included in reports, regardless of whether cash inflow 

or outflow was part of the transaction. For example, invoices appear in 

accrual basis reports even when unpaid. All journals and reports are 

Accrual.  

• 
Choose Accrual if you are required to report on an Accrual basis. 

Cash 
Transactions appear on reports only when cash impact occurs (in or out). 

For example, bills are reflected in cash basis reports only when paid. 

• 
All journals and reports are Cash. 

• 
Choose Cash if you always report on Cash basis. 

Cash is available only for new RealPage Accounting companies 

Accrual and cash 
Gives you the flexibility to generate reports using either accounting 

method or reporting and can then decide on a report-by-report basis 

which method to use. For reporting, the company might: 

• 
Set the accounting method to Accrual and cash. 

• 
Select Accrual as the default for reporting. This saves time if most 

reports will be run on accrual basis. 

• 
Override the default, selecting Cash on the filters tab when 

needing to report on a cash basis. 

---



### Dual-method: Accrual and Cash
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 75*

Chapter 3: Accounting Methods 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Dual-method: Accrual and Cash 

When you select dual-method accounting, you have the flexibility to report on either accrual or 

cash basis. This flexibility impacts setup and (to some extent) usage of the system. 

Why Use Both Accrual and Cash: An Example 

Suppose that a company used cash-basis accounting at some point in the past and later 

transitioned to accrual method. 

To handle reporting, the company might: 

• 
Set the accounting method to Accrual and cash. 

• 
Select Accrual as the default for reporting. This saves time because most reports will be run 

on accrual basis. 

• 
Override the default, selecting Cash for certain reports that compare against prior years. 

---



### Setting Up Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 76*

Accounting Methods 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up Accounting Methods 

Creating the ability to report on either method involves enabling the feature, providing a cut-over 

period, creating the cash-basis or accrual-basis journals, and then choosing those journals in the 

appropriate applications. Applications that can make use of this feature include the General 

Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Cash Management. 

Considering switching from Accrual to Accrual and cash? Talk to your account manager 
about setup and best practices. 

Workflow 

This is a high-level overview of the setup process: 

1. 
Enable Accrual and cash in the General Ledger Setup page. 

At this time, you also select: 

• 
The cut-off date for switching over to dual-method accounting. 

• 
Your default account method for reporting. 

2. 
Create journals that are Accrual, Cash, or both Accrual and Cash. 

• 
On the Journal Information page, there’s a new option to select whether to Include 

this journal when reporting in Accrual, Cash, or both. 

• 
As a best practice, it’s recommended that you name journals in such a way that you 

can identify them as journals that are cash, accrual, or both. This is because, in several 

locations, the system displays lists of selectable journals that contain all three types. 

For example, Accounts Payable (C) for the cash-basis version. 

3. 
Choose those journals in the configuration pages for the appropriate applications. 

• 
In the setup for Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Cash Management, you’re 

prompted for accrual journals and cash journals. 

• 
In each case, the setup page indicates which type of journal it is expecting. 

You can use dual-reporting only going forward; you cannot re-categorize prior data. The cut-over 

period is chosen in the General Ledger Setup page. It is a good idea to close the books as of the 

cut-off month and work as if you are switching to a new system as of that date. 

During cutoff, you also make a journal entry to correct your books in a journal that has a 

reporting method that is opposite of your default reporting method. In other words, if you were 

accrual based during cutoff, you need to make a journal entry to eliminate payables, receivables, 

expenses, and revenues in a cash-based journal. 

The moment you select the dual-method reporting option in the General Ledger Setup page and 

save, the system unconfigures any of the following applications to which you have subscribed: 

A/P, A/R, and CM. More specifically, the system deselects any journals you previously chose,

Transaction entry 

In most cases, entering transactions is the same, regardless of accounting method. For example,

### Changing Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 78*

Accounting Methods 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Changing Accounting Methods 

You can change your accounting method from cash method or accrual method to the multi-book 

accrual and cash method. RealPage recommends that you discuss this change with a trained 

consultant beforehand, because making the change requires more than only changing the 

selection on the General Ledger configuration page. An analysis of journal configuration to ensure 

the system is prepared for the change must take place ahead of time, because the system will 

make journal updates that cannot be undone. 

Also, the change isn’t retroactive, so you should understand that in addition to configuration 

you’ll need to align your expectations about how reporting will work after the change. 

Before making any changes, read this entire topic and contact your RealPage Accounting 
account manager so that you fully understand the impact and ensure proper deployment. 

Why Companies Change Accounting Methods 

There can be a number of reasons to change accounting methods. For example: 

• 
A company that’s had (or expects) significant growth might want to change from 

cash-based to cash-and-accrual-based accounting. 

• 
An organization that’s been happy with accrual-only based accounting might want the 

deeper insight that cash-and-accrual-based accounting can provide. 

• 
A company that generally run reports in one or the other method has acquired other 

entities and wants to incorporate both accounting methods. 

Before You Change Methods 

You can change your accounting method from cash method or accrual method to the multi-book 

accrual and cash method. RealPage recommends that you discuss this change with a trained 

consultant beforehand, because making the change requires more than only changing the 

selection on the General Ledger configuration page. For example: 

• 
An analysis of journal configuration to ensure that the system is prepared for the change 

must take place ahead of time, because the system will make journal updates that cannot be 

undone. 

• 
Changing accounting methods isn’t retroactive: in addition to configuration, you’ll need to 

align your expectations about how reporting will work after the change. 

• 
Transaction processing should cease while the change is being made. 

• 
While the system will adjust some existing journals, you’ll need to manually add other 

journals. The specific journals to create depends on the method you are moving from. For 

example, if you change to multi-book cash and accrual method from the accrual method, 

you will need to add journals tied to the Cash method for Accounts Payable and Account 

Receivable and for other areas employed such as Credit Cards, and so on.

• 
Further configuration steps are required in many application areas such as Accounts 

Payable, Accounts Receivable, and so on, to connect to the journals that have been created. 

Completing the setup correctly will ensure accurate reporting. 

• 
A temporary mock journal is created and used during the change-over, because some 

journals should remain Cash only or Accrual only. When you perform the change-over, all of 

the configured journals are affected, so to ensure that past transactions aren’t changed, this 

mock journal needs to be used to replace the previous setup. The mock journal is used 

temporarily in the configuration for the subledger application areas (Accounts Payable, 

Accounts Receivable, Cash Management, Time and Expenses, and any others). In a shared 

company, configure the multi-entity inter-company payments and receivables journals from 

the subscription console to use the mock journal as well. This allows you to freshly configure 

the system post-change for the new multi-book setup you have elected. 

• 
Ensure that no journals are selected in your bank accounts because those will also be 

updated. 

• 
When importing historical journal entries to account for legacy data, consider that data is 

now separately gathered for each accounting method with regard to opening balances. 

Thus, data imported must designate the accounting method impacted through the selection 

of the correct journal (associated to Cash or Accrual) to ensure all history is accurately 

captured in both reporting books. If you are converting from Accrual to Cash and Accrual, 

you will import Cash Basis opening balances (you already have the accrual opening 

balances). 

• 
Bank register reporting requires special attention: when you make the switch, the bank 

register pulls in the activity posted in both reporting books, essentially duplicating the 

numbers. In this case three journal entries are needed to correct the bank register. Also note 

it is recommended that this change only apply at the end of a reconciled period. 

• 
Integrations posting journal entries will also be impacted so also be sure to consider what 

integrations you have in place and how they should be configured going forward. 

Contact your RealPage trained consultant before making this change so that you can fully 
understand the impact and ensure proper deployment. 

Transaction Entry 

In most cases, entering transactions is the same, regardless of accounting method. For example, 

users entering a bill don’t need to know whether the transaction is accrual, cash, or both. The 

system handles the posting to accrual and cash journals behind the scenes. 

However, entering a journal entry directly in the General Ledger requires that you consider the 

accounting method(s) that should be affected and select the appropriate journal accordingly. 

Before switching from Cash or Accrual to Accrual and cash, talk to your RealPage account 
manager about setup and best practices.

Preparing for the Change 

1. 
Best practice is to close the books as of the cut-off month and work as if you are switching 

to a new system as of that date. 

2. 
Create the mock journal and assign it to all the configurations to ensure that existing data 

isn’t changed without your specific intent during the switch. When you enable the account 

method change for Cash and Accrual, all journals that are set in the application 

configuration will automatically be changed to both. To ensure that you control this change, 

the best practice is to create the mock journal for temporary use during the changeover. For 

easier troubleshooting, this specific title is recommended for the journal. 

3. 
Verify which applications your company is subscribed to by navigating to Company > 

Subscriptions. For each application, select Configure. 

4. 
Have other users stop processing transactions.

For each application, configure that application to use the new mock journal. Common 

applications to check are: 

• 
Accounts Receivable 

• 
Accounts Payable 

• 
Cash Management 

• 
(Shared environment only) Multi-Entity Console Subscription area for Inter-Company 

Payments and Receivables 

6. 
Verify that all bank accounts (checking accounts, credit card accounts, and savings accounts) 

don’t have a journal assigned. 

7. 
Change any other applications and any integration-related setup areas as needed.

in the future.

### About Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 83*

Chapter 3: Accounting Methods 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

About Periods 

The RealPage Financial Suite refers to periods in different contexts. This topic lists and describes 

each type of period.  

• 
Accounting periods: Custom accounting periods can be set up when you first configure the 

company. Custom accounting periods allow you to establish a non-standard month-end. 

After the initial configuration, the company’s accounting periods cannot be changed. The 

use of accounting periods lets you compare past and present performance. Transactions are 

recorded and separated into different periods such as months, quarters, and years. See also 

Reporting period. 

• 
Aging period: An aging period is a range of days used to categorize outstanding invoices 

by how long they have been unpaid. 

• 
Analysis period (on page 617): Used for budget variance analysis, an analysis period is a 

specific time interval used for analyzing data. 

• 
Close period (on page 517): A close period is a set time frame when a company finalizes its 

financial results and prepares to release them to the public. During this time, the company 

freezes its financial data to ensure accuracy and prevent manipulation.  

• 
Open period (on page 523): An open period is a period of time that a ledger is open for 

transactions.  

• 
Reporting period: Reporting periods are used for reports and budgets, and when you open 

and close books. A reporting period is a time frame that that defines the scope of a report 

or budget. You can predefine reporting periods with the Reporting Period menu option, or 

set the period on-the-fly as you create reports.  

• 
Timesheet period: A timesheet period is the time interval covered by a timesheet.

combined into one deposit to the bank. 

• 
A/P trade accounts: Set up an account for each vendor used by the property. 

• 
Create account records to mirror your bank accounts so that you can track transactions as 

you draw from your bank accounts to fund repairs and other operating expenses.

Types of Accounts: Financial and Statistical 

There are two types of accounts in the system — financial accounts and statistical accounts. 

Unlike financial accounts, which track monetary value, statistical accounts track operational data 

(such as headcount) and can be used in combination with financial accounts to track metrics such 

as revenue per headcount. 

Both types of accounts are located on the General Ledger menu, under:

RealPage Accounting Simplifies the Chart of Accounts 

RealPage Accounting features such as dimensions and account groups enable you to maintain a 

clean chart of accounts, with only the accounting and operational data that you need to track. The 

system support two dimensions: department and location. 

Because the system tracks department and location separately using dimensions, there’s no need 

for duplicate accounts with different combinations of departments and locations. 

In RealPage Accounting, you do this: 

• 
Expenses - Payroll 

But not this: 

• 
Expenses - Payroll Dallas 

• 
Expenses - Payroll New York 

• 
Expenses - Payroll Los Angeles 

In addition, you can use segments to track your data without having to complicate your accounts. 

See Segments (on page 686).

### Accounts with Budgets
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 92*

Accounts 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accounts with Budgets 

It’s possible to budget for both income statement and balance sheet accounts (on page 77), 

although many companies include only income statement accounts in the budget. 

Income statement accounts 

Income statement accounts are reported as the activity for the reporting period, and can be 

described as for the period. The budget entry should be the budgeted activity for the period. For 

example, if the budget amount for an income statement account is 4 for January and 4 for 

February and 4 for March, the reported amount for the monthly period of March would be 4 and 

the amount for the first quarter would be 12. 

Balance sheet accounts 

The system reports balance sheet amounts as of a point in time, which can be described as 

cumulative balance as long as there’s a budget amount for each period. The budget entry for a 

period is the change in the balance sheet account. For example, if the ending budget account 

balance for January is 2 and the ending budget account balance for February is expected to be 6, 

the February budget amount is entered as 4. 

For balance sheet accounts, you must enter a budget amount for every period in order to keep a 
cumulative balance. If there’s no budget amount for a period, the system sees this as no budget, 
so there won’t be a cumulative amount. In this case, the budget amount isn’t carried forward 
from the last period. 

Statistical accounts 

Statistical accounts can also be included in a budget, and can be defined as for the period or 

cumulative when they are created. 

• 
If the statistical account is defined as for the period, the budget amount should be entered 

as the change for the period. For example, suppose that a headcount account has an 

opening budget balance of 243. If you expect headcount to go up by 10 in a particular 

month, you would enter 10 as the budget amount. 

• 
If the statistical account is defined as cumulative, the budget amount should be entered as 

of ending balance. For example, if the headcount has an opening budget balance of 243 

and you expect the headcount to go up by 10, you would enter 253 as the budget amount.

Accounts with Categories 

With account categories, you can group accounts easily without worrying about restrictive 

account numbering. Out-of-box account groups and financial reports are built based on these 

account categories, automatically pulling in accounts tagged with the appropriate category, which 

means you don’t have to reconfigure reports and account groups every time you add an account. 

Instead, assign the right category, and the data will be pulled in at runtime. Using categories is 

the quickest way to get data into a report. 

Categories are available only to those companies that were created with a QuickStart setup 

template. 

You can see if your company was set up using a QuickStart on the Company information page. If 

the Setup template field on the Accounting tab is populated, then that is the template type that 

your company uses. If it is blank, then a template was not specified during setup and categories 

aren’t available to you. 

Out-of-box account groups included with a QuickStart template are already mapped to a 

category which are used in out-of-box financial reports and graphs. When you map an account to 

one of these categories, that account is automatically rolled up to the correct place in the financial 

reports and graphs. 

Import an Account-to-Account Category Mapping 

Categories are part of the QuickStart template, and are included in the chart of accounts import 

template.  

Use the template to import chart of account information, including the categories assigned to 

your accounts. 

You can’t create new categories. 

The Category field works differently from other template fields to ensure that you select a 

category. You can select a category from the drop-down list or type a category in the field. The 

system validates the category. If you typed a category in the field and a category with that name 

doesn’t exist, the system sends an error message. 

---


<!-- Page 94 -->
Accounts 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The system depends on a pre-defined list of categories. You can assign a category to an account, 

but you can’t change the category name in the template. If you change the name or type 

category that doesn’t exist, the import will fail. 

Account Categories List 

Download a list of account categories for your template and QuickStart type. 

Mapping Accounts to Account Categories Using CSV 

The best way to associate a large list of accounts with the existing categories is by uploading a 

CSV file. You edit your data in Excel, choose the appropriate categories for the accounts, and then 

upload the file to RealPage Accounting. 

Categories are used to create pre-defined, out-of-box reports and other elements in the system. 

To ensure that these reports work correctly, you can’t change existing categories or create new 

ones in the system. 

Instead, you can create your own account groups to group accounts however you’d like, and then 

use those account groups in reports.

The Category field is displayed only for companies that were created with a setup template 

or chose one later. If you need to assign categories to many accounts, the easiest way is to 

export your chart of accounts, make the changes in the file, and then upload the file. 

When Your System Was Set Up With the Services Template 
By default, the categories Manpower and Direct materials are assigned to account groups 
that are only used in the reports Project Profitability and Project Estimation Versus Actual. 
These two categories do not appear in balance sheet reports or income statements. If you 
assign an account to either of these two categories, and you want it to show up in your 
balance sheet, income statement, or other reports, you must manually assign these 
categories to the appropriate account groups. 

6. 
In the Account type drop-down list, select either Balance sheet account or Income 

statement account. 

• 
Balance sheet accounts are snapshots of the current state of a company’s assets, 

liabilities, and equity at a specific time. 

• 
Income statement accounts (sometimes called profit and loss statements) are 

cumulative for the selected period. 

7. 
For Normal balance, select either Debit or Credit. 

When you create an account, you specify whether the normal balance, from an accounting 

standpoint, is a debit or credit. For example, expense accounts are normally debit accounts. 

Sales accounts are normally a credit. If you were to run a Trial Balance report, the normal 

balance of the accounts is what determines whether the account is a credit or debit. 

8. 
For the Period end closing type, select whether the account is a closing or non-closing 

account. For closing accounts, select an account in the Close into account drop-down list. 

• 
Instead of manually closing accounts at year-end, you can set them to be closing 

accounts and then specify the account in which to close that period. 

• 
Income statement accounts should be closing accounts; balance sheet accounts 

should be non-closing accounts. 

• 
For all income statement accounts, the close-into account will typically be Retained 

Earnings. The system then zeros closing-type accounts into retained earnings at 

year-end. 

9. 
In the G/L account alternative drop-down list, select a G/L account for the system to use as 

an alternative payables account. The account override must be enabled for this field to 

appear. 

10. 
The default status is Active. If you want to prevent this G/L account from appearing in lists, 

select Inactive in the Status drop-down list. (You can still list inactive accounts by clicking 

the Include inactive check box in lists.)

You cannot make a G/L account inactive when the account is selected on the configuration 
page of an application or if the account is being used in a budget. 

11. 
Select the Disallow Direct Posting check box to prevent direct entry of journal entries to the 

subledger control account (for example, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, etc.). 

Use this control to ensure that the account balance for the subledger account is accurate 

and has the necessary subledger details supporting the figure, rather than a direct entry that 

would not be reflected in the subledger application area. 

When a G/L account is marked as Disallow Direct Posting, the system allows OneSite 
transactions to be created for that G/L account (as these are system
-created entries) 
but still disallows manually created journal entries to post to the G/L account.  

12. 
Select the Require Unit check box to require the user to select a unit when using this 

account. 

13. 
Select the Require asset category/type during invoice entry check box if you want to 

require users to enter asset information whenever they select this G/L account when 

entering an A/P invoice. 

This option appears when the Enable asset in invoice entry check box is selected in 
Accounts Payable settings. 

14. 
Select the Use for budgeting check box if you want to use this G/L account in budgets. 

15. 
Select the Allow as Elimination Account check box to allow this account to be selected 

when creating an elimination entity. 

Requiring Dimensions 

Dimensions drive visibility into the parts of your business that matter most. You can require users 

to select dimensions when selecting the G/L account. When you require a dimension for a G/L 

account, all transactions that post to that account must include the dimension or dimensions that 

you select here. If you require multiple dimensions, all dimensions must be included to post to the 

G/L account. 

Use the Require Dimensions section to select the dimensions that you want to require for this 

account. 

• 
To require dimensions for transaction entries assigned to this account, select the dimension 

check boxes to require. All selected dimensions will be required. Supported dimensions 

include: 

• 
Department 

• 
Location 

• 
Customer 

• 
Vendor

Employee 

If This Account Overrides Other Accounts 

To flag this account as an override of the default A/P or A/R G/L account, select the type of G/L 

account that it can override. Although you can flag any account as an available override account, 

typically, you flag an A/R or A/P account. 

• 
Payables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts available as 

override accounts for bill and adjustment transactions, and for transactions involving a 

specific vendor. 

• 
Receivables account: Adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts available as 

override accounts for invoice and adjustment transactions, and for transactions involving a 

specific customer. 

As you enter transactions, you can select the same alternative G/L account for all line items, or 

select alternative accounts individually per line item. On the Vendor and Customer pages, you 

can select one alternative G/L account to use for balancing all transactions involving that vendor. 

Currently, this feature applies to A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments only. It doesn ’t 
apply to recurring A/P invoices or A/R invoices, manual payments, manual deposits, quick check 
entry, quick A/P invoice entry, quick A/R invoice entry, or advances. 

Including the Account in Chart Types 

You can simplify the accounting task by creating subsets of the chart of accounts. These subsets 

are called chart types. The Chart types option appears when your company has the chart type 

feature enabled. 

If your company uses chart types, every time you create a new account, consider adding the 

account to each appropriate chart type. 

To add an account to a chart type: 

1. 
Click the Chart types’ Select button. The multi-select box opens. 

2. 
Select the chart type in which to include this account. 

You can select more than one chart type if you need to add the account to multiple chart 
types. 

Filling In the Reporting Accounts Mapping Section 

•

Reporting accounts mapping section to map G/L accounts (on page 203). 

• 
You can also generate and display reports using account sets other than your General

governing bodies who need to see reports in their charts of accounts. See the Reporting

Filling In the Tax Code Fields 

The Tax return code and M-3 return code fields display only if you have enabled tax codes on 

the General Ledger setup page. Use these fields if you use third-party software applications to 

prepare client tax returns. 


> **Navigation Path:** `To enable tax codes for your G/L accounts, point to Company > Setup > Subscriptions. On the`


Subscriptions page, click General Ledger, and then click Configure. When the General ledger 

setup page appears, find the GAAP and tax section, and select Enable tax codes. 

Enter the tax code in the Tax return code field to map tax codes to the tax forms you need to use. 

(Whether you fill out one or both of these tax code boxes depends on which item or items your 

tax software requires.) 

For example, if you use Thomson Reuters GoSystem Tax, and you want to map tax return codes to 

a tax form (such as Form 1120, Form 1065, etc.), you must enter the tax code in the Tax return 

code field. Similarly, to map M-3 return codes to your M-3 form, you must enter the tax code in 

the M-3 return code field. 

You can also input tax codes for all of your G/L accounts as a group and then import the 
spreadsheet that will map all of the required data from the system to its corresponding places 
on your tax forms. 
To do this:  
Open the Company menu, and then click Import Data. 
When the Import data page opens, in the Set Up Company Master List section, next to the listing 
for Account Tax Return Codes, click Import.

Importing G/L Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Chart of Accounts`


This import allows you to add new accounts and to update existing G/L account records. 

Workflow for Importing G/L Accounts 

• 
Download the chart of accounts template. 

• 
Fill the template with account data. 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the file. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Chart of Accounts row, and then click the Template link in the row. The system 

either downloads the template to your browser’s default download folder, or prompts you 

to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template  

To fill in the template with your data: 

1. 
Open the template file in your spreadsheet application. 

2. 
For each G/L account, add the required information: 

• 
ACCT_NO: Account number. The account number must conform to the primary/sub 


> **Navigation Path:** `account specification as it is defined in Company > Setup.`


• 
ACCT_NAME: Type the account name. It can be up to 80 characters long. 

• 
ACCT_TYPE: Type N for Balance Sheet, I for Income Statement 

• 
NORMAL_BALANCE: Type DB if the account has a debit normal balance, type CR for a 

credit normal balance. 

• 
CLOSEABLE: Type N for non-closing, type C for closing to, type R for closed to. 

• 
CLOSETOACCT_NO: Type the account number that this G/L account closes to. This 

field is required if you set CLOSEABLE to C. The account number that you specify must 


> **Navigation Path:** `conform to the primary/sub account specification as it is defined in Company > Setup.`

#### Inactivating or Deleting an Account
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 109*

Chapter 5: Accounts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Inactivating or Deleting an Account 

You can inactivate an account you no longer want to prevent yourself and users from seeing it in 

lists. You can also delete an account from the Accounts list, unless the account is used in a book 

transaction. After you delete an account, it cannot be restored. If you’re unsure about deleting an 

account, set its status to Inactive. 

If you want to be warned when you’re about to delete an account or other type of record from the 
system, click your login name in the upper-left corner of any page, and then click My preferences. 
On the Preferences page, select the Warn on delete check box. 

You can make a G/L account inactive only if it is not associated with any open online purchase 

orders or eInvoices. 

To inactivate an account: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Click the Accounts option to open the list of your accounts. 

3. 
Find the account that you want to inactivate, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
On the General Ledger Accounts page, change the Status of the account to “Inactive,” and 

then click Save. 

If the G/L account that you are trying to inactivate is associated with a transaction, then the 
system displays an error message warning you that you cannot delete a G/L account that is 
associated with an open online purchase order or eInvoice. This warning ensures that all orders 
and electronic invoices successfully arrive in RealPage Accounting. 

To delete an account: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Click the Accounts option to open the list of your accounts. 

3. 
Find the account you want to remove, and then click the Delete link. 

4. 
Click OK to confirm the deletion. 

If a G/L account is referenced by an account label, you must remove the account label 

before you can inactivate or delete the account. Account labels are set up in A/P and A/R.

#### Viewing and Printing Account Information
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 110*

Accounts 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide

Viewing and Printing Account Information 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Accounts`


You can view a list of accounts from the Accounts list, or you can view and print the details of a 

particular account from the General Ledger Account page. 

The items you can see on this page vary slightly depending on whether your company is an 

Enterprise, or a multi-entity shared company.  

If your company is a multi-entity shared company, when viewing the list of G/L accounts at the 

top level, you initially see all items regardless of where they were created. To see items created 

only at the top level, clear the Include private check box.  

G/L account records created prior to 2021 could be created at the entity level. G/L account 

records that you create today can be created only at the top level.  

• 
To include the older private records in the list, select the Include private check box. The 

Entity column appears in the list and shows the entity to which the (vendor) record belongs.  

• 
To exclude private records, clear the Include private check box. 

Also, when you edit an item that was created in an entity, your changes apply to that entity. After 

you save your changes, you are returned to the top level. 

To view accounts: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Accounts. The list of accounts opens showing your chart of accounts.  

3. 
Find the account you want to view in more detail, and then click the View link. 

To print account information: 

1. 
From the Accounts list, find the account you want to print, and then click the View link. 

2. 
On the General Ledger Accounts page, click Print to, and then select either PDF or XML for 

your printing format.

Specifying Different Default Accounts by Property 

You can select default accounts at the entity level that are different from those specified at the top 

level. 

To use this feature: 

• 
The chart types feature must be enabled. 

• 
You must have administrator-level privileges. 

• 
Your system must be a multi-entity shared environment. 

•

### G/L Accounts vs Bank G/L Accounts
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 120*

Accounts 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

G/L Accounts vs Bank G/L Accounts 

A Bank G/L account is a cash account linked to a real bank and used for reconciliation, while a 

regular G/L account is any other account in the chart of accounts used for financial reporting and 

posting. 

• 
A G/L account is any account in your chart of accounts. 

• 
A Bank G/L account is a special type of G/L account that is tied to a real-world bank 

account and used for cash management. 

They behave differently in the system because they serve different purposes. 

Use bank G/L accounts for cash, reconciliation, and system controls. Use regular G/L accounts for 

everything else. 

G/L Accounts 

This is the broad category. It includes every account in your chart of accounts: 

• 
Assets 

• 
Liabilities 

• 
Equity 

• 
Revenue 

• 
Expenses 

Examples: 

• 
1100 – Accounts Receivable 

• 
2100 – Accounts Payable 

• 
4100 – Rental Income 

• 
5200 – Repairs & Maintenance 

A regular G/L account: 

• 
Is used for financial reporting 

• 
Can be posted to by journals, subledgers, allocations, etc. 

• 
Does not have any special cash-handling rules 

• 
Does not connect to a bank feed or reconciliation workflow 

It’s part of the accounting structure. 

Bank G/L Accounts 

A Bank G/L account is a G/L account but with extra properties and system behavior because it 

represents actual cash in a real bank. 

---


<!-- Page 121 -->
Chapter 5: Accounts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Bank G/L accounts include system controls that protect cash integrity — such as restricted 

posting, required reconciliation, and automated matching — while regular G/L accounts behave 

like standard ledger accounts without these cash-specific rules. 

Examples: 

• 
1000 – Operating Cash 

• 
1010 – Security Deposit Bank Account 

• 
1020 – Reserve Account 

A Bank G/L account: 

• 
Is linked to a real bank account 

This allows the system to track: 

• 
Bank feeds 

• 
Bank statements 

• 
Cleared vs. uncleared transactions 

• 
Reconciliation status 

• 
Has special rules in Financial Suite 

Bank G/L accounts are used by: 

• 
Cash Management 

• 
Bank Reconciliation 

• 
AP/AR cash posting 

• 
Deposit workflows 

• 
Payment processing 

• 
Cannot be treated like a normal G/L account 

You cannot: 

• 
Reclassify into/out of it the same way 

• 
Post certain journal types directly (but you can post a manual journal entry to a bank 

G/L account). 

• 
Use it for non-cash activity 

• 
Because the system protects the integrity of cash. 

---

#### Changing the Default G/L Account for a Bank Account
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 123*

Changing the Default G/L Account for a Bank Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Customer Utility Tool > Default Bank G/L Account 
Change`


Use this workflow when you need to switch banks, but you want to use the same G/L account that 

you used for your original bank. 

To assign the original bank account to the historical G/L account: 

1. 
Create a G/L account for the purpose of tracking records from the original bank account. 

Give the account a name that indicates that the G/L account is for historical records. 

2. 
Switch the G/L account of the old bank account to the historical G/L account.  

• 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

• 
Point to the Customer utility tool option, and then select Default bank G/L account 

change from the drop-down list. 

• 
In the Bank account drop-down list, select the bank G/L account that you plan to use 

for the new bank account. 

• 
In the To drop-down list, select the historical G/L account to assign the old account to 

the historical G/L bank account. 

• 
In the Up to date field, type the date that you want the system to make the 

switchover.  

3. 
Add the new bank account to the system. In the Default bank G/L account drop-down list, 

select the G/L account that you used for the original account.  

The system recodes all transactions from the old G/L account to the new G/L account up to 

the date that you specified.

either downloads the template to your browser’s default download folder, or prompts you 

to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template  

To fill in the template with your data: 

1. 
Open the template file in your spreadsheet application. 

2. 
For each statistical account, add the required information: 

• 
ACCT_NO: Account number. The account number must conform to the primary/sub 


> **Navigation Path:** `account specification as it is defined in Company > Setup: Company Info.`

REQ_DEPT: Type T if you want to require the selection of a department. Otherwise, 

type F. The default is false. 

•

for later use. 

• 
REPORT_TYPE: Type N to set the account to a cumulative balance, type the letter I for

### Statistical Accounts Page
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 130*



#### Adding Statistical Accounts
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 130*

Statistical Accounts 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Statistical Accounts Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Statistical Accounts > 
Add/Edit/View`


Use this page to manage statistical accounts. 

When your company has multiple shared entities, you can share statistical accounts either by all 

entities or it can be reserved for use by a specific entity (private). 

Adding Statistical Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Statistical Accounts`


When you add statistical accounts, assign numbers to them from a completely different account 

range so that statistical accounts are not inadvertently grouped with G/L accounts. Statistical 

accounts can be consolidated similarly to G/L accounts if you have a consolidated structure of 

companies with subsidiaries. 

Individual statistical accounts are typically rolled up into account groups for use in reports. 

A good way to see if your account groups are mapped correctly is to view the Account Group 

Hierarchy report in the General Ledger application. 

To create a statistical account: 

1. 
On the Statistical accounts page, enter the account number. 

• 
The sub account is optional. 

• 
The number of characters allowed for account numbers is set when the Chart of 

Accounts is created (to a maximum of 24), so the number of characters allowed might 

differ between companies. 

• 
When you add statistical accounts, you should assign a number in a different account 

range so that statistical accounts are not inadvertently grouped with G/L accounts in 

reports. 

2. 
In the Title field, enter the account title, such as Headcount, as it should appear in reports. 

3. 
From the Report type drop-down list, choose how per-period amounts for the account 

should be reported in financial reports. 

• 
For the period: Reports the net change for the period, similar to how income and 

expense amounts are reported. 

• 
Cumulative balance: Reports the balance of the account for the period, similar to how 

balance sheet amounts are reported. 

Regardless of the report type, data entry is always a net change (increases and

graphs, and performance cards. If you are new to account groups, we recommend that you start by reviewing the 

Account Groups overview (on page 124).

groups such as “Cash and Cash Equivalents,” and then use them across many different reports, graphs, and 

dashboard performance cards.

### Account Groups Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 138*

Account Groups 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Account Groups Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Account Groups`



> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Account Groups`


Account groups are the fundamental building blocks of financial reporting in RealPage 

Accounting. 

Account groups simplify reporting by organizing accounts into reusable structures (such as 

“Assets” and “Expenses”) that are separate from the reports, graphs, and performance cards that 

use them. These structures: 

• 
Roll up and organize accounts. 

• 
Create the headings and subtotals in reports. 

General Ledger accounts are shown on financial statements only if they are included in an 
account group. Accounts can’t be added directly to a report. 

Although every company’s account groups will be different, your account groups will likely 

contain groupings related to assets, expenses, revenue, and more. 

The most basic types of account groups contain either individual accounts or other account 

groups. 

• 
Account groups of type Accounts, Statistical accounts, Category, or Statistical category (on 

page 133) are used to select individual accounts. 

For example, “Cash and Cash Equivalents” might contain some bank accounts and petty 

cash. 

• 
An account group of type Group of account groups contains other account groups. 

For example, “Assets” might contain other account groups, such as “Current Assets” and 

“Fixed Assets,” which in turn contain other account groups. 

---


<!-- Page 139 -->
Chapter 7: Account Groups 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

By nesting groups, you can create a hierarchy of groupings for reporting purposes, with the 

lowest level containing individual accounts. 

a) Account groups can contain other groups. Nesting groups creates hierarchy. 

b) At the lowest levels, account groups contain individual accounts. 

You cannot use computation account groups in financial forecasting reports. Because in 
forecasting reports you could use an “As of date ” in a partial month, mixing part actual numbers 
and part budget, the computation needed cannot accommodate computation account groups. 

---



#### Reusable Building Blocks
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 140*

Account Groups 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide

Reusable Building Blocks 

Since account groups are maintained separately from the financial statements that use them, they 

are easy to manage and update. 

• 
Account groups (such as Assets) can be used in multiple reports. 

• 
As you add or modify accounts, you need only make sure that they’re in the right account 

groups. 

• 
Changes to the account group affect all reports that use the account group.

#### Role in Financial Reports, Graphs, and Performance Cards
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 141*

Chapter 7: Account Groups 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Role in Financial Reports, Graphs, and Performance Cards 

Account groups can be used across any number of reports, graphs, and dashboard performance 

cards. 

When you create a financial report or graph, you are asked to select the account group or groups 

that you want to include. In the example below, the rows in a balance sheet report are formed by 

adding two account groups: Assets, and Liabilities and Equity. 

---


<!-- Page 142 -->
Account Groups 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

When these top-level account groups are included in a report, the system automatically includes 

all subgroups and accounts. In the report, each account group gets a heading row and a total 

row, with indentation used to depict the hierarchy. Additionally, each top-level account group 

(such as Assets and Liabilities and Equity) receives a grand total. 

Account groups let you organize accounts and facilitate headings and totals on reports. 

When you design your account groups, keep in mind where you want headings and totals to 

appear, and where you want your grand totals. In income statements, it’s typical to have only one 

account group (Net income), which contains other account groups. That way, your income 

statements contain a grand total for Net income. 

By default, account groups are fully expanded on reports to show the complete hierarchy. 
However, you can create reports using the same account groups, but with different levels of 
detail. 

---



#### Account Groups and the Calculation Method
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 143*

Chapter 7: Account Groups 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Performance cards, often included at the top of dashboards, are also based on account groups. 

Each performance card is based on a single account group, which determines the value that users 

see. Although you can use any account group as the basis for a performance card, it’s common to 

use a computation account group, which consist of a mathematical equation. For example, Net 

Profit Margin can be constructed as Net Income divided by Total Income. 

Account Groups and the Calculation Method 

When using account groups in reports, you’ll want the report to calculate only the amounts in the 

period you select. Every account group has a default method of calculating amounts on reports. 

For example, account groups that contain income or expense accounts are typically calculated for 

the period. Calculation methods can be: 

• 
For period: calculate only the amounts in the period you selected 

• 
Start of period: calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the start of the selected period 

• 
End of period: calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the end of the selected period 

The latter is useful in a balance-forward situation. For example, say your fiscal year runs from 

January 1 to December 31. If you run a report in March, choosing Start of period totals the data 

from January 1 to March 1. 

The Interest expense category is configured to Credit normal, even though sometimes it’s 
assumed to be Debit normal. This is intentional. The interest expense account has a debit 
balance as the default, but in reporting it appears as a negative amount, offsetting the interest 
income. 

---



#### Organize Accounts and Create Hierarchy
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 144*

Account Groups 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Organize Accounts and Create Hierarchy 

You’ll notice that your chart of accounts is flat, without hierarchy. For example, individual expense 

accounts aren’t rolled up into Expenses or Operating Expenses. Instead, the organization of 

accounts for reporting is done outside of the chart of accounts, using account groups. 

For example, your chart of accounts might include: 

• 
Revenue - Services 

• 
Revenue - Subscriptions 

• 
Expenses - Marketing 

• 
Expenses - Payroll 

• 
Expenses - Utilities 

These accounts aren’t included directly in financial reports, such as a Net Income report. Instead, 

financial reports are built from account groups, which organize accounts and determine where 

subtotals and totals are created. 

The same account can be part of multiple account groups, and you can create a hierarchy of 
account groups. 

Groups of Accounts 

The simplest account group is one level deep, and consists of member accounts. When you are 

establishing an account group hierarchy, start by creating groups of member accounts. 

• 
To create a group of G/L accounts, select Accounts as the structure type. 

• 
To create a group of statistical accounts, select Statistical accounts as the structure type. 

---

G/L accounts.

b) The Structure type is Accounts. 

c) This is the range of accounts in this group. 

In the example above, notice that the structure type is Accounts, which means that it contains 

individual accounts or ranges of accounts. 

If your company was configured using a setup template, you already have a set of pre-defined 

account groups based on the Category or Statistical category. These work the same way as 

groups of accounts or statistical accounts, except that they are based on the category assigned to 

accounts rather than a specific list of accounts.

For example, you might create a Current Assets account group that contains other account

a) The Structure type is Group of account groups. 

b) Select the groups of account groups to include.

Types of Account Groups 

When you create a new account group, you indicate the type that you want it to be. Different 

account group types yield different results in your financial reports. These are they available types 

of account groups: 

• 
Accounts 

• 
Account Groups 

• 
Statistical Accounts 

• 
Category or Statistical Category Accounts 

• 
Computation Account Groups 

Accounts Account Groups 

Accounts are the most basic type of account groups and consist of one or more G/L accounts 

from your chart of accounts. You can include individual named accounts or ranges of accounts. 

For example, you might create a Cash and Cash Equivalents account group that contains various 

bank and investment accounts.

Statistical account groups include accounts that contain specific non-financial data – for example, 

occupancy, square footage, or hotel rooms. Using statistical account groups, you can calculate 

against and report on data to get a virtually unlimited variety of ratios and business metrics, such 

as average deal size or revenue per hotel room.

Category or Statistical Category Account Groups 

These apply if you used a setup template when you first created your company in the system. If 

so, the system automatically assigns pre-configured account groups to each of the accounts in 

your chart of accounts; those account groups, in turn, are used in pre-designed standard financial 

reports and graphs.  

As you create new accounts, you tag each new account with a category, which automatically 

includes that account in the relevant account groups. 

A group that is based on a category displays the same way as a group of accounts. The only 

difference is that the accounts for the group are selected by category. 

To find out if your company was created using a QuickStart template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Configuration section, click Company, and then select the Accounting tab. 

3. 
Check under Setup template. If the field is blank, the company was not set up using a 

template. 

---


<!-- Page 152 -->
Account Groups 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Computation Account Groups 

Computation account groups consist of other account groups or individual accounts that you use 

as components in a mathematical equation. The system displays results of the equation in your 

financial report. For example, the “Revenue per Unit” equation consists of the “Total Income” 

account group divided by the “Total Units” account group. 

Computation account group is the only type of account group that allows you to set the number 

of decimal places. Any computation account group includes this option. 

• 
A commonly used computation-type account group shows an operating margin using the 

formula Operating net income divided by Net sales. Define the number of decimal places 

and type, and optionally include the unit used, such as number or percent. 

• 
To use more than the default two decimal places without affecting the actual numbers, 

create a computation account group that: 

• 
Includes only one account group. 

• 
Has a computation formula as Constant, and that constant is set to one. 

• 
Has an action to multiply the selected account group. 

• 
Has Decimal places set to the number of decimal places to display when no rounding 

is applied. The minimum is zero and the maximum is nine. 

You can then use that group as part of other groups, as a standalone group, or in performance 

cards on dashboards.

#### Account Groups and Normal Balance
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 153*
