Account Groups and Normal Balance 

The normal balance of the account group adjusts whether the accounts in the group are a credit 

or debit, in the context of a financial report. 

• 
If the Normal balance of an account group is Credit, then credit accounts appear as a 

positive and debit accounts appear as a negative. 

• 
If the Normal balance of an account group is Debit, then credit accounts appear as a 

negative and debit accounts appear as a positive. 

For example, Expenses is a debit account group and the accounts in the group, such as Utilities, 

are typically debit accounts. This causes the accounts in Expenses to appear as a positive number 

on income statements. Additionally, Net Income is a credit account group, which causes Expenses 

to be treated as a debit when determining total net income. 

Organize Through Account Groups 

You’ll also notice that your chart of accounts is flat, without hierarchy. For example, individual 

expense accounts aren’t rolled up into Expenses or Operating Expenses. Instead, the organization 

of accounts for reporting is done outside of the chart of accounts, using account groups. 

For example, your chart of accounts might include: 

• 
Revenue - Services 

• 
Revenue - Subscriptions 

• 
Expenses - Marketing 

• 
Expenses - Payroll 

• 
Expenses - Utilities 

These accounts aren’t included directly in financial reports, such as a Net Income report. Instead, 

financial reports are built from account groups, which organize accounts and determine where 

subtotals and totals are created. 

The same account can be part of multiple account groups, and you can create a hierarchy of 

account groups.

#### Account Group Examples

Account Group Examples 

These are some examples of account groups that you might find useful. 

• 
An account group called “Withdrawal” that’s filtered for credit only on your bank accounts; 

the system will display only credit transactions such as withdrawal transactions in the report. 

• 
An account group that contains summary revenues for a single location, such as Sales - 

Location 1, and include it as a row in a report. 

• 
An account group that contains only the debit transactions to an equipment account, such 

as Equipment Purchases. 

• 
The Core AP/PO entry account group contains the accounts that can be used when creating 

purchase orders. 

Assign accounts to this account group when you want to limit the accounts that can be used 

with purchase orders. If no accounts are assigned to the Core AP/PO entry account group, 

then all accounts can be associated with purchase orders.  

Multi-Entity Report Structures 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Subscriptions`


Multi-Entity Shared > Multi-Entity Report Structures 

You can create report structures both at the top level and at the entity level of a multi-entity 

shared company. 

In practice, many companies create and manage the majority of account groups and dimension 

structures at the top level of the company. These report structures are then automatically shared 

by all entities, and available for use in financial reports, graphs, and performance cards. 

Best Practices 

To determine whether to create a report structure at the top level or entity level, consider who 

needs to access the structure. 

• 
If a report structure should be available to all entities, create it at the top level. Account 

groups and dimension structures created at the top level automatically appear in the 

corresponding lists in each entity. 

Report structures created at the top level can be edited only at the top level. 

• 
If an entity has particular reporting needs, users can create report structures at the entity 

level. These report structures can then be used within that entity, along with any report 

structures that were inherited from the top level. 

When a user switches to an entity, the user can’t see report structures that were created 
in another entity. 

---



#### Viewing the Account Groups List
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 156*

Account Groups 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Top-Level Report Structures 

From the top level of a multi-entity shared company, you can edit and use all reporting structures, 

including those created at the entity level. 

• 
By default, lists initially display only report structures that were created at the top level. 

• 
Click the Include private check box at the top of the list to see report structures that were 

created in an entity. You can edit and use these report structures provided that you have 

access to the entities in which they were created. 

• 
You can Add new top-level report structures and Edit existing structures that were created 

at either the top level or entity level. 

Include Private Does Not Appear on Your Page 

The most common reason that you don’t see this feature is because you’re using a custom view. 

When you select a custom view, some options are hidden. Depending on the page you’re on, the 

Include inactive, Include one-time, Include private, and Display hierarchy options aren’t visible. 

For example, if you’re viewing from a custom view, the Financial reports list won’t provide the 

Include inactive option. 

To see the options again, switch back to View all. See Custom Views for more information. 

Entity-Level Report Structures 

When you switch to an entity, you can use report structures that were created at the top level, 

plus any report structures that were created in that entity. 

• 
You can add new report structures and edit existing structures that were created at the 

entity level. 

• 
View (but not edit) report structures that were inherited from the top level. You’ll recognize 

these by the Not owned status. This means that the entity can use these report structures, 

but they can be edited only at the top level. 

Viewing the Account Groups List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Account Groups`


When you first display the Account groups list (on page 143), the default view shows your 

existing account groups. 

For each account group, the list displays its name, the Display as title that’s used on reports and 

graphs, and the type of account group. Other links allow you to get more information about the 

hierarchy of the account group and how it is used in reports and graphs.

The Account groups list has two views, which you can switch between by using the Flip view 

button: 

• 
Account groups: Use this view to review and edit your account groups.  

• 
Accounts to account group map: Use this view to see if any accounts have not been 

assigned or have been assigned twice. 

Financial reports, graphs, and performance cards consist only of account groups – not individual 
accounts. For this reason, every account should be a member of an account group. 

When you first display the Account groups list, the default view shows your existing account 

groups. From this list, you can click the Add button to create a new account group. 

For each account group, the list displays its name, the Display as title used on reports and graphs, 

and the type of account group. Other links allow you to get more information about the hierarchy 

of the account group and how it is used in reports and graphs. 

For multi-entity shared users, account groups can either be common (accessible) to all entities, 
or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. 

Options vary for account groups in a multi-entity shared environment. For example, the top level 

includes an Include Private check box for displaying entity-level account groups. At the entity 

level, account groups created at the top level are listed as Not owned and can’t be edited. Learn 

more about account groups in a multi-entity shared environment. 

When the Include Private Check Box Does Not Appear 

The most common reason that you don’t see this feature is because you’re using a custom view. 

When you select a custom view, some options are hidden. Depending on the page you’re on, the 

Include Inactive, Include One-Time, Include Private, and Display Hierarchy check box options 

aren’t visible. For example, if you’re viewing from a custom view, the Financial reports list won’t 

provide the Include Inactive option. 

To see the options again, switch back to View all. See Custom list views for more information.

Before You Begin

Permissions

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

You must be at the top level to add and import G/L accounts. 

Account Groups Workflow 

It is typical to begin by creating account groups that will consist only of individual G/L accounts or 

discrete categories. Then create the other types of account groups (those that contain other 

account groups, those that are part of a computational formula, and so on) that are more likely to 

form the basis of your financial reports. 

The creation of an account group breaks down into four steps: 

1. 
Specify basic information about the account group. 

2. 
Define the group structure type and calculation method. 

3. 
Add members to the group. 

4. 
(Optional) Add filters to the account group.

Defining the Group Structure Type and Calculation Method 

1. 
In the Structure type drop-down list, select the structure type that you want to assign to the 

account group: 

• 
Accounts 

• 
Group of accounts 

• 
Statistical accounts 

• 
Computation 

• 
Category 

• 
Statistical category 

The page options change depending on which group type (on page 133) you select. 

Each structure type is designed for a specific use and has different features. You can no 
longer change the structure type after you save the account group. If you mistakenly 
assigned a different structure type and have not used the account group in any report, 
delete the group and recreate it with the correct structure type. 

2. 
Select the calculation method from the Calculation method drop-down list. 

• 
For period: Calculate only the amounts in the selected period. 

• 
Start of period: Calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the start of the selected 

period. 

• 
End of period: Calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the end of the selected 

period. 

---

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

For example, in a balance-forward situation, you can set up balance sheet account groups as 

End of period and set up income statement account groups as For period. 

Computation structures use calculation methods that enable you to create formulas for your 

account group. You can add, subtract, multiply, or divide between selected accounts or account 

groups. You can also use a constant number as part of the calculation. Display the amount result 

as a ratio, percentage, or average, based on the formula that you select. 

Calculation structures can take as few as two accounts, account groups, or constants. For example, 

you can: 

• 
Divide the revenue G/L account by the employee statistical account to obtain your revenue 

per employee. 

• 
Divide your total debt by your current assets to get the debt ratio. 

A G/L account can be a member of more than one account group. 

Next, add accounts to the account group (on page 148).

Adding Filters to the Account Group (Optional) 

You can use the Report filters section to restrict the data displayed by department or other factors. 

Before you create filtering for the account group, consider how you will use it in reports and if 

filtering here might be too restrictive. 

In most cases, RealPage recommends that you use the filtering on the report or graph instead of 
on the account group. Filtering on the account group limits the flexibility in reporting. 

To help you decide which filtering method is best, consider who will see the report. For reports 

that you create for a single audience and are sure that the information needed is always the same, 

filtering by account group might be best. 

For reports with multiple audiences, filtering at the report or graph level might be a better 

solution. In this way, you can create one report and filter it at runtime so that the report displays 

the results for different departments, for example, based on who will receive the report. You can 

set report filtering without having to create multiple account groups and reports. 

Another advantage to filtering on the report instead of the account group is when you need to 

include multiple members of the same department for the same report. When you use filtering on 

---


<!-- Page 165 -->
Chapter 7: Account Groups

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

the report or graph instead of on the account group, you have the option to filter on multiple 

department members by using a department group. 

To set up the report filters: 

1. 
In the Debit/Credit drop-down list, select whether you want the report to display Debit 

only, Credit only, or No filter. 

2. 
For each department, select one of the following options: 

• 
No filter: Include all of the objects in the report (such as all departments, all projects, 

all classes, and so on) in addition to all of the object’s children. 

• 
Specific department(s), including sub-departments: Include the parent object that 

you chose in the corresponding drop-down list along with all of its children. 

• 
Specific department(s): In most cases, RealPage recommends that you use the 

filtering on the report or graph instead of on the account group. Filtering on the 

account group limits the flexibility in reporting. Select this option to include only the 

department that you chose in the corresponding drop-down list. 

• 
No departments specified: Select this option to show transactions that are not 

associated with any department. 

3. 
Click the Save button when done. 

To save this account group and create another one, click Save & new. The system opens a 
blank Account group information page after saving. 

Examples 

Here are some examples of account groups that you might find useful. 

• 
An account group called “Withdrawal” that’s filtered for credit only on your bank accounts. 

The system will display only credit transactions such as withdrawal transactions in the report. 

• 
An account group that contains a summary of revenues for a single location, such as “Sales - 

Location 1,” and includes it as a row in a report. 

• 
An account group that contains only the debit transactions to an equipment account, such 

as “Equipment Purchases.”

You can import and export account group data and group member data. Each type of data has its 

own template file. Note that the account group template is different from account group member 

template. 

This procedure describes importing account group data. You must import account groups first 

and then import account group members second, because the account groups must exist before 

you can import the account group members. 

If this is the first time that you are creating account groups, then follow the instructions in First 

Time Account Group Imports. Otherwise, follow the instruction in Importing Account Groups to 

Update the System. 

First Time Account Group Imports 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Set Up Company Master List section, and then find the Account groups row. 

4. 
Click the Default template link. The system downloads the file to your browser’s default 

location.  

5. 
Go to Step 2, Preparing the Data. 

Importing Account Groups to Update the System 

Step 1: Exporting from the Account Groups List  

You can export account group information from the Account Groups list.  


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to the Account Groups list (General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Account groups).`


2. 
Click the Export button. A box appears with two choices, Account Groups or Member 

Groups.  

3. 
Select Account Groups. 

Step 2: Preparing the Data 

When you download a template from the Import data list, the correct headers are in the template 

already. Fill in the columns with your data, save it as a CSV file, and then upload the file. The 

header titles in the template that you download correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header 

titles will cause an upload error.  

For more information about the CSV upload process, including best practices, common errors, 

and how to upload your CSV file, see Preparing Your CSV File for Import (on page 692).

### Account Group Information Page
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 177*

Chapter 7: Account Groups 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Account Group Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Account Groups > Add/Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Account Groups > Add/Edit`


Use the Account group information page to create and modify account groups that you use for 

reporting purposes. You can also duplicate the account group and view the account group 

record’s audit trail from this page. 

Account groups are the fundamental building blocks of financial reports. Every account that you 

have must be part of an account group if you want to use its data in a balance sheet, income 

statement, cash flow, or other report. If you are new to account groups, we recommend that you 

review the Account groups overview (on page 124). 

This page has three sections: Summary, Middle, and Report Filters. 

• 
Summary: The summary section at the top of the page lets you set up how the account 

group’s name and total appear in a report. You also set the normal balance and select the 

manager and purpose of the account group. You can also designate the account group as a 

key performance indicator (KPI). 

• 
Middle: Use the middle section to select the calculation method and add accounts to the 

account group.  

• 
Report filters: Use this section to filter the account group as needed. 

Filtering on the account group restricts the information displayed to certain dimensions. 

Before you define filtering for the account group, consider how you will use it in reports, 

and if filtering on the account group would be too restrictive. In most cases, we recommend 

filtering on the report or graph instead of on the account group. Filtering on the report or 

graph at runtime increases flexibility in reporting. 

Filtering on the account group limits selection to one member of a dimension. If you need 

more than one member of a dimension—for example, multiple vendors or 

customers—filtering at the report level allows you to use dimension groups that contain 

multiple members of the same dimension. 

Consider who will see the report. For reports that you create for a single audience and are 

sure that the information needed is always the same, filtering by account group could be 

your best option. 

For reports with multiple audiences, filtering at the report or graph level might be a better 

solution. In this way, you can create one report and filter it at runtime so that the report 

displays the information based on who will receive the report, for example, different 

department managers or business unit leaders. With this method, you can set report 

filtering without having to create multiple account groups and reports. 

---


<!-- Page 178 -->
Account Groups 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About the Structure Type  

Every account group has a default method of calculating amounts in reports, based on structure 

type. For example, account groups that contain income or expense accounts are typically 

calculated “for the period.” Calculation methods can be: 

• 
For the period: Calculate only the amounts in the period you selected. 

• 
Start of period: Calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the start of the selected period. 

• 
End of period: Calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the end of the selected period. 

Computation structures use a mathematical formula for calculation between account groups. 

These calculation methods enable you to create formulas for your account group. You can add, 

subtract, multiply, or divide one side of the formula by the other, then display the amount results 

as a ratio, percentage, or average, based on the formula that you select. 

Calculation structures are basically equations. They require two accounts, account groups, or 

constant numbers. Each side of the formula is an account, account group, or constant number. For 

example, you could: 

• 
Divide the revenue G/L account by the employee statistical account to obtain your revenue 

per employee. 

• 
Divide your total debt by your current assets to get the debt ratio. 

You can use an account group of type “Computation” to define a mathematical computation that 

you want to include as a section in financial reports. For example, you might want to include a 

section called “Revenue per Employee,” where the amount is computed by dividing revenue by 

the number of employees. 

Unlike computations that appear in the columns of a financial report, a computation account 

group enables you to add a computation to report rows. 

For Multi-Entity Shared Companies 

The account group is a master object that can either be common (that is, accessible) to all entities, 

or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. Learn more about account groups in a multi-entity 

shared environment (on page 141).  

---

Report Filters on the Account Group Information Page 

Filtering on the account group restricts the information displayed to certain dimensions. Before 

you define filtering for the account group, consider how you will use it in reports and if filtering 

on the account group would be too restrictive. In most cases, we recommend filtering on the 

report or graph instead of on the account group. Filtering on the report or graph at runtime 

increases the flexibility in reporting. 

Filtering on the account group limits selection to one member of a dimension. If you need more 

than one member of a dimension—for example, multiple vendors or customers—filtering at the 

report level allows you to use dimension groups that contain multiple members of the same 

dimension. 

Consider who will see the report. For reports that you create for a single audience and are sure 

that the information needed is always the same, filtering by account group could be your best 

option. 

For reports with multiple audiences, filtering at the report or graph level might be a better 

solution. In this way, you can create one report and filter it at runtime so that the report displays 

the information based on who will receive the report (for example, different department 

managers or business unit leaders). With this method, you can set report filtering without having 

to create multiple account groups and reports.

Customizing and Running the Account Groups Hierarchy Report 

If you want to see every result for a particular category, do not make selections from any of the 

data entry boxes. You can run this report without entering any search information. If you do that, 

however, the report may take a long time to run and may return too many results to be useful. 

Before running the report, you can select the types of items to include and specify how you want 

the report to appear. 

To customize and run an Accounts group hierarchy report: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Account groups. 

3. 
Find the account group for which you want to view the report, and then click the Hierarchy 

link. The report is displayed. 

4. 
Click the Customize button. 

Set the Filters  

Set the filters to get the specific data you want. 

1. 
Select one of the following options to focus the report on the set of account groups either 

you or the system created: 

• 
User Defined Account Groups 

• 
System Account Groups 

These choices are available for companies that were initially created with a setup template 

that automatically generated categories mapped to account groups and standard financial 

reports based on the account groups. 

2. 
To filter by a specific type of account group, select the type of account group to include in 

the report in the Account group type drop-down list. 

3. 
To filter by a specific range of account groups, select the account group to include in the 

report in the Account group from drop-down list. Do the same in the Account group to 

drop-down list. 

4. 
To filter by a specific range of accounts, select the starting account to include in the report 

in the Account number from drop-down list, and then select the ending account in the 

Account number to drop-down list. 

5. 
To filter by a specific range of categories, select the starting category to include in the 

report in the Category from drop-down list. Select the ending category in the Category to 

drop-down list. 

---

The Category field is available for companies that were initially created with a setup 
template. 

Format the Report 

To change the page layout, click the Page orientation drop-down field, and then select either 

Portrait or Landscape. Portrait is the default layout. 

• 
Portrait: Display or print the report pages vertically. 

• 
Landscape: Display or print the report pages horizontally. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Run the Report 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of this report (click Print to get the PDF version). 

The system completes the Report title 1 field with the system-assigned report name. This title 

displays in large type at the top of the page directly under your company name. 

1. 
You can leave the title as the default or change it by typing over the default name in Report 

title 1. 

2. 
In Report title 2, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. This 

subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. Footer text 

displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report.  

View, process, memorize, export, or customize the report or add it to the dashboard by 
clicking one of the buttons at the top of the page. You can go back and forth between 
customizing the report and running the report to get the precise results you want. Fill in 
the desired fields, and then click View to see the report. If after viewing the results you 
want to refine the report, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 
process until you’re satisfied. Also, for complex financial reports you plan to run regularly, 
save the report when you are done setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the 
report, change only the As of date before running the report.

#### Viewing a Monthly Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 199*

Chapter 7: Account Groups 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Viewing a Monthly Report 

On the report customization page, click View. 

The report displays all results for the default reporting period. 

To refine the report, click the Customize button. 

Reports have two kinds of settings, persisting and non-persisting. 

Persisting settings retain any changes you make from session to session. When you return to this 

page to run this report again, each setting displays exactly as you set it before. For example, if you 

type “My Latest Report” into the Report title 1 field, the next time you run this report, the Report 

title 1 box displays My latest report. 

Persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Format section 

• 
Settings in the Titles section 

• 
Check boxes in the Filters section 

Non-persisting settings do not retain your changes. Instead, every time you return to this page to 

run this report or chart, the settings are set to the system defaults. If you changed these settings 

the last time you ran this report, you will have to change them again. 

Non-persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Time Period section 

•

### Reporting Account Sets Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 204*

Reporting Account Sets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reporting Account Sets Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reporting Accounts`


The reporting accounts feature is an optional feature in the General Ledger that enables you to 

generate and display reports using an alternate set of accounts instead of the standard G/L chart 

of accounts. Think of each reporting account set as a separate chart of accounts that you want to 

report on.  

For example, you might define a reporting account set for a part owner named Davis Associates 

who has 70 accounts.  

Use reporting accounts to: 

• 
Define reporting account sets that represent alternate charts of accounts. Within each 

account set, you define reporting accounts and how they map to your General Ledger 

accounts. 

• 
Let yourself or others display reports using an alternate reporting account set. The option to 

select a reporting account set is available for all financial reports and some standard reports. 

• 
All existing financial reports and some standard reports can take advantage of this new 

feature without any additional setup or changes to the report. You don’t need to create 

additional reports. 

• 
Navigate from financial reports to the transaction page using reporting accounts. 

• 
(Optionally) Set a default reporting account set for users who log into your company. 

Every reporting account set is a separate chart of accounts, each of which has a unique name and 

list of reporting Accounts. For example, you might define a reporting account set for a part owner 

named Investor A who has 150 accounts. The ability to select a reporting account set is available 

for all financial reports and for selected standard reports. 

In a multi-entity environment, you must configure reporting accounts at the top level. From the 
top level, follow the instructions for enabling the feature, creating reporting account sets, 
setting up permissions, and mapping reporting accounts to G/L accounts. 
You can use reporting account sets that you define at the top level when running reports at the 
entity level.  

---



### Using Reporting Account Sets with Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 205*

Chapter 8: Reporting Account Sets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Using Reporting Account Sets with Reports 

In your company, you have a set of General Ledger accounts that you use for transactions and 

reporting. These General Ledger accounts are equivalent to your chart of accounts. If you have 

clients or owners with their own chart of accounts, you can still provide reports that show 

accounts that make sense to them.  

For example, you have a part owner named Example PMC Company. This owner uses a different 

chart of accounts, with different account numbers and titles. In addition, this owner categorizes 

income and expenses differently – for example, the owner rolls up expenses like painting and 

carpet cleaning into a single Maintenance account. 

By creating a reporting account set for Example PMC Company, reports can be generated 

specifically for Example PMC Company because the reporting account set contains the mapping 

of General Ledger accounts to reporting accounts. 

When reports using a reporting account set are displayed: 

• 
General Ledger accounts are automatically translated to the corresponding reporting 

accounts, so that the report reflects the account numbers and titles of the reporting account 

set. 

• 
If more than one General Ledger account is mapped to a single reporting account, the 

report automatically rolls up amounts into the single reporting account. 

• 
Clicking an amount displays supporting detail, which is also translated to reporting 

accounts. 

---

### Creating Alternative Charts of Accounts
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 207*

*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 207*

Chapter 8: Reporting Account Sets

Creating Alternative Charts of Accounts 

RealPage Accounting provides two different features that create an alternative chart of accounts:  

• 
Reporting account sets 

• 
Chart types 

Each feature offers different strengths and limitations: 

• 
Reporting account sets are limited to using G/L accounts. Chart types allow you to include 

both G/L accounts and statistical accounts. 

• 
Create chart types based on property types.  

• 
Assign management reporting codes to chart types.  

Managing Reporting Account Sets 

When you enable alternate reporting account sets, you: 

• 
Enable the ability to define reporting account sets, each of which corresponds to the chart 

of accounts of another individual or company. The list of reporting account sets that have 

been created are available on the Reporting Account Sets list (on page 196).  


> **Navigation Path:** `Go to General Ledger > Reporting Accounts.`


• 
For each reporting account set, define how General Ledger accounts map to reporting 

accounts (on page 203). This mapping is what enables reports to be displayed using a 

reporting account set. 

• 
Enable financial reports and selected standard reports to be displayed using an alternate 

reporting account set. Users can display a report in any reporting account set that they have 

permission to use. Reporting account set permissions are defined in each reporting account 

set rather than with system permissions.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1.

Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again.

Mapping a Reporting Account to a G/L Account 

You can map a single reporting account to one or more General Ledger accounts. All reporting 

accounts that you map must be the same type (balance sheet, income statement, or statistical 

accounts). In addition, the G/L account and the reporting accounts must be the same type. 

To map a reporting account to a G/L account:  

1. 
Select the check box of the G/L Account that you want to map. 

2. 
Click the Reporting account column, and then open the drop-down list. Select the desired 

reporting account to map to the G/L account. 

You can create reporting accounts on the fly by selecting the Add link in the drop-down 
list, and then creating a new reporting account. You can also change a reporting account by 
selecting the reporting account that you want to change and then clicking the View link in 
the drop-down list. The reporting account page opens. Click the Edit button to make 
changes.  

3. 
Click Save to save the mapping. The pages refresh to show that the Mapped check box is 

now selected. 

Mapping a Reporting Account to Multiple G/L Accounts

Select the reporting account in one of the selected G/L account’s drop-down lists.

Click Save.

#### Mapping Rules
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 219*

Chapter 8: Reporting Account Sets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Mapping Rules 

Every reporting account set is a separate chart of accounts, each of which has a unique name and 

list of reporting accounts. For example, you might define a reporting account set for a part owner 

named Investor A who has 150 accounts. 

Mapping Rules 

• 
One G/L Account to One Reporting Account Mapping is allowed. 

• 
Many G/L Accounts to One Reporting Account Mapping is allowed. 

• 
One G/L Account to Many Reporting Accounts Mapping is not allowed. 

This is a sample expense report for Example PMC Company. 

When many G/L accounts across different account groups are mapped to a single reporting 

account, the reporting account will be displayed several times across different account groups in 

the report output. However, this will not affect the report balances. If you want to see the 

reporting account only once in the report, create a new account group and a new report with 

appropriate desired groupings. 

Rules 

The following rules apply regardless of the method used for mapping. 

Rule 1. In general, all General Ledger accounts should be mapped to reporting accounts. 

To ensure that all reports can be displayed using the reporting account set, be sure to map all 

General Ledger accounts. 

Reports that include an unmapped General Ledger account won’t have an equivalent reporting 

account to display. In this case, the report will display the General Ledger account with an asterisk 

(*) and a footnote indicating the unmapped GL account. 

---


<!-- Page 220 -->
Reporting Account Sets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Rule 2. One or more General Ledger accounts can be mapped to a particular reporting account. 

From General Ledger to reporting account, mappings can be either: 

• 
1-to-1 

• 
Many-to-1 

If there is a direct equivalent between a General Ledger account and a reporting account, you can 

create a one-to-one mapping. 

Example of one-to-one mappings 

General Ledger accounts 
Reporting accounts 

5015-Gardening > 
85320-Landscaping 

1700-Security Deposits > 
13-3045-Prepaid Deposits 

Alternatively, multiple General Ledger accounts can be consolidated into a single reporting 

account. 

Example of many-to-one mappings 

General Ledger accounts 
Reporting accounts 

5013-Interior painting > 

5016-Carpet Cleaning > 
85310-Maintenance 

2420-Office Supplies > 

2430-Postage and Delivery > 

2440-Printing costs > 

24578-Office supplies 

---


<!-- Page 221 -->
Chapter 8: Reporting Account Sets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Rule 3: You can’t map multiple reporting accounts to the same General Ledger account. 

To allow General Ledger accounts to be translated to reporting accounts, you can’t map a single 

General Ledger account to multiple reporting accounts. 

Not allowed: One General Ledger account to many reporting accounts 

General Ledger Accounts 
Reporting Accounts 

5013 - Remodeling 
85310 - Painting 

83540 - Furniture 

Allowed: Many General Ledger accounts to one reporting account 

General Ledger Accounts 
Reporting Accounts 

5013-Interior painting 

5016-Carpet Cleaning 
85310-Maintenance 

Rule 4: Mapped accounts must be the same type. 

There are three types of accounts: 

• 
Accounts--Balance Sheet 

• 
Accounts--Income Statement 

• 
Statistical accounts 

When you set up your mappings, the General Ledger account and reporting account must be the 

same type of account.

There are two places where you can import reporting accounts.  

• 
From the Reporting Account Sets list. Use this method to import a new chart of accounts 

(COA). 

• 
From the Reporting Account Set page. Use this method to import reporting accounts into a 

reporting account set. 

A reporting account set must already exist before you can import reporting accounts or 
mappings.  

Workflow for Importing Reporting Accounts 

• 
Download the reporting account template. 

• 
Fill the template with reporting account data. 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the file. 

If the reporting accounts and/or mappings are created in a CSV file outside the application, 

import it by clicking the Import button on the Reporting account sets page. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data.

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

3. 
Find Reporting Accounts and Mappings row, and then click the Template link on the row. 

The system either downloads the template to your browser’s default download folder, or 

prompts you to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template with Reporting Account Data 

To fill the template with your data: 

1. 
Open the file in your spreadsheet application. 

2. 
For each account that you want to be able to use in reports, add the following information 

in the required columns: 

• 
NAME: Type the name of the reporting account set to add this data to. 

• 
GL_ACCT_TYPE: Type the code for the account type. When importing into a statistical 

account, type N for Cumulative, or type I for For period. Otherwise, type N for Balance 

sheet or type I for Income statement. 

• 
REPORTING_ACCT_TYPE: Type the code for the reporting account type. When 

importing into a statistical account, type N for Cumulative, or type I for For period. 

Otherwise, type N for Balance sheet or type I for Income statement. 

3. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining columns. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the purpose of the account. 

• 
GL_ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number 

• 
GL_ACCT_NAME: Type the name of the G/L account that is mapped to the reporting 

account. 

• 
REPORTING_ACCT_NO: Add the account number to map to the G/L account. 

• 
REPORTING_ACCT_NAME: Type the desired name of the reporting account. 

• 
STATISTICAL: Type T (True) if the account is a statistical account type. Type F (False) if 

the account is not a statistical account. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the CSV File 

1. 
Return to the Reporting Account Sets list, and then click the Import button. 

2. 
In the Import box, click the Choose file button, and select the CSV file that you just 

updated. 

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select the date format used in the file that you are 

importing. 

4. 
Type your email address in the Email results to this address field. 

5. 
Click the Import button.

### Types of Journals
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 234*

Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Types of Journals 

RealPage Accounting offers many kinds of journals, including: 

• 
Journals: The journals in your Journals list categorize the transactions that you directly enter 

in the General Ledger, and the transactions that are posted from subledgers such as 

Accounts Payable. 

• 
Statistical journals: The journals in your Statistical journals list allow you to track statistical 

information, like square footage or number of units.  

• 
Adjustment journals: The journals in your Adjustment journals list contain adjusting journal 

entries for accounting periods that are already closed. Your Adjustment journals list can 

contain as many or few adjustment journals as you need. In addition to the adjustment 

journals, you may also have Statistical adjusting journals, Tax adjustment journals, and GAAP 

(compliance) adjustment journals. 

• 
User-defined journals: You can create custom journals that allow you to track and report on 

journal entries specific to your company or an industry. Before you begin creating 

user-defined journals, create at least one user-defined book to contain them. See 

User-defined books to get started. 

Common Journals and Private Journals 

For multi-entity, shared companies, journals are master objects, which can either be common 

(that is, accessible) to all entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. 

---

#### Adding a Journal
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 237*

Chapter 9: Journals

Adding a Journal 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > 
 Journals`


If you have administrator-level privileges, then you can create new journals from the Setup tab of 

the General Ledger application. 

To add a standard journal: 

1. 
Select General Ledger, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select 
 Add next to Journals. 

3. 
In the Symbol field, type an abbreviation for the journal. After you’ve saved the journal, you 

can no longer edit the symbol. 

In most places, the symbol appears along with the title of the journal, as in APA--Accounts 

Payable Accrual. 

4. 
In the Title field, type the full name of the journal as it should appear in reports and other 

places. 

5. 
In the Include this journal when reporting in section, select the desired reporting book that is 

to include this journal: Accrual, Cash, or Cash and Accrual. 

If your accounting method is set to both accrual and cash in the General Ledger, follow these 

additional instructions: 

1. 
In accrual and cash companies, reports can be run on either accrual basis or cash basis. Use 

the Include this journal when reporting in option to determine whether the journal should 

be included in reports run on accrual-basis, cash-basis, or both. 

2. 
Make sure the Symbol and Title clearly distinguish whether the journal is for cash, accrual, 

or both. This is because, in several locations, the system lists all three journal types. For 

example, you might want to identify an Accounts Payable journal as APC and Accounts 

Payable - C for the cash-basis version, and APAC and Accounts Payable - AC for the accrual 

and cash version. 

If you’re editing an existing journal and you’re unable to change the accounting method, 

this means that either: 

• 
The journal is being used in the configuration for an application (such as Accounts 

Payable). 

• 
Transactions have already been posted to the journal. 

3. 
Set the Status to Active or Inactive. 

4. 
Select the System Journal check box if this is a system journal. 

5. 
Click Save.

### Transaction Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 239*

Chapter 9: Journals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Transaction Lists 

See the How to get here (on page 279) topic for a list of paths to access transactions lists. 

Every journal has a transactions list associated with it, regardless of the journal type. The 

transactions list contains a journal’s entries. The transaction list is the central place to go to work 

with existing journal entries for a specific journal, or to add new entries to the journal.  

To access the transactions in a journal, open the desired journal, and then click the View 

transactions link. You can access all of the journals’ transaction lists from the All tab of the 

General Ledger with the exception of the statistical journals. To access statistical journals list, 

open the Setup tab of the menu, and then select Statistical. 

The names of transaction list are composed of the journal’s symbol and “Journal Transactions. ” 
transactions. For example, the General Journal Accrual journal has the symbol GJA, so the 
journal’s transactions list name is “GJA - Journal Transactions. ” The user-defined journal for 
CAM adjustments might be named “ADJ CAM - Journal Transactions. ”  

The transactions list has a standard set of functions, columns, and buttons. From a journal’s 

transactions list, you can: 

• 
Add a new entry to the journal. 

• 
Open an entry to view or change it. 

• 
Delete one entry or select multiple entries to delete. 

• 
Print a journal entry or select multiple journal entries to print. 

• 
Check the status of an entry. See which entries have been saved as a “draft” or “posted.” 

• 
Post one or multiple entries.  

If the Journal entry approval feature is enabled, then the Post button is replaced with the 

Submit button.

submitted the entry, you are not the approver, and the approver hasn’t approved the 

entry. 

•

### About Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 244*



#### About Importing Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 244*

Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Journal Entry`


A journal entry is a record of one transaction that contains a complete explanation of what took 

place. 

Every journal entry must include at least two equal and offsetting entries. This is because every 

transaction involves a change in at least two places in the accounting records, and the total of all 

debits and credits must balance. 

Types of Journal Entries 

• 
Journal entries: Normal journal entries reflect transactions that occur while the reporting 

period is open. 

• 
Adjusting entries: After the reporting period is closed, you can create an adjusting entry to 

make changes to the closed period. There are multiple kinds of adjusting entries:  

• 
Statistical journal entries: Statistical entries increase or decrease a value that your company 

is tracking. 

You can set up a threshold for journal entries. When a user creates a journal entry that is over the 

threshold’s limit, the system sends the user or group of users an email. To set up the threshold, 

go to the Ledger Sentry (Company > Ledger Sentry) 

About Importing Journal Entries 

Importing historical G/L data in the form of journal entries allows you to bring past accounting 

activity—typically from a prior system—into your current accounting environment.  

When you bring journal entries from another system into the RealPage Financial Suite, those 

entries represent: 

• 
Past accounting activity 

• 
Closed or prior periods 

• 
Legacy balances 

• 
Historical adjustments 

All of this is, by definition, historical data. 

Imported journal entries are considered historical data when they are loaded from a prior 
system or prior period to preserve accounting history. They are not automatically historical just 
because they were imported. 

Importing historical journal entries ensures that your general ledger reflects a complete financial 

history, supports comparative reporting, and maintains a full audit trail. 

Historical journal entry imports are most commonly used during system migrations or when you 

need to load prior-period activity for reference, reporting, or compliance.

You can import any external or historical journal entry data into the general ledger. 

Prerequisites 

Before you import journal entries, confirm the following: 

• 
You must have permissions to import data into the General Ledger application. 

• 
The property/entity structure must be already set up. 

• 
The chart of accounts must be configured. 

• 
Create the journals in the General Ledger application that your system needs to 

accommodate the journal entries that you are importing.  

• 
Accounting periods and books must be open or available for posting. 

• 
A final trial balance or legacy journal detail must have been approved. 

• 
RealPage Accounting recognizes debits as positive numbers and credits as negative 

numbers. Each journal entry must net to zero in order to balance. The system does not 

include accounts with zero (0) balances. 

• 
Save a backup copy of the source data. 

Best Practices 

• 
Test in a non-production environment first. 

• 
Import a small sample batch before the full load. 

• 
Separate historical conversion data from live operational entries. 

• 
Use clear batch naming conventions, such as HIST-CONV-YYYYMM. 

• 
Keep a detailed mapping and reconciliation workbook. 

Order of Precedence 

Import parent records before you import child records. Child records that incorrectly reference a 

parent ID fail to import. For example, when you try to import a child record and its parent record 

does not exist, the child record import will fail. 

Import into Any Journal 

You can import journal entries into any of these journals: 

• 
G/L journals 

• 
GAAP (Compliance) 

• 
Tax 

• 
User-defined books 

• 
Adjustment journals 

• 
Statistical adjusting entries 

• 
Any custom journal

With the Data Import wizard in the Company application.

Import account beginning balances into multiple journals

Import Account Beginning Balances

journal entries manually. Follow the instructions based on whether you are using the Data Import

•

• 
Import journal entries manually 

Importing Offline 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much processing the 

system must do to the data. When in doubt, select the Process offline option on the import utility 

page. 

When the offline process is complete, the system sends an email to the address you entered in 

the Import Company Information dialog (where you imported your file). 

RealPage recommends selecting Process offline when importing CSV files, and then provide your 
email address. If your import fails, the system notifies you, and sends the failed records to your 
email.

Importing Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up General Ledger Transactions > 
General Ledger Journal Entries > Template/Import`


Use this procedure to import historical journal entries from an external accounting system into 

RealPage Accounting and you are not using the Data Import wizard. If you are using the Data 

Import wizard, see Importing External and Historical Journal Entries. 

Downloading the Template 

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
In the Set Up General Ledger Transactions section, find the General Ledger Journal Entries 

option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

Filling In the Template 

Dates 

Typically, the Date is the next day after you close your old accounting system and start a new set 

of books in the system. In the event that you do not enter a date, the default is today. The choice 

of date is important: for example, if you choose to enter a date of two fiscal years ago because 

you want to be able to print comparative financial statements, you must then make Journal 

entries for the ending G/L balances for all of the periods between your starting balance date and 

the date you actually begin using RealPage Accounting. 

If you are uploading historical transactions, make sure that your starting balances contain these 

uploaded transactions, and set the date to that date. 

If you find you have set the wrong starting date for your G/L balances, you can clear the 

transactions from the Import data page, and then start again. 

Department and Location 

Because G/L Transactions contain fields for both department and location, you can enter as many 

unique G/L transaction department/location combinations as you need. DEPT_ID and 

LOCATION_ID must refer to a valid department and location. 

Line Items 

The uploaded file must contain a number in either the DEBIT or CREDIT field. One or the other is 

required. For example, if you do not have a debit amount, you must have a credit amount. You 

---


<!-- Page 248 -->
Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

can import negative numbers for either, in which case a negative debit amount is treated as a 

credit, and a negative credit is treated as a debit. 

The LINE_NO must be unique per journal entry and per journal. For example, Summary 1 might 

contain line numbers 1-20, Summary 2 1-44 and so on. For more information on line numbers, 

see Importing Data with Line Numbers. 

To fill in the template: 

1. 
Open the template in a spreadsheet application. 

2. 
Fill in the required fields in the template: 

• 
JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DATE: Type the date of the journal entry. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of up to 80 characters. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number, starting with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DEBIT: Type the debit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

CREDIT field. 

• 
CREDIT: Type the credit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

DEBIT field. 

• 
SOURCEENTITY: Type the name of the entity. This value is required when the option to 

automatically create inter-entity transactions is enabled for journal entries and the 

journal entry is not balanced by location. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date. This field is required unless you provide a value in 

the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

3. 
Optionally, fill in any of the remaining columns. Refer to the template itself for more 

information about the additional data that you can import. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

5. 
After you’ve entered your data, look through the file for any of the common issues (on page 

703) that imports can have.

Journal Entry States 

There are multiple types of journals, each with its own journal entries. The information included in 

a journal entry might be different across journal types, but when it comes to making changes, 

there are some rules that apply across them all. 

If a journal entry is: 

• 
Draft: You can edit, reverse, and delete it. 

• 
Posted: You can reverse, delete, then resubmit it. 

• 
Approved: You can reverse, delete, then resubmit it. 

• 
Previously reversed: You can delete, then resubmit it. 

• 
Included in a closed period: No changes are allowed. 

• 
Submitted: You can wait for the journal entry to be approved. 

New: Only users with Limited or Full admin privileges can edit journal entries that are in system 
journals.  

The following sections explain how to view, edit, reverse, and delete journal entries.

Adding a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find 
 Journal Entry`


When you add a transaction to a journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft or posting it 

right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be complete—you or another 

user can review them later, make changes, and then post them. When you post a journal 

transaction, the entire transaction must balance, and all required information must be entered. 

You can substantiate a transaction by associating it with a supporting attachment. You can also 

use the transaction allocations to automatically distribute amounts across departments and 

locations. 

You can add a journal entry directly or add it from the General Ledger workbench (on page 19). 

This topic describes how to add a journal entry directly. 

This topic describes how to add a standard journal entry. If you want to create a statistical journal 

entry, see Creating statistical journal entries (on page 16). 

To add a new journal entry: 

Enter general information about the transaction. The top part of the page is where you enter the 

transaction date, description, and other basic information. 

1. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want to add the new journal 

entry. 

Specifying the journal is necessary only when you selected 
 Journal entry rather than 
the Add button from inside of a journal. 

2. 
In the Posting date field, accept the current date or enter a different one. This is the posting 

date for the entry. 

When your system sends journal entries through the approval process, and you make a 

journal entry in a closed period, RealPage Accounting offers a feature to have the system 

advance the posting date of the journal entry to the next open period.  

3. 
In the Automatic reversal date field, if you want to reverse this transaction on a specific 

date, type a date or select a date from the 
 Calendar. 

An automatic reversal date is the same thing as a reverse transaction except that inverts the 

line items and zeros out the transaction. You can enter today’s date or later. 

To reverse a transaction that you have previously posted, select the check box next to the 
journal transaction that you want to reverse, and then click the Reverse button.

write a comment to indicate what the change was or why it was made. Comments appear

Setting Default Line-Item Values 

Setting default values is a time-saver when you need to fill in a long list of line items.

1. 
In the Entries section of a transaction’s page, click the Show defaults link. 

The area expands to display all fields for which you can set defaults. The type of fields that

dimensions, or created and deployed user-defined dimensions, multi-currency processing 

fields, or revenue-recognition fields, then you can set default values for them here.

that value. 

3.

depending on where the field is located.

them to the list.

Customizing or Overriding an Allocation 

You can apply an allocation either to individual lines of a transaction or to the entire transaction. If 

you apply it to the entire transaction, all of the line item entries inherit the distribution of the 

allocation. However, you can override that allocation on a line-by-line basis. When you change 

the allocated dimensions/values, the allocation resets as Custom, as it now contains a specific 

allocation distribution unique to that line item. 

The unique allocated values are stored with your line item for audit trail purposes.  

Click a line item, and then click the Show/Hide Details button to open and close the Allocations 

Splits detail area for a line item. 

To override a line allocation:  

1. 
Click the line item you want to override.  

2. 
Click the Show details tab or press CTRL + 
 Down Arrow to open the Details section. 

3. 
Find the Allocation splits section, and then click the Customize allocation button. The 

Custom Allocation box opens. 

4. 
Override the template distribution by customizing allocation amounts across departments 

or locations. 

5. 
Click Yes. 

Even when an allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to a line 

item, you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation at 

the line-item level of the relevant transaction page (A/R invoices, A/P invoices, or journal 

entries).  

If you change the amounts such that the total is different from what you entered in the 

transaction page, the system updates the total when you save and return to the transaction page.

Making Changes to Journal Entries 

There are multiple types of journals, each with its own journal entries. The information included in 

a journal entry might be different across journal types, but when it comes to making changes, 

there are some rules that apply across them all. 

If a journal entry is... 
...you can 

Draft 
Edit, reverse, delete. 

Posted 
Reverse, delete, then resubmit. 

Approved 
Edit, reverse, and delete. 

Previously reversed 
Delete then resubmit. 

Included in a closed period 
No changes allowed. 

Not subject to approval 
Edit posted journal entries. 

In a system journal 
View only. 

Editing a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Journal Entry > View Transactions > Edit`


 You can edit a journal entry only if: 

• 
The entry hasn’t been posted. 

• 
The entry is not in a system journal.  

If an Edit link does not appear by a journal entry, the entry is in a closed period or the journal 
entry is in a system journal.  

To edit a journal entry: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select the Journal entry option. 

3. 
Find the journal that has the journal entry that you want to change, and then click the View 

Transactions link. The list of transactions in the journal opens. 

4. 
Find the journal entry that you want to change, and then click the Edit link.  

When you open a journal entry for editing, you can access two new tabs, History and 

Messaging.  

• 
Use the History tab to review the activity log for the journal entry.

Journal Entries Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > 
 Journal Entry`


Use the Journal entries page to add an entry in a journal or make changes to a journal entry.  

When you add a journal entry, you can either post it right away or save it as a draft. When you’re 

adding a new journal entry, the record has only one page. After you complete the journal entry by 

posting or saving it as a draft, the additional tabs appear.  

If your company uses the approval workflow for journal entries, then you submit the journal entry 
for approval rather than posting it. 

The Journal entries page is composed of three tabs: 

• 
Transactions: Use this tab to create and manage the journal entry. 

• 
History: This tab displays information about the entry. Like an audit entry, this tab tracks the 

entry’s creation, who created it, and when. It also displays the current state of the 

transaction. 

• 
Messaging: Use this tab to create and review messages about this journal entry. 

The Transactions tab contains the following sections: 

• 
The Transaction section 

• 
The Documents section 

• 
The Entries and/or Job cost entries section 

Transaction Section 

In this section, you select the journal to which you are adding the journal entry and add 

descriptive information about the journal entry. You will also: 

• 
Select the source entity. 

• 
Specify whether the line entries will be standard line entries or Job Cost entries. 

• 
Select the approval workflow, if any. 

Documents Section 

Use the Documents section to attach a file to the journal entry. You can either attach a file that 

resides on your computer or scan a document in and attach it, right from the journal entry page. 

You can also view an attached document from the journal entry page by clicking the 

Attachment button. 

---

Entries Section 

If you are creating a standard journal entry, use the Entries section to classify the journal entry by 

selecting an account, and then assigning the expense or revenue to a specific department, 

location, and unit.  

The Entries list lets you define defaults (on page 251) before you begin to have the system fill in 

the columns that may all have the same value. 

Job Cost Entries Section 

If you are creating a Job Cost journal entry, use the Job cost entries section to record the line items 

of that journal entry, including the job location, job name, cost code, and job unit.  

Line Item Details 

Fill in the details of a line entry by clicking the Show details tab. This tab appears when you click a 

column in a row. The Details section lets you define: 

• 
Journal entry type 

• 
Dimensions 

• 
Segment types and their values. 

You can also customize allocation splits between dimensions in the Entries section’s Details 

section.

Creating a Recurring Journal Entry As You Create a Single Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find 
 Journal Entry > Make Recurring`


To create a recurring journal entry as you add a new journal entry: 

1. 
Fill in the required fields of the journal entry: 

• 
Journal 

• 
Posting date 

• 
Description 

2. 
Select the Make recurring check box. The Schedules section appears. 

3. 
If you want to make the journal entry a memorized transaction, select the Create 

memorized transaction check box. 

Filling In the Schedules Section 

1. 
Select the date that you want the system to begin creating the recurring journal entry in the 

Journal entry start date field. 

2. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select: 

• 
Never: To keep the journal entry creation perpetually running, select Never.  

• 
Number of occurrences: The End after field appears. To have the journal entry run for 

a limited number of times, type the number of times you want the journal entry to 

recur in the End after field. This setting is often used for debts that are being paid over 

time. Setting the number of occurrences eliminates the possibility of making payments 

after the debt is paid off. 

• 
End date: To have the journal entry recur until a specific date, select End date and 

then, in the End on field, type the date on which the last journal entry is to recur.  

3. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, select the frequency that you want the system to 

generate the recurring journal entries. The options are: 

• 
None 

• 
Days 

• 
Weeks 

• 
Months 

• 
Years 

4. 
In the Every field, type the number of time frames to repeat by. For example, if you selected 

“Months,” then type the number of months to repeat by, such as 6 to have the system 

create a journal entry every 6 months. 

5. 
If you selected Months, then you can select the End of month check box to have the journal 

entry created at the end of the month. 

---

Type the email address of the person to whom to send notifications about the recurring

• 
Select the time frame.

None 

• 
Days

Weeks

Months

Years

After you add a journal entry, you can save the journal entry as a draft or post it to the general 

ledger. This topic describes the ways you can post the journal entry. 

There are multiple ways to post a journal entry to the general ledger. 

After adding a journal entry (on page 242), you are ready to post it.  

To post a journal entry: 

• 
From the Journal Entries page: 

• 
Click the Post button. This option posts the journal entry to the general ledger. 

• 
Click the Post & New button. This option posts the journal entry to the general ledger, 

and then opens a new journal entry record.

#### Saving a Transaction as a Draft
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 288*

Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Saving a Transaction as a Draft 

When you are not ready to post that A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment, you can save it as a 

draft without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save transactions in the draft 

state, you can save your progress so far. Later on, you or another user can come back to the 

transactions list and post the transaction or submit the transaction for approval. 

The system validates transactions only when they are posted or submitted. For example, required 

departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

Prerequisites: Your ability to add a transaction in draft state or post or submit a transaction 

depends on your permissions: 

• 
Add permission enables you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as a draft. 

• 
Add, Edit, and Post permissions enable you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as 

draft, and edit and post the transaction when you’re ready. 

To save a transaction in draft format: 

1. 
Add a new transaction. 

2. 
Save the transaction as a draft by clicking Draft & New or selecting Draft, or Draft & 

Continue from the drop-down button. The system saves the transaction but doesn’t post it. 

Finding Draft or Posted Transactions 

There are two ways to locate and view items in the draft and posted state. 

• 
Filter for draft or posted transactions on the fly: In the appropriate transaction list view, 

type either “Draft” or “Posted” in the State column. The list displays only those items you 

filtered for. 

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for draft or posted transactions: Create a 

view, and then set the filter to State = Draft or State = Posted. The custom view is available 

for use whenever you go to the list. 

---

#### Using a General Ledger Report to Search for Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 291*

Chapter 10: Journal Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Finding a Journal Entry 

Every journal maintains a list of the transactions (or summaries of transactions) that were posted 

to it. However, if you’re not sure which journal to look in, or if you want more options for 

searching, a General Ledger report can help you find what you need. 

You can find tips and tricks about using wildcards, sorting, and other times -savers to find 
entries in Managing lists using filtering, sorting, and views. 

Using a General Ledger Report to Search for Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Daily Tasks > General Ledger Report`


A General Ledger report lets you search for transactions based on different criteria. For example, 

you can enter a date range and even specify which accounts the transaction might have posted 

to. 

When you find the transaction in the General Ledger report, you can click any of the active links 

(for example, the date or an amount) to jump directly to the transaction. 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General ledger. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select the General ledger report option. 

3. 
Narrow the report results by adding a date rate or adding filters. 

• 
Date range: For the Time period, enter a Start date and End date. 

• 
Accounts: Use the options for G/L account group selection to select accounts that the 

entry might have posted to. 

You can even pick a range of accounts, for example, if your Revenue accounts are in 
the 4000 range, you might limit the report to accounts from 4000 to 4100.

• 
Other criteria: Enter additional filters to narrow the search. For example, select a 

location or department. 

4. 
When you’re ready, click the View button to display the report. The report groups 

transactions by account and sorts them by date. 

5. 
If you locate the entry, click any of the active links (for example, the date or an amount) to 

jump directly to the transaction. 

If you didn’t find what you were looking for, you can change your report filters and try again. 
Click the Customize button at the top of the report to return to the filter selections. 

To make it easy to locate draft and posted journal entries and other transactions, the Transactions 

list for each object contains a State column. This column indicates whether the entry was saved as 

Draft or Posted.

### Transaction Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 292*

Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide

Transaction Lists 

See the How to get here (on page 279) topic for a list of paths to access transactions lists. 

Every journal has a transactions list associated with it, regardless of the journal type. The 

transactions list contains a journal’s entries. The transaction list is the central place to go to work 

with existing journal entries for a specific journal, or to add new entries to the journal.  

To access the transactions in a journal, open the desired journal, and then click the View 

transactions link. You can access all of the journals’ transaction lists from the All tab of the 

General Ledger with the exception of the statistical journals. To access statistical journals list, 

open the Setup tab of the menu, and then select Statistical. 

The names of transaction list are composed of the journal’s symbol and “Journal Transactions. ” 
transactions. For example, the General Journal Accrual journal has the symbol GJA, so the 
journal’s transactions list name is “GJA - Journal Transactions. ” The user-defined journal for 
CAM adjustments might be named “ADJ CAM - Journal Transactions. ”  

The transactions list has a standard set of functions, columns, and buttons. From a journal’s 

transactions list, you can: 

• 
Add a new entry to the journal. 

• 
Open an entry to view or change it. 

• 
Delete one entry or select multiple entries to delete. 

• 
Print a journal entry or select multiple journal entries to print. 

• 
Check the status of an entry. See which entries have been saved as a “draft” or “posted.” 

• 
Post one or multiple entries.  

If the Journal entry approval feature is enabled, then the Post button is replaced with the 

Submit button.  

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled on your system, you can: 

• 
Submit transactions for approval. 

• 
Recall a journal entry from the approval queue. You can recall a journal entry if you 

submitted the entry, you are not the approver, and the approver hasn’t approved the 

entry. 

• 
Duplicate an entry. 

• 
Reverse one or multiple entries. 

• 
Attach a supporting document to one or multiple entries.  

When an entry has an attachment, an 
 Attachment icon appears next to the Excel link. 
Click the 
 Attachment icon to open the Attachments page.

Attaching Files to Multiple Transactions at a Time 

When you add the same attachment to multiple transactions, the system assigns a unique ID to 

the attachment so that the attachment has the same ID across all of the transactions that it is 

attached to.  

If you make changes to the attachment, it changes the attachment for all of the transactions that it 

is attached to. The system recognizes the attachment as being the same because it has the same 

attachment ID.
