#### Duplicating Journal Entries to Other Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 296*

Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicating Journal Entries to Other Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Journal Entry > View Transactions > View > 
Duplicate`


The ability to duplicate entries into a journal associated with a different book provides a new way 

to review entry impact prior to recording the transaction to your main books. For example, to see 

the impact an entry will have, create a user-defined book named “Provisional” and record the 

transaction to that book. Review the impact from a financial statement and if the change is 

acceptable, move (duplicate) the entry to your main book (usually accrual) and reverse it from the 

Provisional book. 

To duplicate a journal entry from one book to another book: 

1. 
Locate the type of journal entry to duplicate and click that type. For example, you might 

choose Journal entry, GAAP, Tax, User-defined, Adjusting, or Statistical. If you don’t see the 

book in the selection list, you might not have the right permissions to see it. Only books 

that you have access to are visible. 

2. 
View the journal entry and click View transactions to open the transactions list. 

3. 
Locate the transaction you want to duplicate and click View, and then click the Duplicate 

button. The Duplicate to box opens. 

4. 
Select the book and journal that you want to duplicate the entry into. The duplicated entry 

has a new transaction number and today’s date, but everything else is the same.  

5. 
In the Date section, specify whether to use the original date or a different date. If you 

choose to replace the date, then type or select the desired replacement date. 

---

If you want to reverse the entry or entries, select the Reverse date check box, and then type 

or select the desired reversal date. 

7. 
Click the Continue button. The system copies the entries to the book and journal that you 

specified. 

8. 
Go to the journal to which you duplicated the entries, and then submit or post the entries, 

or save them as draft entries. 

Deleting a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry > View Transactions > Delete`


You can delete a journal entry as long as the entry isn’t in a closed period. 

If you want a warning to appear before you attempt to delete a transaction, select the Warn on 

delete check box in your My preferences page. Click your sign-in name at the top of any page, and 
then select My preferences. 

To delete a journal entry:  

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select the Journal entry option. 

3. 
Find the desired journal, and then click the View Transactions link. The list of the journal’s 

transactions opens. 

4. 
Select the journal entry to delete by selecting the check box in the Delete column. 

5. 
Click the Delete button at the top of the page, and then click OK. 

GAAP Compliance Prevents Editing a Transaction in a Closed Period 
To ensure GAAP compliance and keep accurate audit trail activity and historical reporting, you 
cannot edit a transaction in a closed period.  
To make such a change: 
1. Re-open the book.  
2. Make the edits. 
3. Close the book again.

#### Reversals
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 298*



#### Reversing a Journal Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 298*

Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversals  

When you reverse a transaction, the General Ledger:  

• 
Creates an identical transaction that is the inverse of the original transaction, which zeros 

out the original transaction. You now have two transactions for audit purposes. You can see 

this by navigating through the G/L.  

• 
Links the reversal with the original transaction to help keep the two entries stay the same.  

• 
Adds a Reversed on link under the Date field. This shows the date on which the transaction 

was reversed.  

• 
Removes the Reverse button from the Transaction Edit page because you can no longer 

reverse this transaction.  

If you’re reversing an inter-entity transaction, the General Ledger works the same way, but it 

reverses the transactions on both sides – that is, for both the source entity and the target entity.  

How the system helps keep original and reversing journal entries in sync 
To help keep the original entry and the reversing entry the same, users will be warned if they 
attempt to change a journal entry that is linked to another journal entry.  

Changes to the original entry: If a user attempts to change the original journal entry, the 
system warns the user that the reversing entry will also be modified and asks for confirmation 
to continue.  

Changes to the reversing entry: If the user attempts to change the reversing entry, the system 
warns the user and asks whether the changes should also be reflected in the original entry.  

Reversing a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry > View 
Transactions > Reverse`


You can reverse any journal entry that was entered by you or another user that hasn’t already 

been reversed, as long as it is in an open period. You can reverse statistical journal entries, 

adjusting G/L journal entries, and adjusting statistical journal entries in the same way. To reverse a 

different type of journal entry, start from the corresponding journal entry list in the General 

Ledger menu. 

This example reverses a G/L journal entry.  

To reverse an entry: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Journal entry.  

---


<!-- Page 299 -->

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

3. 
Click the View transactions link in the row of the desired journal. 

4. 
In the list of transactions, locate the transaction that you want to reverse, and then select 

the check box in the Select column.  

See our tips for finding journal entries (on page 277). 

If you don’t see the option to reverse, another application might have created the entry, 
such as Accounts Payable. To undo other types of transactions, you must go to the 
application in which the transaction was created and void or reverse it there. 

5. 
Click the Reverse button.  

• 
Accept the default Reverse date, or type another date. You can reverse the transaction 

as of another date in the past or future. 

• 
Type a description so that you leave an appropriate audit trail. 

• 
In the Reference number field, the word “Reversed” appears, followed by the original 

transaction number. If the number does not appear, type the original transaction 

number if you have it. 

6. 
Click the Reverse button. 

After you reverse a journal entry, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create 
another journal entry to replace it. 

When you reverse a journal entry, the General Ledger: 

• 
Adds a Reversed on link below the Date field. This shows the date on which the 

transaction was reversed. 

• 
Creates an identical transaction that is the inverse of the original transaction, which 

zeros out the original transaction. 

• 
You now have two transactions for audit purposes. 

To see the date on which you reversed this transaction, click the Reversed on link. Click it 

again to see the Reversed from date.

#### Processing Multiple Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 301*

Chapter 10: Journal Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Processing Multiple Journal Entries 

Journal entries are core transactions in a financial system. Working with these entries one by one 

makes sense in many circumstances, but there is also a need to be able to post, duplicate, or even 

reverse a group of entries. Easily process multiple journal entries within the same journal, or 

across journals, or even across books. 

Bulk updates can be used to process multiple transactions, including: 

• 
Post 

• 
Duplicate (same or different book) 

• 
Reverse 

• 
Delete 

Bulk actions are for your convenience. the system is still required to apply all validations 
for your selected transactions. This means that the processing time is the same for these 
entries, as if you recorded each entry one by one. Be aware that for a large batch of entries, 
the processing time for the batch might take too long for the system to complete. The 
number of transactions selected, and the size of each transaction, are factors in 
processing time. 

Mass Updates 

Mass update processes multiple selected transactions at one time. Select as many journal entries 

as needed and process them in a single step. 

These updates work for transactions in the same journal. Duplicate and Reverse adhere to the 

posting approval rules associated with the journal into which the entries are recorded. 


> **Navigation Path:** `To see Journal entries, go to General Ledger >All > Journal entries and click the View`


Transactions link to display the transactions for the journal. Then, click the Add button to add a 

new journal entry, or click Edit or View next to an existing journal entry. 

If you’re performing mass updates for journal entries that contain a large amount of data, your 

browser could time out or you could impact the system. Consider running several updates with 

fewer items included. 

Top Level/Entity Restrictions 

Bulk updates are only allowed to be performed at the same entity level. For example, if you make 

bulk updates at the top level, you can’t perform bulk updates on journal entries created at the 

entity level. Likewise, if you make bulk updates at the entity level, you can’t perform bulk updates 

on journal entries at the top level.

#### Attaching a Document to Multiple Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 302*

Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Attaching a Document to Multiple Journal Entries 

To attach a document to several journal entries at the same time: 

1. 
Open the desired journal. 

2. 
Click View Transactions. 

3. 
Click the check boxes in the Select column of the journal entries to which you want to 

attach the document. 

We recommend that you perform this operation on small sets of journal entries rather 
than attaching a document to hundreds of journal entries at a time. If your browser times 
out, then select fewer journal entries to attach to. 

4. 
Click the Attach button. 

5. 
Click OK to confirm that you want to proceed. The Attach box opens. 

6. 
Use the Attachment drop-down list to find and select the document to attach. The file can 

either be on your computer or you can attach a file that has already been added to the 

system.  

Select an attachment from the drop-down list or click the Choose Files button to upload a 

file from your computer. 

• 
Show all/Show unattached: This link changes the contents of the drop-down list 

between showing all files to showing unattached files. Unattached files are files that 

are not yet attached to any other record in the system. 

• 
Add: Click to upload a file from your computer to the system. 

• 
View: You can view a document before attaching it. Click the document that you want 

to review, and then click the View link. 

• 
Find: Click this link to search the files that are stored in the system. 

7. 
Click the Continue button. 

When you add an attachment to multiple journal entries simultaneously, the attachment in 
those journal entries all have the same ID. This means that any changes that you make to 
the attachment in the future will affect all of the journal entries with this attachment. 

---



#### Posting Multiple Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 303*

Chapter 10: Journal Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Conversely, if you attach the same document to the journal entries one at a time, then any 
changes that you make to the attachment will affect only the attachment to the one 
journal entry to which it was attached. 

Posting Multiple Journal Entries 

When you post journal transactions, the entire transaction must balance, and all required 

information must be entered. Posting multiple transactions simultaneously is used primarily for 

transactions that have been left in the Draft state. 

Because you’re selecting transactions within the same journal, the selections will be posted to that 

journal. 

The process to post or submit mass updates is similar - the submit button appears when 
approval is required. Only draft journal entries can be posted or submitted. Draft journal entries 
can also be duplicated. 

To post or submit multiple entries: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Journal entries, and then click the View transactions link to display the transactions 

for the journal. 

At the left of the transactions list is a check box for each transaction.  

3. 
Select the check box for each draft transaction to post or submit for approval. To select all, 

select the check box at the top of the list, directly under the Select label. 

4. 
Click the Post or Submit button at the top of the page. 

5. 
An alert opens, asking you to confirm your action. Click OK. 

Journal entries will either be posted or submitted, depending on whether or not the entry is 
subject to an approval process. 

6. 
On the Post/Submit dialog box, information about your bulk action is displayed. Click 

Continue. 

Entries that are part of an approval process will be submitted for approval, not posted.

### Memorized Transactions
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 307*



#### View the List of Memorized Transactions for a Journal
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 307*

Chapter 10: Journal Entries

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Memorized Transactions 

Memorized transactions are recurring transactions whose amounts and other details can vary 

from month to month. For example, you might set up a memorized transaction for payroll, which 

you plan to post to the Accounts Payable journal on a regular basis. With a memorized 

transaction, you enter a description for the transaction and other basic information, such as the 

accounts and dimensions to use, only once. Each time the transaction recurs, you can edit the 

transaction header and line items as needed before posting the transaction. 

In practice, many companies duplicate the previously memorized transaction (for example, the 

last payroll transaction) and edit the amounts and other details as needed. They then post the 

new memorized transaction. 

View the List of Memorized Transactions for a Journal 

Click to view a list of memorized transactions for the journal. Memorized transactions are 

transactions that you frequently enter, but whose amounts can vary (for example, a utility bill). 

From the Memorized Transactions list, you post transactions that you’ve previously memorized, 

and add or edit memorized transactions. 

To view or edit memorized transactions in a journal: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Journal entry. 

3. 
Click the Memorized transactions link to display the memorized transactions in the journal. 

4. 
On the row with the transaction, click the Edit link or View link. 

5. 
Enter changes as needed. 

6. 
Click Post to save your changes.

The Adjustment Journal Entries list shows the list of adjustment journals available in the system.

submitted the entry, you are not the approver, and the approver hasn’t approved the 

entry.

Duplicate an entry. 

• 
Reverse one or multiple entries.

Attach a supporting document to one or multiple entries.

Adding a New Adjusting Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > 
 Adjusting Journal`



> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > Setup > Adjustments > View Transactions > Add`


You can adjust a journal entry for any reason. For example, you can adjust a journal entry by 

adding an attachment to a transaction, as it is a good way to substantiate the transaction. You can 

also distribute amounts across departments and locations automatically by using the transaction 

allocations. 

To add an adjustment journal entry: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General Ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Adjusting entry and then select the 
 Add button next to Adjusting journal. 

3. 
Click the appropriate journal to select it. The Journal drop-down list does not appear when 

you add a journal entry directly from a journal. 

In companies that use dual-method reporting (both accrual and cash), consider to whom 
you grant permission for this page. It could be easy for someone to mistake a cash journal 
instead of an accrual journal, especially if they are not named clearly. It is best for 
everybody else to use templated transactions. 

4. 
Accept the current date as the Posting date of this transaction or type or select a different 

one by clicking the 
 Calendar button. 

If you are using non-standard accounting periods, you can’t save a G/L transaction that falls 

outside the accounting periods you have defined. If you need to do this, add a new 

accounting period. 

The Automatic reversal date appears only when you create the transaction to give you an 

opportunity to reverse the transaction later. To actually reverse a transaction, use the 

Reverse link that is displayed only when you have reversed a transaction. 

5. 
In the Description field, type a description of the transaction.  

6. 
Add a Comment about the reason for the adjusting journal entry. 

7. 
In the Reference number field, type any identifying number associated with the adjusting 

entry. 

8. 
In the Line entry type section, select the type of line items that are associated with this 

adjusting entry: 

• 
Standard 

• 
Include Job Cost

In the Source entity drop-down list, select the paying entity that is associated with the 

adjusting entry. Your selection affects the locations that are available in the entries section. 

Filling In the Documents Section 

Use this section to associate a document in the system to support the transaction. You can either 

select a file on your computer or scan a document. 

You can attach any type of file to the transaction, including scanned images, spreadsheets, and 

word-processor documents. Attached files are uploaded to the system for permanent, safe 

storage. You must have Attachment permissions (on page 709) to attach documents to records. 

To attach a file on your computer: 

1. 
Click the Choose file button. A box opens to enable you to find the file. 

2. 
Find the desired file that you want to attach to this journal entry, and then click the Open 

button. 

3. 
Click the Attach button. 

To scan a document: 

1. 
In the File name field, type a name for the document that you are about to scan. 

2. 
Click the Scan button. The Select source box opens. 

3. 
Select the scanner and then click the Select button. 

4. 
Follow the on-screen instructions of your scanner. 

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 
attach the file to this record. 

Filling In the Entries Section 

In the Entries section, you can add values directly to each line item where needed, or click Show 

defaults (on page 251) to proactively select default values to auto-fill each line item. After the 

system fills in the default values, you can override any default value on any line item as needed.  

1. 
To set up a value as a default for each existing and new line item, click the drop-down list of 

a field, and select the desired default value. 

Any dimensions that your company has chosen to use appear in the Entries list. Supported 
dimensions include Department, Location or Property, Customer, and Vendor. 

In the list, enter information for each journal entry line item as follows. 

2. 
In the Account drop-down list, click the account to which the entry should apply. If the 

account doesn’t exist, you can use the field level controls to Add a new G/L account, View a 

G/L account’s record, or Find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you 

must be at the top level.

The entire transaction must balance. Out -of-balance transactions, in which required 
information is not entered, are not saved, and an error message appears. 

Saving and Submitting 

When you add a transaction to an adjustment journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft 

or submitting it right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be 

complete—you or another user can review them later, make changes, and then submit them. 

When you submit a journal entry, the entire transaction must balance, and all required 

information must be entered. 

When you finish entering or editing the transaction information, click one of the buttons: 

• 
Submit: Submits this journal entry to be approved.  

• 
Draft: Saves this journal entry without submitting it for approval or posting it.  

• 
Submit & New: Submits this journal entry and sends the journal entry to be approved, and 

then creates another blank journal entry record.

Finding transactions in a specific state 

Use list views of transactions to view and access all transactions of a 

specific type, for example, A/P invoices or A/R invoices.  

There are two easy ways to locate transactions in a specific state: 

• 
Filter for the transaction state on the fly: In the transaction list 

view, enter the state in the State column, then click Go. The list 

includes only those transactions in that state. 

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for the transaction 

state: Create the view, and set the filter to State = <state>, 

where <state> equals the state that you are seeking, such as 

Draft, Posted, Paid, Reversed, and so on. This custom view is 

always available from the transaction list.

Buttons 

Transactions List 

Add 
Opens a blank record for creating a new transaction 

The transaction type that the system opens corresponds with the type of 

journal. 

Print 
Prints the selected transactions 

Delete 
Deletes the selected transactions 

Done 
Closes the transaction list and returns to the list that corresponds to the 

transaction type 

Export 
Exports the list of transactions to a file in the format that you select, CSV, 

Excel, Word, or PDF 

Post 
Posts the selected transactions 

Duplicate 
Creates a duplicate of the selected transaction 

If you select multiple journal entries to duplicate, then you must specify 

the book and journal to which you want to copy the journal entries. See 

Duplicating journal entries to other books (on page 282). 

Reverse 
Reverses the selected transactions 

After selecting one or more transactions that you want to reverse, click 

the Reverse button. The Reversal entry parameters box opens to allow 

you to specify the date to reverse the transactions. You can select either 

the original date, or you can specify a different date. 

While there is no set limit to the number of entries that you can 
reverse, reversing many journal entries or multiple large line-item 
journal can cause your browser to time out. 

Attach 
Attaches a file to the selected transactions 

When you add an attachment to multiple transactions, the system 

assigns a unique ID to the attachment and the attachment has the same 

ID across the transactions that it is attached to.  

If you make changes to the attachment, it changes the attachment for all 

of the transactions that it is attached to with the same attachment ID.  

Attachments are allowed only on transactions that are directly 
posted to the General Ledger. If the transactions were posted to a 
subledger, the system displays an error message:  
“Attachment allowed only on Direct G/L Posting.”

### Adjusting Entries Page
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 338*

Adjusting Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adjusting Entries Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Adjustment > View Transactions > 
Add/Edit/View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > Adjusting Journal > 
Add/Edit/View`


Use the Adjusting Entries page to add, edit, and reverse transactions to an adjustment journal. To 

add an adjusting journal entry, the books must be closed. If they are open, enter a normal journal 

entry instead. See Adding a journal entry (on page 242). 

When you create an adjusting entry, all information appears on one page. 

When you open an adjusting entry in edit mode, the page has three tabs:  

• 
Transaction: This tab contains all of the most important information about the adjusting 

entry.  

• 
History: This tab displays information about the adjusting entry. Like an audit entry, this tab 

tracks the adjusting entry’s creation, who created it, and when. It also displays the current 

state of the transaction. 

• 
Messaging: This tab lets you communicate with other users in the system about a particular 

journal entry. Use this tab to create and review messages about the entry. See Sending a 

message regarding a journal entry (on page 259). 

When adding an adjusting entry, you can: 

• 
Post the adjusting entry to the General Ledger. 

• 
When the journal entry approvals feature is enabled, click the Submit button to submit the 

transaction to the approval queue. 

• 
Click Draft to save the transaction without posting or submitting it.  

• 
Click Post & New to post the entry to the General ledger, and then open a new blank record 

for creating another adjusting entry. 

• 
Click Submit & New to submit this transaction to the approval queue, and then open a new 

blank record for creating another adjusting entry. 

• 
Click Draft & new to save this transaction without submitting it and then open a new blank 

record for creating another adjusting entry. 

• 
Click Cancel to discard your changes and return to the Adjusting entries list. 

---

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

When viewing this record, you can: 

• 
Click the link under Source entity to view more information about the entity that is the 

source of funds for the adjusting entry. 

• 
Click the link in the Unit column of the debit entry for information about the invoicing unit, 

if any. 

• 
Click the link in the Unit column of the credit entry for information about the paying unit, if 

any. 

• 
Click the Edit button to make changes to the adjusting entry record. 

• 
Click the Reverse button to reverse the adjusting entry. 

• 
Click the Duplicate button to make a copy of this adjusting entry record. 

• 
Click the Print button to print this record. 

• 
Click the Excel button to export the transaction to Microsoft Excel. Optionally, go to the 

More Actions button and click the Excel option. 

• 
Click the Done button to close this record. 

• 
Click the More actions button to navigate to Previous and Next adjusting entry records. 

Select the View audit trail option to open the audit trail for this record. The audit trail 

contains additional event history of the transaction. 

• 
Click the More actions button and select Previous and Next to navigate the list of adjusting 

entries. 

When editing this record, you can: 

• 
Click the More actions button to reverse, duplicate, print, export to Excel, and view the audit 

trail. 

• 
Click the Save button to save the transaction.

#### Editing an Adjusting Journal Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 340*

Adjusting Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add and manage adjusting journal entries. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

General Ledger 
Adjusting journal entries  
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 664) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 664) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Editing an Adjusting Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > Adjusting Journal > Edit`


To edit an adjustment journal entry: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select General ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Click the Adjusting entry option, and then select Adjusting journal. 

3. 
Click the appropriate journal to select it.  

In companies that use dual-method reporting (both accrual and cash), consider to whom 

you grant permission for this page. It could be easy for someone to mistake a cash journal 

for an accrual journal, especially if they are not named clearly. It is best for everybody else to 

use templated transactions. 

4. 
Accept the current date as the date of this transaction or enter a different one. 

If you are using non-standard accounting periods, you can’t save a G/L transaction that falls 

outside the accounting periods you have defined. If you need to do this, add a new 

accounting period. 

5. 
The Reverse date appears only when you create the transaction to give you an opportunity 

to reverse the transaction later. To actually reverse a transaction, use the Reverse link that is 

displayed only when you have reversed a transaction. 

6. 
Enter a description of the transaction. Example: Setup Opening balances. 

7. 
Optionally, enter your own number by which you can reference this transaction. 

---


<!-- Page 341 -->
Chapter 11: Adjusting Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

8. 
If you enabled transaction allocations in the General Ledger Setup page, you can apply 

automatic distribution rules to all the lines in the Items section below.  

Click the down arrow in the Allocation drop-down list, and then click the allocation to apply 

to the line items. (Alternatively, you can select a different transaction allocation for each line 

item in the Journal entries section, or use a combination of both techniques.) 

To be able to apply a transaction allocation, you must first enable the allocation feature in 

the General ledger Setup tab. 

If your entity belongs to a multi-entity company, you can use transaction allocations only 
at the level in which they were created. In other words, if the allocation was created at the 
top level, a subordinate entity cannot use it. 

9. 
To store a digital version of a supporting document permanently and safely, in the 

Attachments field, click the drop-down arrow, and click Add to upload your attachment. 

You must have Attachments permissions (on page 709) to add attachments to records. 

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 
attach the file to this record. Attachments are available for regular journal entries, but not 
for statistical journal entries. 

10. 
In the Entries section, you can add values directly to each line item where needed, or click 

Show defaults to proactively select default values to auto-fill each line item.  

11. 
To set up a value as a default for each existing and new line item, click the drop-down list 

beside the appropriate field, and choose a value. You can override any default value on any 

line item as needed. 

Fill In the Journal Entries Section 

In the Journal Entries section, enter information for each journal entry line item as follows: 

1. 
Use the Account drop-down list to select the account to which the entry should apply. If the 

account doesn’t exist, click the 
 Add button. 

2. 
To assign the item to a department or location, click the Department or Location field, then 

click the appropriate department or location. 

If you enabled Validate JE Balancing for Location, Department, or another dimension on the 


> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger Setup page (go to General Ledger > Setup > Configuration), you must 
select the same dimension member (such as the same department or location) or no 
dimension member for both the debit and credit.`


For more information, see Configuring General Ledger in the online help or download (on 

page 718) the RealPage General Ledger Setup User Guide. 

3. 
Enter the amount to debit or credit. In either the Debit or Credit column, enter the amount 

of the transaction.  

---


<!-- Page 342 -->
Adjusting Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A single line can have a value in only one of these fields. As you enter debits and credits, the 

Total boxes keeps a running total. This is a quick reference to ensure a balanced entry. 

4. 
To add a memo regarding the purpose or reason for the entry, in the Memo field, type a 

note. (Example: To set up opening balances.) You can use up to 1,000 characters in a memo. 

When you add a new journal entry line, the memo description is copied from the previous 

line. You can overwrite the memo as needed. 

5. 
If there are boxes for one or more reporting dimensions, such as Customer or Vendor, click 

the down arrow for the dimension that you want to complete, and from the list that 

appears, select the entry that you want. 

To add more lines to the Entries list, click the 
 Add button.  

6. 
When you finish entering or editing the transaction information, click Submit, Draft, or 

Submit & New.  

Out-of-Balance Transactions 

The entire transaction must balance. Out-of-balance transactions (in which required information is 

not entered) are not saved, and an error message appears. 

If you receive the error message Transactions do not balance for locations X and Y when you save, 

the Enforce balance sheet by location feature has been enabled. To correct this error, make both 

locations the same. You can also choose no location.  

For more information, see Configuring General Ledger in the online help or download (on page 

718) the RealPage General Ledger Setup User Guide.

To view the list of tax adjusting journal entries:

Click the Applications menu, select General ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section of the menu, click the Adjusting entry option, and then select 

Tax Adjusting. The Journal entries for tax adjustment list displays your tax adjustment 

journals.

Tax Adjustment Journal Transactions List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > Tax Adjusting > View 
Transactions`


This page contains a list of transactions in a tax adjustment journal. 

Use this list to work with tax adjustments to accounting periods that are already closed. You can 

add a tax adjusting journal entry only if the books are closed. If they are open, enter a standard 

journal entry instead. From the transactions list, you can: 

• 
Add an entry to the tax adjustment journal. 

• 
Open an entry to view or change it. 

• 
Delete one entry or select multiple entries to delete. 

• 
Print a journal entry or select multiple journal entries to print. 

• 
Check the status of an entry. See which entries have been saved as a “draft” or “posted.” 

• 
Post one or multiple entries.  

If the Journal entry approval feature is enabled, then the Post button is replaced with the 

Submit button.  

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled on your system, you can: 

• 
Submit transactions for approval. 

• 
Recall a journal entry from the approval queue. You can recall a journal entry if you 

submitted the entry, you are not the approver, and the approver hasn’t approved the 

entry. 

• 
Duplicate an entry. 

• 
Reverse one or multiple entries. 

• 
Attach a supporting document to one or multiple entries.

The entire transaction must balance. Out -of-balance transactions, in which required 
information is not entered, are not saved, and an error message appears. 

Saving and Submitting 

When you add a transaction to an adjustment journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft 

or submitting it right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be 

complete—you or another user can review them later, make changes, and then submit them. 

When you submit a journal entry, the entire transaction must balance, and all required 

information must be entered. 

When you finish entering or editing the transaction information, click one of the buttons: 

• 
Submit: Submits this journal entry to be approved.  

• 
Draft: Saves this journal entry without submitting it for approval or posting it.  

• 
Submit & New: Submits this journal entry and sends the journal entry to be approved, 

and then creates another blank journal entry record. 

• 
Draft & New: Saves the progress on this journal entry without posting it. Later, you or 

another user can review the entry and post it. The system displays another blank 

journal entry record. 

If you receive the error message Transactions do not balance for locations X and Y
 when you save, 
the Enforce balance sheet by location feature has been enabled. To correct this error, make both 
locations the same. You can also choose no location. For more information, go to Configuring 
General Ledger.

GAAP Overview 

Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) is an accounting standard. Set by the standards 

organizations Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), Governmental Accounting Standards 

Board (GASB), and Financial Accounting Foundation (FAF), GAAP ensures uniform and consistent 

financial reporting across governments, businesses, and not-for-profit organizations. 

GAAP works to make sure that financial reporting is transparent and adheres to well-defined 

rules. 

RealPage adheres to these standards when creating workflows that help maintain GAAP 

compliance. 

For example, some accounting software allows editing transactions in closed periods. RealPage 

requires books to be reopened to make changes. This way, RealPage ensures GAAP compliance, 

an accurate audit trail, and complete historical reporting.

GAAP Journal Transactions List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > GAAP Adjusting > View 
Transactions`


This page lists the transactions of a GAAP adjustment journal. Use this list to work with GAAP 

adjustments to accounting periods that are already closed. You can add an GAAP adjusting 

journal entry only if the books are closed. If they are open, enter a standard journal entry instead. 

From the transactions list, you can: 

• 
Add an entry to the GAAP adjustment journal. 

• 
Open an entry to view or change it. 

• 
Delete one entry or select multiple entries to delete. 

• 
Print a journal entry or select multiple journal entries to print. 

• 
Check the status of an entry. See which entries have been saved as a “draft” or “posted.” 

• 
Post one or multiple entries.  

If the Journal entry approval feature is enabled, then the Post button is replaced with the 

Submit button.  

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled on your system, you can: 

• 
Submit transactions for approval. 

• 
Recall a journal entry from the approval queue. You can recall a journal entry if you 

submitted the entry, you are not the approver, and the approver hasn’t approved the 

entry. 

• 
Duplicate an entry. 

• 
Reverse one or multiple entries. 

• 
Attach a supporting document to one or multiple entries.  

When an entry has an attachment, an 
 Attachment icon appears next to the Excel link. 
Click the 
 Attachment icon to open the Attachments page. 

• 
Export the transaction list to a file. You can export the data as a CSV, Excel, Word, or PDF 

file. 

Manage the list using any of the standard controls: 

• 
Sorting 

• 
Filtering 

• 
Manage views 

• 
Include private 

• 
Advanced filters 

• 
Clear all filters

In multi-entity companies, transaction lists at the entity level include transactions created at

Adding a GAAP (Compliance) Adjusting or Tax Adjusting Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Adjusting Entry > 
 GAAP 
Adjusting/ Tax Adjusting`


The entire transaction must balance. You cannot save out-of-balance transactions. An 

out-of-balance transaction is one in which you did not enter required information. If you try to 

save an out-of-balance transaction, the system displays an error message. 

You can substantiate a transaction by associating it with a supporting document that has attached 

files.  

To add a GAAP or Tax adjusting entry: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section, under Entries, click Adjusting entry, and then select the 

Add button next to GAAP adjusting or Tax adjusting. 

If you are using non-standard accounting periods, you can’t save a G/L transaction that 
falls outside the accounting periods you have defined. 

3. 
Click the View transactions link for the journal to which you want to add a transaction, and 

then click the Add button. 

If you don’t see a drop-down list, there are no journals to which you can add entries.  


> **Navigation Path:** `To quickly add a new entry, you can also go to General Ledger > All > Journal Entry and`


click the 
 Add button next to GAAP Adjusting or Tax Adjusting. 

4. 
Select the Journal. This drop-down list appears only when you have opened the page from 


> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > GAAP Adjusting or Tax Adjusting.`


5. 
In the Posting date field, accept the current date or enter a different one. 

6. 
Select a date in the Automatic reversal date field. 

The Reverse date appears only when you create the transaction to give you an opportunity 

to reverse the transaction later. To actually reverse a transaction, use the Reverse link that 

opens only when you have reversed a transaction. 

7. 
Enter a description of the transaction. Example: Setup Opening balances. 

8. 
Optionally, enter your own number by which you can reference this transaction.

Filling In the Documents Section 

Use this section to associate a document in the system to support the transaction. You can either 

select a file on your computer or scan a document. 

You can attach any type of file to the transaction, including scanned images, spreadsheets, and 

word-processor documents. Attached files are uploaded to the system for permanent, safe 

storage. You must have Attachment permissions (on page 709) to attach a file to a record.

button. 

3. 
Click the Attach button.

1. 
In the File name field, type a name for the document that you are about to scan.

Click the Scan button. The Select source box opens.

Select the scanner and then click the Select button.

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to

or submitting it right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be

Finding transactions in a specific state 

Use list views of transactions to view and access all transactions of a 

specific type, for example, A/P invoices or A/R invoices.  

There are two easy ways to locate transactions in a specific state: 

• 
Filter for the transaction state on the fly: In the transaction list 

view, enter the state in the State column, then click Go. The list 

includes only those transactions in that state. 

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for the transaction 

state: Create the view, and set the filter to State = <state>, 

where <state> equals the state that you are seeking, such as 

Draft, Posted, Paid, Reversed, and so on. This custom view is 

always available from the transaction list.

Buttons 

Transactions List 

Add

The transaction type that the system opens corresponds with the type of

Print 
Prints the selected transactions 

Delete 
Deletes the selected transactions 

Done 
Closes the transaction list and returns to the list that corresponds to the

Export 
Exports the list of transactions to a file in the format that you select, CSV, 

Excel, Word, or PDF 

Post 
Posts the selected transactions 

Duplicate 
Creates a duplicate of the selected transaction 

If you select multiple journal entries to duplicate, then you must specify 

the book and journal to which you want to copy the journal entries. See 

Duplicating journal entries to other books (on page 282). 

Reverse 
Reverses the selected transactions 

After selecting one or more transactions that you want to reverse, click 

the Reverse button. The Reversal entry parameters box opens to allow 

you to specify the date to reverse the transactions. You can select either 

the original date, or you can specify a different date. 

While there is no set limit to the number of entries that you can 
reverse, reversing many journal entries or multiple large line-item 
journal can cause your browser to time out. 

Attach 
Attaches a file to the selected transactions 

When you add an attachment to multiple transactions, the system 

assigns a unique ID to the attachment and the attachment has the same 

ID across the transactions that it is attached to.  

If you make changes to the attachment, it changes the attachment for all 

of the transactions that it is attached to with the same attachment ID.  

Attachments are allowed only on transactions that are directly 
posted to the General Ledger. If the transactions were posted to a 
subledger, the system displays an error message:  
“Attachment allowed only on Direct G/L Posting.”

Journal Entry for User-Defined Books 

User-defined books are most commonly used to track specialized adjustments to your normal, 

operational books; however, you can use them for any purpose that you want. Before you can 

create user-defined journal entries, your system must have at least one user-defined book and 

one user-defined journal.  

To create new user-defined books and journals, you must have administrator level permissions 

with access to the Setup tab of the General Ledger menu. See Setting up user-defined books in 

online help, or download (on page 718) the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User 

Guide. 

Viewing the Transactions in a Particular Journal 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > User-Defined > View 
Transactions`


To view journal entries in a user-defined journal: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Adjusting entry, and then select User-defined. The list of user-defined opens. 

3. 
On the row with the journal containing the transactions you want to see, click View 

transactions. 

When you click View transactions next to a journal, you can: 

• 
View the list of transactions in the journal. 

• 
Add, edit, delete, or print transactions. 

• 
See which transactions have been saved as a draft or posted.

### Journal Entries for User-Defined Journals
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 391*

Journal Entries for User-Defined Journals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > User-Defined`


When you add a transaction to a journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft or posting it 

right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be complete—you or another 

user can review them later, make changes, and then post them. When you post a journal 

transaction, the entire transaction must balance, and all required information must be entered. 

You can substantiate a transaction by associating it with a supporting attachment. You can also 

use the transaction allocation feature to automatically distribute amounts across departments and 

locations. 

User-defined books are most commonly used to track specialized adjustments to your actual 

books; however, you can use them for any purpose that you want.  

Using the User-Defined Journal Entries list, you can: 

• 
See your list of your journals. 

• 
Add new entries to your journals. 

• 
Navigate into entries for a particular journal. 

• 
Create a new journal entry. 

You can sort and filter lists to see just the journal entries you want. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with statistical journal entries.

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 664) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 664) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

Entering General Information About the Transaction 

The top portion of the Transaction tab is where you type the transaction date, description, and 

other basic information. 

1. 
In the Posting Date field, accept the current date or enter a different one. This is the posting

2. 
In the Automatic reversal date field, type a date only if you want to reverse this transaction 

on a certain date.  

The reverse transaction is identical, except it is the inverse and therefore zeros out the 

transaction. You can enter any date of today or later. 

The option to enter a reversal date does not apply to draft journal entries. However, you can 

enter a Reverse date at the time that you post the entry.

4. 
Optionally, enter a Comment that you want to record in the transaction history.

Entering Line Items 

For the entry to be posted, you must specify at least the account and a debit or credit value for 

each line item. Depending on your company’s configuration, you may also be required to enter 

other information, such as the department or location. 

1.

In the Account drop-down list, select the account to which the entry should apply.

To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

In the Txn Currency drop-down list, select the currency used for this transaction. This field 

appears only when your system is set up for multiple currencies.

A single line can have a value in only one of these fields.

As you enter debits and credits, the journal entry automatically enters net debit or credit 

amounts and keeps a running total in the Total boxes at the bottom of the section. This 

helps you enter large numbers of journal entry lines efficiently and helps ensure a balanced 

entry.

Job Cost line items. 

Debit and Credit fields appear when your system is a single currency system. 

Transaction debit and Transaction credit fields appear when your system is set up for

Finishing the Journal Entry 

When you finish entering or editing the journal entry: 

• 
If journal entry approvals are disabled, you can either save the transaction as a draft or post 

it. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the entry without posting it. Later, 

you or another user can review the entry and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the journal entry. 

• 
You can also click the More actions button and then select Post and Print to post the 

journal entry and then print the record. 

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled, submit the journal entry for approval. 

• 
Click Submit to send the journal entry to the approval queue.  

• 
Click Submit & new to submit the journal entry to the approval queue, and then open 

a new journal entry. 

After a journal entry transaction has been approved and posted, editing the entry is not 
allowed and the Edit link isn’t available. To make any changes, reverse the transaction or 
delete it and resubmit it. After the period is closed, no changes are allowed to the entry, 
including reversal and deletion.

#### Importing Adjusting Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 400*

Journal Entries for User-Defined Books 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Adjusting Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Template`


Downloading the Template 

To download the adjusting journal entries template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Import data option, and then download the template for General Ledger Journal 

Entries. 

Filling In the Template 

Dates 

Typically, the Date is the next day after you close your old accounting system and start a new set 

of books in the system. In the event that you do not enter a date, the default is today. The choice 

of date is important: for example, if you choose to enter a date of two fiscal years ago because 

you want to be able to print comparative financial statements, you must then make Journal 

entries for the ending G/L balances for all of the periods between your starting balance date and 

the date you actually begin using RealPage Accounting. 

If you are uploading historical transactions, make sure that your starting balances contain these 

uploaded transactions, and set the date to that date. 

If you find you have set the wrong starting date for your G/L balances, you can clear the 

transactions from the Import data page, and then start again. 

Line Items 

The uploaded file must contain a number in either the DEBIT or CREDIT field. One or the other is 

required. For example, if you do not have a debit amount, you must have a credit amount. You 

can import negative numbers for either, in which case a negative debit amount is treated as a 

credit, and a negative credit is treated as a debit. 

---


<!-- Page 401 -->
Chapter 12: Journal Entries for User-Defined Books 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

The LINE_NO must be unique per journal entry and per journal. For example, Summary 1 might 

contain line numbers 1-20, Summary 2 1-44 and so on. For more information on line numbers, 

see Importing Data with Line Numbers. 

1. 
Minimally, add the required journal entry data to the template. 

• 
JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DATE: Type the date of the journal entry. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of up to 80 characters. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number, starting with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DEBIT: Type the debit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

CREDIT field. 

• 
CREDIT: Type the credit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

DEBIT field. 

• 
SOURCEENTITY: Type the name of the entity. This value is required when the option to 

automatically create inter-entity transactions is enabled for journal entries and the 

journal entry is not balanced by location. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date. This field is required unless you provide a value in 

the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

2. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

---


<!-- Page 402 -->
Journal Entries for User-Defined Books 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide

Importing the Data 

To import the data: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section, click the Adjusting Entry option, and then select the type of 

adjusting entry that you want to import. 

3. 
Click the Import transactions button. 

4. 
Click the Choose files button, find the CSV file with the data that you want to import, and 

double-click it. 

5. 
If the data in the CSV file includes dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format, select the date 

format used in the data that you are importing.  

6. 
Leave the File encoding setting set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
Select the Process offline check box if you want to process the import offline. Select this 

option for large files.  

8. 
In the Email results to this address field, type the email address where you want the system 

to send import results and error data. 

9. 
Click the Import button.

#### Editing User-defined Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 403*

Chapter 12: Journal Entries for User-Defined Books 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Editing User-defined Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > User-Defined > View 
Transactions > Edit`


 You can only edit a journal entry if: 

• 
The entry hasn’t been approved. 

• 
The entry hasn’t been posted. 

• 
The entry is not in a system journal. Only users with Limited or Full admin privileges can edit 

journal entries that are in system journals.  

If an Edit link does not appear by a journal entry, the entry is in a closed period. 

To make any changes, reverse the transaction or delete it and then resubmit it.  

• 
After the period is closed, no changes are allowed to the entry, which includes reversal and 

deletion. 

• 
After a journal entry transaction has been approved and posted, editing the entry is not 

allowed, and the Edit link isn’t available.  

To edit a journal entry: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Click the Adjusting entry option, and then select User-defined. 

3. 
Find the desired journal and then click the View Transactions link. The list of the journal’s 

transactions opens. 

4. 
Find the desired journal entry to edit, and then click the Edit link.  

When you open a journal entry for editing, you can access two additional tabs, History and 

Messaging.  

• 
Use the History tab to review past activities of the journal entry. 

• 
Use the Messaging tab to communicate with other users about the journal entry. 

5. 
When you finish making changes, you can either save the transaction as a draft or post it. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & New to save your progress on the entry, without posting it. 

Later, you or another user can review the entry and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & New to post the journal entry. 

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled on your system, click Submit to submit the 

journal entry for approval or click Submit and New to submit the journal entry for 

approval, and then open a new journal entry record.

*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 404*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicating Journal Entries to Other Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Journal Entry > View Transactions > View > 
Duplicate`


The ability to duplicate entries into a journal associated with a different book provides a new way 

to review entry impact prior to recording the transaction to your main books. For example, to see 

the impact an entry will have, create a user-defined book named “Provisional” and record the 

transaction to that book. Review the impact from a financial statement and if the change is 

acceptable, move (duplicate) the entry to your main book (usually accrual) and reverse it from the 

Provisional book. 

To duplicate a journal entry from one book to another book: 

1. 
Locate the type of journal entry to duplicate and click that type. For example, you might 

choose Journal entry, GAAP, Tax, User-defined, Adjusting, or Statistical. If you don’t see the 

book in the selection list, you might not have the right permissions to see it. Only books 

that you have access to are visible. 

2. 
View the journal entry and click View transactions to open the transactions list. 

3. 
Locate the transaction you want to duplicate and click View, and then click the Duplicate 

button. The Duplicate to box opens. 

4. 
Select the book and journal that you want to duplicate the entry into. The duplicated entry 

has a new transaction number and today’s date, but everything else is the same.  

5. 
In the Date section, specify whether to use the original date or a different date. If you 

choose to replace the date, then type or select the desired replacement date. 

6. 
If you want to reverse the entry or entries, select the Reverse date check box, and then type 

or select the desired reversal date.

Journal Entry for User-Defined Books Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > 
 User-Defined`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > User-Defined > Add/View`


Use this page to add, edit, and view the details of a journal entry in a user-defined journal. 

Transactions that you add can be posted right away or saved as a draft. 

User-defined books are most commonly used to track specialized adjustments to your actual 

books; however, you can use them for any purpose that you want. 

When you add a transaction to a journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft or posting it 

right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be complete—you or another 

user can review them later, make changes, and then post them. When you post a journal 

transaction, the entire transaction must balance, and all required information must be entered. 

You can substantiate a transaction by associating it with a supporting attachment. You can also 

use the transaction allocation feature to automatically distribute amounts across departments and 

locations.

### Statistical Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 420*

Statistical Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Statistical Journal Entries 

You enter statistical transactions in the same way that you enter standard journal entries. The only 

difference is that statistical transactions do not need to balance. Instead, you increase or decrease 

a value. For example, you might increase the number of locations in the month of June. In this 

case, you would use the Locations statistical account and the journal you created for locations. 

Statistical Journals 

Statistical journals are non-monetary and do not have a debit or credit as transactions. Instead, 

statistical journals simply increase or decrease a value. 

Before you can begin adding statistical journal entries, you need one or more statistical journals in 

the system. Then, you can create statistical journal entries to add to the journals.  

Accessing the List of Statistical Journals 

You can add statistical journal entries from the All tab of the General Ledger menu, but you 

cannot view the list of statistical journals. The list of statistical journals is accessible only from the 

Setup tab of the General Ledger menu, and you must have administrator permissions to access 

the options on the Setup tab. For information about adding statistical journals, see Adding a 

statistical journal in the online help or download (on page 718) the RealPage Accounting General 

Statistical Journal Entries 

You can add a statistical journal entry directly, or add it from the General Ledger workbench. After 

you have entered statistical transactions, you can use statistical accounts in your financial reports. 

Approvals and Statistical Entries 

Statistical entries and statistical adjusting entries are not eligible for the approval process. 

---



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 421*



#### Creating Statistical Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 421*

Creating Statistical Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Statistical Journal Entry`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Workbench`


You enter statistical transactions in the same way that you enter G/L transactions. The only 

difference is that statistical transactions do not need to balance. Instead, you increase or decrease 

a value. 

After you have entered statistical transactions, you can use statistical accounts in your financial 

reports. 

Adding a Statistical Journal Entry 

You can add a statistical journal entry directly, or add it from the General Ledger Workbench. 

To add a statistical Journal entry from the General Ledger workbench: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Workbench. 

3. 
Click the Add button, and then select the Statistical Journal Entry option. 

To add a new statistical journal entry directly: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Create Statistical Journal Entry. 

---


<!-- Page 422 -->
Statistical Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Creating the Statistical Journal Entry 

1. 
In the Journal field, select the journal to which you want to post this transaction. 

This field does not appear when you add a statistical journal entry from within a statistical 

journal, as the journal is already determined. 

2. 
In the Posting date field, type the date you want to post this transaction to the Statistical 

journal or click the 
 Calendar button to select a date. 

3. 
In the Automatic reversal date field, type the date you want to reverse the transaction. 

Enter a date only if you want to post a reverse transaction to this transaction. The reverse 

transaction is identical, except it is the inverse and therefore zeros out the transaction. You 

can enter any date of today or later. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description of this transaction. 

5. 
Optionally, add a comment about the transaction in the Comment field. 

6.

#### Adding a Recurring Statistical Journal Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 432*

Statistical Journal Entries

Recurring Statistical Journal Entries List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Recurring Statistical`


Recurring statistical journal entries work the same as standard entries, except that the statistical 

journal entry is repeated according to a schedule that you set. You also have the option to set a 

reversing schedule, for statistical journal entries that are always reversed at a later time. 

Using the Recurring Statistical Journal Entries list, you can: 

• 
Add a new recurring statistical journal entry. 

• 
View the list of recurring statistical journal entries defined for your company. 

• 
Find out the next date on which recurring statistical journal entry will be posted. 

• 
Navigate to the transactions that have been generated by each recurring statistical journal 

entry. 

If you need to update the amount or other details before the transaction is posted, use a 
memorized transaction instead. 

Adding a Recurring Statistical Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Recurring Statistical Journal Entry`


Adding a statistical journal entry comprises these steps:  

• 
Set the schedule 

• 
Schedule an automatic reversal (optional) 

• 
Add basic information about the statistical journal entry 

• 
Add the line items 

To add a recurring statistical journal entry: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add button next to Recurring statistical journal entry. 

Setting the Schedule 

In the Schedules section, indicate when the first journal entry should be created, how often it 

should be repeated, and when it should expire. 

1. 
In the Journal entry start date field, type the date that the system should create the first 

journal entry. 

2. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select a fixed number of transactions to be created or a 

specific date when the recurring journal entry should expire. To keep the journal entry 

running perpetually, select Never.  

---


<!-- Page 433 -->
Chapter 13: Statistical Journal Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

3. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, select how often you want the system to repeat 

journal entry creation: Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, and then type the number of 

intervals. 

4. 
To send an email alert when a scheduled entry fails, in the Email field, type one or more 

email addresses. Separate multiple addresses with a comma or semicolon. 

Scheduling an Automatic Reversal 

If the recurring journal entry is always reversed, you can schedule the reversing entry at the same 

time. 

1. 
Select the Automatically reverse this journal entry check box. 

2. 
Select the type of reversing schedule you want to create, and then specify the schedule 

details. You can either choose to link the reversing entry to the original journal entry, or you 

can create an independent reversal schedule, but not both. 

• 
Link reversing entry to original journal entry: Lets you schedule the reversing entry 

for a certain number of days, weeks, months, or years after the original entry. 

---


<!-- Page 434 -->
Statistical Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Create independent reversal schedule: Lets you create a reversing schedule that isn’t 

tied to the date of the original entry. If you select this option, you can use the same 

scheduling options that are available for the original journal entry. 

Adding Basic Information to the Transaction Section 

Add basic information about the recurring statistical journal entry. 

1. 
From the Journal drop-down list, choose the statistical journal for which you want to 

schedule a recurring statistical entry. 

2. 
In the Description field, type a brief description of the recurring statistical entry.  

The description is displayed on the Recurring Statistical Journal Entry list. A good 

description can help ensure proper use by other users. 

3. 
To add a reference number such as an account number, in Reference number, type a 

number.  

Reference numbers can be used to sort and filter recurring journal entries. 

4. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, select an attachment to add to this transaction or click 

Add and then click the Choose Files button to upload a file into the system.  

You can attach any type of file to the transaction, including scanned images, spreadsheets, 

or word-processor documents. Attached files are uploaded to the system for permanent,

safe storage. You must have Attachment permissions (on page 709) to attach a file to a 

record.

Adding the Entries  

In order for the transaction to be posted, you must specify at least the statistical account and an 

increase or decrease for each line item. Depending on your company, you may also be required to 

enter other information, such as the department or location. 

You can fill in the Entries list with default values by clicking the Show defaults link, or by adding 

values directly to each line item.  

Using Defaults 

In the Entries section, click the Show defaults link to display the defaults fields. Add values 

to the desired fields in the defaults section to have the system complete each line item. 

To set up a value as a default for each existing and new line item, type the value in the field, 

or click the drop-down beside the appropriate field and then choose a value. You can 

override any default value on any line item as needed. 

For example, you can set dimension values for tracking and reporting purposes. After you 

select the account, any dimension value that you set as a default is automatically reflected 

for each line item. 

1. 
Skip the Doc field. The system assigns this document number when you save the 

transaction. 

2. 
Choose the Statistical account to which the entry should apply. If the account doesn’t exist, 

click Add in the drop-down menu. 

3. 
Enter the amount to Increase or Decrease the account. 

Enter numbers only, without any commas or other punctuation. 

4. 
To assign the item to a department or location, click the Department or Location down 

arrow, and then click the appropriate department or location. 

---


<!-- Page 436 -->
Statistical Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
Select other dimensions as needed, such as a customer or vendor.  

To save space, some dimensions may not appear as fields on the main page. 

To display the complete list of dimensions available to you, click in a field (such as the 

Statistical Account field), and then click the Show details tab. 

You can edit the layout of transaction pages to suit the needs of your company. This allows 
you to customize which fields appear on the page, and their order. 

6. 
To add a memo regarding the purpose or reason for the entry, in the Memo field, type a 

note. Example: Head count change for June. 

You can use up to 1,000 characters in a memo. 

When you add a new journal entry line, the system copies the memo description from the 

previous line. However, you can overwrite this memo description. 

To add another line item, click the  Add button to the right of the line item. 

Saving Recurring Journal Entries 

When you create a recurring journal entry of any kind, journal entries are not created until the 

scheduled date. By saving a recurring journal entry, you are really saving the scheduled task.  

When you finish entering or editing the recurring transaction information, click one of the 

buttons: 

• 
Save: Saves the journal entry details and the schedule.  

• 
Save & New: Saves the journal entry details and the schedule, and then opens a new 

recurring statistical journal entry record.

Saving and Submitting 

When you add a transaction to an adjustment journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft 

or submitting it right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be 

complete—you or another user can review them later, make changes, and then submit them. 

When you submit a journal entry, the entire transaction must balance, and all required 

information must be entered. 

When you finish entering or editing the transaction information, click one of the buttons: 

• 
Submit: Submits this journal entry to be approved.  

• 
Draft: Saves this journal entry without submitting it for approval or posting it.  

• 
Submit & New: Submits this journal entry for approval, and then creates another blank 

statistical adjusting journal entry record. 

• 
Draft & New: Saves the progress on this journal entry without posting it. Later, you or 

another user can review the entry and post it. The system displays another blank statistical 

adjusting journal entry record.

The Site Experience is a scaled-down version of Spend Management in a simplified interface. 

While the Spend Management application in the RealPage Financial Suite offers more robust 

functionality, most users can accomplish their procurement-to-payment processes from the Site 

Experience. 

The Site View option opens Site Experience. The Site View menu option is available in the Spend 

Management, General Ledger, and Accounts Payable application menus.

### Recurring Journal Entries List
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 450*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 450*

Recurring Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Recurring Journal Entries List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Recurring Journal Entries`


Recurring journal entries are the same as standard journal entries except that the journal entry is 

repeated according to a schedule you set. You also have the option to set a reversing schedule, 

for journal entries that are always reversed at a later time. 

Using the Recurring journal entries list, you can: 

• 
Add a recurring journal entry. 

• 
View the list of recurring journal entries defined for your company. 

• 
Find out the next date on which recurring journal entry will be posted. 

• 
Navigate to the transactions that have been generated by each recurring journal entry. 

When you need to update the amount or other details before the transaction is posted, use a 

memorized transaction instead. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add and manage recurring journal entries. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

General ledger 
Recurring Journal Entries 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 664) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 664) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.
