#### Setting the Schedule for the Journal Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 451*



#### Scheduling an Automatic Reversal for the Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 451*

Chapter 15: Recurring Journal Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Setting the Schedule for the Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Recurring Journal Entries > Add/Edit`


As you add a recurring journal entry, you create the schedule for the recurrence. 

The system runs scheduled tasks shortly after midnight in the time zone set on the Preferences 
page unless a global offset is included. Scheduled recurrences adhere to this setting. However, 
jobs with past dates and jobs that are run offline aren’t constrained by the offset. 

To schedule the journal entry: 

1. 
In the Journal entry start date field, type or select the date when the first journal entry in 

the series should be created. 

2. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select Never to keep the journal entry running perpetually. 

Otherwise, select a fixed number of transactions to be created or a specific date when the 

recurring journal entry should expire. 

3. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, to have the journal entry repeat at regular intervals, 

select Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, and then type the number of intervals. 

4. 
In the Email field, type one or more email addresses to send an email alert when a 

scheduled entry fails. Separate multiple addresses with a comma or semicolon. 

See our tips for scheduling recurring transactions (on page 441). 

Scheduling an Automatic Reversal for the Entry 

If the recurring journal entry is always reversed, you can schedule the reversing entry at the same 

time. 

1. 
Select the Automatically reverse this journal entry check box. 

2. 
Select the type of reversing schedule you want to create, and then specify the schedule 

details. 

Link Reversing Entry to Original Journal: Select this option to schedule the reversing entry 

for a certain number of days, weeks, months, or years after the original entry. 

Create Independent Reversal Schedule: Select to create a reversing schedule that isn’t tied 

to the date of the original entry. If you select this option, you can use the same scheduling 

options that are available for the original journal entry. 

Setting up a link between the reversing entry and the original journal entry 

1. 
In Reverse by, type the number of time increments after which the reversal recurs.  

2. 
In the field below the Reverse by field, select the time increment (frequency) of the reversal. 

(None, Days, Weeks, Months, or Years) 

Changes to the original entry are automatically reflected in the reversal entry. 

---

#### Tips for Scheduling Recurring Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 455*

Chapter 15: Recurring Journal Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Tips for Scheduling Recurring Journal Entries 

For weeks, months, and years, the journal entry will recur at the next interval on the same day as 

the start date. For instance, if you set a journal entry to start on March 15th and recur monthly, 

the first journal entry will be created on March 15th, with subsequent journal entries recurring on 

the 15th of each month thereafter. 

---


<!-- Page 456 -->
Recurring Journal Entries 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Option for repeating How to use 

None 
Select this option if you want the journal entry to be created 

only once, which can be useful if you are setting up a journal 

entry for an item that might become recurring later. 

Days 
Enter the number of days until the journal entry should be 

repeated. 

For example, if the Start date is 1/1/2021 and you enter 5 

days, the first journal entry will be created on 1/1/2021 and 

the next one 5 days later (on 1/6/2021). The journal entry will 

continue to be repeated every 5 days. 

Weeks 
Enter the number of weeks until the journal entry should be 

repeated. 

For example, if the Start date is 1/1/2021 and you enter 1 

week, the first journal entry will be created on 1/1/2015 and 

the next one 1 week later (on 1/8/2021). The journal entry will 

continue to be repeated every week. 

Months 
Enter the number of months until the journal entry should be 

repeated. 

For example, if the Start date is 1/1/2021 and you enter 2 

months, the first journal entry will be created on 1/1/2021 and 

the next one on 3/1/2021. The journal entry will continue to be 

repeated every two months. 

Months with “End of 

Month” option 

Select this option if you want the journal entry to be created at 

the end of the month, rather than on the same day as the start 

date. 

For example, if the Start date is 1/1/2021 and you want to 

repeat the journal entry every month, the first journal entry will 

be created at the end of January, the next bill at the end of 

February, and so on. 

Years 
Enter the number of years until the journal entry should be 

repeated. 

For example, if the Start date is 1/1/2021 and you enter 1 year, 

the first journal entry will be created on 1/1/2021, the next one 

on 1/1/2021, and so on every year after.

#### Deleting a Recurring Journal Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 457*

Chapter 15: Recurring Journal Entries 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Deleting a Recurring Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Recurring Journal Entries > 
Delete`


Deleting a Recurring Journal Entry 

If there’s no chance you’ll use a recurring journal entry anymore, you can delete it instead of 

turning off the recurring schedule. The system removes the recurring journal entry from the list 

and creates no more JEs. 

To delete a recurring journal entry: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section of the menu, click Recurring journal entries. 

3. 
In the list, find the recurring journal entry that you want to delete, and then click the Delete 

link.  

A delete confirmation box opens. 

4. 
Click OK. 

Ending the Schedule 

If there is a chance that you will need the recurring journal entry again, instead of deleting the 

record, you can choose to change the recurring journal entry’s Schedule settings. For example, if 

you had the Ending on field set to Never, you can change that setting to End date and then set 

the End on date to the date that you want the recurring journal entries to stop being created. 

---

Journal Entry Approvals 

This chapter describes how to use the journal entry approval process. The journal entry approval process apples to 

all types of journal entries, including standard journal entries, adjusting entries, user-defined journal entries, tax 

adjusting entries, and GAAP (Compliance) entries.

### Approving Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 462*

Journal Entry Approvals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approving Journal Entries 

See the How to Get Here (on page 449) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

Use the Approval workbench to review journal entries that are assigned to you. As you approve 

or decline the transactions, add a comment (optional) to explain your decision. The Approval 

workbench is in the Company application. See Using the Approval Workbench to Work with 

Transaction Approvals (on page 453). 

A journal entry saved as a draft does not appear in the Approval workbench. The journal entry 

must be submitted to appear in the Approval workbench. 

The journal entry approval process does not include inter-entity journal entries (IEP or IER) or 
system journal entries.  

Prerequisites 

Journal entry approvals must be configured in the Company application on the Approval 

Configuration page.  

• 
Select the Enable journal entry approval check box. 

Who Can Approve Journal Entries 

• 
You can approve journal entries when you are assigned to be an approver directly or if you 

are assigned to a role that is assigned to be approvers.  

• 
You can approve journal entries if you are set up on the Approval Configuration page as an 

unrestricted user. See Configuring Transaction Approvals for more information. 

• 
You can assign a default approver for journal entries. This user is designated to fill in for 

approvers who are unavailable. The default approver is set up on the Approval 

Configuration page in the Approver assigned if a user is inactive or a user is not present 

in a role drop-down list. 

---

• 
Users who have bypass approval permissions can submit transactions without sending the 

transactions for approval, thereby having their transactions approved automatically. See 

Bypassing the Approval Workflow for more information. 

Notifications 

During the approval process, the system can be configured to notify you when journal entries are 

waiting for approval. You can set up how you want to receive these notifications in your 

preferences (on page 450). 

Before You Begin 

To approve journal entries, the journal entry approvals must be enabled, and you or your role 

must be listed in an approval policy for journals as an approver. To enable journal entry approvals, 

see Configuring transaction approvals in online help or download (on page 718) the RealPage 

Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide. 

Consider enabling the Advance posting date feature. This feature allows the system to advance 

the posting date of a journal entry when it is submitted to a closed period. To enable the feature, 

see Enabling the advance posting date feature in online help, or download (on page 718) the 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.

additional options to access the workbench, depending on your permissions.

### Journal Entries Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 465*



#### Viewing Journal Entries Waiting for Approval
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 465*

Chapter 16: Journal Entry Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Journal Entries Approval Process 

This section describes how to use the journal entry approval process. 

User (Requester) Creates and Submits Journal Entry 

1. 
A user creates and submits a journal entry. 

2. 
The approver (or an assigned alternate approver) is notified of the need to approve the 

transaction. 

Approver Approves or Declines Entries 

1. 
Approver approves or declines the journal entry. 

2. 
If approved, the system posts the entry.  

If declined, the entry is edited or sent back for resubmission. 

Journal Entry Types and Their Approval Processes 

• 
A one-time journal entry with an automatic reversal requires only one approval because the 

initial journal entry and the reversing journal entry are posted in a single action by the user.  

• 
A scheduled recurring journal entry requires an approval for each occurrence. Each journal 

entry created from the recurring schedule goes through the approval process. 

Viewing Journal Entries Waiting for Approval 

See the How to Get Here (on page 449) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

To view the list of journal entries awaiting approval: 

1. 
Open the Approval workbench. 

2. 
Select the Journal entry option. The list of journal entries that are going through the 

approval process loads into the workbench. 

• 
To see all journal entries that have been submitted for approval, click the View all 

button. 

• 
To see all transactions that are waiting for your approval, click the My approvals 

button.

Reviewing Transaction Details and History 

See the How to Get Here (on page 449) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

To see details and history for one transaction: 

1. 
Open the Approval workbench. 

2. 
Select Journal entry. 

3. 
Find the journal entry that you want to view. 

4. 
Click the View link. The journal entry page opens. 

The Transaction tab displays the details, and the History tab contains the history of this 

journal entry. 

Editing an Approved Journal Entry 

After a transaction has been fully approved, it is posted, and you can’t make changes. Instead, 

reverse the transaction and re-enter it. 

Reversing preserves the original transaction and creates a matching one to balance it. Re-entering 

the transaction sends it to the beginning of the approval chain. Anyone who has already 

approved needs to approve again. See Reversing a journal entry (on page 284). 

Partially Approved Journal Entries 

If an entry appears in the Partial approval state, it means that your company has set up approval 

for multiple approvers (an approval chain) and that at least one but not all of the approvers have 

approved the entry. 

To complete the approval or declination of the entry, contact the user whose approval is required 

to take the appropriate action. 

To find out who the next approver is: 

• 
Click the View link (to the left of the transaction). 

To view the journal entry’s approval status:  

• 
All approvers: Click the View all button. 

• 
You: Click the View submitted button.

Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver 

See the How to Get Here (on page 449) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

Some transactions require approvals from multiple levels. If a transaction pending your approval 

was approved by someone else, you can send the transaction back to that approver instead of 

declining the transaction outright. 

To send a transaction back to the previous approver: 

1. 
On the Approval workbench - My approvals page, click the Send back link in the Send 

back column next to the transaction. 

The Send back box opens. 

2. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

3. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transaction no 

longer appears in your queue. 

Sending Back Multiple Transactions 

To send back multiple transactions to the previous approver: 

1. 
From the Approval workbench - My approvals page, select the check box next to each 

transaction that you want to send back to the previous approver. 

2. 
Click the Send back link in the Send back column next to any of the transactions that you 

selected. 

The Send back box opens. 

3. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

4. 
Select the additional approver from the Additional approver drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transactions no 

longer appear in your queue.

Prepaids 

Use the Prepaids feature to automate amortizations and track prepaid expenses. The system 

allows you to create prepaid amortization schedules and post prepaid expenses each month 

based on the schedule. 

Prepaid journal entries can only be added at the top level. 

RealPage Accounting offers two related reports: 

• 
Amortization Schedule report

### Prepaid Journal Entries List
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 481*

Chapter 17: Prepaids 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Prepaid Journal Entries List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Prepaids`


Use the Prepaid Journal Entries list to create and manage prepaid journal entries. Prepaid journal 

entries are recurring (scheduled) journal entries that automatically apply a prepaid amount to a 

recurring charge (like insurance). 

By default, the Prepaid journal entries list shows only active prepaids. You can have the system 

include completed prepaids in the list by selecting the Include Complete check box.  

From the list, you can: 

• 
Add a new prepaid journal entry (on page 468). 

• 
View and edit an existing prepaid journal entry (on page 474). 

• 
View the schedule of a prepaid journal entry (on page 475). 

• 
View the result of the last scheduled journal entry (on page 476). 

• 
Delete a prepaid journal entry (on page 475). 

• 
Export the list of prepaid journal entries (on page 200). 

---



#### Adding a Prepaid Journal Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 482*

Prepaids 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding a Prepaid Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Prepaids`


To create a prepaid journal entry: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section of the menu, click the 
 Add button next to the Prepaids 

option. 

Filling In the Schedules Section 

1. 
In the Start date and End date fields, type the dates for the time frame that the prepaid 

payment applies to.  

2. 
In the Posting drop-down list, select when you want to post the prepaid amount. Prepaids 

post monthly, based on your selection: 

• 
Based on start date: The prepaid journal entry posts on the same date every month 

based on the start date. For example, if the start date is the 15th, then the prepaid 

journal entry posts on the 15th of the month. 

• 
Beginning of the month: The prepaid journal entry posts on the first day of the 

month. 

• 
End of the month: The prepaid journal entry posts on the last day of the month. 

When you create a prepaid journal entry with a start date that is before today’s date, the 
system creates journal entries for the earlier dates. 

3. 
In the Total prepaid amount field, type the total amount of the prepaid journal entry. 

4. 
Select the Round last entry to the nearest dollar check box when the monthly amount and 

occurrences will not equal the amount in the Total prepaid amount field. When you select 

this check box and the last prepaid journal entry of the schedule is posted, the system posts 

a second entry as the rounding entry, tying out the prepaid.  

For example, after six months, $4,999.98 is recorded towards insurance. A seventh rounding 

entry is recorded for $0.02.  

When you select the check box, the Rounding account drop-down list appears. Select the 

account that you want to use for the rounding transaction at the end of the prepaid 

schedule. 

5. 
In the Email field, type the email address that you want to send notifications about this 

prepaid journal entry to. The system sends an email when the prepaid journal entry posts. 

6. 
In the Previously expensed amount field, type the amount for prepaid journal entries that 

were accounted for outside of RealPage Accounting.  

---


<!-- Page 483 -->
Chapter 17: Prepaids 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

7. 
In the Date starting expense in RealPage Accounting field, type the date to determine 

when prepaid journal entries start being created in RealPage Accounting. 

8. 
In the Expense Paid Date field, type the date when the expense was paid if the date was 

before the date that the payments are scheduled to begin.  

Filling In the Transaction Section 

1. 
In the Book drop-down list, select All books, or select the book that you want the prepaid 

journal entry to appear in.  

2. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the desired journal for prepaid journal entries. Prepaid 

journal is the default, but you can change it based on your business needs. 

3. 
In the Description field, type a description that identifies the prepaid entry. 

You can define prepaids for only one location. 

4. 
Optionally, in the Reference number field, you can enter an external identifier associated 

with the prepaid journal entry.  

5. 
In the Source entity drop-down list, select the paying entity. 

6. 
In the Attachments field, you can attach any type of file to the transaction, including 

scanned images, spreadsheets, and word-processor documents. Select an attachment from 

the drop-down list or click the Choose Files button to upload a file into the system.  

• 
Show all/Show unattached: Click this link to toggle between showing all existing files 

in the system to showing only files that are not attached to any other record in the 

system. 

• 
Add: Click to upload a file on your computer into the system. 

• 
View: Click this link to view the highlighted file.  

• 
Find: Click this link to search the files in the system. 

Attached files are uploaded to the system for permanent, safe storage.  

You must have Attachment permissions (on page 709 ) to attach files. 

Set Up Default Values for All Line Items (Optional) 

In the Entries section, you can add values directly to each line item where needed or click the 

Show defaults link to set up default values that the system will use to complete each line item. 

To set up a value as a default for each existing and new line item: 

1. 
Click Show defaults. 

2. 
In each drop-down list that you want the system to complete, choose a value.  

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button to save the selections.  

---


<!-- Page 484 -->
Prepaids 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Keep in mind that you can override any default value on any line item.  

Learn more about setting up default line-item values (on page 251). See Line-Item Entry Tips in 

the online help or download the RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide for more tips.  

Filling In the Entries Section 

Note that the order of the columns might vary depending on your company’s customizations. 

1. 
In the Doc field, type a document reference or identifier. 

2. 
In the Account drop-down list, select the G/L account to categorize the line item. 

• 
To use an account that is already in the system, select that account from the 

drop-down list. 

• 
To use an account is not yet in the system, click Add, enter the account details, and 

then click Save.  

To add G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

3. 
Select the currency used for the prepaid journal entry in the Transaction currency 

drop-down list. This column appears only when your system is set up for multiple 

currencies. 

Debit and Credit fields appear when your system is a single currency system. Transaction 

debit and Transaction credit fields appear when your system is set up for multiple 

currencies.  

4. 
In the Debit (Transaction debit) or Credit (Transaction credit) fields, type the amount of the 

transaction. A line item can have a value in only one of the fields, Debit (Transaction debit), 

or Credit (Transaction credit). When you fill in one of these fields, the system fills in the 

corresponding Base debit or Base credit field automatically. 

A single line can have a value in only one of these fields.

As you enter debits and credits, the journal entry automatically enters net debit or credit 

amounts and keeps a running total in the Total boxes at the bottom of the section. This 

helps you enter large numbers of journal entry lines efficiently and helps ensure a balanced 

entry. 

5. 
In the Department drop-down list, select a department to associate it with the line item. 

If this is an inter-entity transaction (if you have selected a source or paying entity), you must 

also select the target or receiving entity. 

6. 
In the Location (Location area) drop-down list, select the location to assign the line item to 

a location (entity). 

The entity may be either an entity that you specify directly or the parent entity of the 

location that you specify. The system automatically credits the journal of the target entity 

---


<!-- Page 485 -->
Chapter 17: Prepaids 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

and also automatically creates balancing entries in the respective journals of both the 

source and target entities. 

7. 
To assign a segment to the line item, select the segment in the Segment type 1 drop-down 

list, and then select the segment type that you want to assign. Select the value in the 

Segment value 1 drop-down list. 

If the Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system may not 
have the segments feature enabled (on page 687 ). 

8. 
In the Memo field, type a memo for the line item. 

9. 
In the next row, fill in the offsetting field. For example, if you entered the debit in the first 

row, record the credit in the second row. 

Details Section 

To save space, some fields do not appear on the main transaction page.  

To display the complete list of fields available to you: 

• 
Click a field in the Entries section (such as the Account field) to display the hidden tab, 

and then click the Show details tab. The Details section expands to show the 

additional fields. 

• 
Fill in the additional dimensions as needed. 

• 
In the Segments section, select the segment type(s) and value(s). You can add up to 

three additional segments (on page 686). 

• 
Click the Previous row and Next row buttons to move from one line item to the next. 

• 
Click the Hide details tab to collapse the Details section. 

10. 
Click Save. You can also click the Save & New button if you want to create another new 

prepaid journal entry.

#### Importing Prepaids
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 486*

Prepaids 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide

Importing Prepaids 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Prepaids > Import`


Before You Begin 

• 
Download the template and fill it with your prepaids data. 

• 
Save the template as a CSV file.  

To download the prepaids template: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Prepaids in the Periodic Tasks section of the menu. 

3. 
in the Prepaid Journal Entries list, click the Import button. 

4. 
In the Prepaids Import box, click the Download template link. 

Filling the Template File with Your Data 

Open the template using a spreadsheet application and then enter the information. By default, 

the file opens in Excel. 

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each prepaid journal entry that you want to import: 

• 
START_DATE: Type the date that payments are scheduled to begin. Prepaids post 

monthly. 

• 
END_DATE: Type the date that payments are scheduled to end.  

• 
POSTING: Type one of the following to determine when you want to post the prepaid: 

Based on start date, Beginning of month, End of month 

• 
TOTAL_AMOUNT: Type the total. The amount must be equal to the total amount of 

the posted prepaid. 

• 
ROUNDING_ACCT: Type a G/L account. This value is required when Round is set to 

True. 

• 
DATE_STARTING_PREV_EXP: Type the date that the amount for prepaid journal entries 

were accounted for outside of RealPage Accounting. A value is required when a 

previously expensed amount is defined. 

• 
EXP_PAID_DATE: Type the date when the expense was paid if the date was before the 

date that the payments are scheduled to begin. 

• 
BOOK: Type the name of the book that you want the prepaid journal entry to appear 

in. 

• 
JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal for prepaid journal entries. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description that identifies the prepaid entry. 

• 
SOURCE_ENTITY: Type the paying entity’s name. 

---


<!-- Page 487 -->
Chapter 17: Prepaids 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number, starting with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number to associate the journal entry. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the location.  

• 
DEBIT: Type the debit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

CREDIT field. A negative number is treated as a credit. 

• 
CREDIT: Type the credit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

DEBIT field. A negative number is treated as a debit. 

2. 
Optionally, fill in any of the remaining columns. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

4. 
After you’ve entered your data, look through the file for any of the common issues (on page 

703) that imports can have. 

You are ready to import your file to your system. 

Importing the Data 

To import prepaids data: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Prepaids in the Periodic Tasks section of the menu. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Import box appears. The box’s title and on-screen instructions 

above the Choose file button reflect the type of data that you are importing. 

4. 
Select the file that you want to import and click the Open button. 

The file you import must be in CSV format. 

5. 
If your data contains dates, then in the Date format field, select the date format used by the 

data that you are importing. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding field set to the default status auto detect. 

7. 
Select the Process offline check box to have the system import the data with the least 

impact to system processing speed. 

8. 
To have the system send an email when the import is finished, type your email address in 

the Email results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses; separate 

each address by a semi-colon or comma. The system sends an email when an offline import 

is finished and when errors occur. 

9. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row that starts with a # symbol.

Changing a Prepaid’s Status to Inactive Pauses the Schedule 

You can edit a prepaid record and change the status to Active or Inactive. When you change a 

prepaid journal entry to Inactive status, the system stops creating automatic prepaid records in its 

schedule. To have the system begin creating prepaid journal entries again, change the status to 

Active. The system will not create prepaid journal entries that should have been created while the 

status was set to Inactive. 

After a prepaid finishes its amortization schedule, the system marks the prepaid record with a 

status of Complete.  

You cannot change the status to Complete. Only the system can mark a prepaid journal entry as 
Complete. 

Viewing the Prepaid Schedule 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Prepaids > Schedule`


To view a prepaid journal entry’s schedule: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select the Prepaids option. The Prepaid journal entries list opens. 

3. 
Find the desired prepaid journal entry, and then click the Schedule link. The Prepaid Journal 

Entry Schedule list opens. 

To pause a scheduled prepaid journal entry, edit the record and change the status to 
Inactive. When you are ready to resume, you can change the status to Active. 

Deleting a Prepaid Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Prepaids > Delete`


To delete a recurring prepaid journal entry: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select the Prepaids option. The Prepaid journal entries list opens. 

3. 
Find the desired prepaid journal entry, and then click the Delete link.  

4. 
Click OK to confirm the deletion.

Prepaid Journal Entries Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Periodic Tasks > Prepaids > Add/View/Edit`


Use this page to add, view, and change the prepaid journal entry details. The page is divided into 

three sections: 

• 
Schedules: This section contains fields related to the duration of the recurring journal entry, 

the amount, the account that you want to use for rounding, and the email address to which 

you want to send notifications when the record is posted. 

• 
Transaction: This section contains details about the journal entry, including its unique 

identifier, the book and journal where it is stored, a description of the transaction, the 

reference number, the entity that is the source of funds, and any attachments. 

• 
Entries: This section contains the line items associated with the prepaid journal entry.

### Accruals Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 508*

Accruals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accruals Overview 

Accountants spend a significant amount of time determining what the accrual postings should be 

each month, from deciding which transactions should be included to determining the total 

amount of the accrual. The RealPage Accounting automated accruals feature reduces the time 

that you spend making these decisions for your month-end closing.  

Accounting systems use accruals to recognize revenue and expenses that have been earned or 

consumed but for which you have not received payment. Examples of accrual candidates include: 

• 
Invoices that haven’t been received: When a vendor delivers goods or services without an 

invoice at the time of delivery, then there is a gap between delivery and invoicing. In accrual 

systems, you want to account for the receipt of the goods and services, and you want the 

books to show that your company owes a payment to the vendor, even if the invoice has 

not been received yet. Your company accrues the estimated amount of the expense in the 

current month in advance of the invoice receipt. 

• 
Invoices advanced: Move advanced invoices through the dead zone. 

• 
G/L postings: These are transactions that the system has advanced to the first of the next 

month. These are transactions from Leasing & Rents. 

Working on Accruals 

When you want to work on accruals, open the Accrual workbench (on page 496), filter the 

accruals that you want to work on, apply the filter, and then select the accruals that you want to 

calculate and post.  

---



### Accruals Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 509*

Chapter 18: Accruals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Accruals Workflow 

Step 1: Each month, open the Accrual workbench and apply each accrual template that you have 

created, and review the suggested accruals that you need to make. 

Step 2: Choose the transactions that you want to accrue. 

Step 3: Calculate the accruals. 

Step 4: Evaluate the accruals that the system calculated. 

Step 5: Post the accruals. The system posts the accrual and creates a reversing entry on the first of 

the next month. 

---



### Accrual Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 510*

Accruals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accrual Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Accrual > Accrual Workbench`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Accounts Payable > Accrual Workbench`


The Accrual workbench contains accrual information based on accrual templates. 

Use the Accrual workbench to filter and search for calculated accruals. You can view the 

suggested accruals, select what you want to accrue, and then post the accruals. After an accrual is 

posted, the system creates a reversing entry. The reversal date defaults to the first day of the next 

month. You can change the reversal date in the Reversal Date field.  

Using the Accrual Workbench with the AI Finance Agent 

If your company subscribes to the AI Finance Agent, the workbench contains accrual information 

based on accrual templates that the AI Finance Agent creates in addition to any accrual templates 

that you created manually. Note that only the Accrual workbench in the Finance Agent application 

includes both regular and AI agent-processed accruals. 

Use the Accrual workbench to find accruals that the AI agent has calculated.  

• 
Use the filters for Property, Accrual for (month), or an Accrual ID and then click Apply to find 

the calculated accruals.  

• 
Click the Amount in the list to view the missing expenses for the vendor.  

• 
After you validate the accrual, you can post it here by selecting the accrual, and then clicking 

the Post button. The system posts an accrual entry based on the accrual template and then 

reverses it on the first day of the next month. 

• 
Use the Accrual Activity report to check which missing expenses that the AI agent calculated 

or posted, and the date it occurred. 

You can receive an email from the system when accruals are calculated or posted when you are 
assigned to the Finance Agent - Automated Accrual Notifications role. 

---


<!-- Page 511 -->
Chapter 18: Accruals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

The Accrual workbench is divided into two sections: Filters and the list. 

a) Filters: The top section contains options that allow you to filter for the accruals that you 

want to work with.  

b) List Controls: These controls affect what happens to the accruals in the bottom section. The 

Calculate, Post, Unpost, and Delete buttons act on the selected expenses in the list. The 

Refresh button updates the list with any new expenses that match your filters. 

c) List of expenses to accrue: After you click the Apply button, the list of expenses that fall 

within your filter settings appear in the bottom section. Use this section to select the 

expenses that you want to act on (Calculate, Post, Unpost, or Delete).  

d) Save View As: When you have the filters set to retrieve accruals that you want to use again 

later, save the settings in a view.  

e) Export: Exports the list of expenses that appear in the list in the selected file format.  

f) 
Done: Closes the workbench and returns to the application’s home page. 

You can also: 

• 
Click the text in the Accrual ID column to open the accrual template. 

• 
Click the number in the Amount column to open the Calculated Accruals box. 

• 
Click the number in the Journal Entry column to open the journal entries associated 

with the accrual.

### Calculate Accruals Box
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 521*

Chapter 18: Accruals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Calculate Accruals Box 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Accrual > Accrual Workbench > (Amount)`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Accounts Payable > Accrual Workbench > 
(Amount)`


Use this box to review the calculated accrual and post the accrual amounts to the General Ledger. 

You can also click a number in the Amount column to view an invoice’s details. 

Interpreting the Calculate Accruals Box 

The box shows how the system calculates the accrual amount. The accrual template determines 

the calculation: 

---


<!-- Page 522 -->
Accruals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Invoices Not Received accrual template. The amount is based on the last invoice amount. 

The box lists the last invoice that the system uses to base the accrual amount on. 

• 
Invoices Not Received accrual template.  

The accrual amount is the average of the last three invoices. The box lists the invoices that it 

used to calculate the amount. The system uses the last three invoices, but if there are only 

two invoices in the system, it averages the two invoices that it has to calculate the accrual 

amount. 

---


<!-- Page 523 -->
Chapter 18: Accruals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

• 
Invoices Advanced accrual template. The system evaluates three invoice attributes: 

• 
The invoice must have an invoice date that is prior to the posting date of the first of 

the month after the accrual period. 

• 
Invoices must fall into the Account To/From range specified in the template. 

• 
Invoices must be selected for accrual in this box. 

The system sums the items that meet the criteria, and then uses the total as the accrual 

amount. 

• 
Invoices Not Received accrual template. When you post the accrual to the General Ledger, 

it posts with the fixed amount that is specified in the template. 

• 
G/L Posting Date: If the account was credited in an advanced journal entry, then the system 

evaluates the credit line items of the accounts in the accrual template in the invoice.

### Open and Close Process
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 529*

Chapter 19: Books 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Open and Close Process 

Closing procedures and policies vary from company to company. Consequently, RealPage 

Accounting offers flexibility so that the system can adapt to your business practices. 

Before you finally close the books for a period, you can close individual transaction summaries in: 

• 
Accounts Payable (AP) 

• 
Accounts Receivable (AR) 

You can also close periods in Cash Management. 

Closing Books 

All open books are automatically closed when you close books for a subsequent period. For 

example, suppose you have closed books for Q1, but not Q2. If you close the books for Q3, the 

books for Q2 are closed automatically. 

Closing the books should be a regular part of your period-end process. It prevents users from 

posting transactions to the wrong period and ensures that you can finalize your financials. 

Closing the books for a period also closes all of the summaries and Cash Management periods. 

When you close the books for a period, the system closes all open transaction summaries and the 

Cash Management period. If you need to make a change to a particular summary in A/P, A/R, or a 

period, you do not need to re-open all the books for that period. You can re-open only the 

application subledger you need. 

By subledger, we mean all transactions in a given application. For example, in Accounts Payable, 
this includes not only the A/P invoice and adjustment summaries users can directly access, but 
invisible transactions that involve payments or even inter-entity transfers. 

Suppose you have different staff for A/P and A/R. Your procedure is to stop writing checks as you 

approach your monthly closing of the books, and then close down the A/P books while leaving 

the A/R clerks free to continue entering invoices and payments. First, close all of the books, and 

then re-open the A/R subledger.  

To re-open A/R: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Month End section, click Open Books. 

3. 
In the Open Books page, select the Open Accounts Receivable check box. 

---


<!-- Page 530 -->
Books 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Permissions 

Because the permissions check boxes for the Close/Open Books pages in G/L, Close/Open 

Subledger in A/P, A/R, and Close/Open Periods in Cash Management are separate, you can assign 

different staff to different tasks.  

For example, an A/P supervisor might have permissions to close and open A/P summaries, but 

only the Accounting Manager has permissions to close books and open books in the G/L. While 

this is useful in a stand-alone company, it is even more useful in a shared structure of multiple 

companies. Users in the top-level company have control over the entities directly from the top 

level, and do not need to slide into the entities to close books or open them. More specifically, 

they can open the books for all entities or a single entity, and open specific subledgers in the 

selected entities. In other words, the top-level user can open one subledger in one entity to make 

a change without exposing other subledgers in that entity or any subledgers in any other entities. 


> **Navigation Path:** `You open and close books with the General Ledger > All > Month End > Open Books and Close`


Books options.

Close Books Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Month End > Books > Close`


Use the Close Books page to select the ending period for which you want to close the books. 

After books are closed, you cannot post transactions in any application for any date older than 

the end of the selected period. 

Closing the books is a way to prevent transactions from being posted to prior periods. The system 

retains all of your transaction detail at all times.  

For example, after your annual audit is completed and the audit adjusting entries are posted, you 

close the books to prevent anyone from posting additional transactions to the already-audited 

fiscal year. If you need to post adjusting entries after your books are closed, you may use the 

adjustment journal to do so at any time. 

To make a change to a closed book, create an adjusting entry (on page 316 ). 

Finding Which Periods Are Closed 

If you need to determine which months or periods are closed, open the Close books page. 

Because closing one period closes all prior periods, there can’t be any unclosed books before the 

last closed date. The Close company books from field shows you the date that the company 

books were last closed.

### Opening and Closing Summaries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 541*

Opening and Closing Summaries 

Open and close summaries with the Open Subledger and Close Subledger menu options 

available on the following application menus: 

• 
Accounts Payable 

• 
Accounts Receivables 

Closing Summaries 

You can close all summaries in a period or individually by summary name, provided the books are 

still open for the period in question. When a summary is closed, you cannot post transactions to 

that summary unless you reopen it. 

When closing summaries in A/P and A/R, select To the end of period, to close both A/P invoice 

(or A/R invoice) summaries and adjusting summaries. To close a specific invoice or adjusting 

summary, select that summary from the Close Summary drop-down list. 

Open summaries that have not been closed are NOT automatically closed when you close 

summaries for a subsequent period. For example, suppose you have closed summaries for Q1, but 

not Q2. If you close summaries for Q3, Q2 remains open. 

Opening Summaries 

You can open previously closed summaries either by period or by summary name. After a 

summary is opened, you can again post transactions to that summary. If you opened a closed 

summary to post a single transaction, remember to close it again immediately so that users 

cannot inadvertently post additional transactions to that summary. 

Open and close periods with the application > All > Subledger options.

### Close Periods and Open Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 542*

Books 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Close Periods and Open Periods 

Close Periods 

Closing periods is analogous to closing summaries as described previously, except that Cash 

Management does not have summaries. Consequently, you close periods so users cannot create 

or change transactions in the Cash Management application for the period in question. If you 

need to make a change to a closed period, reopen first via Subledger menu option. 

You can close open periods for the Cash Management application independently of other 

applications. The books for the period must be open for the period in which you want to close a 

Cash Management period. 

Open Cash Management periods that have not been closed are NOT automatically closed when 

you close a subsequent period. For example, say you have closed the period for Q1, but not Q2. If 

you close the period for Q3, Q2 remains open. 

Open Periods- 

You can open closed periods for the Cash Management application independently of other 

applications. To create or change transactions in the Cash Management application, you must first 

re-open the books for that period. You can open one or more periods by choosing the 

appropriate value in the To the end of period drop-down list on the Open Periods page. 

Closing Books for the Year 

General Ledger closing for the year is essentially the same process as closing any other period. 

Prerequisite 

For fiscal years that match calendar years, the reporting period is created for you. For fiscal years 

that operate in a different range, create the reporting period first. For example, if your fiscal year 

runs from March through February, create a reporting period named Fiscal year ending 2019 to 

include the full period.  


> **Navigation Path:** `To create a new reporting period, go to General Ledger > Setup > More > Reporting periods.`


Closing the Books 

1. 
Close any transactions in subledgers for the appropriate year ending period. 

2. 
As needed, close subledgers (or summaries) for Accounts Payable (AP), Accounts Receivable 

(AR), and Cash Management. 

3. 
Close the books using the year-end reporting period for the year you’re closing. 

---



### Workflow: Closing Out an Accounting Year
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 543*

Chapter 19: Books 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Workflow: Closing Out an Accounting Year 

You can use the RealPage Financial Suite Financial Close Management application to assist with a 

year-end close. The Financial Close Management application is available for an extra cost.  

If your company does not own the Financial Close Management application, then you can close 

the year by following these steps: 

1. 
Complete All Transactions 

• 
Post all invoices and journal entries. 

• 
Ensure all modules (A/P, A/R, G/L, Cash Management) are up to date. 

2. 
Reconcile Accounts 

• 
Bank accounts, credit cards, intercompany balances. 

• 
Use the Bank Reconciliation menu option to confirm ending balances match 

statements. 

3. 
Review Financial Reports 

• 
Run and review: 

• 
Trial Balance 

• 
General Ledger 

• 
Income Statement 

• 
Balance Sheet 

• 
Look for anomalies or unposted entries. 

4. 
Post Adjusting Entries 

• 
Record depreciation, accruals, prepaid expenses, and other year-end adjustments. 

• 
Use Journal Entries with proper documentation. 

5. Close Subledgers 

• 
Close A/P, A/R, and other subledgers for the year. This prevents new entries from 

being backdated. 

6. Close the General Ledger 

• 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select Close Books. 

• 
Select the fiscal year and confirm all periods are closed. 

The system rolls forward balances and locks the year. 

7. Lock the Period 

Use permissions to restrict edits to closed periods. This ensures audit integrity and prevents 

accidental changes. 

---


<!-- Page 544 -->
Books 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

8. Archive and Backup 

Save copies of key reports and supporting documents. The system retains audit trails, but 

external backups are good practice.

User-Defined Books List

Use this list when you have different reporting standards that you need to manage (beyond GAAP 

and tax books) to create and name your own custom reporting books. User-defined books are 

most commonly used to track specialized adjustments to your normal, operational books; 

however, you can use them for any purpose that you want. 

With user-defined books, you can: 

• 
Create your own reporting books. For example, a property management firm might create a 

real estate book. 

• 
Enter transactions in your books as needed. 

• 
Generate a multitude of reports that represent the reporting books you want to see, in any 

combination. 

Purpose of User-Defined Books 

To understand the benefit of user-defined books, let’s start with the end in mind. Decide what 

you need to track and report on.  

Following is a sample report from a property management company that needs to report on real 

estate-specific adjustments. For maximum flexibility, the firm needs to be able to report on any 

particular book alone, or in combination with other books.

### Setting Up User-Defined Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 550*

Books 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up User-Defined Books 

User-defined books give you a way to manage different reporting standards, beyond what’s 

available with GAAP and Tax books. When it’s enabled in the General Ledger, you can create one 

or more reporting books that you use to track specialized journal entries that are separate from 

your normal, operational books. For example, a property management firm might create a Real 

Estate book for tracking and reporting on journal entries specific to that industry. 

This topic walks you through the process of setting up user-defined books, from enabling it in the 

General Ledger to defining books and journals. If you’re new to user-defined books, we 

recommend that you start with our introduction, User-defined books (on page 532). 

Step 1: Enable User-Defined Books in the General Ledger 

Start by enabling user-defined books in the General Ledger. When you enable the User-defined 

books feature on the General ledger configuration page, additional fees may apply. 

To enable user-defined books: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab.  

2. 
Select the Configuration option. 

3. 
Find the Advanced G/L options section, and then select the option to Enable user-defined 

books. Select the Enable user-defined books check box. 

After you enable user-defined books, RealPage adds two new lists for User-Defined Books

Including or Excluding the Main Reporting Book 

By default, amounts from the main reporting book are included to create a combined amount. 

However, there are times when you might want to clear this option. For example, suppose that 

your GAAP adjustments equal $-1,000 and the accrual amount is $10,000.00.  

What you want to see in the column determines whether to include or exclude the main reporting 

book.  

• 
To see just the GAAP adjustments, include only the GAAP book and exclude the Accrual 

book (the main reporting book).  

The resulting figure is $-1,000.  

• 
To see the GAAP and accrual amount combined, include both the GAAP and Accrual books.  

The resulting figure is $9,000.

Configuration 

Before you can create a budget, several items in RealPage Accounting must be set up:

Budgetable reporting periods  

Reporting periods must exist and must be marked as Budgetable. Most often, budgetable 

periods are monthly. Additionally, budgetable reporting periods can’t overlap. For example, 

in a given year it is not possible to mark reporting periods for January, February, March, and

Dimensions

more about planning a budget with dimensions (on page 551).

### Plan Your Budgets
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 561*

Chapter 20: Budgets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Plan Your Budgets 

Budgets are powerful tools that you can use in financial planning and reporting. Many reports and 

dashboards in the system include budget information that help you monitor your business’s 

progress over the course of a year, and compare actual results against your forecasted results.  

Because budgets can be used in many areas of the system, including your financial reporting, you 

should do a little planning before you create your budget. How you set up your budget impacts 

the detail you can view in reports. Furthermore, you can minimize the need to edit financial 

reports that use budget data by carefully considering how you set up your budgets, including 

how you intend to manage the frequency of budget updates and how you prepare them. Most 

importantly, you should consider the following when planning your budgets: 

• 
Reporting periods 

• 
How often you expect to update the budget 

• 
Number of budgets you are using 

Additionally, many organizations use Spend Management to enforce spending validation against 

budgets, which requires additional configuration and thought as to how you want to validate your 

expenses.  

Prerequisites  

Before you can create a budget, several items must be set up in the system:  

• 
Budgetable reporting periods: Reporting periods must exist and must be marked as 

Budgetable. Most often, budgetable periods are monthly. Additionally, budgetable 

reporting periods can’t overlap. For example, in a given year it is not possible to mark 

reporting periods for January, February, March, and the First Quarter as “Budgetable” 

because those periods overlap.  

• 
Accounts: Each account for which you want to create a budget must exist in the Chart of 

Accounts. 

• 
Dimensions: Although using dimensions in budgets isn’t required, dimensions such as 

Location or Department can be included in a budget only if they have been created in the 

system. 

---



#### Reporting Periods with Budgets
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 562*



#### Multiple Budgets
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 562*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reporting Periods with Budgets 

Budgets are typically created for reporting periods of one month. The monthly reporting period 

will let you roll up individual months to create quarterly, semiannual, and annual reports.  

It’s possible to create a budget for reporting periods that are shorter or longer than a month, as 
long as the reporting period is marked as Budgetable. 

Depending on how you set up your budgets, you might not need to create a new budget for each 

year. Because there is no limit to the number of reporting periods that can be included in a 

budget, you can add reporting periods to your budgets and retain data from the previous year. 

Adding reporting periods to an existing budget can minimize the need to edit financial reports 

later.  

Multiple Budgets 

Many companies develop an annual budget that remains untouched for the entire year. In this 

case, you can create a single budget that can be used for multiple years by adding reporting 

periods for each subsequent year to the existing budget.  

In contrast, some companies use multiple budgets in a fiscal year. This could be because the 

company wants to revise the budget throughout the year or consider multiple forecasts. If your 

company has a need for multiple budgets, consider that it will make the reporting process a bit 

more complicated. Since each financial report (such as an Actuals-to-budget report) refers to a 

specific budget, maintaining multiple budgets may require that you have multiple copies of 

financial reports.  

Even when using multiple budgets, you have options to support efficient reporting. 

---


<!-- Page 563 -->
Chapter 20: Budgets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Options for multiple budgets 

Multiple budgets and 

multiple copies of financial 

reports 

You can create multiple budgets with different Budget IDs, and 

then make copies of all financial reports that include budgets. 

After, edit each financial report to retrieve the desired budget 

ID. 

• 
Pros: Offers the greatest flexibility if using multiple 

budgets. Different reports can be run during a period to 

display different budgets. You can even run a single 

report that refers to multiple budgets.  

• 
Cons: Increases the number of financial reports in your 

company that have similar specifications, resulting in a 

larger list and perhaps requiring extra report 

management. 

One default budget and save 

copies of previous budgets 

for historical purposes 

You can save a copy of the original budget with a new Budget 

ID. With this option, you can still make changes to the default

For example, you may have a budget called Current budget that 

is used in your financial reports. When you want to revise the 

budget amounts, you could make a copy of Current budget and 

instead name it Old budget. After, you make the desired 

changes to Current budget, so that your reports reference this 

updated information. 

• 
Pros: Requires only one copy of your financial reports, 

since each report continues to reference the same 

budget ID.  

• 
Cons: You can only consider and report on a single 

budget at any given time.  

To save the original budget with a new name, follow the

#### Accounts with Budgets
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 564*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accounts with Budgets 

It’s possible to budget for both income statement and balance sheet accounts, although many 

companies include only income statement accounts in the budget.  

Income Statement Accounts 

Income statement accounts are reported as the activity for the reporting period, and can be 

described as for the period. The budget entry should be the budgeted activity for the period. For 

example, if the budget amount for an income statement account is 4 for January and 4 for 

February and 4 for March, the reported amount for the monthly period of March would be 4 and 

the amount for the first quarter would be 12. 

Balance Sheet Accounts 

The system reports balance sheet amounts as of a point in time, which can be described as 

cumulative balance as long as there’s a budget amount for each period. The budget entry for a 

period is the change in the balance sheet account. For example, if the ending budget account 

balance for January is 2 and the ending budget account balance for February is expected to be 6, 

the February budget amount is entered as 4. 

For balance sheet accounts, you must enter a budget amount for every period in order to keep a 
cumulative balance. If there’s no budget amount for a period, the system sees this as no budget, 
so there won’t be a cumulative amount. In this case, the budget amount isn’t carried forward 
from the last period. 

Statistical Accounts 

Statistical accounts can also be included in a budget, and can be defined as “for the period” or 

“cumulative” when they are created.  

• 
If the statistical account is defined as for the period, the budget amount should be entered 

as the change for the period. For example, suppose that a headcount account has an 

opening budget balance of 243. If you expect headcount to go up by 10 in a particular 

month, you would enter 10 as the budget amount. 

• 
If the statistical account is defined as cumulative, the budget amount should be entered as 

of ending balance. For example, if the headcount has an opening budget balance of 243 

and you expect the headcount to go up by 10, you would enter 253 as the budget amount. 

---

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Dimensions with Budgets 

Creating a budget using dimensions offers greater flexibility and detail in reporting. While using 

dimensions is optional, we strongly recommend including them in the budgets for your reporting 

purposes. For example, your company may want to compare budgeted expenses to actual 

expenses by location or department. If your budget doesn’t include those dimensions, you won’t 

be able to run this report. 

Similarly, your company may track revenue by salesperson using the Employee dimension. By 

budgeting for revenue including the Employee dimension, you can run reports comparing budget 

versus actual for each salesperson. 

Any dimension that is available in the General Ledger can be used with budgets.

#### Budgets with Mixed Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 566*



#### Using a Budget with Spend Management
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 566*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Budgets with Mixed Dimensions 

You can budget some accounts using dimensions and others by different dimensions or no 

dimensions. The level of detail is determined by your reporting needs. Each account can be 

budgeted at a different level of detail. The only requirements are that: 

• 
Each budget line must be assigned to a valid G/L account. 

• 
If a G/L account is defined as requiring a dimension, then the dimension must be used in 

the budget. 

If your actual amounts include dimensions, create the budget with dimensions to allow for 
comparison at the same level of detail.  

Using a Budget with Spend Management 

Many organizations use Spend Management to enforce spending validation against budgets, 

which requires additional configuration and thought as to how you want to validate your 

expenses. 

Budgets associated with Spend Management must have a value, even if the value is zero. Spend 

Management won’t include anything left blank for validation; the system assumes that you want 

to skip this spending validation for this account. However, when you want an account used for 

validation, and it has no budget amount, set the amount to 0.  

See Configuring Spend Management for information about setting up budget thresholds. 

See Viewing the budget for a transaction for information about how to view the budgeted 

amount for a transaction that you are entering.

Adding a Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks >

To add a new budget: 

1. 
On the Budget information page, fill in the Budget ID and Description fields. 

2. 
Select the way you want to create the budget: 

• 
To create a budget from scratch, select Create a new budget. 

• 
To create a budget that is based on another budget, select the Create a budget from 

existing budget and reporting period range option, and then select the budget that 

you want to base it on in the drop-down list. 

3. 
Add and change the budget data as needed. 

• 
If you selected Create a new budget, then you can add data to the budget by either 

entering budget amounts manually or by importing budget data (on page 559). 

• 
If you selected the Create a budget from existing budget and reporting period range 

option, review and change the budget amounts as needed. 

Creating a Budget Manually 

Manually creating a budget allows you to enter budget data for each account one by one, month 

by month. Manual budget creation is useful if you are adding budget data for only some of your 

accounts. 

Step 1: Create a new budget and give it a unique Budget ID 

Before you can upload a budget spreadsheet or manually enter budget data, you must first create 

the budget. 

1. 
Create a new budget and give it a Budget ID. Best practice is to give the budget an ID that 

doesn’t reference a particular fiscal year or date. Then you can append new time periods to 

your existing budget. 

2. 
Select Create a new budget. 

3. 
If this is to be a consolidated budget, enable the check box and enter a consolidated 

currency. 

4. 
If this is the default budget to use, enable the check box by that feature. 

Step 2: Add budget information for your accounts  

After you’ve created and named your budget, you’re ready to add budget data for your accounts. 

When you’re manually adding budget data, you can enter data for only one account at a time.  

---


<!-- Page 570 -->
Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you’re tracking budget data at the dimension level, such as tracking data for different 
departments and locations, you’ll need to add multiple entries for each account. For example, if 
you are entering Travel Expense data for three locations, you’ll need three entries for this 
account. 

To enter budget information for an account: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Budgets. 

3. 
Click the Budget details link for the budget. 

4. 
Click the Add button. 

5. 
On the Budget amount details page, add general information about the budget for the 

account. 

• 
Select the Account for which you’re entering budget data. 

• 
Optionally, select dimensions for your budget data. For example, if you are entering 

budget data for a particular location, select the Location.  

6. 
Use Periods from date and Periods to date to select reporting periods for the budget 

period you are creating. You can select a single period or a range of periods. 

7. 
Click the Show periods button to display the reporting periods. 

When you click Show periods, the page refreshes to display both the reporting periods you 

can include in the budget and the fields for entering individual amounts. 


> **Navigation Path:** `If no reporting periods display when you click Show periods, go to General Ledger > Setup`


> More > Reporting periods. For the reporting period to use, click Edit to display the 

Reporting Period Information page, and select the Use for budgeting check box.  

8. 
Enter budget amounts for the reporting periods. (See the next section.) 

Step 3: Enter budget amounts 

There are two methods to assign a budget amount to a reporting period. You can enter the 

amounts manually or you can have the amounts computed for you. 

Option 1: Enter amounts manually  

1. 
Select the check box to the left of the Reporting period to activate it. 

2. 
Type amounts into the Budget amount fields for each budget period. 

3. 
Optionally add a note about the budget or budget amount. 

4. 
After the data has been entered for this account, click Save. 

---


<!-- Page 571 -->
Chapter 20: Budgets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Option 2: Automatically calculate budget data based on amounts from a past period  

1. 
Select the period you want to use as the starting point for the calculation from the Past 

periods drop-down list. 

2. 
Select a method from the Based on drop-down list. You can choose to base the calculation 

on Actual data or Budget data.  

The choices are described below. 

• 
Actuals: This option retrieves the actual amount for the selected past period. The 

system calculates budget values by changing the actual value for the selected past 

period by the amount or percentage entered in the Grow by field. The Compute 

amount field is not required. 

• 
Budget: This option retrieves the budget amount for the selected past period. The 

system calculates budget values by changing the past period value by the amount or 

percentage entered in the Grow by field. The Compute amount field is not required. 

3. 
To add reporting periods to your budget, select the check box for the Reporting periods at 

the bottom of the page. 

4. 
Click the Compute button to calculate the amounts for the selected periods. 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

What’s Next? 

You can have the system warn users who are creating A/P invoices and purchase orders when the 

amount exceeds the budget. You can also have the system prevent users from creating 

transactions when the amount exceeds the budget (on page 584). 

You can also grant permissions to some users to allow them to bypass the budget check.

#### Creating a Budget by Modifying an Existing Budget
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 572*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Creating a Budget by Modifying an Existing Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Budgets`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Budgets`


Creating a new budget based on one that already exists is a quick way to get your budget process 

started.  

When you create a budget from one that already exists, you can include a range of reporting 

periods from the previous year, enabling you to replicate and retain a year’s worth of account 

budgets instantly. 

Before You Begin 

Before you can add data, create a new budget, and then give it a unique Budget ID. 

To create a budget based on an existing budget: 

1. 
In the Budgets list, locate the budget you want to use as the basis for your new budget and 

click the Export link. 

Exporting to a CSV retains the correct field IDs for upload. 

2. 
Update the CSV file using Microsoft Excel or other spreadsheet program. 

• 
Spreadsheet programs enable you to quickly replicate rows and columns, and even 

automatically change the data.  

• 
After the data in the Excel file is changed, it must be saved again as a CSV file. 

Be sure to update the Budget_ID column with the new Budget ID that you created in Step 
1. 

3.

#### Importing a Budget
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 573*

Chapter 20: Budgets

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Importing a Budget 

It’s often easiest to create a budget using Microsoft Excel or other spreadsheet program. Creating 

a budget in spreadsheet form allows you to upload large volumes of data. The spreadsheet can 

include all account and dimension combinations. 

For consolidated budgets, RealPage Accounting does not translate your budget from the entity 
base currency to the consolidated currency. You need to run a global consolidation to do the 
translation for the budget, and then upload the amount into RealPage Accounting.  

Permissions 

In general, the ability to import data requires permission to access the Import data option of the 

Company application’s Setup tab. This permission is required even if the import is performed 

outside of the Import data page. 

Workflow 

Uploading a budget from a spreadsheet is a multi-step process:  

1. 
Create a new budget (on page 560) in RealPage Accounting and give it a unique Budget ID. 

2. 
Download the budget template (on page 560) from the Import data page. 

3. 
Enter your budget data (on page 562) in the spreadsheet. 

The rows in your spreadsheet will refer to the Budget ID that you created in Step 1. 

4. 
Import the spreadsheet (on page 564). 

If you are uploading amounts for a consolidated budget, make sure the amounts are already 
converted into the consolidated currency using your company’s own exchange rate.

Downloading the Budget Template 

Preparing a budget for upload requires that you download the Budget template from the Import 

Data page.  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. You may have to scroll the menu to see this option. 

3. 
Find the Set up General Ledger Transactions section, and then click the Template link in the 

Budgets row. 

The asterisk (*) next to Budgets means that importing budget data updates existing budget 

records. 

4. 
Open the budget template in a spreadsheet application.  

About the Template 

The header line displays information about each field and the data that can be entered in it. 

Each horizontal row in the spreadsheet represents budget detail that combines a G/L account, 

optional dimension-level detail, and the budget amount for each reporting period. You will add a

row for every account and dimension combination that will be budgeted. Budget amounts are 

entered in the Reporting Period columns. 

You can use the budget template to add new budget detail or update existing details. If you 

already have a budget for an Account-Department-Location combination, and if you have the 

same combination in the file you import, the imported data overwrites the existing budget. 

Before you use the Budget template to upload budget data, create a new budget in the RealPage 

Accounting system to which you want to add data. The budget ID must exist before you can add 

it to the template. See Creating a New Budget and Giving It a Unique Budget ID (on page 560). 

Tips for Filling the Budget Template 

• 
BUDGET_ID must already exist in the system.  

• 
ACCT_NO is mandatory and refers to the account being budgeted. 

• 
DEPT_ID and LOCATION_ID are optional and can be empty. If you do use them, they must 

conform to valid IDs in RealPage Accounting. 

• 
Other dimensions are also optional. However, if a G/L account is defined as requiring a 

dimension, then the dimension must be used in the budget. 

• 
You can add any number of period columns for which you want budgets. To do so, those 

periods must already exist in the RealPage Accounting system and be budgetable periods, 

and the column headers must contain the names of those periods exactly as they appear in 

RealPage Accounting. In the field definitions that follow, this field is labeled (BUDGETABLE 

PERIOD 1...n). However, in your upload it would be something like “Month ended January 

2023.” If the period does not exist, the entire file is rejected, and the system sends you an 

email with the errors.
