#### Reasons Budgets Won’t Import
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 578*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing the Spreadsheet 

You can upload your completed budget spreadsheet.  

Before importing the budget, you must first save it in comma-separated value (.csv) 
format. 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to the Budgets list (General Ledger > All > Budget), and then click the Import button.`


2. 
On the Import page, browse to select the spreadsheet you previously created and then 

import it. Make sure that the email address on the import page is correct. 

• 
You will receive an email notification of upload success or failure.  

• 
If the upload fails, the email will have information regarding the errors.  

Reasons Budgets Won’t Import 

Budgets can fail to import for a number of reasons. Some of the most common reasons are: 

• 
A budget ID has not been created for the budget you’re importing. 

• 
Reporting periods haven’t been created for the budget you’re importing. 

• 
The reporting periods haven’t been set as budgetable. 

• 
The budget contains duplicate line items. 

• 
Budgets won’t import if they contain duplicate line items. 

• 
The budget import template hasn’t been correctly formatted. 

Before you import a budget 

Before you import your budget, make sure that you have done the following. 

Create a Budget ID 

Before importing a budget, use the General Ledger to create a Budget ID for the budget you plan 

to import. If you do not create the budget ID before an import, an error message occurs 

referencing an invalid Budget ID. After the new Budget ID has been created, you can then import 

your Budget Details. For more information, see Adding a budget (on page 555). 

Create reporting periods 

Create reporting periods before importing a budget. Reporting periods used in a budget must be 

marked as Use for Budgeting and can’t overlap with another reporting period. 

If the reporting period already exists, and you receive an error message when attempting to 

import, check your reporting period dates and the reporting period in your import file. The 

budgetable periods may be overlapping and causing an import error. 

---


<!-- Page 579 -->
Chapter 20: Budgets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Budgetable periods 

There can only be one budgetable reporting period per time frame. To mark a reporting period as 

budgetable or to verify that time frames are not overlapping, view the Reporting periods list and 

make changes, as necessary. 

To make a reporting period budgetable: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the More section, select the Reporting periods option. 

3. 
Click Edit next to the appropriate period in the list. 

4. 
Select the Use for budgeting box. 

5. 
Adjust the Start and End dates if needed. 

6. 
Click Save. 

Remove duplicate line items 

Line items that have the same dimensional values, but different budget amounts cannot be 

imported. 

For example, if you have two line items that have the same ACCT_NO, DEPT_ID, PROJECTID, and 

EMPLOYEEID, but different budget amounts, when the file is imported, you get Error BL05000161 

RealPage Accounting has no way of knowing which line contains the correct budget information. 

To avoid this error, delete duplicate line items, or ensure that all line items have different 

dimensional values. 

Best practices 

The following best practices will help you prepare your CSV file for upload. 

1. 
From the Import data page, download a template. 

• 
Use the latest template, especially following a product release. 

• 
Use the correct template for the area in which you want to upload information. 

Different templates organize different types of information. Use a template specifically 

for the information that you need to upload. 

2. 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to entering information. 

• 
Read the header descriptions in the template. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format 

or with an incorrect accepted value, it will cause an error in your upload. 

• 
Enter required information.

#### Deleting Budgets
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 586*

Deleting Budgets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Budgets > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Budgets > Delete`


It’s important to consider the implications of deleting a budget. After you delete a budget, you 

will no longer be able to use its data to create future budgets, and it can no longer be used in 

financial reports. 

You can delete any budget as long as it’s not being used by a financial report and it’s not the 

default budget. 

• 
A budget that is being used by a financial report can’t be deleted until you modify the 

report and remove the Budget ID. After the budget is no longer tied to the report, it can be 

deleted.  

• 
A default budget cannot be deleted. If you want to delete a budget marked as default, you 

must first assign another budget as the default budget. 

If you want a warning to appear before you attempt to delete a transaction, select the Warn on 

delete check box on the My preferences page. 

To delete a budget: 

1. 
Select the Budgets menu option. 

2. 
Locate the budget in the Budgets list, and then click the Delete link.

Troubleshooting Budget Import Errors 

There are several reasons why a budget upload might fail. The following are some of the common 

error messages you might encounter, with the steps to resolve them. 

Error 
Steps to resolve 

G/L account not valid 
Verify that you have entered the account number correctly and 

that the account has been created in the General Ledger. 

Duplicate budget 

accounts for a period 

Verify that only a single amount has been entered by period for 

each G/L account/dimension combination. 

For example, if you are budgeting by G/L account only, then you 

cannot have two rows for account 4010. If you are budgeting by 

account and dimension, then you cannot have amounts in two 

rows for the same account/dimension combination. 

Incorrect, not budgetable 

or missing reporting 

periods 

Verify that your reporting periods are correct and that the 

reporting periods are marked as budgetable. 

The reporting periods in your import file must exactly match the 

reporting periods in the system. 

To make a reporting period budgetable, edit the reporting period 

(on page 682), and then select the Use for budgeting option. 

The dates of periods selected for budgets cannot overlap. For 
example, you have two reporting periods: one includes January 1 
to January 31, and another includes January 15 to February 15. 
If you select the first to be used for budgeting, then you can’t 
select the second. 

Invalid budget ID 
Verify that the Budget ID has been created and that the value 

entered in the Budget_ID column exactly matches the Budget ID in 

the system.

Additional Rules for Department and Location 

Calculations are based on the combination of account, department, and location. In other 

words, if you specify the account 6020 Freight, the department Operations and the location 

California, the calculations are based on numbers only for that account and department 

combination that is also located in California.  

All children of parent departments and locations are included in the calculations. You might 

want to budget at the child level, and not budget at the parent level, for example. This 

enables you to track costs and revenues to budget, at a very detailed level. For this reason, 

we recommend that you plan your budget before you begin entering, such as preparing 

your budget first on a separate piece of paper or Excel spreadsheet, for faster entry into the 

system.

computed for you. 

9. 
To enter them manually, enter them into the End of period budget amount fields. 

To automatically compute budget amounts: 

1. 
Click the Past period drop-down list, and then select the monthly period to use. 

2. 
Select the desired method from the Based on drop-down list: 

• 
Actuals. Selecting Actuals retrieves the actuals for the selected period. You do not 

need to enter any information in the Compute amount field. 

• 
Budget. To base your budget on a fixed value, enter that amount in the Compute 

amount field. 

• 
Employee count. The number you enter in the Compute amount field is multiplied by 

the number of employees to populate the Budget amount field. The employee list is 

used in budgets so that budgets can be based on head count. More specifically, the 

calculation is performed from the start date to the end date of employment, which you 

can check via Company > Employees. A budget calculation based on head count 

retrieves data for all employees who were in active status during the selected period. 

Thus, it is important that your employee list be current if you plan to use this function 

in your budgeting process. 

3. 
Type a number in the Grow by field. This number can be a positive or negative (or zero) 

amount or a percentage. 

4. 
Select either the Percent or Amount option, depending on how you want the budget 

growth to be based. 

5. 
Type a starting amount in the Compute amount field. 

6. 
Select the check box of each line item to which you want to apply the results.

#### Setting Up a Budget Check As Part of Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 597*

Chapter 20: Budgets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Setting Up a Budget Check As Part of Approvals 

As part of the approval process, you can have the system check the default budget against the 

amount of a transaction to see if it will exceed the budget. The budget checks A/P invoices and 

purchase orders. You can either have the system prevent the user from creating an A/P invoice or 

purchase order that exceeds the budget or display a warning when the user tries to save the 

transaction that exceeds the budget. 

Configuring Budget Checking 

To allow the system to perform the budget checks: 

1. 
Open the Company application from the Applications menu.  

2. 
On the All tab, in the Approvals section, select Approval Configuration. 

3. 
To allow the system to prevent or warn users when they create an A/P invoice that exceeds 

the budgeted amount, go to the A/P invoice approvals section, and then select the Enable 

preventing or warning a user when adding an AP Invoice that exceeds the budget check 

box. 

4. 
In the Purchase Orders section, select the Enable preventing or warning a user when 

adding a Purchase Order that exceeds the budget check box. 

5. 
In the Budget Check section, the system uses the budget check Duration setting in the 

approval configuration to determine whether to use the amount budgeted for the current 

month, for the current year, or for the year-to-date.  

You can also assign a user permission to bypass budget check for one or both transaction types. 

---



#### Setting a System Action When a Transaction Exceeds the Budget
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 598*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting a System Action When a Transaction Exceeds the Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


Use this procedure to determine what happens when an A/P invoice or purchase order exceeds 

the budgeted amount.  

To set up the system action: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval Configuration menu option. 

The Approval configuration page opens. 

3. 
To enable the budget warning or prevention for A/P invoices: 

• 
Find the A/P Invoice Approvals section. 

• 
Select the Enable preventing or warning a user when adding an AP Invoice that 

exceeds the budget check box. 

• 
To have the system display a warning message that the user is about to exceed the 

budgeted amount by posting an invoice, select Warn. 

• 
To have the system prevent the user from posting the invoice, select Prevent. The 

system both prevents the invoice from posting and displays the warning message. 

4. 
To enable the budget warning or prevention for purchase orders: 

• 
Find the Purchase orders section. 

• 
Select the Enable preventing or warning a user when adding a Purchase Order that 

exceeds the budget check box. 

• 
To have the system display a warning message that the user is about to exceed the 

budgeted amount by the purchase order, select Warn. 

• 
To have the system prevent the user from posting the purchase order, select Prevent. 

The system both prevents the purchase order from posting and displays the warning 

message. 

5. 
Find the Budget check section, and then review the Default duration setting: 

• 
Current month: Select this option to use the amount budgeted for the G/L account for 

the current posting month. 

• 
Current year: Select this option to use the amount budgeted for the G/L account for 

the current posting year. 

• 
Current year through current month: Select this option to use the amount budgeted 

for the G/L account for the year to date. 

6. 
Click Save.

### Budget Data
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 600*



#### Viewing Account and Budget Details
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 600*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Budget Data 

You can use RealPage Accounting to import budget data or enter budget data manually. 

Viewing Account and Budget Details 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Budgets > Budget Details > View`


Any accounts that you want to track the budget for must be added to the budget before they 

appear in the list. If you want to track different dimension combinations, those must be added 

separately to the list. 

If you don’t see the Budget option on the General Ledger menu, see your administrator to add it 
to your application. 

Accounts can be either G/L accounts or statistical accounts. Normal G/L accounts are dollars. 

Statistical accounts are units. Statistical accounts enable you to create computations. For example, 

you could budget your head count, and then perform computations based on the actual number 

of employees. The actual number of employees would be a statistical function. 

When used in income statements, statistical accounts are cumulative. That is, January, February 

and March all have ten. If you do a quarterly budget, the budget is 30. However, if you are using 

the account in a balance sheet, the ending balance is used, which would be ten in this case. 

To view details about a budget for an account: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select the General Ledger option, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Budgets. The Budgets list opens. 

3. 
In the Budgets list, click Budget details to display the Budget details list to see all of the 

budgets assigned to a particular account. 

4. 
In the row with the account to view, click View. The Budget Account Information page 

opens to show the details about the budgeting for the account, dimensions for the account, 

the periods for the budget, and the budget amount for that account for each period. 

You can view details about a specific budget, edit an existing one, or create a new one.

#### Modifying Budget Data
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 601*

Chapter 20: Budgets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Modifying Budget Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets > Budget Details > 
Budgets > Edit`


You have several options when it comes to modifying your budget data. The best way to modify 

your budget data depends on two aspects: 

• 
How much modification is needed for your budget 

• 
The year of the budget you want to modify 

Modifying Budget Data for the Current Fiscal Year 

If you have a budget overage, an update to your budget, or perhaps you want to update your 

budget to reflect your actuals more accurately. There are two options for modifying budget data 

for the current fiscal year. 

• 
Edit a couple of numbers  

• 
Revise several numbers 

Editing a Couple of Numbers 

Maybe you forgot to add a budget for an account, or maybe you entered the data wrong for two 

accounts. Whatever the case, you can easily update your budget for these accounts from within 

RealPage Accounting. 

When you modify budget data in RealPage Accounting, you can modify only one account at a time. 
For this reason, we recommend this method only if you have a couple of accounts to edit at 
most. 

To modify budget data: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select the Budgets option. 

3. 
Find the budget you want to change, and then click the Budget details link. 

4. 
Find the account for which you want to adjust the budget, and then click Budgets. At least 

one account must be marked as budgetable. If no accounts are assigned as budgetable, you 

might not see any accounts listed. 

You can filter on Account to quickly find the account you want to modify.  

5. 
Click the Edit button in the upper-right corner to edit the budget over multiple reporting 

periods for this account.  

6. 
Make any changes, and then click Save. 

7. 
Repeat these steps for any other numbers you want to change in your budget. 

---


<!-- Page 602 -->
Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Revising Several Numbers 

To make more significant changes to your budget data, it’s best to export the budget, and then 

manipulate the budget data in Microsoft Excel. In Excel, you can change numbers across all 

accounts and reporting periods, and then upload the revised budget one time. 

Before you do this, we recommend that you make a copy of the original budget in RealPage 

Accounting first to retain a historical reference. After you have a copy, you can make your 

changes to the original budget, which will be used in any actual-to-budget financial report you 

have already created, since the budget ID remains the same. 

To create a budget by copying an existing budget: 

1. 
From the Applications list, select General ledger, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
Select the 
 Budgets option. 

3. 
Enter a Budget ID and Description. 

When copying a budget, the best practice is to use a naming convention that represents 
the original budget for the specified fiscal year. 

4. 
Select the Create a budget from existing budget and reporting period range option. 

5. 
In the drop-down list below, select the budget you want to copy. 

6. 
In the two new fields, ensure that the reporting period range is the one you want to copy. 

7. 
Save your budget. 

Exporting and Revising a Budget 

To export and revise a budget: 

1. 
From the Applications list, select General ledger, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
Select the Budgets option. 

---


<!-- Page 603 -->
Chapter 20: Budgets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

3. 
Click the Export link on the same row as the budget you want to revise. 

4. 
Specify your Start period and End period. 

Only select reporting periods that you want to revise to ensure that other budget data 
remains unchanged. 

5. 
In the Filters section, verify that: 

• 
The specified Budget is the one you want to revise. 

• 
The Display notes check box is selected to include a column about the budget notes. 

6. 
In the Format section, verify that the CSV importable format check box is selected so that 

your dimension values are exported without totals. 

7. 
Click Export and then select CSV. 

8. 
Download the file. 

9. 
Open the file to revise your budget data in Excel. When you’re done, save your changes, and 

then import your budget data into RealPage Accounting.  

Be careful when you import budget data back into RealPage Accounting. The system 
overwrites the budget amounts for all accounts, dimensions, and reporting periods 
included in the budget import file. 

Appending Budget Data for the Next Fiscal Year 

You can append budget data for the next fiscal year onto your current budget so that there are 

no disruptions in your reporting.  

Create a new budget import file that uses the existing Budget ID, but includes the next fiscal year 

of reporting periods. Adjust the numbers per account per reporting period, save the file, and then 

import it into the system to append the data.

### Consolidated Budgets and Financial Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 612*



#### Adding a Consolidated Budget
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 612*

Budgets 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Consolidated Budgets and Financial Reports 

To select a consolidated budget in a financial report, the budget must be tagged as consolidated, 

and the currency must match the consolidation book selected on the Filters tab of the Financial 

Report Writer. 

Adding a Consolidated Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Budgets`


Consolidated budgets are useful for tracking your annual plan and forecasts and comparing them 

side-by-side in any financial report. For example, if you consolidate into Euros, you might create 

one or more budgets where budget amounts are entered in Euros (EUR). This allows for 

side-by-side comparison between actual and budget amounts in the same financial report. 

Before You Begin 

• 
The Global Consolidation application must be enabled to create a consolidated budget. 

• 
Be sure to convert your local budget from the entity-level currency into your consolidated 

currency and then upload amounts to your consolidated budget. 

To add a consolidated budget: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add button next to Budgets. The Budget information page opens. 

3. 
In the Budget ID field, type a unique identifier for the new budget. The budget ID you 

provide is the one that you will reference on financial reports, such as an “actual to budget” 

report. To upload budgets, you must have an existing Budget ID. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description of the purpose of the budget. 

The description you provide appears only in the Budgets list to help you identify the correct 

budget. It is especially useful when you have several budgets with similar names, but you 

can also make notes that point out the differences between similar budgets and other 

comments about the budget. 

5. 
Select one of the following: 

•

Additional Rules for Department and Location 

Calculations are based on the combination of account, department, and location. In other 

words, if you specify the account 6020 Freight, the department Operations and the location 

California, the calculations are based on numbers only for that account and department 

combination that is also located in California.  

All children of parent departments and locations are included in the calculations. You might 

want to budget at the child level, and not budget at the parent level, for example. This 

enables you to track costs and revenues to budget, at a very detailed level. For this reason, 

we recommend that you plan your budget before you begin entering, such as preparing 

your budget first on a separate piece of paper or Excel spreadsheet, for faster entry into the 

system.

value.

These dates represent the period for which you are preparing the budget. Typically, this 

covers a fiscal or calendar year.

More > Reporting periods. For reporting period to use, click Edit to display the Reporting 

period information page, and then select the Use for budgeting check box. 

If the period has been selected for use in another existing budget combination of reporting 
period, account, department, and location, it is not saved. An error message appears 
informing you that it is already in use. 

18. 
Click the Select check box for the reporting periods to add to your budget, and then assign 

budget amounts to those periods. You can either enter the amounts manually or have them 

computed for you. 

19. 
To enter them manually, enter them into the End of period budget amount fields. 

To automatically compute budget amounts: 

1. 
Click the Past period drop-down list, and then select the monthly period to use. 

2. 
Select the desired method from the Based on drop-down list: 

• 
Actuals. Selecting Actuals retrieves the actuals for the selected period. You do not 

need to enter any information in the Compute amount field. 

• 
Budget. To base your budget on a fixed value, enter that amount in the Compute 

amount field. 

• 
Employee count. The number you enter in the Compute amount field is multiplied by 

the number of employees to populate the Budget amount field. The employee list is 

used in budgets so that budgets can be based on head count. More specifically, the 

calculation is performed from the start date to the end date of employment, which you 

can check via Company > Employees. A budget calculation based on head count 

retrieves data for all employees who were in active status during the selected period. 

Thus, it is important that your employee list be current if you plan to use this function 

in your budgeting process.

How to Create a Budget Report with the Financial Report Writer 

To create a new financial report: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select the General Ledger option. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add button next to Financial Reports. 

Create the Report Overview 

There are four basic steps for creating this type of report: 

1. 
Select your basic report structure (on page 603) on the Report Info tab. 

• 
For this type of report, choose Accounts on rows in the Report structure section. Then 

select the option to Filter by dimension structure on rows. 

2. 
Add account groups to your report rows (on page 604). 

Your account groups organize your accounts into hierarchies, allowing you to reflect how 

you report on assets, expenses, liabilities, and more. In this example, we’re adding an 

Expenses (total) account group. 

3. 
Filter the account groups by dimension structure (on page 604) and set the detail level. 

This is where you add your custom analysis. You can create any number of re-usable 

dimension structures that correspond to how you want to slice and dice your data. 

In this example, we’re using dimension structures to filter expenses by location, but this 

technique can be used to create any type of analysis. 

4. 
Create columns for different reporting periods (on page 605). Add columns for actual, 

budget, and budget difference variance. 

Select Your Report Structure 

Step 1. Select your report structure 

When you create a new financial report, the Report Info tab of the Financial Report Writer asks 

you to select a basic report structure. Based on your selection, the remaining tabs update to help 

you create that type of report. 

To select your report structure: 

1. 
Create a new financial report. 

2. 
On the Report Info tab, name your report. 

3. 
In the Report structure section of the Report Info tab, select the option for Accounts on 

report rows. 

4. 
Select the option to Filter by dimension structure.

Adding Account Groups to Your Report Rows 

Step 2. Add account groups to your report rows 

In this example, separate account groups are added for Revenue and Expenses. In each case, the 

account group is collapsed to hide any subgroups. 

To add rows: 

1. 
On the Rows tab, click the Select account groups button.

and Expenses.

example, you might want to show Assets, Liabilities, or Accounts Payable. 

When you’re done adding the two groups, the Rows tab is updated to show Revenue and 

Expenses with any subgroups indented underneath.

Filtering Account Groups by Dimension Structure and Set the Detail Level 

Step 3. Filter account groups by dimension structure and set the detail level 

While still on the Rows tab, you’ll filter each account group by different dimension structures in 

this case, by dimension structures that represent all customers and all projects. You’ll then set the 

Detail level to show individual customers and projects. 

Dimension report structures are named structures that are created for the purpose of adding 

dimensions to the rows or columns of a financial report. You can add any number of report 

structures for the dimensions you track, including structures for locations, departments, 

customers, vendors, projects, or even user-defined dimensions. 

To filter the rows: 

1. 
If necessary, create the Customer structure and Project structure that you need for filtering. 

This example report uses two dimension structures: 

• 
A Customer structure that contains a single group whose members are all customers. 

• 
A Project structure that contains a single group whose members are all projects. 

2. 
Set the dimension filter for the Revenue row. 

• 
Locate the Revenue row and click the Filter by dimension structure column. 

• 
On the Set dimension structure page, select Customers as the dimension and then 

select the dimension structure that represents all customers.

#### Variations of the Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 620*

Budgets

Variations of the Report 

By changing the dimension structures that you use in columns, you can easily adjust this report to 

any dimension and any type of analysis that you want to perform. 

For example, you might create dimension structures that enable you to look at: 

• 
All customers, customers of a particular type, or a specific set of key customers. 

• 
Items in the same product line or a particular set of items (such as your top-tier items). 

• 
Projects by type or projects that have the same manager. 

Control which dimension members are included 

In many cases, you don’t want to include all customers or projects. Based on the analysis you’re 

trying to create, you might only want to see particular members, or members that meet certain 

filter criteria. 

For example, you might want to see only your Direct customers or only Training projects. These 

types of dimension structures can be created by including a group that uses filters to select 

members. 

Examine an account group by two different dimensions 

You can also examine an account group by two different dimensions. In this case, revenue is 

shown only for direct customers, with detail by project. 

This type of hierarchy can only be displayed for account groups that contain individual accounts 
(for example, Revenue-Sales but not Revenue). See the instructions below for more details. 

To create this type of analysis in report rows: 

1. 
Create a hierarchical dimension structure.  

2. 
On the Rows tab, add your account groups. 

3. 
Locate the row where you want to add your hierarchical breakdown. 

This row must contain an account group that either contains individual accounts or that 
selects accounts based on their category. 

4. 
Click the Filter by dimension structure column for the account group and select your 

hierarchical dimension structure. 

5. 
In the same row, click the Detail level column and set the detail level to show the dimension 

structure. 

• 
Set the Detail level to Summary - hide accounts. 

• 
Select the option to Expand by dimension, and then select Dimension structure as 

the expand by option.

Controlling Which Dimension Members Are Included 

In many cases, you don’t want to include all customers or projects. Based on the analysis you’re 

trying to create, you might only want to see particular members, or members that meet certain 

filter criteria. 

For example, you might want to see only your Direct customers or only Training projects. These 

types of dimension structures (on page 676) can be created by including a group that uses filters 

to select members.  

Examine an Account Group by Two Different Dimensions 

You can also examine an account group by two different dimensions, as with the following 

example. In this case, revenue is shown only for only direct customers, with detail by location. 

To create this type of analysis in report rows: 

1. 
On the Rows tab, add the Revenue account group (or another account group). 

2. 
Click the Filter by dimension structure column for the account group and filter it by 

dimension structure. 

3. 
In this case, revenue is being filtered for direct customers. However, you could choose any 

account group and then filter it by any dimension structure. 

4. 
In the same row, click the Detail level column and expand by location (or another dimension 

of your choice). 

To do this: 

1. 
Set the Detail level to Summary - hide accounts. 

2. 
Select the option to Expand by dimension. 

3. 
From the Dimension drop-down list, choose Location as the expand by option.

Using a Hierarchical Structure for More Complex Analysis on Rows 

You can also organize dimension structures into hierarchies, which gives you more options for 

organizing dimension data.  

Suppose you want a report that shows customers by type, subdivided between direct and channel 

customers. You can set up a hierarchical Customers by type structure with two substructures that 

each filter for customers of a particular type (direct or channel). 

This type of hierarchy can only be displayed for account groups that contain individual accounts 
(for example, Revenue-Sales but not Revenue). See the following instructions for more details. 

To create this type of analysis in report rows: 

1. 
Create a hierarchical dimension structure. 

2. 
On the Rows tab, add your account groups. 

3. 
Locate the row where you want to add your hierarchical breakdown. 

This row must contain an account group that either contains individual accounts or that 
selects accounts based on their category. 

4. 
Click the Filter by dimension structure column for the account group and select your 

hierarchical dimension structure. 

5. 
In the same row, click the Detail level column and then set the detail level to show the 

dimension structure. 

• 
Set the Detail level to Summary - hide accounts. 

• 
Select the option to Expand by dimension, then select Dimension structure as the 

expand by option.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Budget Variance Analysis > Periods > Open New

When you open a new budget variance analysis (BVA) analysis period, the system initiates the 

account group specified to be run against the variance rules defined, notifies users that the period 

is open, and allows users to begin making comments. 

You can open a BVA period either at the top level or at an entity level.

the budget variance analysis feature.

Budget Variance Periods Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periods > Open New Analysis Period`


Use this page to open an analysis period by specifying the year and period (month or quarter) of 

the year you want to open. 

To save time, you can close all the prior periods as you open a new budget variance period.  

Configurations refers to the Budget Variance Configuration rules (on page 672) that the 

administrator set up in the General Ledger Setup tab. You can open a period using one or more 

Budget Variance Configuration rule sets. 

Closing an Analysis Period 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periods`


To close an analysis period, your account must have permissions to configure the budget 
variance analysis feature. See Before You Begin (on page 610 ). 

To close an analysis period report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks column, in the Budget Variance Analysis section, select Periods. The 

Budget Variance Analysis Locations by Period list opens. 

3. 
Select the check boxes of the period reports that you want to close. 

4. 
Click the Analysis period button, and then select Close. 

Reopening an Analysis Period 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periods`


To re-open an analysis period, your account must have permissions to configure the budget 
variance analysis feature. See Before You Begin (on page 610 ). 

To re-open a closed analysis period report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks column, in the Budget Variance Analysis section, select Periods. The 

Budget Variance Analysis Locations by Period list opens. 

3. 
Select the check boxes of the period reports that you want to re-open. 

4. 
Click the Analysis period button, and then select Reopen.

Deleting an Analysis Period 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periods`


Be sure to close any period reports before attempting to delete them. 

To delete an analysis period, your account must have permissions to configure the budget 
variance analysis feature. See Before You Begin (on page 610 ). 

To delete an analysis period report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks column, in the Budget Variance Analysis section, select Periods. The 

Budget Variance Analysis Locations by Period list opens. 

3. 
Select the check boxes of the analysis period reports that you want to delete.

Refreshing Budget Variance Analysis Users 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periods > Analysis Period > Refresh Users`


Users who are flagged as budget variance analysis (BVA) users can view the open period and 

location. When you flag a user as a BVA user after the period opens, use the Refresh users option 

to allow recent BVA users to view the open period and location. 

To refresh budget variance analysis users: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks column, in the Budget Variance Analysis section, select Periods. The 

Budget Variance Analysis Locations by Period list opens. 

3. 
Click the Analysis Period button, and then select Refresh Users.  

Recently flagged BVA users can now view the open budget variance analysis period.

Checking the Status of Budget Variance Analyses 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Budget Variance Analysis > Periods > Incomplete`


When a Budget Variance report’s analysis is not yet complete, you can check the status to see who 

has not completed their review. You can then either send the user a reminder or mark the analysis 

complete on their behalf. 

To check the status of a property’s budget variance analysis: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select General Ledger, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks column, in the Budget Variance Analysis section, select Periods.  

3. 
Find the Budget Variance Analysis that you want to report to check.

Click the Incomplete link. The Budget Period Location list opens to show the users who 

have not completed their analyses. From here, you can: 

• 
Send the user a reminder to complete their analysis.  

• 
Click the Mark Complete link to mark the user’s comments as complete on their 

behalf.

Creating a Journal Entry from a Budget Variance Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Budget Variance Analysis > 
Periods > Create JE`


After displaying a Budget Variance report, you can create a journal entry for any line that needs 

one. 

Requirements 

• 
Only users who have the Add permission for Journal Entries can see the Create JE link.  

• 
The Create JE link appears only after the period has been closed.  

To create a journal entry: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section of the menu, find the Budget variance analysis section, and then 

click Periods. 

3. 
Identify the G/L account for which you want to create a journal entry. 

4. 
Click the Create JE link. The Journal Entries page opens in a new browser window. 

5. 
Fill in the journal entry (on page 242) record and then click Post to post it to the general 

ledger. You can also click the Draft button to save the journal entry without posting it. 

When you click Post, or Draft, or Cancel, the system returns to the Budget Period Location 

page so that you can continue working on the budget period analysis report, adding journal 

entries and notes. 

6. 
Click the Done button to close the Budget Period Location page.

#### Adding Budget Variance Analysis Notes to a Financial Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 646*

Budget Variance Analysis 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide

Adding Budget Variance Analysis Notes to a Financial Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reports > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Reports > Edit`


If you want to see the budget variance analysis (BVA) notes in a financial report, then you can add 

it to the report as a column. 

To add the BVA notes column to a custom financial report: 

1. 
In the Financial reports list, click the Edit link next to the desired financial report. The 

Financial report writer opens. 

2. 
Click the Columns tab. 

3. 
Find where you want to insert the new column, and then click the drop-down arrow of the 

Column heading to display its submenu. 

4. 
Select Add column left or Add column right. The new column appears to the left or right of 

the selected column. 

5. 
In the Column type field, find the Budget section, and then select the Budget variance 

notes option. 

For information about column types, see Column types in online help or download (on page 
718 ) the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide
. 

6. 
Select the Include variance amount, date, and user check box to display this information in 

the BVA note in the financial report. 

7. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the desired reporting period to include. 

For information about reporting periods, see Reporting periods in online help or download 
(on page 718 ) the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide
. 

8. 
If you selected a “Year to Date” reporting period, then you can select the Include prior 

period notes check box to include budget variance notes from a previous reporting period. 

For example, if you select this option and you run the report on March 31, then the report 

will display notes for January, February, and March. If you do not select this option and you 

run the report on March 31, then the report will display only YTD notes for March. 

9. 
In the Column heading 1 field, click the drop-down arrow to select a heading from the list. 

---

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

If the heading you want to use is not listed, select the Custom header option. A field is 
displayed that allows you to type a custom column heading. Click 
 Help for information 
about the column header. 

10. 
In the Column heading 2 field, click the drop-down arrow to select a heading from the list. 

If the heading that you want to use is not listed, select the Custom header option. A field 
is displayed that allows you to type a custom column heading. 

11. 
In the Column title field, the column header is pre-populated with the information in the 

Column type field. 

12. 
You can set the Expand by drop-down list to Location or Time period as needed. 

13. 
Select the Hide column check box when you want to hide this column from the financial 

report. 

14. 
When you run the report, the notes made during the budget variance analysis process 

appear in the column that you added, including the variance amount when the note was 

entered, the date the note was entered, and which user entered it. 

Notes made on individual accounts will appear in the financial reports while notes made on 

account groups will not.

Budget Variance Analysis Troubleshooting 

Situation: User cannot add notes, even though all permissions are correct, the user’s record is 

designated as a Budget Variance Analysis User, and the user has access to the entity. 

Reason: If the user is set up as a console user, they may not have access to the company. To 

change the entity assignment: 

1. 
Open the entities list by selecting Clients/Entities.  

2. 
Find the entity where Budget Variance Analysis is being run, and then click the Edit 

Assignments link.  

3. 
Look for the user’s name in the Assigned column. If it isn’t there, find the name in the 

Available column, and then click the >> button to move it to the Assigned column.  

4. 
Click Save. 

Situation: A customer that uses the console selects the Budget Variance Analysis User check box 

on the user’s record, but the user does not show up on the list of users who have not completed 

their report. 

Reason: When you open a period in Budget Variance Analysis, and a user record is created after 

this time, or the user record is not flagged as a BVA user until after the period was opened, you 

need to refresh the users. For instructions, see Refreshing Budget Variance Analysis Users (on 

page 612).

### Allocations Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 660*

Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Allocations Overview 

RealPage Accounting offers two ways to allocate revenue and expenses: 

• 
Transaction allocations 

• 
G/L allocations 

Transaction Allocations 

Transaction allocations enable you to automatically distribute amounts during transaction entry 

across multiple dimensions, such as departments and locations. You can allocate either a 

percentage or a set (absolute) value. If you allocate by percent, your total allocations must equal 

100%. 

For example, you can create a transaction allocation that distributes costs such as occupancy 

across several departments. Select that allocation when you enter the expense line. The amount of 

that expense is then automatically distributed across the appropriate departments. 

G/L Allocations 

Use G/L allocations to have the system calculate expense and revenue allocations. This feature 

saves time and effort by generating allocations to properties. Allocating revenue and expenses 

allows your organization to gain a better understanding of the performance of departments, 

properties, and projects. 

G/L allocations allow you to distribute expenses or revenue equally, in a tiered method, or based 

on a template that prescribes the properties, departments, and accounts involved.  

Allocation Differences 

Transaction allocations are applied when you enter a transaction. You need to know the 

parameters before you use transaction allocations. 

The G/L allocations feature automates allocation calculations and are applied post-transaction. 

---



### Transaction Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 661*



#### Where to Apply Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 661*

Chapter 22: Allocations 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Transaction Allocations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Allocations > Transaction Allocations`


Allocations distribute revenue or expense amounts across multiple dimensions, such as 

departments and locations. 

For example, you can create a transaction allocation that distributes costs such as insurance 

premiums across several regional sales offices. Select that allocation when you enter the A/P 

invoice. The amounts of that A/P invoice are then automatically distributed across the appropriate 

locations. 

You can allocate an amount by either a percentage or a set value. If you allocate by percent, your 

total allocations must equal 100%, for example, 25% to each of four projects. 

Transaction allocations are based on dimensions. You split allocation by a dimension across 

multiple entries (lines) in the Allocation setup, such as locations, departments, or vendors. 

When you create an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or journal entry and apply an allocation to it, 

RealPage Accounting automatically divides the item based on the way it is defined in the 

allocation. For example, if a company distributes rental revenues across five sales offices, the 

allocation would assign a value of 20% each to sales office. When you choose this allocation in a 

transaction, for example, an invoice, 20% of that invoice is automatically owed to each sales office. 

To see how an allocation is divided on an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or journal entry, view the item, 

and then click Show details on the line in the Entries section. 

Where to Apply Allocations 

Transaction allocations can be applied in any or all of these pages: 

• 
Accounts Payable invoices and recurring A/P invoices 

• 
Accounts Receivable invoices and recurring A/R invoices 

• 
General Ledger journal entries, recurring journal entries, and adjusting entries

#### Using a Transaction Allocation
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 663*

Chapter 22: Allocations 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Using a Transaction Allocation 

To use the allocation in a transaction: 

1. 
Open a transaction. 

2. 
Click the line item, and then select the allocation in the Allocation drop-down list.  

After you’ve selected the allocation, the system removes any dimension values selected for 

the line item. Instead, it populates the dimension values from the allocation directly.  

To change the dimensions for the line item: 

1. 
Click the Show Details tab. 

2. 
Select the Customize Allocation button. 

The line item offers two methods for allocating the cost or revenue of the line item: 

a) 
Select a pre-defined allocation. 

b) 
Select Show details, which opens the Details section where you can create a custom 

allocation. 

Overriding an Allocation on a Line Item 

Even when an allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to a line item, 

you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation at the line 

item level of the relevant transaction page (A/P invoices, A/R invoices, or journal entries). For 

detailed instructions on overriding allocations, see Overriding an Allocation (on page 650). 

---



#### Overriding a Line Allocation
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 664*

Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Overriding a Line Allocation 

You can apply an allocation either to individual lines of a transaction or to the entire transaction. If 

you apply it to the entire transaction, all of the line item entries inherit the distribution of the 

allocation. However, you can override that allocation on a line-by-line basis. When you change 

the allocated dimensions/values, the allocation resets as Custom, as it now contains a specific 

allocation distribution unique to that line item. 

The unique allocated values are stored with your line item for audit trail purposes.  

Click a line item, and then click the Show/Hide Details button to open and close the Allocations 

Splits detail area for a line item. 

To override a line allocation:  

1. 
Click the line item you want to override.  

2. 
Click the Show details tab or press CTRL + 
 Down Arrow to open the Details section. 

3. 
Find the Allocation splits section, and then click the Customize allocation button. The 

Custom Allocation box opens. 

4. 
Override the template distribution by customizing allocation amounts across departments 

or locations. 

5. 
Click Yes. 

Even when an allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to a line 

item, you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation at 

the line-item level of the relevant transaction page (A/R invoices, A/P invoices, or journal 

entries).  

If you change the amounts such that the total is different from what you entered in the 
transaction page, the system updates the total when you save and return to the 
transaction page.

Chapter 22: Allocations

G/L Allocations 

Use G/L allocations to have the system automatically generate allocations to properties. 

Allocating revenue and expenses allows your organization to gain a better understanding of the 

performance of departments, properties, and projects. 

You can allocate an expense or revenue on a recurring basis, at the segment level, and across 

multiple properties.  

The difference between transaction allocations and G/L allocations is that transaction allocations 

are performed as you enter a transaction into the system. You set up G/L allocations in advance.  

This section describes how to set up G/L allocations.

#### Generating a G/L Allocation
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 668*

Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Generating a G/L Allocation 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Generate Allocation`


During generation, the system gets the source amount, applies the calculation to the source 

amount, and creates a journal entry documenting the allocation. 

To begin the allocation: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Generate allocation. The Generate allocation page opens. 

3. 
In the G/L posting date field, type the G/L posting date for your allocation. The system 

posts the allocation to the General Ledger on the date that you enter here. 

4. 
In the Your email address field, type your email address.  

The system processes allocations offline. When the system processes the allocation, it sends 

an email about the allocation to the email address that you enter here. 

5. 
In the As of date field, type the date for your allocation or click the 
 Calendar button, 

and then select the desired date. The system uses the As of date to determine the source 

balance. 

6. 
In the Filters section, select the Allocation method from the drop-down list.  

7. 
Click the Apply filters button. The system displays a list of the selected type of allocations. 

---


<!-- Page 669 -->
Chapter 22: Allocations 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Previewing the Allocation 

To preview the allocation journal entries: 

1. 
Select the allocations in the list, and then click the Preview button.  

2. 
Review the G/L allocation definition before generating the allocation. The preview for the 

tiered allocation method only appears for sequence one, and not for all sequences in the 

G/L allocation definition. Subsequent sequences display when their allocations are posted. 

Generating the Allocation 

• 
From the Preview page, click the Generate button.  

The account’s Allocation Log page opens. This page shows the status of the allocations you 

generated as the calculation processes offline. The Last posted date field displays the last 

allocation journal entry posting date. See Allocation log list (on page 658).

### Roles and Permissions

#### Assigning Permissions for a New Feature
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 678*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

Assigning Permissions for a New Feature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Subscriptions > Permissions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > Permissions`


When RealPage adds a new feature, it often comes with new permissions that you must enable 

before users can use the new feature. 

To add permissions for a new feature: 

• 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

---


<!-- Page 679 -->
Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

If using Role-based permissions 

1. 
Select Roles. 

2. 
Find the role that you want to change. 

3. 
Click the Subscriptions link.  

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions window opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions. 

Be sure to check the Reports section at the bottom of the permissions page for any new 
reports that have been added to support the new feature. 

6. 
Click the Save button on the application’s permissions page. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the Roles subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list. 

If using User-based permissions 

1. 
Select Users. 

2. 
Locate the user who needs to be able to use the new feature.  

3. 
Select the Subscriptions link. 

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions page opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions.  

Be sure to check the Reports section at the bottom of the permissions page for related 
reports. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the User application subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list.

Using the Multi-Select Box 

Use the Multi-select box to select the items that you will act on in the next step. The goal is to 

find items in the Available items column that you want to act on and then move them into the 

Selected Items column. 

1. 
Click the Select button to open the Multi-select box. 

• 
To search for an item, type one or more letters in the Search items box. The system 

filters the items in the list to show only items that begin with the characters that you 

type.  

• 
To add an item, click the 
 Add button. The item moves to the Selected items 

column. 

• 
To add all items, select the Add all link. All items move from the Available items 

column into the Selected items column. 

• 
Click the 
 Delete button to remove an item. 

• 
To rearrange the list, drag an item to a new position in the list using the 
 Rearrange 

button. Repeat as necessary. 

2. 
When you have finished selecting items, click the Done button. The Selection box closes 

and is replaced by a smaller box that lists the items that you selected. The number of items 

appears in parentheses. The Select button changes to an Add/Edit link. 

In this box, you can: 

• 
Click the 
 Delete button to remove an item. 

• 
Click the Add/Edit link to reopen the Multi-select box and change your selections.

#### Exporting Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 681*

Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option. 

---

Click the Open file link to view the file in the file type’s associated program. 

If you selected PDF, the exported list opens in the browser window.

Click the 
 Save button to save the file.

 Navigation > 
 Library >

Automatically for Files Like This from Now On check box.

Save the file named with an XML extension. Example: Test.XML

#### Adding A/P Allocation Templates
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 684*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding A/P Allocation Templates 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > 
 Templates`


A/P allocation templates allow you to tell the system how to distribute costs amongst properties 

when applied to an A/P Invoice entry. A/P allocation template provides the ability to enter line 

items on A/P invoices faster using preset lists of properties (property groups). 

To add an A/P allocation template: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add next to Templates. The Templates page opens. 

3. 
In Name, type a name for the allocation template. 

Suppose you have four offices, and you divide rental income proportionately to square 
footage, but you divide interest income equally. You create an allocation for each set of 
allocation types. Your IDs might be RENT and INTEREST along with corresponding 
descriptions. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description for the allocation to help users identify which 

allocation to use. 

5. 
In the Template type drop-down list, select Percent or Amount. 

Percent: Select this type to allocate a percentage of the A/P invoice to multiple properties. 

Amount: Select this type to allocate a specific amount to multiple properties. 

6. 
In the Memo field, type a memo that describes this allocation.  

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active to allow users to select this allocation template. 

Select Inactive to prevent users from being able to select this allocation template. It will not 

appear in selection lists. 

Select Inactive to hide unused items. When set to Inactive, the system retains the data 
but hides the inactive item on lists, drop-down lists, and so on. If you want to permanently 
remove an allocation template, you must delete it. 

If you selected Percent, the Template list contains these columns: Property, Account, 

Department, and Percent. 

If you selected Amount, the list contains these columns: Property, Account, Department, 

and Amount. 

---


<!-- Page 685 -->
Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Filling In the Template List 

You can specify an individual property or select a group of properties.  

To specify an individual property: 

1. 
Select a property from the drop-down list. 

2. 
Specify the account. 

3. 
Select a Department. 

4. 
Type the percentage or amount for each property.  

5. 
Continue selecting individual properties as needed, and then click the Save button. 

Specifying a Group of Properties 

Use the Create from Property Group drop-down list to fill the list with properties from an existing 

Property group.  

To specify a group of properties: 

1. 
Select a property group from the Create from property group drop-down list. 

2. 
Click the Apply button. 

When you select a property group that has a Percent template type, the system evenly 

distributes 100 percent of the costs to the properties in the list. 

When you select Amount, you must manually type the amount to charge each property. 

The user can override the percentage or amount in the A/P invoice.

#### Adding Budget Variance Rules
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 686*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Budget Variance Rules 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > 
 Budget Variance Analysis`


Configuring the Budget Variance Analysis feature involves creating variance rules that determine 

whether the budget variance is favorable or unfavorable, and whether the budget variance falls 

within or outside of that defined rule. You can set up budget variance analysis configurations for 

multiple locations.  

The purpose of a budget variance analysis rule is to allow one rule to apply to multiple locations. 

To configure a budget variance rule: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to Budget variance analysis. The Budget variance analysis 

configuration information page opens. 

3. 
In the Configuration name field, type a name for this configuration. 

4. 
Select the scope of the budget variance analyses in the Reporting time frame drop-down 

list, Monthly or Quarterly. 

5. 
In the Reporting account group name drop-down list, select an account or account group 

to which to restrict the user when performing budget variance analyses. 

Reporting account sets, statistical, computation, category, and statistical category 
account group types are not available for Budget Variance Analysis. 

6. 
In the Locations drop-down list, select one or more locations that you want to measure with 

this budget variance check. 

7. 
Set up a budget in the Budget Override field when you need to compare actuals to a 

budget that is not the default budget. 

8. 
In the Book drop-down list, select the book, Cash or Accrual, that you want to analyze 

budget variance for. 

---


<!-- Page 687 -->
Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

9. 
Select the Favorable variances require explanation check box. When selected, a favorable 

variance requires an explanation even if it exceeds variance rules in the positive or negative 

depending on the expense or revenue. When cleared, a favorable variance does not require 

explanation. 

10. 
Select the Calculate fiscal properties as calendar check box if any of your entities are 

running on a different fiscal year other than the regular calendar year, but you want to 

calculate the budget variance analysis year-to-date amounts based on the calendar. 

Filling In the Variance Rules Section 

1. 
In the Period variance type drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
Percent or amount: Select this option to set a threshold expressed as a percentage or 

an amount of currency for the reporting period. You can enter either a percentage or 

an amount. If you choose to enter both values, then either value is accepted. 

• 
Percent but at least amount: Select this option to enter both a percent value and an 

amount value. Both values must be a match before the system deems the threshold to 

be met. 

2. 
In the Period variance percent field, type the threshold percentage for the variance during a 

reporting period. 

3. 
In the Period variance amount field, type the threshold amount for the period. 

4. 
In the YTD variance type drop-down list, select an option. 

Percent or amount: Select this option to set a threshold expressed as a percentage or an 

amount of currency for the year to date. 

Percent but at least amount: Select this option if you want to set a threshold percentage or 

a threshold amount as a minimum amount in currency for the year to date. 

5. 
In the YTD variance percent field, type the threshold percentage for the year to date. 

6. 
In the YTD variance amount field, type the threshold amount for the year to date. 

• 
If you set a variance threshold for an account group, the threshold applies to all accounts in 

that group. 

---


<!-- Page 688 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
If you set a variance threshold for a group of account groups, the threshold applies to all 

account groups and accounts in that group of groups. 

• 
If the variance is set to either Current or YTD, and Percent, but at least amount, the system 

requires both Percent and Amount values. If both fields are not completed, the system 

displays an error message: 

“Unable to create a Budget Variance Analysis Configuration. A Percent value and Amount 

value must be entered when Percent, but at least amount variance option is selected.” 

Filling In the Variance Rules Overrides Section 

As an option, you can fill in this section if you want to select different thresholds for a selected 

account or account group. 

1. 
Select the account or account group that you want to override with unique threshold values.  

2. 
In the Period variance type drop-down list, select the override type: 

Percent or amount: Select this option to set a threshold percentage or an amount for the 

reporting period. 

Percent but at least amount: Select this option to set a threshold expressed as a percentage 

or a threshold amount expressed as a minimum amount in currency for the reporting 

period. 

If you select the Percent, but at least amount option, then you must enter both Percent 
and Amount values.  

3. 
In the Period variance percent field, type the override percentage threshold for the variance 

during a reporting period, expressed as a percentage. 

4. 
In the Period variance amount field, type the override threshold amount for the period, 

expressed as currency. 

5. 
In the YTD variance type drop-down list, select the override type for the year to date: 

Percent or amount: Select this option to override the threshold expressed as a percentage 

or an amount of currency for the year to date. 

Percent but at least amount: Select this option to override the threshold expressed as a 

percentage or a threshold amount expressed as a minimum amount in currency for the 

reporting period. 

If you select the Percent, but at least amount option, then you must enter both Percent 
and Amount values.  

6. 
In the YTD variance percent field, type the override percentage threshold for the variance 

during the year to date, expressed as a percentage. 

7. 
In the YTD variance amount field, type the override threshold amount for the year to date. 

---


<!-- Page 689 -->

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

8. 
Click Save.
