### Dimension Report Structures
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 690*



#### Finding Dimension Structures for Financial Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 690*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension Report Structures 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Structures`


Dimension report structures provide a flexible way for you to organize dimension data that you 

want to see on the rows or columns of a financial report. For example, instead of showing all 

locations on a report, you might want to select a Location structure that is named for a particular 

region and includes a subset of locations. 

You can add any number of structures for the dimensions you track. 

The list of standard dimension structures may include: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

If you have additional dimension structures listed in the Dimension structure submenu, they are 

custom structures and are not discussed in this document. 

Creating a dimension structure from a group enables you to add the group to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. 

A dimension structure can only be used for filtering reports if you don’t select the Dimension 

Structure check box when you are creating a dimension group. 

Viewing the Available Dimension Report Structures 

Select a dimension structure option to view the available report structures. 

See also Dimension analysis in financial reports and Dimension structures for financial reports (on 

page 676). 

Finding Dimension Structures for Financial Reports 

To find your dimension structures: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the Dimension structures section, select the desired dimension. 

The system opens the list of dimension structures. 

For multi-entity shared users: Dimension structures can either be common (accessible) to all 
entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. 

Learn more about dimension structures in a multi-entity shared environment (on page 141). 

---



#### Adding an Account Group
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 691*

Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Adding an Account Group 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > 
 Account Groups`


To add an account group: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click 
 Add next to Account groups. The Account group 

information page opens. 

3. 
Type a name for the new account group in the Name field. 

The name of the account group determines how it appears in lists. After saving the account 
group, you cannot change the name. However, you can control how the name is displayed in 
reports using the Display as fields. 

It requires an administrator to change the name. The administrator can use the Company 
application’s Customer Utility Tool to change the account group name with the ID Change 
menu option.  

4. 
In the Display on report as field, you can change the name that the system displays in the 

report. 

5. 
In the Display total line as field, type the name that you want the system to use for the 

heading for totals. 

6. 
In the Normal balance drop-down list, select Debit to use this account group as a debit 

balance, or select Credit to use it as a credit balance. Cash is typically a debit balance; sales 

is typically a credit balance. 

7. 
In the Account group purpose drop-down list, select the intended use for the account 

group. 

Assigning an account group purpose can help you organize your accounts into more 

manageable groups for financial reports, graphs, and performance cards. Think about how 

the account group will be used. 

8. 
In the Account group manager field, type the name of the person who should be consulted 

about changing this account group. It can be a fellow staff member or a partner who 

implemented the account group.  

If you’re using the Account group manager option, consider creating a custom view for the 
list of account groups that includes the Account group manager column. 

9. 
If your company uses Global Consolidations, then select the Is a KPI check box to make the 

account group available as a key performance indicator (KPI). 

---


<!-- Page 692 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

This check box is available only for multi-entity shared companies that use Global 
Consolidations. 

You can view real-time KPI data for any entity or location in the Organization view when KPI 

rollup is enabled. You can have as many KPIs as you want selected in account groups, but 

only the first 10 KPIs (alphabetically) are shown in the Organization view. 

Only the first 10 account groups marked as KPIs appear in the organization view ’s KPI 
pop-up. To ensure that your desired KPIs appear in the list, name (or rename) them with a 
letter or number prefix, such as a_Assets, b_Cash and equivalents, c_Expenses, and so on. 

10. 
If you enable KPIs for account groups later, the Refresh button in the Organization chart 

refreshes only existing data. Refresh the page in the browser to see the new KPI data. 

Defining the Group Structure Type and Calculation Method 

1. 
In the Structure type drop-down list, select the structure type that you want to assign to the 

account group: 

• 
Accounts 

• 
Group of accounts 

• 
Statistical accounts 

• 
Computation 

• 
Category 

• 
Statistical category 

The page options change depending on which group type (on page 133) you select. 

Each structure type is designed for a specific use and has different features. You can no 
longer change the structure type after you save the account group. If you mistakenly 
assigned a different structure type and have not used the account group in any report, 
delete the group and recreate it with the correct structure type. 

2. 
Select the calculation method from the Calculation method drop-down list. 

• 
For period: Calculate only the amounts in the selected period. 

• 
Start of period: Calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the start of the selected 

period. 

• 
End of period: Calculate the amounts cumulatively up to the end of the selected 

period. 

---


<!-- Page 693 -->
Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

For example, in a balance-forward situation, you can set up balance sheet account groups as 

End of period and set up income statement account groups as For period. 

Computation structures use calculation methods that enable you to create formulas for your 

account group. You can add, subtract, multiply, or divide between selected accounts or account 

groups. You can also use a constant number as part of the calculation. Display the amount result 

as a ratio, percentage, or average, based on the formula that you select. 

Calculation structures can take as few as two accounts, account groups, or constants. For example, 

you can: 

• 
Divide the revenue G/L account by the employee statistical account to obtain your revenue 

per employee. 

• 
Divide your total debt by your current assets to get the debt ratio. 

A G/L account can be a member of more than one account group. 

Next, add accounts to the account group (on page 148).

#### Adding a New Custom View
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 697*

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Adding a New Custom View 

To add a new custom view: 

1. 
Under Manage views, click Create new view. 

The Create new view wizard opens. 

When you create a custom view, some options become hidden. Depending on the page, the

Include inactive, Include one-time, Include private, and Display hierarchy options aren’t 
available to users of this view. They can switch to View all to see the options again. 

2. 
Follow the steps in the wizard to set up the custom view. 

Step 1: Select Columns 

The first step is to choose which columns to show in the list when you use this view. The available 

columns change based on the list for which you are creating the view. 

1. 
Select the columns that you want to include in the view. 

2. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

---


<!-- Page 698 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Step 2: Select Column Sequence 

The second step is to determine the order of columns from left to right. 

1. 
Drag and drop columns to rearrange them in the order that you want them to appear in the 

list. 

2. 
Optionally, if you want to change a column’s label, then you can type its new name in the 

text box. 

3. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

---


<!-- Page 699 -->
Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Step 3: Select Filters 

The third step is to set up any filters that you want to apply to the columns. 

1. 
In the Columns drop-down list, select the column to filter on. 

2. 
In the Operator drop-down list, select the comparison operator. 

3. 
In the Value field, type the value for the system to use for the comparison. 

For example, Columns equals  

4. 
Continue adding filters as needed. Click the Add filter link if you need more filter rows. You 

can also click the Delete last filter link to delete the bottom filter row. 

The more filters you add, the more granular the list view will be. 

5. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 4: Sort Results 

The fourth step is to set the default sort order for the data in each column. 

1. 
For each column, select whether to sort the data in ascending or descending order. If you 

do not want to sort the column, leave it as --None--. 

2. 
Drag and drop columns to determine their sort priority. The column at the top will have the 

highest priority and will be sorted first, followed by the second column, followed by the 

third column, and so on. 

3. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 5: Save Advanced Options 

The fifth and final step is to deploy the view. 

1. 
In the Name field, type a meaningful name for the new custom view.

In the Description field, type the purpose of use of the view.

When finished, click Save to save and deploy the custom view.

### Segments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 700*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 700*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide

Segments Overview 

Segments are custom classifications that help you organize, sort, and report on your company 

information in meaningful ways. Think of a segment as a tag with a set of values that you can 

associate with transactions and G/L entries. For example, you might add a custom segment to 

report on your expense types, employees, or special projects. 

When you enter a new transaction, you can assign a segment to that transaction and then tag it 

with one or more segment values. Segmenting transactions is optional; however, it can be useful 

for identifying transactions and analyzing data in your reports. 

You can define up to 15 segments for your company. An additional segment, called 

Intercompany segment, is available by default. Because it’s a system segment, it cannot be 

modified. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add and manage segments. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Segments 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 664) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 664) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Enable Segments 

Before you can use segments, you must enable the segments feature in the General Ledger. See 

Enabling Segments (on page 687).

### Importing Data into RealPage Accounting
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 705*



#### Best Practices for Preparing Data for Import
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 705*

Chapter 23: Common Tasks

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Importing Data into RealPage Accounting 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Import data`


To import data from an external, non-OneSite source, follow these steps: 

OneSite users can refer to a faster process to import their data. Contact your Customer 
Support Representative for assistance. 

1. 
Download the template (on page 695) 

2. 
Fill in the template (on page 697) 

3. 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 698) 

4. 
Import the CSV file (on page 698) 

Best Practices for Preparing Data for Import 

Follow these best practices to prepare your data. 

• 
Download a template from the Import data page. 

Always use the latest template, especially following a product release. 

Use the correct template for the data object that you want to import. 

• 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to enter information. 

Do not change the titles in the header row. 

The header titles correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header titles may cause an 

upload error. When you download a template from the Import data page, the correct 

headers are in the template. 

Read the header descriptions in the template. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains the type of 

information to include in each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, or with 

an incorrect accepted value, it may cause an error in your import. 

Enter required information. 

Read the description field to determine which information is required. If you do not enter 

the required information, your import may fail. 

• 
Save the data as a comma-separated value, or CSV, file. When saving from Excel, choose the 

comma delimited file (.csv) type. 

The file has the file extension .csv after you save it. 

• 
Leave the file open until your import is successful. Excel can sometimes reformat the file if 

you close it before the import is successful. 

---



#### Preparing Your CSV File for Import
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 706*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Preparing Your CSV File for Import 

The Import data page is a quick way to import your information into the system. However, the 

way you prepare your CSV files directly affects the success or failure of importing your data. Learn 

the CSV import process to streamline the import process. 

This topic provides general information about preparing CSV files for import. Links to information 
about specific templates can be found in the Import data into the system, which lists all import 
topics. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 

Most imports start with getting the most recent template from the Import data page. When you 

get your templates from this list, you get templates that have been tailored to your specific 

company, including specific dimensions. 

Next you add your data, using the correct formatting as explained in the template. After you’ve 

added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

Downloading a Template 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because: 

• 
Templates in the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage at any time, especially when a new version of 

RealPage Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work. 

To download an import template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. The Import data page opens with a list of information that you can 

import into the system. 

3. 
Decide on the type of information to upload, and then click the Template link associated 

with that information. 

---


<!-- Page 707 -->
Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Other Templates 

RealPage may have additional CSV import templates that are not found on the Import data page. 

Contact your RealPage Support Representative for any templates that have been customized for 

your company. 

Adding Your Data 

After you download the appropriate template, add your data. 

The following example shows a portion of a standard CSV file for importing accounts receivable 

invoices after it has been opened in Excel, but before data has been added. The top row is the 

header row, (the data labels for all of your data), and the second row contains descriptions of the 

kinds of data to enter in the column. 

a) Some fields are not required. 

b) Some fields are required. 

c) Header row 

d) Header description row 

Each template contains a set of pre-defined headers, such as BUDGET_ID, ACCT_NO, and soon. 

You enter your data into the blank cells below the header and header description rows without 

changing the headers. 

It is important to read the description for each of the column headers. Some columns are 
required and if left blank will cause your import to fail. 

---

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The following illustration shows a portion of the template after the data has been added. The 

description row has been hidden for this example. 

To add your data: 

1. 
Open the template that you downloaded from the Import data page. 

2. 
Enter your information. Use the header descriptions as a guide for how to enter information 

correctly. 

• 
Do not change the headers. 

The header titles in the header row correlate to fields in UI. Incorrect header titles will 

cause an import error. When you download a template, the correct headers are in the 

template. 

• 
Read the header descriptions. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with a value not accepted by the column, it will cause an error in your import. 

• 
Enter required information. 

Some data is required, while others are not. Read the description field to determine 

which information is required. If you do not enter the required information, your 

import will fail. 

3. 
After entering your data, save the file as a comma-separated value (CSV) file. When saving 

from Excel, select the comma delimited file type. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it.

Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
Find the type of data that you want to import.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

A prompt opens at the bottom of the web page, asking if you want to Open, Save, or 

Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your browser’s default download folder. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Save the template to your computer, and then continue downloading templates as needed until 

you have downloaded all of the templates for data that you want to import. 

If you have a database administrator (DBA) of your other system, give the downloaded templates 

to your DBA. Ask the DBA to: 

• 
Export the data from your other system, as specified in the import template spreadsheets. 

• 
Put the applicable data into each spreadsheet. 

• 
Save the spreadsheet as a comma-delimited file (CSV). 

If you do not have a DBA, or if your DBA does not have time to complete the whole task, you can 

complete the tasks. Refer to the following topics for guidance on creating importable data.

Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 698). 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.

#### Importing the CSV File
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 713*

Chapter 23: Common Tasks

Importing the CSV File 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file into the system. 

To import your CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Find the information type you want to import, and then click the corresponding Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you want to import. 

5. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in mm/dd/yyyy format, select the date format that 

the data uses in the Date format field. 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
If your import box includes a Post to section, select one of the following: 

• 
Select Historical if your data is not active. 

• 
Select General Ledger to post imported invoices to the G/L. 

8. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

9. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

10. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify that all of the 

records in your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify 

them.

### Resolving Import Errors
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 714*



#### Import Error Notification
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 714*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Resolving Import Errors 

This section describes how to resolve errors when your data fails to import properly. 

If any records contained errors and the import failed, then the system notifies you with a list of 

the errors and how to correct the problems in an email. 

Import Error Notification 

There are a number of reasons imported records fail, such as duplicated entries or invalid field 

content. RealPage provides information about the failed records in an attempt to help you fix the 

import error. 

Finding the Error Message 

The Import confirmation page indicates how many records failed. This page also contains a link 

to download a CSV file, which contains only the failed records. 

Records that are successfully imported are not returned in the CSV file. 

Click the link and download the CSV file. 

If you entered your email address into the Import Company Information box, an email is sent 

that contains the error messages for your attempted import. The email lists the error code, and 

then each unique instance of that error in the file you attempted to import. 

The error message email is sent to the email address associated with the user ID logged in at the 

time of the file upload; otherwise, the email address for the company contact is used. 

The import pages also allow another email address to be explicitly entered in the Email results to 

this address field. 

If you did not enter your email in the Import Company Information box, and you do not click the 
link in the Import confirmation page, there is no way to retrieve the CSV error report file for the 
import you just did. 

Best practice: Enter your email in the Import Company Information box at the beginning of every 
import. 

The reason you are sent a separate email with the error messages is because a record could fail 

for more than one reason. Displaying all of the text for each record in the CSV file could become 

quite cumbersome and hard to read. Furthermore, it is often the case that thousands of records 

are uploaded. If thousands of errors fail, the CSV file could become quite bloated. 

---


<!-- Page 715 -->
Chapter 23: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Read the Error Message Email 

The error messages for your failed upload file can be challenging to read. RealPage recommends 

the following strategy: 

• 
Start at the top of the email and look at each error message section. 

• 
In each section, start reading from the bottom up. The error at the bottom of the section is 

the first error encountered during import. 

a) Start here. 

b) Read from the bottom up. 

c) In each section, the specific error is listed at the top. 

---


<!-- Page 716 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Start at the Top of the Email 

Error messages are presented in sections, and the sections are listed in the order that the errors 

are encountered in your file. 

Example: 

=================================================== 
Error BL01001973 
=================================================== 
BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number.  
The account number ‘4150’ already exists. 
BL01001973-1 Correction: Enter unique account number. 
BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record Could not create  
GL Account record! 
=================================================== 

When you read the error messages such as the one above, start with the error number. 

The error codes, such as BL01001973 above, are internal codes. These internal codes can help 
RealPage locate the source of a systemic issue if one is identified. 

=================================================== 
Error BL03000019 
=================================================== 
BL03000019-1 Description: Invalid contact data entered. 
TRANSACTION TYPE is a required field and cannot be empty 
BL03000019-1 Correction: Some of the fields you have entered 
are invalid. Please correct them with proper values. 
=================================================== 

Read from the Bottom of the Error Message Up 

In the example, the error code is BL01001973-2. 

Description: Unable to create record Could not create G/L Account record! first. 

This identifies the first error that occurred during import. It’s not informative, however, so look at 

the next error message for more information. 

The next error message in the list (as read from the bottom up), BL01001973-1 Correction: 

Enter unique account number, identifies the reason the G/L account record couldn’t be 

created, but it’s not yet clear what to do to fix the problem. 

The final error message in the example above (as read from the bottom up) describes more fully 

the cause of the error and suggests a fix: find and delete the duplicate account number. 

---

#### Handling Import Errors
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 720*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Handling Import Errors 

If you experience import errors, review the tips in About CSV Templates and review the common 

errors (on page 703).  

Import errors occur when you try to import information that does not match the requirements of 

the template. Each template has a set of required information that you must enter to successfully 

import the file, and formats to follow for certain kinds of information. Read the descriptions in the 

template to determine the most accurate way to enter your data.  

If individual transactions are in error, the rows in the transaction that are in error are saved in a 

CSV file for you along with an error code for each row. The system sends an email with 

information about specific errors (on page 700).

### Attachments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 722*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 722*

Attachments 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Attachments Overview 

Attachments are bundles of one or more files that you associate with a transaction or record, such 

as a letter of credit, an invoice, or a photo. For example, if you have a contract signed by a 

customer, you can attach the contract to the customer record. You can attach as many files or 

combinations of file types as you need and bundle them into a single attachment record. 

To attach a document, you first need to create an electronic version of it. If it is a paper copy, scan 

the document, and then save it as one of the supported file types:  

• 
Word 

• 
PDF 

• 
Excel 

• 
Text 

• 
JPG 

• 
PNG 

Attaching Files to Transaction Records 

The Enable single scan upload setting in your user preferences changes the way that the system 

treats attachments. These differences are described below: 

When scanning is disabled: 

• 
You can select one attachment record to associate with a transaction, but the attachment 

record can contain multiple files as needed. 

• 
You can create folders for storing attachments from the transaction record. 

• 
You can access the attachment folders from the transaction record. 

When scanning is enabled: 

• 
You can add multiple attachments to a transaction record. 

• 
You can scan a document to attach it directly to the transaction record. 

• 
You cannot create or access attachment folders. 

For instructions on enabling the Enable single scan upload option, see Enabling the Scanning 

Feature. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

• 
Decide if you need to add an attachment that is already stored in the system or if you need 

to upload a new document into the system. Existing attachments are files that someone has 

already added to the system. 

---



#### Permissions for Attachments
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 723*

Chapter 24: Attachments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

• 
Open the record to which you want to add an attachment with the Attachments field 

displayed. It must be a type of record that can accept attachments. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 664) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 664) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Permissions for Attachments 

To work with attachments, you must have List and View permissions in the Company application 

for both Attachments and Attachment Folders. You cannot restrict access to attachment folders 

by individual user. If a user has permission to view attachments and attachment folders, they will 

be able to view all attachments and folders in the system. 

To grant access to attachments: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Locate the user to whom you want to allow access to attachments. 

4. 
Click the user’s View permissions and roles link. The Permissions & roles report box opens. 

5. 
Click the Roles tab (a), and then select the View link (b) below Subscriptions. 

The Roles subscriptions box opens. 

6. 
Click 
 Expand to expand the window. 

7. 
In the Company row, click the Permissions link.  

The Company permissions box opens.

#### Adding a New Attachment to a Record
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 724*

Attachments 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

8. 
Select the List and View permissions for Attachment folders and Attachments. 

9. 
Click the Save button. 

Adding a New Attachment to a Record 

This topic describes how to attach a file to a record when the file is not yet stored in the system. 

To attach a file to a record when the file is already in the system, see Adding an Existing 

Attachment to a Record (on page 712). 

The steps for attaching documents to transactions and records are different depending on 

whether the Enable single scan upload option is enabled or disabled in your user preferences. 

Adding a New Attachment to a Record When Scanning is Disabled  

To add a new attachment to a record when scanning is disabled: 

1. 
Add a new record or edit an existing record to open the information page. 

2. 
Click the Attachments drop-down list, and then click the Add link. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

3. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

4. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

---


<!-- Page 725 -->
Chapter 24: Attachments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

5. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

6. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment. 

7. 
In the Attach files section: 

• 
Click the Choose files button, select the file(s) you want to attach, and then click the 

Open button. Alternatively, you can drag and drop files directly from your file explorer 

into the browser window. 

• 
If you have Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-Op, and you 

purchased the portal add-on, then the Display on portal check box also appears. 

Select the check box for any attachment that you want the tenant or owner to be able 

to access on their portal. 

8. 
Attach additional files as needed. 

9. 
Click the Save button. 

Adding a New Attachment to a Record When Scanning is Enabled 

To add a new attachment to a record when scanning is enabled: 

1. 
Add a new record or edit an existing record to open the information page. 

2. 
Find the Documents section. 

3. 
Click the Choose file button, select the file you want to attach, and then click the Attach 

button to upload it to the record. The file appears in the list of attachments. 

Alternatively, you can scan documents into the record. See Scanning a Document into a 

Record for more information. 

4. 
Continue attaching files as needed. 

5. 
Save the record. 

When you save the record, the system stores the attached files in a new attachment record 

in the Attachments list. 

---



#### Adding an Existing Attachment to a Record
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 726*

Attachments 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding an Existing Attachment to a Record 

This topic describes how to attach a file to a record when the file is already stored in the system 

and you do not have scanning enabled. To attach a file to a record when the file is not yet stored 

in the system, see Adding a New Attachment to a Record (on page 710). 

To add an existing attachment to a transaction or record: 

1. 
Open the record to which you want to attach a file. 

2. 
Click the Attachments drop-down list. 

3. 
Select the file that you want to attach to the record. If you do not see the file that you want 

to attach, you can filter the list or search for it. 

• 
Click Show unattached to show only files that have not yet been attached to a record; 

click Show all to view all files. 

• 
Click Find to search for a specific attachment. 

4. 
Click Save to save the record. 

---



#### Viewing a File that Is Attached to a Record
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 727*

Chapter 24: Attachments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Viewing a File that Is Attached to a Record 

When a file is attached to a record, you can view the file from the Select Attachments box. 

1. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, select the attachment that you want to view. 

2. 
Click View. The Attachments box opens, showing the meta-data about the attachment: its 

name, folder, description, the date it was attached, and the name of the user who attached 

it. 

At the bottom of the Attachments box, the attached file’s name appears. 

3. 
Click the name to open the file. 

With the Attachments box open, you can: 

• 
Delete the attachment. 

• 
Add more attachments. Click the Browse button to select more files to attach. 

• 
Click the Edit button to view or change the attachment information. 

Things you can change: 

• 
The attachment’s name 

• 
The attachment’s description 

• 
The folder in which the attachment is stored

#### How to Read Paths
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 733*

Chapter 25: Help and Support

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

---


<!-- Page 734 -->
Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record. 

---


<!-- Page 735 -->
Chapter 25: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

### Audit Trails
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 736*



#### Viewing Audit Trails
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 736*



#### Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 736*

Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view. 

---



##### Fields
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 737*



##### Buttons
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf`, Page 737*

Chapter 25: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide 

Fields 

Audit Trail Columns 

Date 
This is the date and time of the change to the record, presented in the time zone 

defined in your preferences. 

Action 
This column indicates the type of update made to the record (whether it was 

created, modified, or deleted). It also indicates whether the system performed the 

action as part of a workflow, or if a user performed the action. 

Completed by This is the ID of the user who made the change. 

If the transaction is an eInvoice or oInvoice, the audit trail displays 

realpageaccounting as the user who submitted the transaction. This is because 
eInvoices and oInvoices are created electronically, either by the vendor through 
Storefront or through Invoice Processing. 

The system previously designated CPAUser as the user who submitted 
electronic invoices. 

Source 
This is the source from which the record was accessed or changed. 

Field 
This is the name of the field that was changed. 

Before 
This is the data that appeared in the field before the user saved the change. 

After 
This is the changed data that appears in the field after the user saved the change. 

Buttons 

Audit Trail Box/Audit Trail Page 

Done 
Saves any changes and opens the previous page 

Help 
Opens the Online Help page 

More actions 
Opens a drop-down list with the following options: 

• 
Export to CSV: Downloads the report as a CSV file 

• 
Export to Excel: Downloads the report as an XLS file 

• 
Export to PDF: Downloads the report as a PDF file 

• 
Table size: Allows you to select the number of rows you want to 

display per application page

### Configuring the Accounting Method
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 16*

Configuring the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring the Accounting Method 

The accounting method can be set to Accrual, Cash, or both (Accrual and Cash). 

Accounting Section 

Select the accounting method you use for reporting: 

• 
Accrual 

• 
Cash 

• 
Accrual and cash 

Selecting Accrual and Cash gives you the flexibility to report on either method. To save time, you 

select the default accounting method to use for reporting and can then make changes on a 

report-by-report basis. 

The accounting method that’s right for you depends on your reporting needs and other factors. 
Cash is available as an option only for new companies. Selecting Accrual and cash affects your 
setup and (to some extent) usage of the system. 

Start As Of 

When you select Accrual and cash, tracking data in both accrual and cash journals begins 

immediately after you save the configuration. The Start as of date lets you know when you 

configured this option. Learn more about dual-method (accrual and cash) accounting (on page 

434). 

When you select a Start as of date, the processing starts immediately and the Start as of field is 

set to the next available future period. Then the Start as of field is set to read only and can’t be 

edited. 

In a new company with no transactions, the Start as of field is not displayed. 

GAAP and Tax 

See Enabling GAAP and Tax Adjustment Journals (on page 62)

### Changing Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 17*



#### Prepare for the Change
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 17*

Chapter 1: Configuring the General Ledger 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Changing Accounting Methods 

After you have determined that changing to a dual accounting method is necessary, understand 

the implications, and possibly have talked it over with your RealPage trained consultant you’re 

ready to set up for the change. 

Creating the ability to report on either method involves enabling the feature, providing a cut-over 

period, creating the cash-basis or accrual-basis journals, and then choosing those journals in the 

appropriate application configuration areas. Applications that are impacted by this feature include 

the General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Cash Management.  

Integrations can also be impacted but must be separately evaluated according to how the 

integration is designed for data to flow. 

Before switching from Cash or Accrual to Accrual and cash talk to your RealPage account 
manager about setup and best practices. 

Prepare for the Change 

1. 
Best practice is to close the books as of the cut-off month and work as if you are switching 

to a new system as of that date. 

2. 
Create the mock journal and assign it to all the configurations to ensure that existing data 

isn’t changed without your specific intent during the switch. When you enable the account 

method change for Cash and Accrual, all journals that are set in the application 

configuration will automatically be changed to both. To ensure that you control this change, 

the best practice is to create the “Mock” journal for temporary use during the changeover. 

For easier troubleshooting, this specific title is recommended for the journal. 

3. 
Verify which applications your company is subscribed to by navigating to Company > 

Subscriptions. For each application, select Configure. 

4. 
Have other users stop processing transactions. 

5. 
For each application, configure that application to use the new “dummy journal.” Common 

applications to check are: 

• 
Accounts Receivable 

• 
Accounts Payable 

• 
Cash Management 

• 
(Shared environment only) Multi-Entity Console Subscription area for Inter-Company 

Payments and Receivables 

6. 
Verify that all bank accounts (Checking Accounts, Charge Card Accounts and Savings 

Accounts) don’t have a journal assigned. 

7. 
Change any other applications and an integration-related setup area as needed. 

---



#### Make the Change
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Configuring the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Make the Change 

After the new accounting method is enabled and fully configured, the system begins booking dual 
entries immediately, which is why it’s important to enable the switch at the beginning of the 
month. Any transactions after this that are backdated will use the Accrual and Cash accounting 
method. 

1. 
Enable Accrual and cash in the Configure General Ledger page (on page 4). 

• 
Select the Start as of date. This period is only a reference. You can only select periods 

in the future. 

• 
Your default account method for reporting. 


> **Navigation Path:** `2. 
Go to General Ledger Setup > Journals and confirm that only the dummy journal is listed`


as Cash and Accrual.  

3. 
Create a new set of journals that are Accrual, Cash, or both Accrual and Cash. For example, 

use the ID and descriptions: 

• 
APJA – Accounts Payable Journal – Accrual 

• 
APJC – Accounts Payable Journal – Cash 

• 
ARJA – Accounts Receivable Journal – Accrual 

• 
ARJC – Accounts Receivable Journal – Cash 

• 
CD – Cash Disbursements Journal – Cash and Accrual 

• 
CR – Cash Receipts Journal – Cash and Accrual 

• 
EEJA – Employee Expense Journal – Accrual 

• 
EEJC – Employee Expense Journal – Cash 

• 
EED – Employee Expense Disbursements Journal – Cash and Accrual 

• 
GJC – General Journal – Cash 

• 
GJCA – General Journal – Cash and Accrual 

• 
Update the name of the GJ from General Journal to General Journal – Accrual 

• 
IC – Intercompany Journal – Cash and Accrual 

4. 
If your company is a shared company, update the multi-entity console configuration to 

specify the new inter-company journals. 

5. 
Go to each application’s configuration settings and assign the newly created journals to it. 

You should be able to tell which journal to assign by its name. 

Do not reassign the previous journals. Assigning the previous journals can inadvertently 
mix transactions posted on different methods and impact reporting adversely. 

6. 
When you’ve assigned all the applications to the new journal, delete the mock journal.

### Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 20*



#### Why Change Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 20*



#### Explanation of Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 20*

Configuring the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accounting Methods 

In RealPage Accounting, you can choose your accounting method—accrual, cash, or both. If you 

choose both Accrual and cash, the system records transactions in separate journals “behind the 

scenes” so you can later report on either basis. For example, you can run a balance sheet report 

on accrual basis and then run the same report on cash basis. 

When you change the accounting method, the Start as of date is set to the next available future 

period by the system. Data tracking for reporting starts immediately, but because the data won’t 

be for a full period it might not be useful. The system doesn’t create journals for you.  

Changing your accounting method requires additional setup changes. When you turn on accrual 

and cash, you need to review all configuration in Cash Management, Accounts Receivable, 

Accounts Payable, and General Ledger to ensure that the appropriate journals are properly added. 

Never change the accounting method without consulting a RealPage trained consultant first as its 

important to understand the impact of changing accounting methods before you do it. 

Why Change Accounting Methods 

There can be a number of reasons to change accounting methods. For example: 

• 
A company that’s had (or expects) significant growth might want to change from 

cash-based to cash-and-accrual-based accounting 

• 
An organization that’s been happy with accrual-only based accounting might want the 

deeper insight that cash-and-accrual-based accounting can provide 

• 
A company that generally run reports in one or the other method has acquired other 

entities and wants to incorporate both accounting methods 

Explanation of Accounting Methods 

Your system administrator can select your accounting method as part of the General Ledger 

Setup. 

Accrual: All transactions are included in reports, regardless of whether cash inflow or outflow was 

part of the transaction. For example, vendor bills appear in accrual basis reports even when 

unpaid.  

• 
All journals and reports are Accrual. 

• 
Good choice if you are required to report on an Accrual basis. 

Cash: Transactions appear on reports only when cash impact occurs (in or out). For example, 

vendor bills are reflected in cash basis reports only when paid. 

• 
All journals and reports are Cash. 

• 
Good choice if you always report on Cash basis. 

Cash is available only for new companies. 

---



#### Before You Change Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 21*

Chapter 1: Configuring the General Ledger 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Accrual and cash: Select this option when you want the flexibility to generate reports using either 

accounting method or reporting. You can then decide on a report-by-report basis which method 

to use. For reporting, the company might: 

• 
Set the accounting method to Accrual and cash. 

• 
Select Accrual as the default for reporting. This saves time if most reports will be run on 

accrual basis. 

• 
Override the default, selecting Cash on the filters tab when needing to report on a cash 

basis. 

Before You Change Methods 

You can change your accounting method from cash method or accrual method to the multi-book 

accrual and cash method. RealPage recommends that you discuss this change with a trained 

consultant beforehand, because making the change requires more than just changing the 

selection on the General Ledger configuration page. For example: 

• 
An analysis of journal configuration to ensure the system is prepared for the change must 

take place ahead of time, because the system will make journal updates that cannot be 

undone. 

• 
Changing accounting methods isn’t retroactive: in addition to configuration, you’ll need to 

align your expectations about how reporting will work after the change. 

• 
Transaction processing should cease while the change is being made. 

• 
While the system will adjust some existing journals, you’ll need to manually add other 

journals. The specific journals to create depends on the method you are moving from. For 

example, if you change to multi-book cash and accrual method from the accrual method, 

you will need to add journals tied to the Cash method for Accounts Payable and Account 

Receivable, as well as for other areas employed such as Order Entry, Employee Expenses, 

Credit Cards, and so on. 

• 
Further configuration steps are required in many application areas such as Accounts 

Payable, Accounts Receivable, and so on, to connect to the journals that have been created. 

Accomplishing the setup correctly will ensure accurate reporting. 

• 
A temporary “mock” journal is created and leveraged during the change-over, because 

some journals should remain Cash only or Accrual only. When you perform the 

change-over, all the configured journals are affected, so to ensure that past transactions 

aren’t changed, this mock journal needs to be used to replace the previous setup. The mock 

journal is used temporarily in the configuration for the subledger application areas 

(Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Cash Management, Time and Expenses, and any 

others). In a shared company, configure the multi-entity inter-company payments and 

receivables journals from the subscription console to use the mock journal as well. This 

allows you to freshly configure the system post-change for the new multi-book setup you 

have elected. 

---



#### Transaction Entry and Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 22*

Configuring the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Ensure that no journals are selected in your bank accounts, because those will also be 

updated. 

• 
When importing historical journal entries to account for legacy data, consider that data is 

now separately gathered for each accounting method with regard to opening balances. 

Thus, data imported must designate the accounting method impacted through the selection 

of the correct journal (associated to Cash or Accrual) to ensure all history is accurately 

captured in both reporting books. If you are converting from Accrual to Cash and Accrual, 

you will import Cash Basis opening balances (you already have the accrual opening 

balances). 

• 
Bank register reporting requires special attention: when you make the switch, the bank 

register pulls in the activity posted in both reporting books, essentially duplicating the 

numbers. In this case three journal entries are needed to correct the bank register. Also note 

it is recommended that this change only apply at the end of a reconciled period. 

• 
Integrations posting journal entries will also be impacted so also be sure to consider what 

integrations you have in place and how they should be configured going forward. 

Contact your RealPage trained consultant before making this change so that you can fully 

understand the impact and ensure proper deployment. 

Transaction Entry and Accounting Methods 

In most cases, entering transactions is the same, regardless of accounting method. For example, 

users entering a bill don’t need to know whether the transaction is accrual, cash, or both. The 

system handles the posting to accrual and cash journals “behind the scenes.” 

However, entering a journal entry directly in the General Ledger requires that you consider the 

accounting method(s) that should be affected and select the appropriate journal accordingly.

### Configuring Multi-Currency Management
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*



#### Configuring Multi-Currency Management
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Configuring the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring Multi-Currency Management 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Configuration > Accounting Settings > 
Multi-currency Management > Enable Multi-Currency Subscription`


Multi-Currency Subscription 

Select the Enable multi-currency subscription check box if your company uses multiple 

currencies. When you select this option, multi-currency options are turned on in other 

applications, and Company options for managing currencies. The other applications that support 

multi-currency include: Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Cash Management, and General 

Ledger. 

Configuring Multi-Currency Management 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Configuration > Accounting Settings > 
Multi-currency Management > Enable Multi-Currency Subscription`


To configure multi-currency management: 

1. 
Select the Enable multi-currency subscription check box in the Multi-currency management 

section. 

• 
Enabling multi-currency in a company is permanent. You can’t disable your 

multi-currency subscription after transactions are recorded in the system.  

• 
If any entity uses a different base currency, you must also configure your multi-entity 

console to enable multiple base currencies. 

• 
The system uses the RealPage Daily Rate to convert the currency of transactions up to 

20 years in the past. 

2. 
In the Rounding account drop-down list, create or select an expense account to be used for 

recording rounding differences during journal entry import. This rounding account keeps 

debits and credits in balance, if the rounding of base currency amounts causes a minor 

difference between debits and credits (typically, a penny). 

Here’s how it works: 

• 
During journal entry import, transaction amounts are converted to the base currency 

and rounded as required for that type of currency. 

• 
If the rounding process causes debits and credits to be out of balance, the system 

attempts to automatically balance the debit and credit line items. 

• 
If there’s a minor discrepancy (typically, a penny) that can’t be distributed across line 

items, the discrepancy is added as a debit or credit to the Rounding account. 

If a rounding entry was needed, it appears in the uploaded journal entry in the Automatic 

balancing entries section at the bottom of the page. 

---



#### Creating a Rounding General Ledger Account
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 25*

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Creating a Rounding General Ledger Account 

Create a rounding General Ledger account in the Multi-Currency Management section of the 

General Ledger setup page. The rounding account is used when importing journal entries, 

whenever converting to the base currency causes a rounding error. 

Here’s how it works: 

1. 
During journal entry import, the system converts transaction amounts to the base currency 

and rounds the amounts as required for that type of currency. 

2. 
If the rounding process causes debits and credits to be out of balance, the system attempts 

to balance the debit and credit line items automatically. 

3. 
If there’s a minor discrepancy that can’t be distributed across line items (typically, a penny), 

the discrepancy is added as a debit or credit to the Rounding account. 

If a rounding entry was needed, it appears in the uploaded journal entry in the Automatic 

balancing entries section at the bottom of the page. 

To create a rounding General Ledger account: 

1. 
On the General Ledger setup page, find the Multi-Currency Management section. 

2. 
Find the Rounding account section. 

3. 
Create or select an expense account for the system to use for recording rounding 

differences during journal entry import. This rounding account keeps debits and credits in 

balance, if the rounding of base currency amounts causes a minor difference between debits 

and credits (typically, a penny).

### Configuring Transactions in General Ledger Setup
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*

Configuring the General Ledger 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring Transactions in General Ledger Setup 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Configuration > Accounting Settings > 
Transactions`


To configure transactions: 

1. 
In the If future GL posting date section, select the desired system response when a user 

attempts to set a future period date as the General Ledger posting date.  

• 
Allow and do not warn: The user can proceed with the transaction without any 

warning. This is the default setting. 

• 
Allow and warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Do not allow: Displays a message requesting the user to select a date within the 

current period. 

The subledgers and general ledger share the same posting period. 

2. 
Select the Enable chart types check box to enable the chart types (on page 292) feature. 

3. 
Select the Enable transaction allocations in journal entry check box to create transaction 

allocation tables by percentage or fixed value. The General Ledger then automatically 

calculates and distributes values to departments and locations. 

For example, if you’re an Enterprise company that distributes insurance premium costs 

across several regional sales offices, you can choose a transaction allocation when paying 

the bill. The bill amount is then automatically distributed across the appropriate locations. 

In multi-entity companies, allocation is particularly useful when a corporate office manages 

the accounting for multiple entities, because corporate can automatically allocate bills 

without manually calculating each entity’s share. For example, a property management 

company could automatically divide the monthly cost of landscape maintenance 

proportionately to the square footage of each property. 

4. 
Select the Ignore closing rules for statistical entries check box to enable posting of 

non-financial data tracked with statistical accounts to closed periods. For example, if labor 

costing is turned off, you can use this in conjunction with Projects to post statistical labor 

hours to a closed period.

Configuring Reports and Budgets in the General Ledger 

Configuring the Financial Reports Section 

1.

to all users. 

• 
To make all new financial reports private, clear the Set default permissions to public 

check box. In this case, the creator’s user ID is set as the owner, and permission is 

denied to the group Everyone. Unless the report creator grants permission to others, 

no one else can access the report. 

• 
To make a financial report available to selected users on a case-by-case basis, edit the 

financial report, click the Permissions tab, and then add the users to whom you want 

to grant access to the Access list. 

This setting is company -wide, applying to all users. It can’t be set at the entity level. 

2. 
Select the Enable additional header titles check box to add a Title field to Department, 

Location, and Entity records, where you can enter additional header text. For example, you 

might include the office name, address, and manager for each location. 

3. 
Select the Enable reporting accounts labels check box 

“Reporting accounts” is an optional feature in the General Ledger that enables you to 

generate and display reports using other account sets, instead of your General Ledger 

accounts. This situation is most common for companies that have clients, owners, or other 

governing bodies who need to see reports in their own charts of accounts. 

You may benefit from reporting accounts if you have clients or owners with their own chart 

of accounts who need to view financial information. By turning on this option, you can: 

• 
Define alternate reporting account sets. Within each account set, you define the 

accounts to be used and how they map to your General Ledger accounts. 

• 
Let yourself or others display reports using different reporting account sets.

within each period. End of period uses a cumulative balance, which is not the best fit for 

budgeting.

For each entity that you want to see the source posting date in the General Ledger report:

Click the Edit link.  

• 
Find the Accounting section. 

• 
Select the Advance posting date check box. 

• 
Type the End of month day. This is the date that the system uses to determine the 

next open period. 

• 
Save the entity record. 

4. 
Click Save.

the feature in the back end. The source post date data is not available for journal entries

### Journals Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 48*

Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Journals Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Journals`


A journal contains a record of your company’s financial transactions. RealPage Accounting uses 

journals to categorize the transactions that you enter in the General Ledger and transactions that 

are posted from subledgers such as Accounts Payable. 

For multi-entity, shared companies: Journals are master objects, which can either be common 
(that is, accessible) to all entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific entity.

You can add as many journals as you need. After you’ve added a journal, it is available for you to 

enter journal entries through the General Ledger. It is also available to be used in the 

configuration of other applications. For example, you might create a Labor Cost journal to be 

used by the Job Cost application. 

Determining the Journals That You Need 

These journals are required: 

• 
Accounts Payable: A/P Invoices Journal, Adjustments Journal, and Payments Journal  

• 
Accounts Receivable: A/R Invoices Journal, Adjustments Journal, and Payments Journal 

• 
Cash Management: Other Receipts Journal  

If you opted for both accrual- and cash-based reporting, you need the following set of journals: 

Accounts Payable 

• 
A/P Invoices Journal - Cash 

• 
A/P Invoices Journal - Accrual 

• 
Adjustments Journal - Cash 

• 
Adjustments Journal - Accrual 

• 
Payments Journal - Cash and Accrual 

Accounts Receivable 

• 
A/R Invoices Journal - Cash 

• 
A/R Invoices Journal - Accrual 

• 
Adjustments Journal - Cash 

• 
Adjustments Journal - Accrual 

• 
Payments Journal - Cash and Accrual 

Cash Management 

• 
Other Receipts Journal - Cash and Accrual

### Transaction Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 54*

Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Transaction Lists 

See the How to get here topic for a list of paths to access transactions lists. 

Every journal has a transactions list associated with it, regardless of the journal type. The 

transactions list contains a journal’s entries. The transaction list is the central place to go to work 

with existing journal entries for a specific journal, or to add new entries to the journal.  

To access the transactions in a journal, open the desired journal, and then click the View 

transactions link. You can access all of the journals’ transaction lists from the All tab of the 

General Ledger with the exception of the statistical journals. To access statistical journals list, 

open the Setup tab of the menu, and then select Statistical. 

The names of transaction list are composed of the journal’s symbol and “Journal Transactions. ” 
transactions. For example, the General Journal Accrual journal has the symbol GJA, so the 
journal’s transactions list name is “GJA - Journal Transactions. ” The user-defined journal for 
CAM adjustments might be named “ADJ CAM - Journal Transactions. ”  

The transactions list has a standard set of functions, columns, and buttons. From a journal’s 

transactions list, you can: 

• 
Add a new entry to the journal. 

• 
Open an entry to view or change it. 

• 
Delete one entry or select multiple entries to delete. 

• 
Print a journal entry or select multiple journal entries to print. 

• 
Check the status of an entry. See which entries have been saved as a “draft” or “posted.” 

• 
Post one or multiple entries.  

If the Journal entry approval feature is enabled, then the Post button is replaced with the 

Submit button.  

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled on your system, you can: 

• 
Submit transactions for approval. 

• 
Recall a journal entry from the approval queue. You can recall a journal entry if you 

submitted the entry, you are not the approver, and the approver hasn’t approved the 

entry. 

• 
Duplicate an entry. 

• 
Reverse one or multiple entries. 

• 
Attach a supporting document to one or multiple entries.  

When an entry has an attachment, an 
 Attachment icon appears next to the Excel link. 
Click the 
 Attachment icon to open the Attachments page.

Journals

Deleting a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry > View Transactions > Delete`


You can delete a journal entry as long as the entry isn’t in a closed period. 

If you want a warning to appear before you attempt to delete a transaction, select the Warn on 

delete check box in your My preferences page. Click your sign-in name at the top of any page, and 
then select My preferences. 

To delete a journal entry:  

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select the Journal entry option. 

3. 
Find the desired journal, and then click the View Transactions link. The list of the journal’s 

transactions opens. 

4. 
Select the journal entry to delete by selecting the check box in the Delete column. 

5. 
Click the Delete button at the top of the page, and then click OK. 

GAAP Compliance Prevents Editing a Transaction in a Closed Period 
To ensure GAAP compliance and keep accurate audit trail activity and historical reporting, you 
cannot edit a transaction in a closed period.  
To make such a change: 
1. Re-open the book.  
2. Make the edits. 
3. Close the book again.

Adjustment Journals 

If you need to make adjustments to accounting periods that are already closed, then you must enter them as 

journal entries in an adjustment journal. Your Adjustment Journals list can contain as many or few adjustment 

journals as you need. 

When you create an adjusting entry, the entry posts to the cash and accrual books. If you have a business case 

that requires a cash-only or accrual-only adjustment journal, then create a user-defined journal and configure it as 

needed.

Deleting or Inactivating an Adjustment Journal 

If you no longer need a journal, you may be able to delete it or inactive it. 

• 
Deleting a journal removes it from the corresponding list. You can delete a journal only if 

there are no transactions in it. 

• 
Inactivating a journal hides it from the corresponding list. You can inactive a journal as long 

as it’s not being used in the configuration page of a service or application and there are no 

open (draft) transactions. 

• 
To inactivate a journal, edit the journal and change the Status to Inactive. 

• 
You can still display inactive journals at a later time by selecting the Show inactive 

check box at the top of the list.
