### Setup for GAAP (Compliance) or Tax Adjustments
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 72*



#### Setting Up GAAP (Compliance) and Tax Adjustment Journals
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 72*

GAAP (Compliance) Adjustment Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setup for GAAP (Compliance) or Tax Adjustments 

At the end of the fiscal year, companies reconcile their accounting for compliance requirements 

and tax rules. In the United States, accountants are required to comply with Generally Accepted 

Accounting Principles (GAAP). As a result of these reconciliations, adjustments are often made for 

compliance requirements (GAAP) and tax compliance. It’s usually desirable to post these 

adjustments without changing historical monthly amounts to maintain the integrity of the 

operational reporting.  

You can configure the General Ledger to include GAAP adjustment journals, tax adjustment 

journals, or both types of journals. By setting up GAAP and tax adjustment journals, you can: 

• 
Post GAAP and tax adjusting entries 

• 
Report on adjustments as needed in financial reports and other General Ledger reports. 

Because RealPage Accounting GAAP and tax adjustments are in separate reporting books, 

you can report on adjustments separately or in combination with other books, such as your 

Accrual book. 

Setting Up GAAP (Compliance) and Tax Adjustment Journals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > GAAP Adjustment`


If your company hasn’t already enabled GAAP or Tax adjustment journals, you can set them up 

with the following steps. 

Step 1. Enable GAAP and Tax in the General Ledger 

In the configuration for the General Ledger, you can enable either or both types of adjustment 

journals. When you enable GAAP and Tax adjustment journals, the system adds separate lists for 

GAAP Adjustment Journals and Tax Adjustment Journals and treats the journals that you add to 

the lists as being part of separate reporting books. 

To enable GAAP and Tax adjustment journals 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
In the Accounting settings section, under GAAP and tax, enable the type of adjustment 

journals you need. 

You can enable GAAP adjustment journals, enable tax adjustment journals, or enable both 

types of journals. 

4. 
Review the options for how adjustments are treated at the end of the fiscal year. 

It’s recommended that keep the default selection to Keep adjustments separate from 

accrual or cash. 

Learn more about the options for GAAP and Tax in the General Ledger (on page 5). 

---


<!-- Page 73 -->
Chapter 4: GAAP (Compliance) Adjustment Journals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Step 2. Grant Permissions To Yourself and Other Users 

You and other users can work with the journals only if you’ve been granted the corresponding 

permissions in the General Ledger. There are separate permissions for the journals and for 

entering adjustments in the journals. This enables you to, for instance, enter transactions to 

journals. 

To locate the permissions for GAAP and Tax adjustments: 

1. 
Display the user’s permissions for the General Ledger. 

If you’re using role-based permissions, edit the user’s role, and then edit the permissions for 

the General Ledger. 

2. 
In the General Ledger Permissions page, grant permissions related to the GAAP and Tax 

adjustments. 

The complete list of permissions includes: 

• 
Tax Adjustment Journals 

• 
GAAP Adjustment Journals 

• 
Tax Adjusting Entries 

• 
GAAP Adjusting Entries 

Granting permission for GAAP, Tax, and user-defined books enables the user to enter transactions 

into these books. However, all users with access to General Ledger reports will be able to see the 

data in the books, even if not granted specific permissions for them. There’s no user access 

restriction to data for user-defined books, GAAP, or Tax books. 

Accrual, cash, GAAP, Tax, and user-defined book transactions can be seen by users with access to 

General Ledger reporting. Users with G/L reporting permissions are allowed to view data in 

journals or books in the reports. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 82*

GAAP (Compliance) Adjustment Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide

GAAP (Compliance) Adjusting Entries 

At the end of the fiscal year, companies reconcile their accounting for compliance (GAAP) 

requirements. As a result of these reconciliations, adjustments are often made for compliance. It’s 

usually desirable to post these adjustments without changing historical monthly amounts to 

maintain the integrity of the operational reporting. Examples of these adjustments are 

depreciation, amortization, and tax liability. 

GAAP Memorized Transactions List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Adjusting Entry > GAAP Adjusting > Memorized 
Transactions`


Memorized transactions are recurring transactions whose amounts and other details can vary 

from month to month. For example, you might set up a memorized transaction for payroll, which 

you plan to post to the Accounts Payable journal on a regular basis. With a memorized 

transaction, you enter a description for the transaction and other basic information, such as the 

accounts and dimensions to use, only once. Each time the transaction recurs, you can edit the 

transaction header and line items as needed before posting the transaction. 

Use the compliance standards (GAAP) memorized transactions list to: 

• 
Draft a memorized transaction. 

• 
Post a memorized transaction. 

• 
Post and reverse memorized transactions. 

• 
Add a memorized transaction. 

• 
Export the list of compliance standards (GAAP) memorized transactions. 

---



#### Adding a GAAP (Compliance) Adjusting or Tax Adjusting Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 83*

Chapter 4: GAAP (Compliance) Adjustment Journals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Adding a GAAP (Compliance) Adjusting or Tax Adjusting Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Adjusting Entry > 
 GAAP 
Adjusting/ Tax Adjusting`


The entire transaction must balance. You cannot save out-of-balance transactions. An 

out-of-balance transaction is one in which you did not enter required information. If you try to 

save an out-of-balance transaction, the system displays an error message. 

You can substantiate a transaction by associating it with a supporting document that has attached 

files.  

To add a GAAP or Tax adjusting entry: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section, under Entries, click Adjusting entry, and then select the 

Add button next to GAAP adjusting or Tax adjusting. 

If you are using non-standard accounting periods, you can’t save a G/L transaction that 
falls outside the accounting periods you have defined. 

3. 
Click the View transactions link for the journal to which you want to add a transaction, and 

then click the Add button.

Statistical Journal Entries List in a Multi-Entity 

In multi-entity companies, transaction lists at the entity level include transactions created at the 

top level that have been tagged to your entity. However, if no transactions have been posted in 

the last six months that fit this criterion, then entity-level transaction lists only show entity-level 

transactions. If you want to see older transactions created at the top level for your entity, then 

select the Include top level transactions check box at the top of your list. 

Statistical journals are master objects. They can either be common (that is, accessible) to all 

entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific entity.

Setting Up Statistical Data Tracking 

Statistical accounts are used to track non-financial data, such as: 

• 
Number of contracts 

• 
Number of hotel rooms, hospital beds, or apartment units 

• 
Square footage 

This chapter describes how to set up the system to capture statistical data. After you’ve set up accounts, journals, 

and account groups for your statistical data, you can: 

• 
Enter transactions that keep track of your statistical data, such as the number of employees by location and 

department. 

• 
Report on your statistical data; for example, creating financial reports that show the headcount per location 

by quarter. 

• 
Create calculations that highlight important metrics, such as revenue per employee.

Setting Up Statistical Data Tracking

Statistical Tracking Setup Workflow 

To set up the system to track statistical data, complete each of the following steps: 

1. 
Accounts: (on page 89) Set up accounts for each type of non-financial data you want to 

track. 

2. 
Journals: (on page 89) Create one journal for posting all statistical entries, or create a 

separate journal for each statistical account. 

3. 
Account Groups: (on page 90) Accounts must be rolled into account groups before you can 

use them for reporting and other purposes. 

After you have completed these steps, do the following: 

1. 
Enter statistical data. You enter statistical transactions in the same way that you enter G/L 

transactions. The only difference is that statistical transactions do not need to balance. 

Instead, you increase or decrease a value. For example, you might increase the number of 

fleet vehicles in the month of June because you hired two more employees. In this case, you 

would use the Fleet statistical account and the journal you created for tracking the fleet. 

Learn more about Statistical journal entries (on page 419). 

2. 
Use dimension count to automate tracking statistical data.

### Automated Dimension Count Posting
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 101*

Chapter 6: Setting Up Statistical Data Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Automated Dimension Count Posting 

Statistical accounts are often used to track the number of dimension members. For example, it’s 

common to track the number of active customers. This information can be reported on by itself or 

used to compute metrics such as the recurring revenue per customer. 

You can: 

• 
Automate counts for any enabled dimension. As you add or remove dimension members, 

the count is automatically updated. 

• 
Set up rules that define what you want to count. For example, in addition to tracking the 

number of active customers, you might set up a separate statistical account for tracking 

different customer types. 

About Dimension Counts 

There are many reasons for automating the dimension count to a statistical account. It saves time 

and effort—especially when you are tracking many dimensions and can increase insight into your 

business. 

Manual vs. Automated Posting 

Your company might already use multiple spreadsheets to track changes for various things like 

new, lost, and long-time customers. With the dimension count posting feature, the system 

updates dimension counts automatically, reducing the need for manual spreadsheets that are 

time-consuming and sometimes error prone. 

You can still post changes manually—for example, when establishing a base count—but 

automating the count eliminates data-entry work by reducing the steps needed to update the 

count accurately and immediately. 

Use in Metrics 

Finely tuned metrics increase insight into your business and provide greater detail when you are 

making business decisions. By providing a way to automate counts, dimension count gives you 

flexibility to ensure that your metrics are appropriate and accurate. 

To increase the granularity of business metrics, analysis, or reporting, different posting rules 

update different statistic counts. You can use the values in computational reports and 

performance cards to increase insight into how your company is doing. 

Dimension counts use a separate dimension group for each dimension rule you create. There is 

no limit to the number of things that can be tracked automatically. 

---


<!-- Page 102 -->
Setting Up Statistical Data Tracking 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setup Overview 

A dimension must be enabled for dimension counts to work. For example, to use the 
Locations 
dimension count, the Location dimension must be active. If you don’t see a particular dimension 
count, verify that the dimension is enabled in Dimension settings. 

The dimension count setup process requires admin privileges and requires setting up a statistical 

account for each dimension count and then defining the rules for posting. Creating a dimension 

count rule is a one-time process. After that, dimension count changes are automatic and don’t 

need any further action. 

For example, you might create a rule to update the count of active customers based in Vermont 

who have a high credit limit. Any time a customer moves into that group, the dimension count 

rule creates a statistical journal entry to increase the count. If a customer moves out of the group, 

then the same dimension count rule creates an entry to decrease the count. 

Best practice: If you’ve already set up a dimension count rule, then don’t disable the dimension. 
Disabling the dimension can cause unexpected behavior. 

For step-by-step setup instructions, refer to Set up dimension count. 

Functionality of Automated Posting 

1. 
Create statistical accounts and dimension groups for dimension count to use. 

2. 
Establish the initial base value of the count, such as the customer count as of the date you 

begin automated posting. 

3. 
As you create the dimension count rules, the system automatically monitors increases and 

decreases and posts journal entries to the statistical journal. 

Establishing a Base Count 

When you enable dimension count, only new updates are included in statistical account updates. 

The existing dimension objects are not included, even if they match the dimension count criteria. 

Enter a manual journal entry to the statistical account to establish a beginning balance as a 

starting point. This step is optional, but if you don’t establish a base count, then the count starts 

at zero and only new changes are recorded. There is no historical starting point. 

In many cases, the company could be maintaining a spreadsheet with the information you want to 

track. After a base count is included in the statistical account, you might be able to get rid of 

these spreadsheets and let the system track and count for you. 

---


<!-- Page 103 -->
Chapter 6: Setting Up Statistical Data Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

For details on manual journal entries, refer to Statistical journal entries (on page 419). 

Functionality of Dimension Count Updates 

After a dimension count is set up, the system automatically posts entries when you create and 

save a new object or delete an object that matches the rule. You can’t create an automated post 

for a previous period. 

For example, if you created a customer record on 12/2/2019, then the customer count is 

increased for the date of 12/2/2019, the date that the record was created. Because the count 

update is automated, the transaction date is not configurable in the dimension count rules. 

Adding Counts to the Previous Period 

Continuing the example, suppose that this customer signed the deal on 11/26/2019. In this case, 

you want the customer count to be posted and counted for the month of November, even 

though the customer record wasn’t created until December, but the system would post the record 

for December. You can’t edit any of the system-posted record counts. This preserves the business 

rule audit trail. However, you can manually adjust the count to November by both increasing the 

count with 11/26/2019 and decreasing the count with 12/2/2019 accordingly. 

As you create new dimension count rules, newly created objects that match the rules are posted 

to the journal and added to the statistical account. Existing objects that match the dimension 

count rules are not added, only new objects are. Deleting a rule doesn’t remove the object from 

the statistical account count, but new count changes aren’t updated automatically. 

Editing a Dimension Record That Is Used by Dimension Count 

When you make a change to a record that is used by dimension count, the appropriate journal 

entry is updated at that time. Record changes are made the same way you change any other 

record for that dimension. 

For example, suppose you have a vendor who is included in the dimension group for California 

vendors and is part of a dimension count rule. If this vendor moved to another state, you would 

change the vendor record to reflect the new address. When you change the record, the 

appropriate changes are made by dimension count: the count of California vendors is decreased 

by one. If there is a dimension group/rule for the new state, then that count is increased by one. 

There is one exception to this: employee records and location. 

Special Case: Changing an Employee Location in a Multi-Entity Company 

For multi-entity companies, the employee record requires a location. This tells the system which 

entity the employee belongs with. If you change the location of an employee from one entity to 

another, then the record is changed correctly. But because the dimension count gets the location 

from the employee record, dimension count handles the change a bit differently, and that affects 

how the count is changed. 

---


<!-- Page 104 -->
Setting Up Statistical Data Tracking 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Best practice: To ensure that the count is correct for both the original and the new location, many 

companies find that the following steps are helpful. 

1. 
Make the employee inactive to remove the count from original location. 

2. 
While the employee is still inactive, change the employee location. 

3. 
Set the employee record back to active. 

Alternatively, you can make statistical journal entries manually to reduce the original employee by 

location count by one and add the employee by location count by one. 

The following examples show some of the possible uses of dimension count. 

Customer Retention Rate 

Automate the count of new customers you acquired for a period, how many existing customers 

stayed, and how many customers left. Count by total customers or filter further, such as by 

location or salesperson. 

Suppose you started out with 365 customers for a period. Over the period you added ten new 

customers but lost three. Rather than just reporting that you now have 372 customers, dimension 

count automates the count, making it available for reports. 

Customer Count by Customer Type 

Using dimension count makes it easy to automatically track by customers of a certain type or 

industry—anything from direct and retail sales, by ZIP Code range, state, or country. Knowing how 

many customers of different types can help your company make business decisions. 

Employee Retention 

One of the most important assets a company has is its employees. You need to know not just how 

many employees the company has at a certain period, but how many are new, how many have 

left, and even how long the average employee stays with the company. You can break it down 

even further and see which locations or departments have higher or lower attrition rates at a 

glance. Dimension count can automate that information for inclusion in reports. 

---

Saving and Submitting 

When you add a transaction to an adjustment journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft 

or submitting it right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be 

complete—you or another user can review them later, make changes, and then submit them. 

When you submit a journal entry, the entire transaction must balance, and all required 

information must be entered. 

When you finish entering or editing the transaction information, click one of the buttons: 

• 
Submit: Submits this journal entry to be approved.  

• 
Draft: Saves this journal entry without submitting it for approval or posting it.  

• 
Submit & New: Submits this journal entry for approval, and then creates another blank 

statistical adjusting journal entry record. 

• 
Draft & New: Saves the progress on this journal entry without posting it. Later, you or 

another user can review the entry and post it. The system displays another blank statistical 

adjusting journal entry record.

### Tax Adjustment
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 124*

Tax Adjustment Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Tax Adjustment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > 
 Tax Adjustment`


Use the Tax adjustment journals page to create new journals for tax entries. At the end of the 

fiscal year, companies reconcile their accounting for Generally Accepted Accounting Principles 

(GAAP) and tax rules. As a result of these reconciliations, adjustments are often made for GAAP 

and Tax compliance. It’s usually desirable to post these adjustments without changing historical 

monthly amounts to maintain the integrity of the operational reporting. Examples of these 

adjustments are depreciation, amortization, and tax liability 

You can configure the General Ledger to include GAAP adjustment journals, Tax adjustment 

journals, or both types of journals. By setting up GAAP and Tax adjustment journals, you can: 

• 
Post GAAP and Tax adjusting entries  

• 
Report on adjustments as needed in financial reports and other General Ledger reports. 

Because the system treats GAAP and Tax adjustments as separate reporting books, you can 

report on adjustments separately or in combination with other books, such as your Accrual 

book.

assigns a unique ID to the attachment and the attachment has the same 

ID across the transactions that it is attached to.  

If you make changes to the attachment, it changes the attachment for all 

of the transactions that it is attached to with the same attachment ID.  

Attachments are allowed only on transactions that are directly 
posted to the General Ledger. If the transactions were posted to a 
subledger, the system displays an error message:

### Setting Up User-Defined Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 146*



#### Enabling User-Defined Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 146*



#### Granting Permissions to User-Defined Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 146*

User-Defined Books and Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up User-Defined Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > User-Defined Books`


User-defined books give you a way to manage different reporting standards, beyond what’s 

available with GAAP and Tax books. After enabled in the General Ledger, you can create one or 

more reporting books that you use to track specialized journal entries that are separate from your 

actual books. For example, a property management firm might create a “Real Estate” book for 

tracking and reporting on journal entries specific to that industry. 

This topic walks you through the process of setting up user-defined books, from enabling it in the 

General Ledger to defining books and journals. If you’re new to user-defined books, we 

recommend that you start with our introduction. 

Workflow 

1. 
Enable user-defined books in the General Ledger (on page 136). 

2. 
Grant permissions to users (on page 136). 

3. 
Define a book (on page 137). 

4. 
Define a journal. 

Enabling User-Defined Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Configuration`


To enable user-defined books in the General Ledger: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
Scroll to the Advanced G/L options section, and then select the Enable user-defined books 

check box. 

4. 
Click Save. 

Granting Permissions to User-Defined Books 

You and other users can work with user-defined books and journals if you’ve been granted the 

corresponding permissions in the General Ledger. There are separate permissions for 

user-defined books, journals, and journal entries. For instance, you can give someone permission 

to enter transactions into user-defined books, but not necessarily to add journal entries to the 

book. 

To locate the permissions related to user-defined books: 

1. 
Display the user’s permissions for the General Ledger. 

---



#### Creating a User-Defined Book
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 147*

Chapter 9: User-Defined Books and Journals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

If you’re using role-based permissions, edit the user’s role, and then edit the permissions for 

the General Ledger. 

2. 
In the General Ledger Permissions page, grant permissions related to user-defined books. 

The complete list of permissions includes: 

• 
User-Defined Books  

• 
User-Defined Journals 

• 
User-Defined Journal Entries 

Granting permission for compliance, tax, and user-defined books enables the user to enter 

transactions into these books. However, all users with access to General Ledger reports can see 

the data in the books, even if they are not granted specific permissions for them. There’s no user 

access restriction to data for user-defined, compliance, or tax books. 

Accrual, cash, compliance, tax, and user-defined book transactions can be seen by users with 

access to General Ledger reporting. Users with G/L reporting permissions are allowed to access 

data in journals or books in the reports. 

Creating a User-Defined Book 

To add a new book, just give it an ID and a description. You can add as many user-defined books 

as you need for reporting purposes. 

To add a user-defined book: 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Display the list of user-defined books (General Ledger > Setup > More > User-defined`


books). 

2. 
Click the Add button to add a new book. 

3. 
Enter a book ID in the Book ID field. Choose an ID that will be meaningful to you at 

reporting time. The Book ID appears in the list of “Other books” when you create financial 

reports or other General Ledger reports. 

4. 
Type a description in the Description field. 

5. 
Optionally, select the Management reporting check box to allow this book to bypass closed 

periods. 

Management reporting books don’t impact your actual books. Furthermore, you can only 
configure user-defined journals (on page 142 ) to post to management reporting books. 
Subledgers, such as Accounts Payable, can ’t post to management books. 

---



#### Creating Financial Reports That Feature Other Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 148*

User-Defined Books and Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Creating Financial Reports That Feature Other Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Reporting > Financial Reports`


In financial reports, you can specify the books to include on a column-by-column basis. You make 

your selections on the Columns tab of the financial report writer. 

For example, the following report includes columns for Accrual, a user-defined book named Real 

Estate, and GAAP. The final column combines the amounts from all selected books. 

a) Accrual book 

b) User-defined book: Real estate book 

c) GAAP book 

d) Combined: Accrual + Real Estate + GAAP books 

To select the reporting books to include in each column: 

1. 
Start by defining the financial report as usual. Go to the Financial Reports list (General 


> **Navigation Path:** `Ledger > All > Financial Reporting > Financial Reports).`


2. 
Add a new financial report or edit an existing one. 

3. 
On the Columns tab of the report definition, scroll down to the Reporting books section of 

the column. 

4. 
Verify the main reporting book that is listed. 

• 
By default, each column is set to report on the book selected on the Filters tab. 

• 
If you opted for dual-method reporting (accrual and cash), you can select a different 

main reporting book. 

5. 
Select any combination of Other books. 

---



#### Creating Standard General Ledger Reports That Feature Other Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 149*

Chapter 9: User-Defined Books and Journals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

• 
When you click the Edit books button, you can select one or more books to include. 

• 
At the same time, you can select whether you want to include amounts from the main 

reporting book. For example, if you include your Accrual book with your GAAP book, 

the report will show Accrual amounts with the GAAP adjustments applied. 

Including or Excluding the Main Reporting Book 

By default, amounts from the main reporting book are included to create a combined amount. 

However, there are times when you might want to clear this option. For example, suppose that 

your GAAP adjustments equal $-1,000 and the accrual amount is $10,000.00.  

What you want to see in the column determines whether to include or exclude the main reporting 

book.  

• 
To see just the GAAP adjustments, include only the GAAP book and exclude the Accrual 

book (the main reporting book).  

The resulting figure is $-1,000.  

• 
To see the GAAP and accrual amount combined, include both the GAAP and Accrual books.  

The resulting figure is $9,000. 

Creating Standard General Ledger Reports That Feature Other Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > [select a report]`


When you create a standard G/L report such as a General Ledger report, you can specify which 

books to include. Your selections are then applied to the entire report. 

To select the books to include on a standard General Ledger report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select the type of report you want to run. 

2. 
In the Filters section, verify the main Reporting book that is listed. 

---



#### Book Information Page
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 150*

User-Defined Books and Journals 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you opted for dual-method reporting (Accrual and Cash) or if your company uses multiple 
currencies and you use the Global Consolidations application to translate your currencies, 
you can select a different main reporting book. 

3. 
Select any combination of Other books. 

4. 
Decide whether to combine amounts from your main Reporting book with the Other 

books. 

By default, amounts from all books are combined together. For example, if you include your 

GAAP book with your accrual book, the report will show accrual amounts with the GAAP 

adjustments applied. 

Including or Excluding the Main Reporting Book 

By default, amounts from the main reporting book are included to create a combined amount. 

However, there are times when you might want to clear this option. For example, suppose that 

your GAAP adjustments equal -$1,000.00 and the Accrual amount is $10,000.00. 

What you want to see in the column determines whether to include or exclude the main reporting 

book.  

• 
To see just the GAAP adjustments, include only the GAAP book, and exclude the Accrual 

(the main reporting book).  

The resulting figure is -$1,000.00. 

• 
To see the GAAP and Accrual amount combined, include both the GAAP and Accrual books.  

The resulting figure is $9,000.00. 

Book Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > 
 User-Defined Books`


Use this page to create a new book, assign it an ID, and give it a description. 

If you select the Management reporting check box, the user-defined books act as a management 

reporting book, meaning it bypasses closed periods and can stack on top of your actual books 

when you run reports. 

Management reporting books don’t impact your actual books. Furthermore, you can only 

configure user-defined journals and the Software Digital Board Book to post to management 

reporting books. Subledgers, such as Accounts Payable, can’t post to management reporting 

books. 

You can’t edit this field after a user -defined book has been created, whether the option was 
selected or not.

Include job cost: To create a journal entry that has both job cost and standard line items, 

select this option. 

If you select the Include job cost option, you can split the debit and credit line items 
between standard line items and job cost line items. 

Attaching a Document to the Journal Entry 

The Documents section appears on a journal entry when scanning is enabled for your system. If 

scanning is not enabled, use the Attachments field in the top section of the Journal entries page. 

Before you begin, you must have permission to work with attachments. Learn more about who 

can add attachments in Permissions for attachments (on page 341). You can then upload a 

scanned image, spreadsheet, or word processor document as an attachment. 

To attach a document: 

1. 
Click the Choose file button, and then find the file that you want to attach. 

2. 
Double-click the desired file to select it. If you accidentally select the wrong file, you can 

detach it by clicking the Choose File button again. 

3. 
Click the Attach button.  

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 
attach the file to this record. See Attachments . 

To scan a document to attach to the journal entry: 

1. 
In the File name field, type a name for the file that you are creating when you scan in the 

document. 

2. 
Click the Scan button. 

Selecting Default Information for All Line Items (Optional) 

In the Entries section, you can add values directly to each line item where needed, or click the 

Show defaults link to open the Defaults section where you can specify default values for the line 

item fields.  

Select default values for each desired field to complete each line item. 

To set up a value as a default for each existing and new line item, click the drop-down beside the 

appropriate field, and choose a value.

Entering Line Items 

For the entry to be posted, you must specify at least the account and a debit or credit value for

1.

drop-down list.  

• 
To use an account that is not yet in the system, click Add, type the account details, and 

then click Save.  

To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

In the Txn Currency drop-down list, select the currency used for this transaction. This field 

appears only when your system is set up for multiple currencies. 

3.

transaction. 

A single line can have a value in only one of these fields.

As you enter debits and credits, the journal entry automatically enters net debit or credit 

amounts and keeps a running total in the Total boxes at the bottom of the section. This 

helps you enter large numbers of journal entry lines efficiently and helps ensure a balanced 

entry. 

If the journal entry is the Both type, debits and credits are separated between standard and 

Job Cost line items. 

Debit and Credit fields appear when your system is a single currency system. 

Transaction debit and Transaction credit fields appear when your system is set up for 

multiple currencies. When you fill in one of these fields, the system fills in the corresponding 

Base debit or Base credit field automatically.

Finishing the Journal Entry 

When you finish entering or editing the journal entry: 

• 
If journal entry approvals are disabled, you can either save the transaction as a draft or post 

it. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the entry without posting it. Later, 

you or another user can review the entry and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the journal entry. 

• 
You can also click the More actions button and then select Post and Print to post the 

journal entry and then print the record. 

• 
If journal entry approvals are enabled, submit the journal entry for approval. 

• 
Click Submit to send the journal entry to the approval queue.  

• 
Click Submit & new to submit the journal entry to the approval queue, and then open 

a new journal entry. 

After a journal entry transaction has been approved and posted, editing the entry is not 
allowed and the Edit link isn’t available. To make any changes, reverse the transaction or 
delete it and resubmit it. After the period is closed, no changes are allowed to the entry, 
including reversal and deletion.

### Budget Variance Analysis Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 170*

Budget Variance Analysis Configuration 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Budget Variance Analysis Overview 

Understanding financial variances to the budget will improve a property manager’s ability to 

reduce waste, seize opportunities to increase income, and forecast in changing environments.  

A budget variance is the difference between the amount that you budgeted for and the actual 

amount that you spent. 

The budget variance analysis feature can assist your company in achieving business targets by 

identifying areas of concern and opportunities for improvement.  

To use this feature, first, you open analysis periods for one property or multiple properties across 

your portfolio. Next, you generate a Budget Variance Analysis report to list the actual and 

budgeted amounts of accounts and the variance between the two. Optionally, you can also use 

the budget variance analysis feature to view and make comments in the Budget Variance Analysis 

report. You can then print or export the report, complete with your notes to share with others. 

Budget Variance Analysis Configuration Workflow 

Configuring Budget Variance Analysis is a multi-step process: 

1. 
Configure the permissions of users who you want to give Budget Variance Analysis abilities. 

See Before You Begin (on page 161) for the list of permissions required. 

2. 
Create a role or a user group to notify when a budget variance analysis is complete (on 

page 162). 

3. 
Update user records to allow them to perform budget variance analysis (on page 163). 

4. 
Configure budget variance rules (on page 167). 

After configuring the system for Budget Variance Analysis, get started by opening a period for 

analysis. See Opening a new analysis period (on page 433) in the online help system or download 

(on page 480) the RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide.

Creating Groups of Users for BVA Notifications 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > 
 Groups`


Supervisors need to know when a Site User marks a budget variance analysis (BVA) complete.  

You can either define a user group or a role for system users who need to be notified when a BVA 

is complete. If you have M-Console users who are BVA supervisors, you must define a role for 

them so that they can receive BVA notifications. If your system does not use the M-console, then 

define a user group.  

To notify supervisory users when a user completes a BVA with a role, create the role, and then 

assign the role to each supervisory user. 

To notify supervisory users when a user completes a BVA with a user group, create the user 

group, and then add the supervisory users who you want to notify to the group. 

Creating the User Group for BVA Supervisors 

To create a user group for budget variance analysis supervisors: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to Groups. 

3. 
In the Name field, type a name for the group, such as “BVA Supers.” 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description of the group, such as “This is a group of people 

who can review BVA analyses.”

#### Adding Budget Variance Rules

Adding Budget Variance Rules 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > 
 Budget Variance Analysis`


Configuring the Budget Variance Analysis feature involves creating variance rules that determine 

whether the budget variance is favorable or unfavorable, and whether the budget variance falls 

within or outside of that defined rule. You can set up budget variance analysis configurations for 

multiple locations.  

The purpose of a budget variance analysis rule is to allow one rule to apply to multiple locations. 

To configure a budget variance rule: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to Budget variance analysis. The Budget variance analysis 

configuration information page opens. 

3. 
In the Configuration name field, type a name for this configuration. 

4. 
Select the scope of the budget variance analyses in the Reporting time frame drop-down 

list, Monthly or Quarterly. 

5. 
In the Reporting account group name drop-down list, select an account or account group 

to which to restrict the user when performing budget variance analyses. 

Reporting account sets, statistical, computation, category, and statistical category 
account group types are not available for Budget Variance Analysis. 

6. 
In the Locations drop-down list, select one or more locations (on page 373) that you want 

to measure with this budget variance check. 

7. 
Set up a budget in the Budget Override field when you need to compare actuals to a 

budget that is not the default budget. 

8. 
In the Book drop-down list, select the book, Cash or Accrual, that you want to analyze 

budget variance for. 

---


<!-- Page 178 -->
Budget Variance Analysis Configuration 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

9. 
Select the Favorable variances require explanation check box. When selected, a favorable 

variance requires an explanation even if it exceeds variance rules in the positive or negative 

depending on the expense or revenue. When cleared, a favorable variance does not require 

explanation. 

10. 
Select the Calculate fiscal properties as calendar check box if any of your entities are 

running on a different fiscal year other than the regular calendar year, but you want to 

calculate the budget variance analysis year-to-date amounts based on the calendar. 

Filling In the Variance Rules Section 

1. 
In the Period variance type drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
Percent or amount: Select this option to set a threshold expressed as a percentage or 

an amount of currency for the reporting period. You can enter either a percentage or 

an amount. If you choose to enter both values, then either value is accepted. 

• 
Percent but at least amount: Select this option to enter both a percent value and an 

amount value. Both values must be a match before the system deems the threshold to 

be met. 

2. 
In the Period variance percent field, type the threshold percentage for the variance during a 

reporting period. 

3. 
In the Period variance amount field, type the threshold amount for the period. 

4. 
In the YTD variance type drop-down list, select an option. 

Percent or amount: Select this option to set a threshold expressed as a percentage or an 

amount of currency for the year to date. 

Percent but at least amount: Select this option if you want to set a threshold percentage or 

a threshold amount as a minimum amount in currency for the year to date. 

5. 
In the YTD variance percent field, type the threshold percentage for the year to date. 

6. 
In the YTD variance amount field, type the threshold amount for the year to date. 

• 
If you set a variance threshold for an account group, the threshold applies to all accounts in 

that group. 

• 
If you set a variance threshold for a group of account groups, the threshold applies to all 

account groups and accounts in that group of groups.

•

then import it. For information, see Importing Users’ Budget Variance Analysis Configuration.

### Accrual Templates Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 192*

Accrual Templates 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accrual Templates Overview 

The system uses the information in accrual templates to identify the invoices to suggest for 

accrual, where to record accruals, the location associated with the invoices, and information that 

helps to categorize the post accrual journal entry including dimensions and segments. 

To use the automated accruals feature, create accrual templates for your company’s typical 

accruals. When you access the Accruals Workbench, you select the template to use, and then the 

system retrieves the invoices that are candidates for accrual.  

The system allows you to base an accrual template on one of three types of transactions:  

• 
Invoices advanced 

• 
Invoices not received 

• 
G/L postings advanced 

You can create multiple accrual templates. For example, you can create an accrual template for 

each accrual type for each location.

Accrual Configuration 

RealPage Accounting lets you choose accrual criteria and save the criteria in a template.  

The system uses an accrual template to generate a list of transactions that are candidates for 

accruing, and then display the candidates in the Accruals workbench. There are three kinds of 

accruals for which you can create templates.

#### Adding an Accrual Template for Invoices Advanced
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 196*

Accrual Templates 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding an Accrual Template for Invoices Advanced 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Accrual Template > Add > Invoices Advanced`


Use the Invoices Advanced accrual type template to have the system calculate accruals based on 

invoices that have been advanced to the first of the next month when calculating the accrual. An 

invoice is considered advanced when the posting date is the first of the month after the accrual 

period and the invoice date is prior to that date. 

To create the accrual template for advanced invoices: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Click the Add button. 

4. 
Type a unique identifier for the accrual in the Accrual ID field. 

5. 
By default, the status is set to Active. If you want to prevent this accrual template from 

being used, select Inactive.  

6. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location for which you want to create scheduled 

accruals. When the user selects an accrual to calculate and post, the system only calculates 

for the locations that the user has access to. 

Filling In the Accrual Type Section  

1. 
In the Accrual type drop-down list, select Invoices Advanced. 

2. 
To define the range of accounts to have the system check for advance invoices, select the 

first account in the range in the Account from drop-down list, and then select the last 

account in the range in the Account to drop-down list. 

The system identifies candidates for accrual by identifying the expenses from invoices that 

fall within the account range that you choose here. 

Filling In the Accounting Section 

1. 
In the Book drop-down list, select the book where you want to store accruals. If your system 

has enabled GAAP (Compliance), then it appears in the list with the Accrual and Tax books. 

The system uses the next three selections (journal, debit account, and credit account) to 

create the journal entry so that the system can post accruals. 

2. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want to store accrual records. 

The system includes the journals in the book that you selected.  

Cash-only journals are not available for selection. 

3. 
In the Credit account drop-down list, select the account that you want the system to use for 

this accrual’s journal entries. 

---


<!-- Page 197 -->
Chapter 11: Accrual Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Filling In the Description Section 

The system includes the text that you enter in this section in the journal entry that it posts for the 

accrual. 

1. 
In the Description field, type a description of this accrual template. 

2. 
In the Reference number field, type any reference number that you want to record with this 

accrual template. 

3. 
In the Attachment drop-down list, you can associate a document in the system to support 

the accrual transaction. You can also upload a new file into the system by clicking the 

Choose Files button. You can attach any type of file to the accrual, including scanned 

images, spreadsheets, and word-processor documents. Attached files are uploaded to the 

system for permanent, safe storage. Learn more about who can add attachments in 

Permissions for attachments (on page 341). 

• 
Show all/Show unattached: Click this link to toggle between showing all existing files 

in the system and showing only files that are not attached to any other record in the 

system. 

• 
Add: Click to upload a file on your computer into the system. 

• 
View: Click this link to open the highlighted file.  

• 
Find: Click this link to search the files in the system. 

• 
Click the 
 Attachment button to view the attachment.  

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 
attach the file to this record. See Adding attachments . 

The next few fields appear depending on your environment’s dimensions and segments if 

enabled. 

4. 
Make selections in the dimensions and segments based on how you want to track the 

accrual transactions with reporting. 

5. 
Click Save. You can also click the More Actions button, select Save & New to save this 

accrual template, and then open a new blank accrual template.

#### Adding an Accrual Template for Invoices Not Received

Adding an Accrual Template for Invoices Not Received 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Accrual Template > Add > Invoices Not 
Received`


Use the Invoices Not Received accrual type to have the system look for prior invoices from a 

vendor when calculating the accrual. You can choose between the last invoice amount, the 

average amount of the last three invoices, or define a fixed amount. 

To add an accrual template for invoices that have not been received: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger application. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Click the Add button. 

4. 
Type a unique identifier for the accrual in the Accrual ID field. 

5. 
By default, the status is set to Active. If you want to prevent this accrual template from 

being used, select Inactive.  

6. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location for which you want to create scheduled 

accruals. When the user selects an accrual to calculate and post, the system calculates only 

for the locations that the user has access to. 

Filling In the Accrual Type Section 

1. 
Select the Invoices Not Received option. 

2. 
Select the vendor from which you are expecting to receive invoices.  

3. 
In the Calculated based on section, select the value to use for the calculation:  

• 
Last invoice amount: Select this option to base the calculation on the amount of the 

last invoice that you received from this vendor. 

• 
Average amount of last three invoices: Select this option to base the calculation on 

the average of the last three invoices from this vendor. 

• 
Fixed amount: Select this option to base the calculation on a specific amount, and 

then type the amount in the field that appears below.

Use the Open Purchase Orders accrual type to have the system pull in invoices that are 

associated with purchase orders. 

To create the accrual template for open purchase orders:

1. 
In the Accrual type drop-down list, select Open purchase orders. 

2. 
To define the range of accounts to have the system check for open purchase orders, select

account in the range in the Account to drop-down list. 

3. 
In the Include section, select the check boxes of the purchase order types to include in the 

accrual template. 

• 
Offline / Manual Purchase Orders. Select this option to have the system use the total 

amount of the PO to be accrued for online purchase orders that are approved. For 

partial received and partial invoice matches, the system considers the total of all items 

that have not been received. 

• 
Online Purchase Orders. Select this option for the system to use the total amount of 

the PO to be accrued for approved online purchase orders. 

• 
When Receipt of goods (ROG) is enabled in Spend Management, the system uses 

the total amount of the PO to be accrued for approved online purchase orders. 

• 
When ROG is not enabled, the system uses the total amount minus the amount 

matched as the amount of the PO to accrue.

Adding an Accrual Template for Allowance for Doubtful Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > 
 Accrual Template`


Use the Allowance for Doubtful Account accrual type to have the system pull in invoices that are 

marked as doubtful accounts. 

If you have $20,000 in rent that you don’t think is going to be paid, it is a good accounting 

practice to be able to make an accrual entry that takes that amount out of rent receipts. The 

amount will potentially be moving over to the bad debt account.  

When you want to account for charges that are not likely to be paid, you can create an accrual 

template using the Allowance for doubtful accounts accrual template. 

RealPage Accounting obtains delinquent rent data from Leasing & Rents and uses this data in 
the accrual calculation of the allowance for doubtful accounts. 

To create the accrual template: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click 
 Add next to the Accrual template option. 

3. 
Type a unique identifier for the accrual in the Accrual ID field. 

4. 
By default, the status is set to Active. If you want to prevent this accrual template from 

being used, select Inactive.  

5. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location for which you want to create scheduled 

accruals. When the user selects an accrual to calculate and post, the system calculates only 

for the locations that the user has access to. 

---


<!-- Page 211 -->
Chapter 11: Accrual Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Filling In the Accrual Type Section  

1. 
In the Accrual type drop-down list, select Allowance for Doubtful Accounts. 

2. 
Select the Account group to use to identify receivables that will probably not be paid. For 

example, the rent due from tenants account is reported in the Accounts Receivable account 

group.  

3. 
In the Include balance for section, select the aging period to accrue for. Typically, you would 

select a higher aging period, like > 90 days. 

4. 
In the Transaction Codes to Include field, type one or more transaction codes. Separate 

multiple codes with semicolons. You can also type “Not required.” 

Example: CODE1; CODE2 

If nothing is defined, then when running the accrual calculation, the process returns all 

activity. 

If some transaction codes are defined, the system returns activity only for the transaction 

codes that you add to the calculation. 

5. 
In the Percent field, type the percentage of the balance to accrue for. 

Filling In the Accounting Section 

1. 
In the Book drop-down list, select the book where you want to store accruals. If your system 

has enabled GAAP (Compliance), then it appears in the list with the Accrual and Tax books. 

The system uses the next three selections (journal, debit account, and credit account) to 

create the journal entry so that the system can post accruals. 

2. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want to store accrual records. 

The system includes the journals in the book that you selected.  

3. 
In the Debit account drop-down list, select the account that you want the system to use for 

this accrual’s debit account journal entries. For example, 1200.00 Accounts due from

Allocations 

This chapter describes the two types of allocation mechanisms available in RealPage Accounting. 

In This Chapter

### Allocations Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 222*

Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Allocations Overview 

RealPage Accounting offers two ways to allocate revenue and expenses: 

• 
Transaction allocations 

• 
G/L allocations 

Transaction Allocations 

Transaction allocations enable you to automatically distribute amounts during transaction entry 

across multiple dimensions, such as departments and locations. You can allocate either a 

percentage or a set (absolute) value. If you allocate by percent, your total allocations must equal 

100%. 

For example, you can create a transaction allocation that distributes costs such as occupancy 

across several departments. Select that allocation when you enter the expense line. The amount of 

that expense is then automatically distributed across the appropriate departments. 

G/L Allocations 

Use G/L allocations to have the system calculate expense and revenue allocations. This feature 

saves time and effort by generating allocations to properties. Allocating revenue and expenses 

allows your organization to gain a better understanding of the performance of departments, 

properties, and projects. 

G/L allocations allow you to distribute expenses or revenue equally, in a tiered method, or based 

on a template that prescribes the properties, departments, and accounts involved.  

Allocation Differences 

Transaction allocations are applied when you enter a transaction. You need to know the 

parameters before you use transaction allocations. 

The G/L allocations feature automates allocation calculations and are applied post-transaction. 

---



### Transaction Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 223*

Chapter 12: Allocations 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Transaction Allocations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Allocations > Transaction Allocations`


Allocations distribute revenue or expense amounts across multiple dimensions, such as 

departments and locations. 

For example, you can create a transaction allocation that distributes costs such as insurance 

premiums across several regional sales offices. Select that allocation when you enter the A/P 

invoice. The amounts of that A/P invoice are then automatically distributed across the appropriate 

locations. 

You can allocate an amount by either a percentage or a set value. If you allocate by percent, your 

total allocations must equal 100%, for example, 25% to each of four projects. 

Transaction allocations are based on dimensions. You split allocation by a dimension across 

multiple entries (lines) in the Allocation setup, such as locations, departments, or vendors. 

When you create an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or journal entry and apply an allocation to it, 

RealPage Accounting automatically divides the item based on the way it is defined in the 

allocation. For example, if a company distributes rental revenues across five sales offices, the 

allocation would assign a value of 20% each to sales office. When you choose this allocation in a 

transaction, for example, an invoice, 20% of that invoice is automatically owed to each sales office. 

To see how an allocation is divided on an A/R invoice, A/P invoice, or journal entry, view the item, 

and then click Show details on the line in the Entries section.

Transaction Allocations List

The Transaction Allocations list is where you set up and maintain allocations that distribute a 

transaction amount. A transaction allocation controls how the system distributes the cost of a 

transaction across several dimensions, such as departments or locations. 

Use this list to add, view, edit, and delete transaction allocations. You can also export the list of

#### Adding a Transaction Allocation
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 226*

Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding a Transaction Allocation 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Allocations > 
 Transaction Allocations`


To add a transaction allocation: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Allocations section, select 
 Transaction Allocations. The Transaction allocation 

information page opens. 

3. 
In the Allocation ID field, type a unique name for the allocation. 

For example, suppose you have four sales offices, and you divide maintenance costs 

proportionately by square footage, but you divide insurance costs equally. You create an 

allocation for each set of allocation types. In this example, you might name your allocations 

as MAINT and INSUR.  

4. 
In the Description field, describe the allocation strategy to help users identify which 

allocation to use. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, Active is the default status. You can select Inactive to hide the 

allocation from view so that users cannot assign it.  

To change the status of an object to hide unused items, select Inactive. When an item is 
set to Inactive, the system retains the data but hides the inactive item on lists, 
drop-down lists, and so on. Examples of data you might want to hide or make inactive are 
employees who are no longer with your company or bank accounts you no longer use. If you 
want to permanently remove an item, you must delete it. 

6. 
Use the Allocate by option to determine whether the allocation is by a portion of the total 

or by a constant value. 

For example, if you choose percentage, then the value of 25 is 25%. You can include up to 

12 decimal points when using percentage values. However, if you choose absolute, the value 

of 25 is $25. Percentage is the most used allocation type. 

7. 
Type the Document number if this allocation is based on a specific document. 

This number appears only on the Allocation list. For example, if the allocation is based on a 

contract, you may want to enter its reference number. 

8. 
Select or upload an attachment to associate an electronic file with this allocation. You could 

attach a complete contract or one page of explanation. You can attach any type of file to 

the transaction, including scanned images, spreadsheets, or document files. Attached files 

are uploaded for permanent, safe storage. See Adding attachments (on page 342). 

---


<!-- Page 227 -->
Chapter 12: Allocations 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Filling In the Entries Section 

The Entries section of this page is where you assign the distribution for the allocation to the 

appropriate combination of dimensions, and to entities in a multi-entity shared company. 

For example, if a company distributes insurance premiums across several regional sales offices, 

you would use this section to assign a value of 25% each to locations East, West, North, and 

South. When you choose this allocation in a transaction, 25% of that transaction is then 

automatically distributed to each location. 

1. 
In Value, type in the value of the allocation. 

Depending on your choice in Allocate by above, the value is either a percentage or a 

constant value. If you select percent, the values must add to 100%. If you select absolute, 

the system uses the fixed amount provided for distribution. 

To add more lines to this page, at the end of the last row, click 
 Add. 

All of the columns after the Value column are dimensions, such as Department, Location, 

Customer, and Vendor. 

2. 
Click the down arrows for the dimensions you want and select from the list that displays. 

The value amounts are distributed to these dimensions, which include entities in the case of 

multi-entity companies. 

For multi-entity companies that use the same base currency, you can allocate an A/P 
invoice, invoice, or journal entry across multiple entities at top level only. To do this, you 
must create and use the allocation at the top level of the company. Allocations created at 
the top level of a company can’t be used at the entity level. 

3. 
Complete and save the desired information. 

This new allocation appears in your list of allocations, and you can select it the next time 

you allocate an A/P invoice, an A/R invoice, or a journal entry. The system automatically 

distributes the money according to the allocation definition that you select.

Importing Transaction Allocations

Workflow 

1.

Downloading the Transaction Allocations Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu.  

2. 
Click the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Transaction allocations row, and then 

click the Template link. 

The system either downloads the Transaction Allocations.xls file or prompts you to open or 

save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling In the Template with Transaction Allocation Data 

Add your data using the correct formatting as explained in the template.  

1. 
Open the template in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
ALLOCATION_ID: Type a unique name for the allocation. 

• 
ALLOCATE_BY: Type P for Percentage, A for Absolute or F for Fixed amount with 

over/under logic. 

• 
ALLOCATE_TO: Type B for both, D for department or L for location. 

• 
LINE_NO: Start with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and increase by one for each 

subsequent line. 

• 
VALUETYPE: Type Amount or Percent. 

• 
VALUE: Type the amount or percentage to allocate. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. Refer to the Transaction Allocations Data 

topic for a full list of columns. 

After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 
mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common Errors 
(on page 473 ) and Best Practices . 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import.

Using a Transaction Allocation 

To use the allocation in a transaction: 

1. 
Open a transaction. 

2.

After you’ve selected the allocation, the system removes any dimension values selected for 

the line item. Instead, it populates the dimension values from the allocation directly.

a)

b)

allocation. 

Overriding an Allocation on a Line Item 

Even when an allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to a line item, 

you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation at the line 

item level of the relevant transaction page (A/P invoices, A/R invoices, or journal entries). For 

detailed instructions on overriding allocations, see Overriding an Allocation (on page 225).

#### Overriding a Line Allocation
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 235*

Chapter 12: Allocations

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Overriding a Line Allocation 

You can apply an allocation either to individual lines of a transaction or to the entire transaction. If 

you apply it to the entire transaction, all of the line item entries inherit the distribution of the 

allocation. However, you can override that allocation on a line-by-line basis. When you change 

the allocated dimensions/values, the allocation resets as Custom, as it now contains a specific 

allocation distribution unique to that line item. 

The unique allocated values are stored with your line item for audit trail purposes.  

Click a line item, and then click the Show/Hide Details button to open and close the Allocations 

Splits detail area for a line item. 

To override a line allocation:  

1. 
Click the line item you want to override.  

2. 
Click the Show details tab or press CTRL + 
 Down Arrow to open the Details section. 

3. 
Find the Allocation splits section, and then click the Customize allocation button. The 

Custom Allocation box opens. 

4. 
Override the template distribution by customizing allocation amounts across departments 

or locations. 

5. 
Click Yes. 

Even when an allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to a line 

item, you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation at 

the line-item level of the relevant transaction page (A/R invoices, A/P invoices, or journal 

entries).  

If you change the amounts such that the total is different from what you entered in the 
transaction page, the system updates the total when you save and return to the 
transaction page.

Determines whether the transaction allocation is by a portion of the

### G/L Allocations
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 240*

Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

G/L Allocations 

Use G/L allocations to have the system automatically generate allocations to properties. 

Allocating revenue and expenses allows your organization to gain a better understanding of the 

performance of departments, properties, and projects. 

You can allocate an expense or revenue on a recurring basis, at the segment level, and across 

multiple properties.  

The difference between transaction allocations and G/L allocations is that transaction allocations 

are performed as you enter a transaction into the system. You set up G/L allocations in advance.  

This section describes how to set up G/L allocations. 

---

### G/L Allocation Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 243*

Chapter 12: Allocations 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

G/L Allocation Methods 

There are three methods of G/L allocations: 

• 
Allocate on a recurring basis. Use the Equal method. 

• 
Allocate at the segment level. Use the Template method. 

• 
Allocate across multiple properties. Use the Tiered method. 

You can use these methods to allocate costs from one source or property to multiple targeted 

properties: 

• 
Equal: Use this method to distribute among the targeted properties equally. 

• 
Template: Define a template, and then use it to create allocation definitions. This method 

distributes only among the properties defined in the template. 

• 
Tiered: Use this method if you have any allocations that need to be processed sequentially 

(such as, if an allocation is dependent on a different allocation being processed first). 

Provide the sequence you want the allocations to be processed in.

After you save the G/L allocation definition, the Allocation ID cannot be changed. If you

Setting Up the Allocation Rules  

1. 
In the Balancing Account drop-down list, select the account that you want to use to balance 

the unbalanced journal entry. This option creates the balancing journal entry against the 

balancing account defined for each of the target property unbalanced journal entries. This 

account is typically the inter-entity due to/from account. 

2. 
In the Period drop-down list, select the source pool time period; it is the default time 

interval for the allocation that you will generate. When you generate the allocation, the 

system compares the As of Date field with the source pool time period to determine the 

source balance. The following time period options are available: 

• 
Current Month 

• 
Current Year to Date 

For example, if you set the source pool time period to the current month when you 

generate the allocation, then the As of date is September 30, 2020. The allocation 

calculations are based on activities that occurred in September 2020. 

3. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want the system to record your 

allocation when it is generated. 

If you have created the allocation definition but have not run and posted the allocation to 

the selected journal, then you can still change the allocation definition journal selection. 

If you have already posted an allocation to the selected journal, then you cannot change 

your journal selection. 

4. 
Select the Auto-reverse JE in next month check box to display the Day drop-down list with 

values from 1 to 31. RealPage Accounting also reverses the prior allocated entry on the day 

specified (in the Day drop-down list) in the next consecutive month. 

---


<!-- Page 246 -->
Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Example: Source: $5,000 as of 08/15/2020 and $10,000 as of 08/31/2020. If you generate a 

G/L allocation on 08/16/2020, then the allocation split would be on $5,000. Select the 

Auto-reverse JE in next month check box, and then select 8 in the Day drop-down list. 

When you re-generate the allocation on 09/09/2020, then the system should distribute 

$10,000 because the previously allocated amount has been reversed as of September 8, 

2020. 

5. 
Select the Allocate delta check box to generate an allocation multiple times and book the 

difference between the previous calculations and the current calculation. If this check box is 

cleared, then the allocation generates only once. 

Example: Source: $5,000 as of 08/15/2020 and $10,000 as of 08/31/2020. If you generate a 

G/L allocation on 08/16/2020, then the allocation split would be on $5,000. When you 

regenerate the allocation on 08/31/2020, the system should distribute the difference 

between the previously created source amount and the new source balance (i.e., $10,000 - 

$5,000 = $5,000). 

6. 
Select the Reverse source check box to create a reverse journal entry for the source amount 

that is allocated out. 

7. 
Select the Multiple Properties on JE check box to create one journal entry for multiple 

properties. If this check box is clear, then the system creates one journal entry for each 

target property. 

8. 
Select the Include Source Segment check box to populate the source segment values to the 

target.

Add the source.

data to it that you want to import.

Filling In the Allocation Definition List 

If you imported an allocation definition, you may change the data in the Allocation Definition list. 

1. 
In the Sequence field, type a number. This number determines the order of the allocation 

generation. 

2. 
In the Type drop-down list, select the type of line item source or target. 

3. 
In the Entity/Property drop-down list, select the source or target and the entity or property. 

4. 
In the Book drop-down list, select the book to determine the source balances and post the 

target entries. 

5. 
In the Account drop-down list, select the target account for the allocated entry. 

6. 
In the Department drop-down list, select the value on source line items to determine the 

source balance by department. Select the value on target line items to assign it to the target 

journal entry department. 

7. 
In the Segment Type and Segment Value drop-down lists, select the value on source line 

items to determine the source balance for the segment type and segment value.  

Select the value on target line items to assign it to the target journal entry segment type 

and segment value. 

If the Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system does not 
have the segments feature enabled (on page 334 ). 

8. 
In the Allocate by drop-down list, select Percent. 

9. 
In the Factor drop-down list, type the percentage to determine the source balance or to 

allocate amounts to the target entries. This field accepts only numeric values. 

The Balancing Account field uses the account defined in the Allocation Rules section by 
default. To override this, assign balancing accounts on the source or target separately.

Definition list) to limit the accounts defined in the selected account group. 

2. 
In the Balancing Account drop-down list, select the account that you want to use to balance 

the unbalanced journal entry. This option creates the balancing journal entry against the 

balancing account defined for each of the target property unbalanced journal entries. This is 

typically the inter-entity due to/from account. 

3.
