---


<!-- Page 252 -->
Allocations 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

system compares the As of Date field with the source pool time period to determine the 

source balance. The following time period options are available: 

• 
Current Month 

• 
Current Year to Date 

For example, if you set the source pool time period to the current month when you 

generate the allocation, and the As of date is September 30, 2020, the allocation 

calculations are based on activities that occurred in September 2020. 

4. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want the system to record your 

allocation when it is generated. 

If you have created the allocation definition but have not run and posted the allocation to 

the selected journal, then you can still change the allocation definition journal selection. 

If you have already posted an allocation to the selected journal, then you cannot change 

your journal selection. 

5. 
Select the Auto-reverse JE in next month check box to display the Day drop-down list with 

values from 1 to 31. RealPage Accounting also reverses the prior allocated entry on the day 

specified (in the Day drop-down list) in the next consecutive month. 

Example: Source: $5,000 as of 08/15/2020 and $10,000 as of 08/31/2020. If you generate a 

G/L allocation on 08/16/2020, then the allocation split would be on $5,000. Select the 

Auto-reverse JE in next month check box, and then select 8 in the Day drop-down list. 

When you re-generate the allocation on 09/09/2020, then the system should distribute 

$10,000 because the previously allocated amount has been reversed as of September 8, 

2020. 

6. 
Select the Allocate delta check box to generate an allocation multiple times and book the 

difference between the previous calculations and the current calculation. If this check box is 

cleared, then the allocation generates only once. 

Example: Source: $5,000 as of 08/15/2020 and $10,000 as of 08/31/2020. If you generate a 

G/L allocation on 08/16/2020, then the allocation split would be on $5,000. When you 

regenerate the allocation on 08/31/2020, the system should distribute the difference 

between the previously created source amount and the new source balance (i.e., $10,000 - 

$5,000 = $5,000). 

7. 
Select the Reverse source check box to create a reverse journal entry for the source amount 

that is allocated out. 

8. 
Select the Multiple Properties on JE check box to create one journal entry for multiple 

properties. If this check box is clear, then the system creates one journal entry for each 

target property. 

9. 
Select the Include Source Segments check box to populate the source segment values to 

the target.

Allocation Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > G/L Allocation Definitions`


Use this page to add, change, and delete G/L allocation definitions. You can also view the list of 

recurring journal entries, as G/L allocations create recurring journal entries.  

Allocation information includes the allocation method, allocation rules, and the allocation 

definition. 

This page is composed of three sections: 

• 
The first section contains essential information about the allocation. 

• 
The Allocation rules section contains the settings that control when and how the system 

generates the allocation. 

• 
The Allocation definition section contains the sequence of allocation, the source and target 

properties, segments, accounts, and allocation. 

Duplicating Records 

If your goal is to create one record and reuse it as the starting point for additional records, use 

the Duplicate function. Most types of records can be duplicated—including A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, recurring invoices, adjustments, entities, vendors, contacts, journals, G/L accounts, 

user-defined books, document numbering sequences, contracts, service tickets, email templates, 

and reporting account sets. When you open a record and it includes a Duplicate button, you can 

use it as a template to quickly create a new record.  

For invoices, you can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add it, and set the date to 

create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually and look for the section called 

“Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

To duplicate recurring invoices, look for the Duplicate option that is located in the More actions 
button menu. 

To duplicate a record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

After you duplicate a record, the copy of the record stays open so that you can change its 

details.  

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists.

record. 

• 
Click the Print to button to save the record in PDF format so that you can print it. 

• 
Click the Duplicate button to create a copy of the current record. 

• 
Click the View audit trail button to view a log of changes to this record. 

When you open an account title by entity record with the Edit link, you can do all of the above, 

and also:

Duplicating Records 

If your goal is to create one record and reuse it as the starting point for additional records, use 

the Duplicate function. Most types of records can be duplicated—including A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, recurring invoices, adjustments, entities, vendors, contacts, journals, G/L accounts, 

user-defined books, document numbering sequences, contracts, service tickets, email templates, 

and reporting account sets. When you open a record and it includes a Duplicate button, you can 

use it as a template to quickly create a new record.  

For invoices, you can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add it, and set the date to 

create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually and look for the section called 

“Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

To duplicate recurring invoices, look for the Duplicate option that is located in the More actions 
button menu. 

To duplicate a record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

After you duplicate a record, the copy of the record stays open so that you can change its 

details.  

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record.

Reporting Periods 

This chapter describes how to set up your system’s reporting periods. Reporting periods are used in financial 

reports that are available in the Reports and General Ledger applications. 

These reporting periods are not used by budget variance analysis. Instead, you can set the reporting period in 
budget variance analysis configuration (on page 171 ) only to Monthly or Quarterly.

### Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 272*

Reporting Periods 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reporting Periods 

See the How to Get Here (on page 263) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Reporting periods are used when you create reports and budgets, and when you open and close 

books. They let you limit the information on the report to specific time ranges. 

There are out-of-the-box (system) reporting periods that are most commonly used, such as: 

• 
Prior/Current/Next month 

• 
Prior/Current/Next quarter 

• 
Prior/Current/Next year 

• 
Current <month/quarter/year> to date 

Companies often work on unique schedules. If the out-of-the-box reporting periods don’t meet 

your needs, create additional ones. For information, see Adding Reporting Periods (on page 432). 

There are some system-based reporting periods, like Current month, that you can run repeatedly 

without modification. For some types of reports, that’s all you need. 

For other reports, you need to specify the period that the report spans. Date-driven reports that 

you create are used with specific calendar periods (for example, for budgeting or opening and 

closing books). For these reports, you need to create a matching reporting period. 

There are many reasons you might want a specific reporting period. For example, manually 

creating a reporting period makes sense for some companies that: 

• 
Run and report on a weekly basis 

• 
Don’t end periods at the end of the month 

• 
Work from a 28-day cycle instead of a calendar month 

• 
Need past or future reporting periods 

Reporting periods enable you to limit the data shown on reports based on the way your company 

works.

#### Adding an Odd-Sized Reporting Period for a Budget
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 276*

Reporting Periods

Adding an Odd-Sized Reporting Period for a Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > Setup > More > Reporting Periods > Add`



> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Budgets > Add`


In accounting, most reporting periods are monthly, quarterly, or annual. But sometimes, 

organizations deliberately create an odd-sized reporting period (like 5 weeks, 10 days, or 13 

months). Odd-sized reporting periods are used to align accounting with real-world changes—like 

fiscal year shifts, business cycles, or special events—so the financial picture stays accurate and 

relevant. 

It is possible to create a budget for reporting periods that are shorter or longer than a month, as 

long as you select the Use for budgeting check box when you create the reporting period.  

Things to Consider 

• 
Budget reporting periods cannot overlap, so when you create an odd-sized period, note 

that it affects your ability to create the normal-sized periods adjacent to the odd-sized 

reporting periods.  

• 
Odd-sized periods are usually temporary and explained in financial statements. 

• 
Odd-sized periods can make comparisons tricky, so companies often provide adjusted or 

normalized figures for consistency. 

Prerequisites 

• 
You must have permissions to create reporting periods. 

• 
You must have permissions to create a new budget. 

Permissions 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

You must have been granted Reporting Periods permissions. The permissions can be either in 

Company or General Ledger, or both.  

These permissions are required to create and edit reporting periods:

Adding Transaction Templates 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > More > Transaction Templates`


Before you can set up transaction templates you must enable permissions for G/L allocation 

definitions.  

To add a transaction template that you can use with G/L allocations: 

1. 
Open General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add button next to Transaction templates.

In the Template ID field, type a unique identifier for the template. 

4. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select a journal where you want to record the resulting 

transactions. 

5. 
In the Offset account drop-down list, select the offset account. 

6.

### Chart Types Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 302*



#### Configuring Chart Types
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 302*



#### Configuration Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 302*

Chart Types 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Chart Types Overview 

A chart type is an alternative chart of accounts. Chart types can include both G/L accounts and 

statistical accounts. You can assign chart types to properties and to management reporting codes 

(MRCs). 

The chart types feature is different from reporting account sets in that you can subdivide the chart 

of accounts into subsets and associate each property with their own subset.  

The chart types feature is ideally suited to companies with multiple entities as it simplifies the 

accounting task and reduces the likelihood of a user selecting an inappropriate account.  

Configuring Chart Types 

To help you configure your system so that you can use multiple charts of accounts, we have 

assembled a checklist to streamline your implementation of chart types. 

When you create a chart type and assign it to a property (or property type), the system links 

properties and locations with the chart. Therefore, it is important to include every necessary 

account in the chart type for this feature to work smoothly. 

Configuration Workflow 

1. 
Create the underlying accounts. See the Chart Types Checklist (on page 293) for a list of 

account types to create. 

2. 
Enable the chart types feature (on page 295). 

3. 
Grant Chart types permissions (on page 296). 

4. 
Add chart types (on page 301). 

---



#### Chart Types Checklist
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 303*

Chapter 16: Chart Types 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Chart Types Checklist 

This checklist is designed to help you set up your chart types. When creating new chart types: 

• 
Link any and all required G/L accounts to each chart type.  

Accounts can be included in as many chart types as needed. Accounts do not need to be 
associated exclusively with one chart type. 

• 
When setting up a chart type for a property, include the property’s bank account. 

• 
If your company uses the Job Cost application, include the WIP accounts related to cost 

codes for the chart types linked to the properties for which you create jobs. 

• 
Set up G/L accounts for Accounts payable and Accounts receivable on their configuration 

pages. RealPage refers to these as the offset accounts.  

• 
Include bank G/L, interest earned, and service charge G/L accounts for all the locations that 

are restricted from being associated with a bank account, if any. 

• 
Create transaction templates. 

---


<!-- Page 304 -->
Chart Types 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Set up G/L allocations or transaction allocations. 

• 
Set up offset accounts related to account labels.  

Offset accounts must be associated with the location ’s chart type when linked to A/P 
loans. 

• 
Create vendor default expense accounts. 

• 
Create customer default revenue accounts. 

• 
Create any Accounts Payable accounts that you need in addition to the default A/P account. 

• 
Create any Accounts Receivable accounts that you need in addition to the default A/R 

account.

 Chart Types`

To add a chart type: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2.

 Add button next to Chart types. The Chart types page opens.

Select the G/L Accounts to Map

•

creating. Keep in mind the needs of the properties to which you plan to link the chart type 

as you select the G/L accounts.  

• 
You can link both General Ledger accounts and Statistical accounts to multiple chart types. 

• 
You cannot link a single property to multiple chart types. 

• 
If a property is not mapped to any chart type, then all of the General Ledger and Statistical 

accounts created in RealPage Accounting are available for selection. 

Best Practice: Know the accounts that you want to add to the chart type before you begin. 
It is easier to add a G/L account later than to remove them. Removing G/L accounts is 
more time-consuming as it requires you to validate each account number that you remove 
separately.

#### Duplicating Records
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 313*

Chapter 16: Chart Types

When you save the chart type, the system creates account groups for General Ledger 
accounts and Statistical accounts. The format of the account group name created is Chart 
Type Name – (type).  

Duplicating Records 

If your goal is to create one record and reuse it as the starting point for additional records, use 

the Duplicate function. Most types of records can be duplicated—including A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, recurring invoices, adjustments, entities, vendors, contacts, journals, G/L accounts, 

user-defined books, document numbering sequences, contracts, service tickets, email templates, 

and reporting account sets. When you open a record and it includes a Duplicate button, you can 

use it as a template to quickly create a new record.  

For invoices, you can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add it, and set the date to 

create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually and look for the section called 

“Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

To duplicate recurring invoices, look for the Duplicate option that is located in the More actions 
button menu. 

To duplicate a record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

After you duplicate a record, the copy of the record stays open so that you can change its 

details.  

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record.

### About Account Group Purposes
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 324*

Account Group Purposes 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Account Group Purposes 

Assigning an Account group purpose to an account group can help you organize your accounts 

into more manageable groups for financial reports, graphs, and performance cards. 

Use the account group purpose to help visualize how reports are going to appear. When you 

build reports, account group purpose can speed selections since it organizes a long list of 

accounts into manageable chunks. 

In multi-entity companies, Account group purpose is available at the top and entity levels. 

Where Account Group Purposes Are Used 

When you create and use an Account group purpose, the purpose filter can be used in multiple 

areas, almost anywhere you select a group. 

• 
In Group of Account groups. 

• 
In Financial reports when defining a report structure or selecting rows or columns. 

• 
In Performance cards (Click the Account Group drop-down list, and then click Find at the 

top of the drop-down list). 

The Account group purpose appears as an optional filter on the Financial Report Writer rows and 

columns that require Account Group selection, as well as other places that have account group 

selection. 

Example 

For this example, create an income report that includes only Direct cash flow - operating revenue. 

1. 
Create an account group purpose called DCF-O (Direct Cash Flow - Operating). 

2. 
Create a report that shows income.  

3. 
On the Rows tab, select the account groups to add to the report. 

4. 
Select DCF-O in the Account group purpose, so that only those account groups tagged 

with the DCF-O purpose appear in the list. 

Strategic Use of Account Group Purposes 

Assigning account group purposes gives you a way to categorize account groups.  

Assign the “Assets” account group purpose to all account groups containing assets.  

Assign the account group purpose “Liabilities” to all account groups containing liabilities. 

Using Prefixes in Account Group Purpose Names 

When creating account group purposes, consider assigning prefixes that help you find the 

purposes for a specific report. For example, you might prefix the account group purpose for 

---

the totaling section for the balance sheet.  

If you plan to use the same structures in other reports, using a prefix might be confusing or 

limiting.

#### Importing Account Group Purpose Data
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 328*

Account Group Purposes 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Account Group Purpose Data 

This procedure helps you add Account group purposes information to an account group. 

If your system does not have account groups, then you must add account group data first, before 

you can import account group purposes.  

Workflow 

1. 
Download the template for Account group purposes. 

2. 
Fill the template with data. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

4. 
Import the file.  

Downloading the template 

To download the import template file for account group purposes: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. The Import data page opens. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Account group purposes row, and then 

click Template. The system downloads the file to your browser’s default download location. 

Filling the Template with Data 

1. 
Open the template file in Excel, and fill in the required column. 

• 
NAME: Type the account group purpose. The name must be unique, and it is 

case-sensitive. 

2. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining column: 

• 
STATUS: Type ACTIVE or INACTIVE.  

3. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 462). 

Importing the File 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the More section of the Setup menu, click Account group purposes. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Account group purpose box opens. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button. 

5. 
Find and select the file with the data that you saved as a CSV file.  

6. 
Click Open. 

7. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format, select the date format 

that the data uses in the Date format field. 

---


<!-- Page 329 -->
Chapter 17: Account Group Purposes 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

8. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

9. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

10. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

11. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify all the records in 

your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify them. 

---

### Segment Rule Set
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 342*

Segment Rule Set 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Segment Rule Set 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > More > Segment Rule Set`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry > Segment Rule Set`


Segment requirements help your company capture more information about specific properties 

and G/L accounts. Segment rules enable you to specify when a segment type is required when a 

user enters a transaction. The system applies segment rules when a user creates a journal entry or 

an A/P invoice. 

There are two kinds of segment rules: Property and Account. 

• 
A property segment rule associates a property with one or more segments. When a user 

creates a transaction with the property, the user must select the segments that are defined 

in the rule. 

• 
An account segment rule associates a G/L account with one or more segments. When a 

user creates a transaction with the G/L account, the user must select the segments that are 

defined in the rule. 

When you create a rule, you must require at least one segment. You can require up to four 

segments in a rule. 

Segment Rule Components 

A segment rule is made up of the type (account or property), the name of the account or 

property, and the list of required segments. 

Rule Type: Account  
Account # 
Segments required: 1, 2, 3 

Rule Type: Property  
Name of property Segments required: 1 

Every time a user creates an A/P invoice or journal entry associated with one of the properties or 

accounts that have rules, the system requires the user to select the segments required by the rule. 

If the user tries to save the A/P invoice or journal entry without selecting the required segment 

values, then the system displays an error. 

---

### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 348*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

---

Adding a New Attachment to a Record 

This topic describes how to attach a file to a record when the file is not yet stored in the system. 

To attach a file to a record when the file is already in the system, see Adding an Existing 

Attachment to a Record (on page 344). 

The steps for attaching documents to transactions and records are different depending on 

whether the Enable single scan upload option is enabled or disabled in your user preferences. 

Adding a New Attachment to a Record When Scanning is Disabled  

To add a new attachment to a record when scanning is disabled: 

1. 
Add a new record or edit an existing record to open the information page. 

2. 
Click the Attachments drop-down list, and then click the Add link. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

3. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

4. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

5. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

6. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment.

### Managing Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 355*

Chapter 20: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Managing Lists 

Lists provide access to like records. After you create a record, you can access it from its list. Most 

lists allow you to add, edit, view, and delete the records in it. You can also export the list to an 

XML file or a PDF file. After exporting a list, you can import the list into an external application like 

Excel, and then print the list from that application. 

Some lists allow you to access related information. For example, from the customers list, you can 

also access the customers A/R ledger and view a breakdown of the total amount that the 

customer owes. 

Since the list page is where you perform most of your work, the system provides several features 

to let you filter and sort lists and create and manage custom views of your data. 

• 
Sorting (on page 346): Sort the list alphabetically by the data in the desired column. 

• 
Filtering (on page 347): Filter lists so that you see only the data that you need. 

• 
Views (on page 362): Create a custom view to determine which columns appear in your lists, 

and apply a filter so that the list appears just the way you want it. 

Lists and Links 

Each list is unique and can offer links to let you navigate into an associated record to see more 

detailed data. For example, some invoice lists have a Preview link that, when clicked, opens the 

invoice in PDF format in a browser window. Another type of list may have a link to the customer 

record or the vendor record. 

Many reports present figures as links that, when clicked, open the associated record. This example 

shows links in the Debit and Credit columns of a journal entry. When you click a link, the system 

navigates to more information, allowing you to delve into the details. 

---



#### Sorting Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 356*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Sorting Lists 

You can display a list by a column’s ascending or descending values by clicking the column name. 

An arrow to the right of the column name indicates the sort direction. The arrow points 
 up for 

ascending order and 
 down for descending order. Only one column can control the list’s sort 

order at a time. 

In this example, the system sorts the list by the data in the Entity ID column. The sort arrow 

appears on the column that the system is sorting on. 

To reverse the sort order, click the column name again. The sort order reverses, and the arrow 

flips direction to indicate that the sort is reversed. 

To sort on a different column, click the desired column name. 

---



#### Filtering Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 357*

Chapter 20: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Filtering Lists 

Using Column Filters 

Column filters are text boxes that appear at the top of each column. Filters let you find items in a 

list that match the text that you enter. 

To apply a column filter: 

• 
Type the text that you want to find in the column filter, and then press ENTER. 

The system searches for matches, and then displays the matches in the list. 

If a text box does not appear at the top of a column, the column is not searchable. 

Using the Wild Card Character 

• 
Use the % symbol as a wild card or placeholder. For example, typing “san%” in the City 

column’s filter would find both San Francisco and Santa Diego. 

• 
Placing the % in front of text tells the system to find these letters in the middle of text in a 

field. 

• 
Placing % at the end of a word tells the system to find the word and any letters that follow 

the word. 

• 
Use % to filter text columns only. The % symbol does not work on non-text columns such as 

date columns or amount columns. 

• 
For best success, anticipate differences and adapt your filter to account for them. 

To find records that contain a specific value: 

• 
Type the first part of the value. 

If you are looking for a contact in a city that starts with “San,” then you can filter the Contact 

list by typing “san” in the City filter field, then and pressing ENTER. The system searches for 

contacts with a city that begins with San, such as San Jose, San Francisco, and Santa Fe. 

---


<!-- Page 358 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
If you know only part of the text that you want to find, type “%” and then type the text that 

you have. 

For example, if you are looking for a contact with the letters “Will” in the name, but you do 

not have the full, correct name of the business, type “%will%” in the Contact name filter of 

the Contacts list, and then press ENTER. The system searches for matches, retrieving all 

contacts that contain the letters “will” in the Contact name field. 

Example 

Your company uses this standard format for naming invoice summaries: Invoices: Month Year. 

When you want to find all June summaries, type “%June” in the filter above the Summary column, 

and then press ENTER to apply the filter. Placing the % in front of June tells the system that the 

word “June” appears in the middle of the text string. Placing % at the end of the word “June” tells 

the system to find the word June and any word with letters that follow the word “June,” such as 

“Juneteenth.” 

Searches for Units 

You can search for a unit by entering any part of the unit ID. The system will find matches for any 

part of the unit ID string. For example, if the units in your property are configured with an 

alphanumeric pattern such as A-10, A-11, A12, B-20, B-21, B-22, then you can enter any part of 

the string, such as “22,” and the system will find B-22.  

The string does not have to start with the entered value to match. Typing “A” finds a list of units 

on the A floor as in our example or all units that have “A” in the unit ID.

Displaying One-Time Items 

Some quick-entry records are set for one-time use. For example, you may have a seasonal

##### Operator Definitions
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 364*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Operator Definitions 

The following operators are available for use when filtering: 

• 
Equals: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column matches the text or 

number in the Value field. 

• 
Less than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is less 

than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

greater than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Less or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

less than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen 

column is greater than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Not equal to: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column does not match 

the text or number in the Value field. 

• 
Contains: Displays all records in which a character or group of characters in the chosen 

column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The characters must 

match in the same order. For example, “ox” typed in the Value field may return records for 

Oxygen Inc., Boxing Agency, and Clorox, if those were values in the chosen column. 

• 
Does not contain: Displays all records in which no character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. 

• 
Starts with: Displays all records in which the first character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you have an item ID scheme that 

uses initial letters to identify the product type, you can select the item ID column and set the 

Value field to these letters to display all records for that product type. 

• 
Ends with: Displays all records in which the last character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you tag the end of the item ID for 

all custom order items with the letters “CO,” you can select the item ID column and set the 

value to CO to display all records for custom order items. 

• 
Includes: Displays all records that match items in a comma delimited list in the Value field. 

• 
Excludes: Displays all records that do not match items in a comma delimited list in the 

Value field. 

• 
Field equals null: Displays all records that have a null or empty field. 

• 
Field not equals null: Displays all records that do not have a null or empty field. 

---


<!-- Page 365 -->
Chapter 20: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

% bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank.

Displaying a Hierarchical View 

Some lists, such as the Locations list, can display a hierarchical structure of parent-child 

relationships using icons and indentations. 

Use the Display Hierarchy check box to view the list to help you identify locations that are 

subsidiaries of parent records. 

Parent records can have up to five levels of child records, allowing you to view and act on the 

records as needed. You can still sort and search for records as you would in any view. 

If the parent record is not visible because of permission restrictions, or if you filtered the list in a 

way that the parent is not visible, the system still shows the child as indented and colored to 

indicate that it is a child in a relationship. 

To toggle between flat view and hierarchical view of a list: 

• 
To switch to a flat view, clear the Display hierarchy check box on the white bar above the 

list. Clearing the check box causes all items to be displayed by their unique ID, whether they 

have relationships to other items. 

• 
To return to the hierarchical view, select the Display hierarchy check box. 

The default for a list that has hierarchical items is to display the hierarchical view. 
Hierarchical items include Locations, departments, vendors, and customers.

Adjusting Table Size 

The More Actions button offers the Table size command to let you change the number of rows 

that you want to see on the page at one time. 

To adjust the table size: 

1. 
Open the page with the table that you want to change. 

Remember, the Table size command only affects a table on the page on which the More 

actions button appears. This command does not affect list pages, such as the Customers 
list. 

2. 
Click the More actions button. 

3. 
Click Table size. The sub-menu opens with a list of numbers of rows from 10 through 100 in 

increments of 10. 

4. 
Choose the number of rows you want the system to display for the currently displayed table. 

For example, this table contains two pages of data. Use the Table size command to 

lengthen the table size so that all rows appear on one page. 

• 
Choose the number of rows to display on each page. 

• 
Choose All rows if you want to show all rows on one page. 

This option can result in a long scrolling table. 

Printing from Lists 

To print a single record: 

1. 
Click Edit on the record you want to print. 

2. 
Click the Print to button. 

3. 
Select PDF to download the record as a portable document file (PDF) and view it. 

The record opens in your PDF reader. 

4. 
Click File and then click Print to print the file. 

Most, if not all, list screens enable you to export the list to an external application file, such as a 

Word, PDF, CSV, or Excel file. After you export the list, you can print it from the external 

application. 

To export a list and print it: 

1. 
On the list page, click the Export button and select the format to export (or click the CSV 

link). The system exports the information and downloads the file. 

2. 
Print the file using the external application’s Print feature.

Exporting from Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

To export a list of records from the system: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box to include items with an Inactive status in the data 

export results or clear the Include inactive check box to exclude inactive items. 

Some lists do not offer an option to filter by active/inactive status. 

2. 
Select the Include private check box to include items that are associated with an entity or 

clear the Include private check box to exclude these items. 

Some lists do not offer an option to include and exclude private items. 

3. 
Click the Export button. 

4. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list.

Finding Transactions in a Specific State 

List views of transactions provide a hub for viewing and accessing all transactions of a specific 

type, for example, bills or invoices. 

There are two ways to locate transactions in a specific state: 

• 
Filter for the transaction state on the fly: In the transaction list view, type the state in the 

State column, then click Go. The list displays only those transactions in that state. 

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for the transaction state: Create the view and 

set the filter to State = <state>, where <state> equals the state you are seeking, such as 

Draft, Posted, Paid, Reversed, and so forth. This custom view is always available from the 

transaction list.

Field Level Options 

The most common field level options are Add, View, and Find. 

•

where you need it. Clicking Add opens a new blank record for the same type of object. For

record that you need, but you believe that it exists. Click the Find option. The system opens 

a box in which you can type the text to search for the desired record. If you don’t find it, you 

can click Cancel and then click the Add option to add a new record.

#### Best Practices for Creating Identifiers
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 389*

Chapter 20: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Best Practices for Creating Identifiers 

• 
Enable the feature that allows the system to auto-number identifiers.  

• 
Use a character as a prefix to your ID. For example, add a V to Vendor IDs: V0001 

We recommend against using leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can 

cause errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel 

removes the leading zeros. 

If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the column of ID numbers to text format in 

Excel before importing the file content. That way, Excel won’t remove the leading zeros 

when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you use a template to import data 

that requires IDs.

### Document Numbering List
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 390*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Document Numbering List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Document Numbering`


The system offers an automatic document numbering feature used to assign unique identifiers to 

new records. 

The system uses numbering plans to assign sequential identifiers, typically when creating new 

records or transactions. The numbering plans, or document sequences, can be composed of 

numbers, letters, and punctuation such as hyphens.  

For instance, in Accounts Receivable, document sequences can be applied to invoices. If you want 

an invoice number to be preceded by the “INV-” prefix, the system will assign a sequential 

number to each new invoice using the prefix that you define (e.g., INV-001, INV-002), making it 

easy to track and organize invoices efficiently. 

Document sequencing is available only for these select transactions and records: 

• 
A/P credit adjustments, A/P debit adjustments, vendor records, and transfer payments in 

Accounts Payable. 

• 
Intercompany billing, A/R invoices, recurring A/R invoices, A/R debit adjustments, A/R credit 

adjustments, and customer records in Accounts Receivable. 

• 
Leases and amenity reservations in Commercial Property Management. 

• 
Ownership records, portal communications, and amenity reservations in Condo and Co-op. 

• 
Purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts in Spend Management. 

---


<!-- Page 391 -->
Chapter 20: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

This targeted use of sequencing ensures clarity and consistency where it’s most critical, without 

applying it universally across the system. 

Document sequencing is a two-step process. First, you configure the document number 

sequence, or numbering format, and then you assign the document sequence to the type of 

record or transaction.  

You create and manage document sequences from this list. You assign a document sequence to a 

transaction or record from the appropriate application’s configuration page. For example, to 


> **Navigation Path:** `assign a document sequence to A/R invoices, go to Accounts Receivable > Setup >`


Configuration, and then find the Document Sequencing section. 

After a document sequence is configured and assigned, the system automatically creates a 

sequential ID to each new transaction or record, ensuring a smooth and consistent flow of unique 

identifiers. 

By auto-generating IDs instead of having users enter unique IDs for new customers, vendors, and 

other records, the system saves time, adds consistency to the document numbering process, and 

avoids duplication. 

The Document Numbering list displays the list of available document sequences in your system. 

Use this list to add and manage document sequences. 

---



### Setting Up Currencies in the System: Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 392*



#### Inter-Entity Transactions and Currency
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 392*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide

Setting Up Currencies in the System: Workflow 

1. 
Enable multi-currency management (on page 387) 

2. 
Configure multi-entity base currencies 

3. 
Configure the transaction currencies (on page 383) 

4. 
Set the default base currency for each entity (on page 394) 

Inter-Entity Transactions and Currency 

Inter-entity transactions can use the same base currency or different ones. Regardless, 

transactions between entities are usually handled differently than transactions between two 

single-entity companies or outside agencies. For example: 

• 
You want to track when one entity pays A/P invoices on behalf of another entity. 

• 
What happens when the top level is used to pay an A/P invoice whose cost is allocated 

across multiple entities. 

• 
You’re sending money from one company to another as a loan. 

• 
Collecting revenue from customers on behalf another company’s work effort. 

• 
The two companies have a revenue-sharing arrangement. 

You can set up the due-to and due-from accounts so that bills can be entered with the 

accounting happening behind the scenes.

### Multi-Entity Console Page
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 397*



#### Enabling Multi-Currency Management
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 397*

Chapter 20: Common Tasks

Multi-Entity Console Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Multi-Entity Console > Configure`


The Multi-Entity Console makes it easy for corporate headquarters to support, manage, and 

control the operations of its operating entities. 

Use the Configure multi-entity page to make basic decisions about how entities operate with 

each other and corporate headquarters, including:  

• 
Selecting whether each entity can have its own base currency. 

• 
Turning on the ability to restrict customer and vendor (supplier) visibility by entity. 

• 
Controlling how the system handles inter-entity transactions. 

Enabling Multi-Currency Management 

When Multi-currency management is enabled, multi-currency controls appear for currency type, 

exchange rate type, transaction amount, base amount, and the exchange rate date. 

To enable multi-currency management: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
In the Account settings section, find the Multi-currency management section. 

4. 
Select the Enable check box. 

5. 
In Rounding account, select the account that you want to use for to keep debits and credits 

in balance. 

The system automatically uses this rounding account to keep debits and credits in balance 

if: 

• 
Journal entries are imported from a spreadsheet, and 

• 
Rounding of base currency amounts during import causes a minor difference between 

debits and credits, requiring a correcting entry (typically, a debit or credit of a penny) 

to the rounding account. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

You may need to close and restart RealPage Accounting to make the changes take effect. 

What’s Next? 

To select the currencies you want to make available in your company, see Adding a Transaction 

Currency (on page 384). You may also want to: 

• 
Enable electronic payments 

• 
Enable a vendor to receive electronic payments

#### Configuring Multiple Base Currencies for a Multi-Entity Company
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 399*

Chapter 20: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Configuring Multiple Base Currencies for a Multi-Entity Company 

Enable multiple base currencies for your multi-entity company. When enabling multiple base 

currencies, it’s a good idea to choose a value approval currency, in case any transactions need to 

be approved. A value approval currency enables the system to translate the transaction currency 

into a common currency used to evaluate transaction approval thresholds and determine whether 

a transaction requires approval. 

Note the following, after enabling multiple base currencies: 

• 
The credit card register is unavailable. Instead, you can view credit card transactions in Cash 

Management > Credit Card Transactions. 

• 
The base currency defaults to the entity level. 

To configure multiple base currencies for a multi-entity company: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select the Subscriptions option. 

3. 
Find Multi Entity Console in the list, and then select Configure. 

In the Entity preferences section, select Enable multiple base currencies. When you select 

the option, the Value approval currency setup section appears. This setting allows you to set 

a value approval currency for purchase transactions. A value approval currency enables the 

system to translate the transaction currency into a common currency used to evaluate 

transaction approval thresholds. It also determines whether a transaction requires approval. 

4. 
To set a value approval currency, select a currency from the Value approval currency 

drop-down list. Only the currencies you enable in the system are available for selection. 

---

Inter-entity transactions 

Manual balancing 

only 

Credits: Select to turn off the automatic recording of inter-entity 

payables and receivables, but only for credits, adjustments, and 

advances. Although you can still continue to create credits, advances, 

and adjustments that involve multiple entities, you’ll be required to 

separately track who owes money to whom. 

Your company won’t automatically track the inter-entity payables and 

receivables by creating offsetting journal entries in the affected entities. 

All subledger transactions: Select if you do not want the system to track 

inter-entity payables and receivables for any transaction. For example, 

although one entity can still pay an A/P invoice on behalf of another 

entity, the system won’t track the inter-entity payables and receivables 

by creating offsetting journal entries in the affected entities. 

Selecting this option also disables the ability to auto-balance GL/Journal 

entries. 

Enable auto-balancing for GL/Journal entries: Select to have the system 

record the inter-entity payables and receivables for you automatically. 

With this option, auto-balancing occurs only by entity. To auto-balance 

journal entries for other dimensions, you must do it manually. 

Enforce journal entry 

balancing by  

This option applies only if you don’t enable auto-balancing for 

GL/Journal entries. In this case, you can choose whether line items 

manually entered by users must balance by location or entity. 

If you enable auto-balancing for journal entries, it occurs at the entity 

level. If you don’t select auto-balancing, then you can choose to enforce 

the balancing at the location or entity level. 

Best practice: Unless you have a clear business requirement to balance 

by location, a best practice is to balance by entity. Balancing by entity 

includes all journal entries for the entity and includes line items for all 

locations in the entity but balancing by location includes only line items 

specific to the location and can cause some line items not to be 

included. 

Journal 
In the Journal drop-down list, select a single journal to use when 

posting inter-entity credit bills or invoices to AP or AR, respectively. 

---


<!-- Page 402 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Limit A/P credits to 

the entity owners 

Select to apply credits to A/P invoices of the owning entity only. 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies the credit to the owning 

entity first and then applies credit from the oldest to the newest A/P 

invoices. If you enable your company to limit credits to only the owning 

entity, then credits are applied to the A/P invoices of the owning entity 

and no others; any remaining credit is reserved for more A/P invoices 

owned by that entity. 

Limit A/R credits to 

the entity owners 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies credit to the owning entity 

first, and then applies credit from the oldest to the newest invoices. If 

you enable your company to limit credits to only the owning entity, then 

credits are applied to the invoices of the owning entity and no others; 

any remaining credit is reserved for more invoices owned by that entity. 

Inter-Entity Account Mapping Section 

Inter-entity account 

mapping plan 

Select the inter-entity account mapping plan you want to use: Basic or 

Advanced. 

Basic 
With the Basic inter-entity account mapping plan, when mapping 

entities to accounts for posting inter-entity transactions (IETs), the plan 

defines a common receivable account and payable account that will be 

used for all transactions involving that entity. Because it’s unnecessary to 

separately settle balances among entities involved, one inter-entity 

receivable (IER) and one inter-entity payable (IEP) account is defined per 

entity. A single set of inter-entity receivable and payable accounts can 

be shared across multiple entities or settled directly through cash or 

investments as needed. 

Advanced 
With the Advanced mapping plan, relationships are mapped between 

pairs of entities. This allows for greater granularity in tracking who owes 

whom, so you can settle between each entity pairing individually, if 

necessary. Any combination of IER and IEP accounts can be used, based 

on the accounts you defined in your previous IET account setup. This 

plan enables mapping each entity to a combination of directional 

accounts tracking IER and IEP, using separate or common IER and IEP 

accounts.

### Base Currency
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 403*

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Base Currency 

If the Multi-currency section and the Transaction Currencies option do not appear on the 

Company menu Setup tab, then multi-currency management is not enabled. To enable it, see 

Enabling multi-currency management (on page 387). 

Several of the core accounting settings on the Company information record’s Accounting tab 

were set during your initial company setup and cannot be changed. Base currency is one of these. 

You can only change the base currency before transactions are created in your company. 

Changing the base currency can have major impacts on your financials. 

Instead, you can add transaction currencies. Learn about Adding a transaction currency (on page 

384). 

For companies that use multiple base currencies, you assign a base currency to an entity when 

you create the entity. Any properties and locations that are associated with the entity use its base 

currency. When you have locations that require a different base currency, create a new entity for 

those locations. 

Entities created prior to activating the Multiple base currencies setting will retain the system 
default base currency.

Setting the Base Currency for an Entity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Edit > Base Currency`


To set the base currency of an entity: 

1.

Configuring A/P Thresholds 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Thresholds`


Use the Thresholds section to configure how the system responds when these events occur:  

• 
When posting in the future 

• 
When a credit limit is exceeded 

• 
When the vendor is on hold 

You can also set up system alerts and controls for additional actions in the system. For more 

information, refer to Ledger Sentry in online help or download (on page 480) the RealPage 

To set up A/P thresholds: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the Configuration option. 

3. 
Locate the Thresholds section. 

You can set thresholds for events so that if an event occurs, the system responds as desired. 

4. 
In the If posting in future period section, select the system response if a user attempts to set 

a future period date as the General Ledger posting date. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message requesting the user to 

select a date within the current period. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

Do nothing is the default. 

The subledgers share the same posting periods as the general ledger. 

5. 
In the If credit limit is exceeded section, select the desired system response to an attempt to 

enter an invoice that exceeds the credit limit with a vendor. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message showing the total due for 

the vendor and your set credit limit. The transaction can’t be created as entered. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

Do nothing is the default.

Filling In the Enable Independent Release and Processing of Payments for Line Items in

The ability to release only specific line items of an A/P invoice for payment gives you tighter 

control over your cash outflows. Pay only certain line items of an invoice, and pay others as 

you want. The invoice remains partially paid in the system until every line item has been 

paid. This is especially helpful for companies that have multiple entities – for example, if one 

entity has funds available to make a payment but another entity does not. For example, if 

you enter a multi-line invoice that has some items due immediately and others due in 30 

days, use this feature to release for payment only those items that are due immediately. 

Then return to this invoice in a month and release for payment the line items that were due 

in 30 days. This gives you greater control over your cash outflows and ensures that only 

those items you are ready to pay are selected for payment.

Adding a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All >

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > 
 Contact`


To create a contact quickly, you only need to assign it a unique Suggested contact name and a 

Print as name for documents. 

The Suggested contact name is the most important field in a contact record. It acts as a unique 

contact ID across the RealPage Financial Suite system, which means you can no longer edit the 

suggested contact name after you create the contact record. Furthermore, although you can 

change the printed name of a contact with the Print as field, the Suggested contact name is the 

name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists across RealPage Accounting. You can change 

the Suggested contact name of a contact in limited situations such as when a vendor’s name has 

changed. 

Additionally, when you create a new vendor, customer, employee, or user, a related contact is 

often created simultaneously based on specific fields in the record. See Creating a Contact from a 

Record to learn about which specific fields in each record create the related Suggested contact 

name. 

To create a more detailed contact record, fill in each tab on the Contact information page. 

Filling In Contact Information 

On the Contact information tab: 

1. 
Type the contact name. 

• 
This name isn’t necessarily the name that is used throughout your company because 

actual names aren’t always unique. For example, a name such as “Jose Hernandez” 

could be the same as a completely different contact in your company. 

• 
The system automatically suggests a unique Suggested contact name and Print as 

name based on the naming details you enter. 

2. 
Add the Primary email address, Primary phone number, and Company name for the 

contact.  

In the Property Management application, the system uses the primary email address that 
you enter here to fill in email addresses for emailing statements.  

3. 
Type a Suggested contact name if you want a different version than the one the system 

auto-populates. This name appears in lists and drop-down lists. 

After you save the contact, the Suggested contact name can’t be edited. 

4. 
Enter the Print as name if you want a different version to appear on printed documents than 

the one the system auto-populates.

Duplicating Records 

If your goal is to create one record and reuse it as the starting point for additional records, use 

the Duplicate function. Most types of records can be duplicated—including A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, recurring invoices, adjustments, entities, vendors, contacts, journals, G/L accounts, 

user-defined books, document numbering sequences, contracts, service tickets, email templates, 

and reporting account sets. When you open a record and it includes a Duplicate button, you can 

use it as a template to quickly create a new record.  

For invoices, you can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add it, and set the date to 

create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually and look for the section called 

“Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

To duplicate recurring invoices, look for the Duplicate option that is located in the More actions 
button menu. 

To duplicate a record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

After you duplicate a record, the copy of the record stays open so that you can change its 

details.  

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record.

### Account Groups Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 420*

Related Accounting Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Account Groups Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Account Groups`



> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Account Groups`


Account groups are the fundamental building blocks of financial reporting in RealPage 

Accounting. 

Account groups simplify reporting by organizing accounts into reusable structures (such as 

“Assets” and “Expenses”) that are separate from the reports, graphs, and performance cards that 

use them. These structures: 

• 
Roll up and organize accounts. 

• 
Create the headings and subtotals in reports. 

General Ledger accounts are shown on financial statements only if they are included in an 
account group. Accounts can’t be added directly to a report. 

Although every company’s account groups will be different, your account groups will likely 

contain groupings related to assets, expenses, revenue, and more. 

The most basic types of account groups contain either individual accounts or other account 

groups. 

• 
Account groups of type Accounts, Statistical accounts, Category, or Statistical category (on 

page 412) are used to select individual accounts. 

For example, “Cash and Cash Equivalents” might contain some bank accounts and petty 

cash. 

• 
An account group of type Group of account groups contains other account groups. 

For example, “Assets” might contain other account groups, such as “Current Assets” and 

“Fixed Assets,” which in turn contain other account groups. 

---


<!-- Page 421 -->
Chapter 21: Related Accounting Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

By nesting groups, you can create a hierarchy of groupings for reporting purposes, with the 

lowest level containing individual accounts. 

a) Account groups can contain other groups. Nesting groups creates hierarchy. 

b) At the lowest levels, account groups contain individual accounts. 

You cannot use computation account groups in financial forecasting reports. Because in 
forecasting reports you could use an “As of date ” in a partial month, mixing part actual numbers 
and part budget, the computation needed cannot accommodate computation account groups. 

---



### Types of Account Groups
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 422*

Related Accounting Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Types of Account Groups 

When you create a new account group, you indicate the type that you want it to be. Different 

account group types yield different results in your financial reports. These are they available types 

of account groups: 

• 
Accounts 

• 
Account Groups 

• 
Statistical Accounts 

• 
Category or Statistical Category Accounts 

• 
Computation Account Groups 

Accounts Account Groups 

Accounts are the most basic type of account groups and consist of one or more G/L accounts 

from your chart of accounts. You can include individual named accounts or ranges of accounts. 

For example, you might create a Cash and Cash Equivalents account group that contains various 

bank and investment accounts. 

---


<!-- Page 423 -->
Chapter 21: Related Accounting Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Here’s how it would display in a report: 

Account Groups of Account Groups 

A “group of account groups” is one that contains other account groups, thus forming a hierarchy. 

You can have groups within groups within groups, and so on, to any level of depth. 

---


<!-- Page 424 -->
Related Accounting Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

For example, the Assets account group might consist of three discrete account groups—Current 

Assets, Fixed Assets, and Other Assets—each of which contain additional subgroups. 

In the graphic above, some account groups (such as Fixed Assets and Other Assets ) are collapsed 
to show only a summary amount, while Cash is expanded to show individual accounts. When you 
view a report, you can use the expand/collapse arrows to control the level of detail. 

Statistical Accounts Account Groups 

Statistical account groups include accounts that contain specific non-financial data – for example, 

occupancy, square footage, or hotel rooms. Using statistical account groups, you can calculate 

against and report on data to get a virtually unlimited variety of ratios and business metrics, such 

as average deal size or revenue per hotel room. 

---


<!-- Page 425 -->
Chapter 21: Related Accounting Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Here’s how the Occupancy statistical account group, with some of its constituent statistical 

accounts, displays in a report: 

Category or Statistical Category Account Groups 

These apply if you used a setup template when you first created your company in the system. If 

so, the system automatically assigns pre-configured account groups to each of the accounts in 

your chart of accounts; those account groups, in turn, are used in pre-designed standard financial 

reports and graphs.  

As you create new accounts, you tag each new account with a category, which automatically 

includes that account in the relevant account groups. 

A group that is based on a category displays the same way as a group of accounts. The only 

difference is that the accounts for the group are selected by category. 

---


<!-- Page 426 -->
Related Accounting Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To find out if your company was created using a QuickStart template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Configuration section, click Company, and then select the Accounting tab. 

3. 
Check under Setup template. If the field is blank, the company was not set up using a 

template. 

Computation Account Groups 

Computation account groups consist of other account groups or individual accounts that you use 

as components in a mathematical equation. The system displays results of the equation in your 

financial report. For example, the “Revenue per Unit” equation consists of the “Total Income” 

account group divided by the “Total Units” account group. 

Computation account group is the only type of account group that allows you to set the number 

of decimal places. Any computation account group includes this option. 

• 
A commonly used computation-type account group shows an operating margin using the 

formula Operating net income divided by Net sales. Define the number of decimal places 

and type, and optionally include the unit used, such as number or percent. 

• 
To use more than the default two decimal places without affecting the actual numbers, 

create a computation account group that: 

• 
Includes only one account group. 

• 
Has a computation formula as Constant, and that constant is set to one. 

• 
Has an action to multiply the selected account group. 

• 
Has Decimal places set to the number of decimal places to display when no rounding 

is applied. The minimum is zero and the maximum is nine.

Statistical Accounts

Statistical accounts are used to track non-financial data, such as employee headcount, number of 

members, or the number of rooms in a hotel. Tracking key metrics in this type of account allows

### Statistical Journal Entries
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 429*

Chapter 21: Related Accounting Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Statistical Journal Entries 

You enter statistical transactions in the same way that you enter standard journal entries. The only 

difference is that statistical transactions do not need to balance. Instead, you increase or decrease 

a value. For example, you might increase the number of locations in the month of June. In this 

case, you would use the Locations statistical account and the journal you created for locations. 

Statistical Journals 

Statistical journals are non-monetary and do not have a debit or credit as transactions. Instead, 

statistical journals simply increase or decrease a value. 

Before you can begin adding statistical journal entries, you need one or more statistical journals in 

the system. Then, you can create statistical journal entries to add to the journals.  

Accessing the List of Statistical Journals 

You can add statistical journal entries from the All tab of the General Ledger menu, but you 

cannot view the list of statistical journals. The list of statistical journals is accessible only from the 

Setup tab of the General Ledger menu, and you must have administrator permissions to access 

the options on the Setup tab. For information about adding statistical journals, see Adding a 

statistical journal (on page 82) in the online help or download (on page 480) the RealPage 

Statistical Journal Entries 

You can add a statistical journal entry directly, or add it from the General Ledger workbench. After 

you have entered statistical transactions, you can use statistical accounts in your financial reports. 

Approvals and Statistical Entries 

Statistical entries and statistical adjusting entries are not eligible for the approval process.
