### Setting Up Accounting Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 444*

Related Accounting Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up Accounting Methods 

Creating the ability to report on either method involves enabling the feature, providing a cut-over 

period, creating the cash-basis or accrual-basis journals, and then choosing those journals in the 

appropriate applications. Applications that can make use of this feature include the General 

Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Cash Management. 

Considering switching from Accrual to Accrual and cash? Talk to your account manager 
about setup and best practices. 

Workflow 

This is a high-level overview of the setup process: 

1. 
Enable Accrual and cash in the General Ledger Setup page. 

At this time, you also select: 

• 
The cut-off date for switching over to dual-method accounting. 

• 
Your default account method for reporting. 

2. 
Create journals that are Accrual, Cash, or both Accrual and Cash. 

• 
On the Journal Information page, there’s a new option to select whether to Include 

this journal when reporting in Accrual, Cash, or both. 

• 
As a best practice, it’s recommended that you name journals in such a way that you 

can identify them as journals that are cash, accrual, or both. This is because, in several 

locations, the system displays lists of selectable journals that contain all three types. 

For example, Accounts Payable (C) for the cash-basis version. 

3. 
Choose those journals in the configuration pages for the appropriate applications. 

• 
In the setup for Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Cash Management, you’re 

prompted for accrual journals and cash journals. 

• 
In each case, the setup page indicates which type of journal it is expecting. 

You can use dual-reporting only going forward; you cannot re-categorize prior data. The cut-over 

period is chosen in the General Ledger Setup page. It is a good idea to close the books as of the 

cut-off month and work as if you are switching to a new system as of that date. 

During cutoff, you also make a journal entry to correct your books in a journal that has a 

reporting method that is opposite of your default reporting method. In other words, if you were 

accrual based during cutoff, you need to make a journal entry to eliminate payables, receivables, 

expenses, and revenues in a cash-based journal. 

The moment you select the dual-method reporting option in the General Ledger Setup page and 

save, the system unconfigures any of the following applications to which you have subscribed: 

A/P, A/R, and CM. More specifically, the system deselects any journals you previously chose, 

---


<!-- Page 445 -->
Chapter 21: Related Accounting Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

under the assumption that you wish to begin using new and accrual journals. Consequently, users 

are prevented from entering transactions into the wrong journal. Thus, these applications are in a 

subscribed-but-unconfigured state until you choose new journals in those applications. 

Consequently, you should plan to immediately create new journals, and then select them in the 

various applications. After you save those application configuration settings, users can access 

those applications again. 

Transaction entry 

In most cases, entering transactions is the same, regardless of accounting method. For example, 

users entering a bill don’t need to know whether the transaction is accrual, cash, or both. The 

system handles the posting to accrual and cash journals behind the scenes. 

However, entering a journal entry directly in the General Ledger requires that you select a journal 

that corresponds to the accounting method that should be affected. 

Reporting 

When you create reports, you have the option to override the accounting method that you 

selected as the Default for reporting in your General Ledger Setup.

### Using Reporting Account Sets with Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 446*

Related Accounting Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Using Reporting Account Sets with Reports 

In your company, you have a set of General Ledger accounts that you use for transactions and 

reporting. These General Ledger accounts are equivalent to your chart of accounts. If you have 

clients or owners with their own chart of accounts, you can still provide reports that show 

accounts that make sense to them.  

For example, you have a part owner named Example PMC Company. This owner uses a different 

chart of accounts, with different account numbers and titles. In addition, this owner categorizes 

income and expenses differently – for example, the owner rolls up expenses like painting and 

carpet cleaning into a single Maintenance account. 

By creating a reporting account set for Example PMC Company, reports can be generated 

specifically for Example PMC Company because the reporting account set contains the mapping 

of General Ledger accounts to reporting accounts. 

When reports using a reporting account set are displayed: 

• 
General Ledger accounts are automatically translated to the corresponding reporting 

accounts, so that the report reflects the account numbers and titles of the reporting account 

set. 

• 
If more than one General Ledger account is mapped to a single reporting account, the 

report automatically rolls up amounts into the single reporting account. 

• 
Clicking an amount displays supporting detail, which is also translated to reporting 

accounts. 

---



#### Individual Reports for Each Department, Location, or Entity
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 447*

Chapter 21: Related Accounting Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Individual Reports for Each Department, Location, or Entity 

For financial reports and other General Ledger reports, you can save time by: 

• 
Creating a single report for a group of departments, locations, or entities. 

• 
Selecting the option to separate the data into individual reports at runtime. 

For example, you might want to run a Profit & Loss report for three locations (London, Miami, and 

Boston). Instead of defining the Profit & Loss report three times (with each report filtered for a 

different location), you can create one combined report that gets split into individual reports (as 

sections) at runtime. 

1. Create a group of departments, locations, or entities 

If you have not already done so, create a group that specifies the departments, locations, or 

entities that you want to report on. 

• 
For departments, create a department group that includes two or more departments. For 

example, you might create an “Engineering” group that contains all departments in 

engineering. 

• 
For locations or entities, create a location group that includes two or more locations. For 

example, you might create an “Asia-Pacific” location group that contains several entities 

worldwide. 

By default, we add two groups for you—one for all active departments and another for all 
active locations. 

2. Set up the report to create individual reports for each group member 

The setup instructions differ for financial reports and other General Ledger reports. However, in 

each case, you: 

1. 
Select the group of departments, locations, or entities that you want to report on. 

2. 
Set options to split the report into individual reports. 

Financial Reports 

The following instructions assume that you are familiar with creating financial reports. You can 

find information about financial reports in the RealPage Financial Suite help system. 

1. 
Create or edit a financial report. 

2. 
On the Columns tab, expand each column of data by department or location. 

For example, if you have a single column that displays actual amounts for the prior year, 

click that column and use the Expand by option to expand the column by departments or 

locations.

Select a group from the Department or Location drop-down menu.

Filling In the Summary Frequency Section 

In the Summary frequency subsection, select how often the system creates and processes A/P 

transactions: 

1. 
In the A/P invoices and in the Adjustments drop-down lists, select the desired summary 

frequency: 

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for each transaction 

day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the most granular reporting. 

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each month and no 

matter what the transaction date is within that period, it will always be posted as of the 

last day of that month. This frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of 

reporting. 

• 
One per A/P invoice, One per A/P invoice adjustment: The system creates and posts a 

summary for each A/P invoice or adjustment. Per-transaction summaries can increase 

system performance, particularly if your transactions result in a large number of 

journal entries with unique G/L account and dimension combinations.

Updating Entity Information in Bulk via Import 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > Entities 
> Template / Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Import`


You can update entity information in bulk using the Import feature. The only field that is required 

when updating information in bulk is the Entity ID. Any additional information that you enter into 

the CSV file either adds to or updates existing information. Fields that are left blank do not 

change or overwrite existing information in the entity record. 

You must have individual permissions for each tab in the entity record to add or edit information 
on that tab. If you don’t have permission for the tab—but you do have permissions for 
entities —then the information on the tab will be read-only. These tab permissions apply when 
adding entities, importing entities, editing entities, or updating entities via import. 

Download the Entities Template from the Import Data Page 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information. This is important because: 

• 
Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage Accounting at any time, especially when a new 

version of RealPage Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not 

work. 

To download the Entities template from the Import data page: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import data menu option. The Import data page opens. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the row labeled Entities, and then click the 

Template link. 

In addition to standard columns, the system dynamically appends columns for any 
dimensions you’ve enabled and any custom fields and custom objects you’ve created so 
that you can import that information as well. 

4. 
Populate the template with any entity information that you want to add or update. Leave 

the cell blank if you do not want to update that field in the existing entity record. 

You must enter the Entity ID; all other fields are optional. 

5. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

6. 
Close the CSV file.

Downloading Import Templates

#### Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 464*

Import Preparation 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
Find the type of data that you want to import.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

A prompt opens at the bottom of the web page, asking if you want to Open, Save, or 

Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your browser’s default download folder. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Save the template to your computer, and then continue downloading templates as needed until 

you have downloaded all of the templates for data that you want to import. 

If you have a database administrator (DBA) of your other system, give the downloaded templates 

to your DBA. Ask the DBA to: 

• 
Export the data from your other system, as specified in the import template spreadsheets. 

• 
Put the applicable data into each spreadsheet. 

• 
Save the spreadsheet as a comma-delimited file (CSV). 

If you do not have a DBA, or if your DBA does not have time to complete the whole task, you can 

complete the tasks. Refer to the following topics for guidance on creating importable data. 

---



#### Filling In an Import Template with Data
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 465*



#### About CSV Templates
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 465*

Chapter 22: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 462). 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.  

About CSV Templates 

There are some things you should know about the CSV templates and how they behave before 

adding your data. 

Removing All Commas from Your CSV File 

RealPage recommends removing all commas from your CSV file. 

A CSV file is a Comma Separated Values file (also sometimes known as a comma delimited file). If 

there are commas in the data of your file (for example, if your numbers are formatted like 10,000 

or if you use commas between words in a field), your data will be shifted one column over 

because that is how the file is intended to work. This will either cause errors in the information or 

cause the whole import to fail. 

RealPage recommends you do not keep your actual data in a CSV file. Instead, use an Excel 
workbook to take advantage of the formatting options of Excel. When you’re ready, export your 
data as a CSV file for import into RealPage Accounting. In this way, your data is formatted 
correctly for import, but you also have Excel functionality in your workbook. 

---


<!-- Page 466 -->
Import Preparation 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Column Order 

You can change the order of the columns as you see fit, as long as the information in the header 

cell doesn’t change. 

Do not rename or otherwise change the headers in your templates. If you change the headers, 
your import will fail. 

However, some templates require information to be imported in a specific order. For example, 

transaction data should not be imported before information about the transactions has been 

imported. Header columns containing information about the entire import need to stay to the left 

of detail columns (columns that contain the details of an account, transaction, vendor, etc.). 

RealPage recommends reviewing the column order of the original template before moving 

columns around. 

Adding Additional Columns 

If you need to keep other related information in your template document, you can add your own 

columns for this information. If you add your own columns, use a # (hashtag) symbol before the 

name of any column you add. Examples: 

#BudgetNotes 

#ClientInfo 

If by chance you use a name already in use by the system, the # (hashtag) will make sure that the 

information in your columns is not imported by accident. 

You can also use the # (hashtag) to write notes to yourself in your template. If you place the # 

(hashtag) at the start of a row, the whole row of information is ignored during import. 

You can create rows of notes by starting the row with # in the first column. 

Hiding Columns for Easy Data Entry 

When editing your file in Excel, you can hide columns you won’t be using for data entry. 

Be sure to enter required information in your file. Hiding required columns and not entering 
required information will cause your import to fail. 

Data Must Conform to the Business Logic of RealPage 

For example, the Budget ID field on the Budget Information page allows a 20-character ID to be 

entered. It follows then that the Budget import template would have the same limitation: if you 

try to import a Budget ID with more than 20 characters in your CSV file, your import fails. 

How data should be formatted is found in the header description row, under the header row. 

You can also see a field-by-field description for your specific template in this help. 

---


<!-- Page 467 -->
Chapter 22: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Go to Importing Data, find the template you want to know more about, and click the 

corresponding link. 

Blank Fields Overwrite Existing Data 

A blank value in a cell is considered to be the desired value (a blank) for the field referenced by 

the column heading for the record being imported. 

In almost all cases, a blank field will overwrite existing data in RealPage to also be blank. 

Say you had the existing value 111 Elm St. as the address for a customer and you import a blank 

for this field. If you go to the normal user interface and examine the contents of that field, you will 

see that the original value 111 Elm St. is replaced by nothing, and the field is blank. 

This is not true, however, for these templates: 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Transactions 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Opening Balances 

If the value is blank in certain fields, the import does not overwrite the existing value. To remove 

the existing value in these few cases, enter the value NULL. These cases are clearly identified in 

their header descriptions. 

Budgets are an exception. Budgets can be appended with new dates, with new lines not 
previously budgeted, or they can be overwritten if same date/account combinations are used. 

Calculated Field Values 

If you used a formula to come to a value in a field, you can leave the result in place as long as you 

match the RealPage field value for decimals. 

Accounting Application Page Help 

In most cases, there is an exact match between the application pages (and the business logic with 

which they behave) and the data that you import. This includes the constraints on that data and 

any dependencies that may exist between the data in the import file and other data in the system, 

or other data that you also import. 

After you have added all of your data, you save the Excel spreadsheet as a CSV file. 

Debits and Credits Must Balance 

When importing a file that includes debits and credits, your debits and credits must balance. 

RealPage adheres to accepted accounting rules, which require debits and credits to balance. 

Likewise, if you require accounts to balance by location, then when you import location balances 

using a CSV template, the location debits and credits must also balance. 

---


<!-- Page 468 -->
Import Preparation 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicating Records 

If an identical record already exists in the system, the import for that record typically fails because 

RealPage detects that the record exists and does not allow duplicates. 

Duplicates are not allowed in account numbers, departments, locations, employees, customers, 

and vendors. Although you can have duplicate transactions, the transaction summary name must 

be unique per application. 

Journal entries are an exception. The system does not check for duplicate journal entries, so 
when importing journal entries, be sure to check that they have a unique ID or name.

Line Numbers 

See the Line number examples (on page 465) page for more information on how to use lines 

numbers in your CSV imports. 

Special Characters 

UTF-8 is supported in imported files, so character accents and other special characters are 

imported correctly. 

RealPage recommends that you remove commas from all numbers and do not use commas in any 

text fields. 

CSV Data Exported from Non-Excel Software 

When exporting data from other applications, the other software might use a non-standard 

approach to quoting, which could cause problems when importing into the system. 

As noted above, RealPage recommends removing all commas from text fields in a CSV file. 

However, there could be times in which removing the commas is not the ideal solution. In this 

case, CSV files do allow quotes around a value that contains a comma, and the system accepts 

this in an import. For example: 

1,2,3, “All, with exceptions” 

There may also be instances when you need to include a quote mark inside a statement with a 

comma. In this case, you would use a second set of quote marks, as follows: 

1,2,3, “All, with “inventory” exceptions”

Preparing Your CSV File for Import 

The Import data page is a quick way to import your information into the system. However, the 

way you prepare your CSV files directly affects the success or failure of importing your data. Learn 

the CSV import process to streamline the import process. 

This topic provides general information about preparing CSV files for import. Links to information 
about specific templates can be found in the Import data into the system, which lists all import 
topics. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 

Most imports start with getting the most recent template from the Import data page. When you 

get your templates from this list, you get templates that have been tailored to your specific 

company, including specific dimensions. 

Next you add your data, using the correct formatting as explained in the template. After you’ve 

added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

Downloading a Template 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because: 

• 
Templates in the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage at any time, especially when a new version of 

RealPage Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.

import into the system. 

3. 
Decide on the type of information to upload, and then click the Template link associated 

with that information. 

Other Templates 

RealPage may have additional CSV import templates that are not found on the Import data page. 

Contact your RealPage Support Representative for any templates that have been customized for 

your company. 

Adding Your Data 

After you download the appropriate template, add your data. 

The following example shows a portion of a standard CSV file for importing accounts receivable 

invoices after it has been opened in Excel, but before data has been added. The top row is the 

header row, (the data labels for all of your data), and the second row contains descriptions of the

b) Some fields are required. 

c) Header row 

d) Header description row 

Each template contains a set of pre-defined headers, such as BUDGET_ID, ACCT_NO, and soon.

changing the headers.

To add your data: 

1. 
Open the template that you downloaded from the Import data page. 

2. 
Enter your information. Use the header descriptions as a guide for how to enter information 

correctly. 

• 
Do not change the headers. 

The header titles in the header row correlate to fields in UI. Incorrect header titles will 

cause an import error. When you download a template, the correct headers are in the 

template. 

• 
Read the header descriptions. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with a value not accepted by the column, it will cause an error in your import. 

• 
Enter required information. 

Some data is required, while others are not. Read the description field to determine 

which information is required. If you do not enter the required information, your 

import will fail. 

3.

from Excel, select the comma delimited file type. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it.

Best Practices 

The following best practices will help you prepare your CSV file for upload.  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import Data option. The Import data page opens. This is the page where you can 

find the latest templates. 

3. 
Find the object that you want to import, and then click its Template link to download a 

template.  

• 
Use the latest template, especially following a product release.  

• 
Use the correct template for the area in which you want to upload information. 

Different templates organize different types of information. Use a template specifically 

for the information you need to upload.  

4. 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to entering information.  

• 
Do not change the titles in the header row.  

The header titles correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header titles will cause an 

upload error. When you download a template from the Import data page, the correct 

headers are in the template.  

• 
Read the header descriptions in the template.  

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with an incorrect accepted value, it will cause an error in your upload.  

• 
Enter required information.  

Read the description field to determine which information is required. If you do not 

include required information, your upload will fail.  

Save the file as a comma-separated value, or CSV, file. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it. Leave the file open until your import is successful. Excel can sometimes reformat 

the file if you close it before the import is successful.

#### Line Number Examples
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 475*

Chapter 22: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Line Number Examples 

When you import information into RealPage Accounting that uses line numbers, such as journal 

entries, invoices, or adjustments, use the following tips to ensure that your line numbers import 

correctly. 

Journal Entry Line Numbers 

When importing general ledger journal entries (including statistical journal entries), the number of 

the line item in the CSV file defines the order in which those lines are imported. There are a few 

things you can do when entering journal entry information into the CSV file that will make 

reconciliation of the journal entries easier after import: 

• 
Group debits and corresponding credits together 

• 
Enter information in the CSV template as if you were entering it in a regular journal (group 

information in a reasonable manner) 

In the G/L journal entry example below, LINE_NO 1 and 2 are entries for legal and professional 

fees and are accounted for in the DEBIT column. The corresponding CREDIT for Accounts Payable 

in line 3 equals the fees; debits match the credits. 

In line 4, a DEBIT is entered for another legal fee, with the corresponding CREDIT in line 5. Again, 

debits match the credits. 

In this example, line items in the LINE_NO start at 1 and proceed sequentially. This example also 

groups related debits and credits together, so that reconciliation is easier. The LINE_NO column 

determines the order in which the line items are imported into the system and how they will 

appear in your journal entry. RealPage recommends entering information in the CSV file as if you 

are entering it in a real journal entry. This way, when you revisit the journal entry after import, 

your entries make sense. 

Exchange Rates in Journal Entries 

When uploading G/L journal entries, the exchange rate is not required. However, if you want to 

use your own exchange rate, you must add the exchange rate to the journal entry line. The journal 

entry line number is referenced by the system. Enter journal entry line numbers as described in 

Journal entry line numbers. Line numbers are important to ensure proper line-header consistency. 

If you don’t enter a line number, or enter line numbers out of sequence, the import will fail. 

---


<!-- Page 476 -->
Import Preparation 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you want to use the exchange rate provided by RealPage, leave the exchange rate column blank 

in the CSV file. 

Multiple Journal Entry, Invoice, or Adjustment Line Numbers 

When you enter multiple journal entries, invoices, or adjustments, you must start the line number 

count over at 1. 

When you enter a single journal entry, invoice, or adjustment into a CSV file, you start the 

LINE_NO column at one for the line entries and continue sequentially. Below is an example of a 

single invoice entered in a CSV file. 

Figure 1: An example of an invoice, with sequential line numbers. 

a) Total Due column 

b) The AMOUNT column adds up to the TOTAL_DUE. 

c) The line numbers start at 1 and continue in sequential order. 

When you enter multiple journal entries, invoices, or adjustments into a CSV file, there are several 

things you can do to ensure your information imports correctly into the system: 

• 
Group information in a reasonable manner. 

• 
When importing invoices, make sure that the AMOUNT column and the TOTAL_DUE column 

have the same amount for each entry. 

• 
LINE_NO refers to the line item number, so when entering formation into the CSV file, start 

the LINE_NO at 1, and then list each following line item in sequential order. 

In the example below, you can see the first line item entry of a customer invoice has been marked 

as line 1 in the LINE_NO column. This invoice has line items entered in sequential order, and the 

AMOUNT column for the first invoice (in orange) and the TOTAL_DUE column equal the same 

amount. 

The second invoice (in pink) has line items that also start at 1 and continue in sequential order. 

This invoice also has the TOTAL_DUE and the AMOUNT columns equaling the same amount. 

These concepts apply to journal entries and adjustments as well: when more than one journal, 

invoice, or adjustment is added to a CSV file, you must restart the line number (LINE_NO) count at 

1 for the line items to be imported correctly. 

---


<!-- Page 477 -->
Chapter 22: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

When adding data for multiple line numbers in the same template file, be sure to start the line 
numbers over at one, as shown in the following image.

If your journals, invoices, or adjustments have line items and you do not enter a line number in the 
LINE_NO column, or enter line numbers out of sequence, the import will fail.

Use Row Numbers to Find Errors 

When importing A/P invoices or A/R invoices using a CSV file, if errors are found during upload, 

the entire CSV file is rejected. You can find the errors in the file if you use row numbers in the Do 

Not Import column. If your CSV file is rejected because errors are found, the error file contains the 

original row number, allowing you to quickly pinpoint where to make changes. 

a) Number the rows in the “Do not import” column. 

b) Error file contains original row numbers.

#### Order of CSV Imports

#### Importing Offline

*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 478*

Import Preparation 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide

Order of CSV Imports 

In some cases, CSV imports must be performed in a specific order because of dependencies 

within the data. For example, if you have transactions that require locations, but you have not 

entered or imported the locations, the transaction import fails. 

It is always best to follow the order of the steps as they are presented in the Import data page 

when performing any type of import. Not all of the steps are required. For example, you may not 

use territories anywhere in your accounting data, therefore creating them is optional. 

In a few cases there are circular references. For example, an employee record can reference a 

department and vice versa. Problems that would otherwise result from such circular references 

have been eliminated for the purposes of importing by removing certain items. If you absolutely 

must have this data, you need to enter it manually. 

Importing Offline 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much processing the 

system must do to the data. If you are in doubt, select the Process offline option on the import 

utility page. 

When the offline process is complete, the system sends an email to the address you entered in 

the Import Company Information box (where you imported your file). 

RealPage recommends selecting Process offline when importing CSV files and providing your 
email address. If your import fails, you will always be notified, and the failed records are sent to 
your email. 

Automating Imports 

You may be able to automate and schedule your imports using a third-party application, such as 

Workato. 

Contact your account representative to learn more about this option.

### Introduction

#### Import Error Notification
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 480*

Resolving Import Errors 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Introduction 

When an import process fails, the system sends an email containing a list of errors and how to 

correct the problems.  

This section details the email notification, common errors associated with importing data, and 

how to handle them. 

Import Error Notification 

There are a number of reasons imported records fail, such as duplicated entries or invalid field 

content. RealPage provides information about the failed records in an attempt to help you fix the 

import error. 

Finding the Error Message 

The Import confirmation page indicates how many records failed. This page also contains a link 

to download a CSV file, which contains only the failed records. 

Records that are successfully imported are not returned in the CSV file. 

Click the link and download the CSV file. 

If you entered your email address into the Import Company Information box, an email is sent 

that contains the error messages for your attempted import. The email lists the error code, and 

then each unique instance of that error in the file you attempted to import. 

The error message email is sent to the email address associated with the user ID logged in at the 

time of the file upload; otherwise, the email address for the company contact is used. 

The import pages also allow another email address to be explicitly entered in the Email results to 

this address field. 

If you did not enter your email in the Import Company Information box, and you do not click the 
link in the Import confirmation page, there is no way to retrieve the CSV error report file for the 
import you just did. 

Best practice: Enter your email in the Import Company Information box at the beginning of every 
import. 

The reason you are sent a separate email with the error messages is because a record could fail 

for more than one reason. Displaying all of the text for each record in the CSV file could become 

quite cumbersome and hard to read. Furthermore, it is often the case that thousands of records 

are uploaded. If thousands of errors fail, the CSV file could become quite bloated. 

---


<!-- Page 481 -->
Chapter 23: Resolving Import Errors 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Read the Error Message Email 

The error messages for your failed upload file can be challenging to read. RealPage recommends 

the following strategy: 

• 
Start at the top of the email and look at each error message section. 

• 
In each section, start reading from the bottom up. The error at the bottom of the section is 

the first error encountered during import. 

a) Start here. 

b) Read from the bottom up. 

c) In each section, the specific error is listed at the top. 

---


<!-- Page 482 -->
Resolving Import Errors 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Start at the Top of the Email 

Error messages are presented in sections, and the sections are listed in the order that the errors 

are encountered in your file. 

Example: 

=================================================== 
Error BL01001973 
=================================================== 
BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number.  
The account number ‘4150’ already exists. 
BL01001973-1 Correction: Enter unique account number. 
BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record Could not create  
GL Account record! 
=================================================== 

When you read the error messages such as the one above, start with the error number. 

The error codes, such as BL01001973 above, are internal codes. These internal codes can help 
RealPage locate the source of a systemic issue if one is identified. 

=================================================== 
Error BL03000019 
=================================================== 
BL03000019-1 Description: Invalid contact data entered. 
TRANSACTION TYPE is a required field and cannot be empty 
BL03000019-1 Correction: Some of the fields you have entered 
are invalid. Please correct them with proper values. 
=================================================== 

Read from the Bottom of the Error Message Up 

In the example, the error code is BL01001973-2. 

Description: Unable to create record Could not create G/L Account record! first. 

This identifies the first error that occurred during import. It’s not informative, however, so look at 

the next error message for more information. 

The next error message in the list (as read from the bottom up), BL01001973-1 Correction: 

Enter unique account number, identifies the reason the G/L account record couldn’t be 

created, but it’s not yet clear what to do to fix the problem. 

The final error message in the example above (as read from the bottom up) describes more fully 

the cause of the error and suggests a fix: find and delete the duplicate account number.

#### Handling Import Errors
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 486*

Resolving Import Errors 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Handling Import Errors 

If you experience import errors, review the tips in About CSV Templates (on page 455) and review 

the common errors (on page 473).  

Import errors occur when you try to import information that does not match the requirements of 

the template. Each template has a set of required information that you must enter to successfully 

import the file, and formats to follow for certain kinds of information. Read the descriptions in the 

template to determine the most accurate way to enter your data.  

If individual transactions are in error, the rows in the transaction that are in error are saved in a 

CSV file for you along with an error code for each row. The system sends an email with 

information about specific errors (on page 470).

#### How to Read Paths
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 491*

Chapter 24: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

---


<!-- Page 492 -->
Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record. 

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

### Audit Trails

#### Viewing Audit Trails
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 493*



#### Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 493*

Chapter 24: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view. 

---



##### Fields
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 494*



##### Buttons
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 494*

Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Fields 

Audit Trail Columns 

Date 
This is the date and time of the change to the record, presented in the time zone 

defined in your preferences. 

Action 
This column indicates the type of update made to the record (whether it was 

created, modified, or deleted). It also indicates whether the system performed the 

action as part of a workflow, or if a user performed the action. 

Completed by This is the ID of the user who made the change. 

If the transaction is an eInvoice or oInvoice, the audit trail displays 

realpageaccounting as the user who submitted the transaction. This is because 
eInvoices and oInvoices are created electronically, either by the vendor through 
Storefront or through Invoice Processing. 

The system previously designated CPAUser as the user who submitted 
electronic invoices. 

Source 
This is the source from which the record was accessed or changed. 

Field 
This is the name of the field that was changed. 

Before 
This is the data that appeared in the field before the user saved the change. 

After 
This is the changed data that appears in the field after the user saved the change. 

Buttons 

Audit Trail Box/Audit Trail Page 

Done 
Saves any changes and opens the previous page 

Help 
Opens the Online Help page 

More actions 
Opens a drop-down list with the following options: 

• 
Export to CSV: Downloads the report as a CSV file 

• 
Export to Excel: Downloads the report as an XLS file 

• 
Export to PDF: Downloads the report as a PDF file 

• 
Table size: Allows you to select the number of rows you want to 

display per application page

General Ledger Reports 

General Ledger financial reports and statements give you the means to collect and share vital information about 

your company’s finances. When your company was set up, it included many standard reports that come ready to 

use, and you can create other financial and custom reports to provide even more insight. 

You can run, view, process, memorize, export, and customize General Ledger reports. 

Additionally, you can create financial reports and graphs. 

Using the Financial Report Writer, you can create innumerable variations of reports, including income statements, 

balance sheets, budget variance reports, gross margin, statement of cash flows, and so on. 

In multi-entity companies that use global consolidation, instead of seeing all the consolidation books listed in the 

book selection, you’ll only see those books that you have permissions to all entities and the elimination entity.

### Summary of Standard G/L Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 12*

General Ledger Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Summary of Standard G/L Reports 

Sometimes your quickest way to enter the data you want is to use the default settings. These 

predetermined (or default) settings are the ones most often selected by others. For example, you 

can run a standard report preset to the current period on all records without setting any filters. 

Click an application link in the following table to see a list of the standard reports available for 

that application. You create standard reports by configuring the filters available in the report 

settings page. Depending on the report, there are between 10 and 30 filters, such as accounting 

period, custom date ranges, detail level, summary views, sorting, grouping, and dimensional 

analysis. 

Some standard reports are available in more than one application, and usually have 
application-specific variations in filters and format. 

Daily Reports 

The Daily Tasks section on the General ledger menu lists the two most frequently used financial 

reports: 

• 
Trial Balance Report: Use this report to show balances of all accounts, including or 

excluding statistical accounts. You can also select the Retain YTD Balances feature to show 

accumulated balances for income statement accounts that close into retained earnings at 

year-end. 

• 
General Ledger Report: Use this report to show data in your General Ledger accounts. You 

can adjust the time period, accounts, and other criteria to meet your reporting needs. 

Reports 

The Reports section of the General Ledger menu divides the reports into two subsections. 

• 
Financial statements 

• 
Financial analytics 

Financial Statements 

• 
Financial Reports: Use this report to run financial graphs and financial reports, including 

financial statements and financial analytics. 

• 
Financial Graphs: Use this option to create graphs for your company. 

• 
Account Balances Report: Use this report to view balances of accounts by a single account, 

a range of accounts or an account group. 

• 
Account Groups Hierarchy: Use this report to display a graphical representation of the 

hierarchy of your account groups, which includes member account groups and their 

accounts.  

• 
Budget: Use this report to slice and dice your budget information. If you have a financial 

report with budget columns, you can also navigate into the Budget report, and from the 

Budget report to the Budget details page. 

---

• 
Chart of Accounts: Use this report to view a filtered list of accounts. 

• 
Journals: Use this report to show the transactions for a journal for a given reporting period. 

You can filter on location and department, and elect whether or not to display columns for 

location and department. 

• 
Reporting Accounts Mapping Report: Use this report to show how General Ledger 

accounts in your company are mapped to accounts in one or more reporting account sets. 

• 
AR - Multifamily: Use this report to review the Accounts Receivables of a multifamily 

property. 

• 
Security Deposits - Multifamily: Use this report to review the security deposit status of a 

multifamily property. 

• 
Amortization Schedule: Use this report to view the payment schedule of a charge for which 

the customer has prepaid. 

• 
Prepaids Report: Use this report to view a list of all prepaid charges for a location or 

location group. 

• 
Rent Roll: Use this report for a snapshot of your property’s current state of occupancy. It 

lists all units by occupancy and rental status, and provides detailed unit information. You 

can see at a glance all of the units in the property that are occupied and unoccupied. The 

system pulls the data from Leasing & Rents. 

Financial Analytics 

• 
Dimension Balances: Use this report to create a summary of balances with dimension and 

account values. 

• 
General Ledger Revaluation: Revaluation reports are a part of the month-end workflow to 

accrue for unrealized AP/AR and General Ledger gains and losses or realized Cash 

Management gains and losses. These reports help you calculate unrealized currency gains 

and losses. This report is available when the multi-currency setting is enabled. 

• 
Trial Balance Comparative: Use this report to compare account balances over time by 

comparing one reporting period against another. 

• 
Journal Activity: Use this report to show a hierarchical list of journal activity across a 

location or the department. 

• 
Department Activity: Use this report to show a hierarchical list of department activity across 

the company. You can view data for one department or all departments, and for all 

accounts, or the data for one account group. For example, suppose you want to know the 

liability position for the manufacturing department company wide. You would choose that 

department and account group. Display the report by department (or by location within the 

department, if you have selected that option), date, and then account. You can print a report 

that contains all departments, or individual departments on separate report pages. You can 

include statistical accounts as well. Display options include the ability to suppress 

departments that have had no activity in the period, and detailed or summary modes.

• 
Location Activity: Use this report to show a hierarchical list of location activity across the 

company. You can view data for one location or all locations, and for all accounts, or the 

data for one account group. For example, suppose you want to know the liability position 

for the San Jose location company wide. You would choose that location and account 

group. Display the report by location (or by department within the location, if you have 

selected that option), date, and then account. You can print a report that contains all 

locations, or individual locations on separate report pages. You can include statistical 

accounts as well. Display options include the ability to suppress locations that have had no 

activity in the period, and detailed or summary modes. 

• 
Unit Activity: Use this report to show a hierarchical list of unit activity across a location or 

the company. 

• 
Segment Activity: Use this report to view the transactions for one segment for a date range. 

Deferred Revenue Reports 

• 
Deferred Revenue Forecast: Use this report to show how deferred income is recognized as 

revenue over time. Use this report to forecast revenue by time period, account, customer, 

and more. 

• 
Deferred Revenue Forecast Graph: This graph shows how deferred income is recognized as 

revenue over time. 

• 
Deferred Revenue Details: Use this report to show the details of customers and transactions 

for which you have deferred revenue for a specific period. For example, if the current month 

is March and you want to see revenue recognized as of March 31, running this report shows 

you any transactions processed in March along with a breakdown of the revenue for the 

transactions that were deferred, recognized, and paid. 

• 
Deferred Revenue Revaluation report: This report is available to companies that use 

multiple transaction currencies and revenue recognition. This report enables you to 

revaluate revenue recognition schedule entries based on the Revaluation As of Date and 

Revaluation Exchange Rate Type. The system calculates the currency gain/loss for every 

row of the revenue recognition schedule-entry table. This report is available when the 

multi-currency setting is enabled.

Using Reporting Accounts with G/L Reports 

Reporting accounts provide flexibility and customization in financial reporting, allowing you to 

tailor financial statements and reports to meet specific requirements or preferences of 

stakeholders, such as management, investors, or regulatory authorities. By using alternative 

reporting account sets, you can present financial information in a more meaningful and relevant 

way, making it easier for report users to interpret and analyze the data. Additionally, having the 

ability to use different reporting account sets can help you comply with different accounting 

standards or regulations, adapt to changes in the business environment, and improve 

decision-making processes. 

These are the standard reports that you can use with reporting account sets: 

• 
General Ledger (on page 57) 

• 
Trial Balance (on page 37) 

• 
Comparative Trial Balance (on page 48) 

• 
Account Balances (on page 144) 

• 
Journals (on page 172) 

For more about reporting accounts, see Reporting Account Sets (on page 519) in online help or 

download (on page 554) the RealPage Accounting General Ledger User Guide.

General Ledger Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Report Libraries 

When your system was set up, it included libraries of financial and standard reports that you can 

install into your application. Installing reports from the libraries saves time and simplifies the 

process of reporting. These preconfigured reports are based on the most common reports that 

companies create and use. 

You must have the right permissions to install items from libraries. 

After you install a report, graph, or dashboard from a library, they’re like any other. You can edit, 

run, and schedule reports and graphs and add them to a dashboard. Additionally, you can add 

other components to dashboards that you installed from a library. 

The system offers four libraries: 

• 
Financial Reports library 

• 
Report Structure library 

• 
Graphs library 

• 
Dashboards library 

Libraries are available only if your company was created using a QuickStart template (on page 7).  

Your system may offer additional libraries for dimension report structures. 

---

How to Determine If Your Company Was Created with a QuickStart Template 

Companies are often set up using a QuickStart setup template. Using QuickStart templates are a 

way to: 

• 
Get started faster. 

• 
Take advantage of predefined categories, structural information, pre-created account 

groups, and financial reports. 

• 
Install dashboards, account groups, and charts from system libraries. 

After setting up your company in RealPage Accounting with a QuickStart template, you can’t 

change or add templates for your system. If your company was set up without a QuickStart 

template, you can add a template. 

To find out if your company was created using a QuickStart template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Configuration section, select Company. 

3. 
Select the Accounting tab. 

---

If a template was used, the template type appears under Setup template. If the field is 

blank, the company was not set up using a template.

Financial Reports Library 

The Financial Reports library gives you many financial reports that you can easily install. The actual 

reports available in the library depend on the QuickStart template used to create your company. 

The financial reports library includes multiple variations of profit/loss reports, balance sheet 

reports, cash balance reports, and revenue reports. 

 In the Financial Reports library, you’ll find a set of report templates that you can install and 

configure to suit more specific requirements. These reports, or report templates, not only provide 

a ready-to-go set of common reports, but also provide a starting point to copy and customize 

them to meet your company’s requirements. Like all reports, you must have the right permissions 

to install reports from the library. 

You cannot change reports in the library, but you can install and then customize them.  

You install a report from the Financial Reports library (on page 10) with a different name, saving 

the report locally. 

Financial Report Categories 

The reports in the Financial Reports library use categories that map the account groups to the 

category. 

To find category assignments: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column of the menu, click the Account Groups Hierarchy option. 

Use the Category from drop-down list to view the available categories. 

3. 
Filter and run the report. You can filter by account groups and categories.

Dimension Report Structure Libraries 

Report structures provide a flexible way for you to organize data that you want to see in the rows 

or columns of a financial report. Report structures are based on a dimension: a location, 

department, customer, vendor, or employee. 

For example, instead of showing all locations in a report, you might want to select a location 

structure that is named for a particular region and includes a subset of locations. 

You can add any number of structures for the dimensions you track. 


> **Navigation Path:** `To find your dimension structures, go to General Ledger > Reports > Financial Statements >`


Dimension Structures.  

For multi-entity shared users: This is a master object, which can either be common (that is, 
accessible) to all entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific entity.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

1. 
Open the Dashboards application.

Click the Dashboards option.

Dimension Balances Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Analytics > Dimension 
Balances`


Use the Dimension Balances report to create a summary of balances with dimension and account 

values. You can select the dimensions to include in a balance style report, with balances shown 

side by side, per dimension, or in a single column view with cascading values. 

The Dimension Balances report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

The dimensions and accounts that you choose form the content of your report. 

The Dimension Balances report gives you visibility into account balances by dimension in 

aggregate, rather than by filtering dimensions. You can include or exclude statistical accounts. 

If you do not see this report in the menu, contact your system administrator to add it to your 
application.

To customize the Dimension Balances report: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column of the menu, in the Financial analytics section, select Dimension 

Balances.  

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report.  

You can either define the report coverage by reporting period or by balance date range but not 

both. Do one of the following: 

• 
Select the reporting period and then type the starting date in the As of date field. You can 

also click the 
 Calendar button, and then select the date from the calendar. Select the 

Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt for the As of date before running the 

report. 

• 
Specify the Opening balance date and Closing balance date to identify the report’s 

coverage period. Set a specific Start date and End date.  

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

---


<!-- Page 31 -->
Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up the filters as needed. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
If your company has multiple reporting books, select the main Reporting book and Other 

books to use for this report. 

2. 
In the Other books section, click the Select button, and then choose the desired books to 

include in the report. For help on using the multi-select box, see Using the Multi-Select Box 

(on page 504).  

The list of journals you can include in the report will be restricted to journals for those 

reporting books. 

3. 
Select the Combine reporting book with other books check box if applicable. 

4. 
In the G/L account number selection section, select the accounts to include: 

• 
Range: Select this option to include a contiguous range of accounts in the report by 

selecting the starting account in the range in the Account from drop-down list, and 

then selecting the last account in the range in the Account to drop-down list. 

• 
Multiple accounts: Select this option to include multiple non-contiguous accounts in 

the report. Click the Select accounts link, and then choose the desired accounts to 

include. 

• 
All accounts: Select this option to include all accounts in the report. 

5. 
To set the report to show results for an account group, select a group of accounts from the 

Account group drop-down list. You can select any type of account group except statistical 

account groups. You can select both an account group and the accounts you selected in the 

previous step. 

6. 
Select the Include statistical accounts in output check box if you want to include statistical 

accounts in the report. Statistical accounts are used to track non-financial data, such as 

number of members. 

7. 
Select the Ignore inactive accounts in output check box to exclude inactive accounts from 

the Dimension Balances report. Inactive accounts are those accounts you have set to a 

status of Inactive because you are no longer using this account. 

If you select the Ignore inactive accounts in output check box in the Dimension Balance 

report, navigating from the Dimension Balance report displays both active and inactive 

account values in the General Ledger report even though these are not included in the 

Dimension Balance report. 

For example, say you have the inactive account 8000--Others that has an activity and is 

assigned to the marketing department. If a Dimension Balance report is generated for the 

Show Dimension value that includes this department, but you chose to ignore inactive 

accounts in the output, the marketing department amounts for account 8000--Others will 

---


<!-- Page 32 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

not be included in the output. However, if you navigate into to the General Ledger report 

because there was account activity from other active accounts for the marketing 

department, the value is still included. 

Setting Up Dimension Filters 

1. 
In the Department drop-down list, select a department to limit report results to one or 

more specific departments. 

• 
Select the Include subs check box to include child departments when filtering. Clear 

this check box if you don’t want the system to include children of the dimension when 

filtering. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you selected a department group. This option 

creates a separate report for the individual departments. The order of the departments 

in the groups determines the order in which the system creates individual reports.  

You must select a department group if you select the Individual Report option. 

2. 
To limit the report to a selected property (location) or location group, click the Select button 

under the Property label, and then select a property or group from the Selection box. After 

choosing a couple of properties, the Select button is replaced with the list of the properties 

that you chose: 

• 
Select the Include subs check box to include child locations when filtering. Clear this 

check box if you don’t want the system to include children of the dimension when 

filtering.

### General Ledger Revaluation Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 41*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 41*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

General Ledger Revaluation Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Financial Analytics > General Ledger Revaluation`


Revaluation reports are a part of the month-end workflow to accrue for unrealized AP/AR and 

General Ledger gains and losses or realized Cash Management gains and losses. 

The General Ledger Revaluation 
report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on 
financial reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

These reports help you calculate unrealized currency gains and losses. Gains and losses are 

computed on a transaction-by-transaction basis using a selected exchange rate for comparison. 

This is usually the ending exchange rate for the period, and is always a “best guess” for the final 

transaction. Foreign currency transactions are recomputed by account using the selected 

exchange rates. 

Revaluation reports do not include information on inter-entity transactions. 

For example, before inter-entity journal entries are paid, you need to account for unrealized gains 

or losses due to currency exchange fluctuations.  

You must still manually book journal entries for the unrealized gains or losses into the cumulative 

translation adjustment (CTA) account you specify. This report provides you with the information 

you need to book the entries.  

This report is available to multi-entity companies using foreign-currency transactions, and who 

have enabled multiple base currencies for their entities. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the General Ledger Revaluation report.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 502) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 502) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

### Trial Balance Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 47*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Trial Balance Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Trial Balance`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Trial Balance`


At the end of an accounting period, you create a trial balance to check for errors and create new 

financial statements. Use the Trial Balance report to view balances of all General Ledger accounts 

at a point in time.  

When running this report, you can: 

• 
Include or exclude statistical accounts. 

• 
Filter the list to specific locations and departments, and filter by accounts and account 

groups. 

• 
Display only accounts with a zero balance or only zero-balance accounts that have had 

activity.  

• 
Show accumulated balances for income statement accounts that close into retained 

earnings at year-end. 

• 
Include or exclude the Debits and Credits columns. 

• 
Export the report to an Excel XLS file. 

We recommend saving any complex financial reports that you plan to run regularly. The next time 

you run the report, you will need to change only the As of date field. 

The Trial Balance report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 

reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296). 

---


<!-- Page 48 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Comparing Balances 

Run the General Ledger (Detail) report for the same period as the Trial Balance and compare 

account balances to tie the balances to the Trial Balance report. The detail version of the General 

Ledger report lists a transaction-by-transaction breakdown for each account, enabling you to 

trace the movements that resulted in the final balance shown in the Trial Balance report.  

Use the Trial Balance to Reveal Errors 

The Trial Balance report lets you compare two sums: total debits and total credits. Total debits 

from all accounts must equal total credits. A mismatch between trial debit and credit sums means 

that one or more accounts include errors or omissions.  

When the trial balance fails to match debits to credits, you must search for the error. Several kinds 

of errors might cause the mismatch: 

• 
A debit entry in one account does not have an equal and offsetting credit entry in another 

account. 

• 
Some transactions either did not enter the system, or they appear in inappropriate accounts. 

• 
Account balance calculations include errors in data entry or mathematics. 

• 
When you have a trial balance difference divisible by two, look for an account balance 

exactly half the difference. That is most likely the misplaced balance. 

• 
When the difference between debit and credit totals is evenly divisible by nine, this is a 

mathematical indicator that the account balances may include a transposition error in 

---



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 49*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

one of the accounts. For example, a debit balance that should be 12,578 may appear 

as something like 12,587. 

• 
When the difference between debit and credit totals is divisible neither by nine or by 

two, a single debit or credit balance may be missing from the account lists. 

The Trial Balance Is Blind to Some Kinds of Errors 

Although the trial balance can help you detect errors, there are some errors that it cannot detect: 

• 
Debit and credit amounts may match but still be incorrect. 

• 
Errors of omission: The Trial Balance cannot account for transactions that are not entered 

into the system.  

• 
Errors of reversal: Someone entered an amount as a debit when it should have been entered 

as a credit, and the corresponding transaction was entered as a debit. When this happens, 

total debits still equal total credits. 

• 
Someone entered a transaction in the correct kind of account (e.g., “Asset account” or 

“Expense account”) but still chose an incorrect account within the category. The 

contributions total debits and total credits will be equal. 

• 
Two or more errors in different accounts may offset each other, thus canceling each other 

out. For example, the Trial Balance will still balance if a credit transaction in one account is 

$55 too high, and in another account a debit transaction is $55 too high.

Filling In the Filters Section

2.

multi-select box (on page 504) to select the Other books that you want to use for this 

report. 

The list of journals you can include in the report is restricted to journals for those 
reporting books. 

3. 
To combine the reporting book and other books, select the Combine reporting book with 

other books check box. 

Learn more about the reporting book options: 

• 
If you opted for dual-method reporting (Accrual and Cash) or if you are using Global 

Consolidations, you can change the main Reporting Book. For Accrual-only companies, 

the Accrual book is automatically selected. 

• 
If you enabled compliance, tax, or user-defined books, you can choose to include 

those Other Books (on page 139), with or without the main reporting book.

In the G/L Account Number Selection section, select the account, range of accounts, or 

account group to cover in the report. 

• 
To specify a range of accounts, select the Range option and then choose the starting 

account in the Account from drop-down list, and then select the ending account in 

the Account to drop-down list. 

• 
To select multiple non-contiguous accounts, select the Multiple accounts option and 

then click the Select accounts link. The Select multiple accounts box opens so that 

you can select the accounts that you want in the report. Click the Save button when 

your list of accounts is complete. 

• 
To include all accounts in the report, select the All accounts option. 

• 
To include all accounts in an account group, select the desired account group from the 

Account group drop-down list.

that this account group has the members that your business needs require. You can edit

Trial Balance, Comparative 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Analytics > Trial Balance, 
Comparative`


Use the Comparative Trial Balance report to compare account balances over time by comparing 

one reporting period against another. Filters let you show all accounts, accounts with a zero 

balance that have had activity, income accounts, and include, exclude, or use only statistical 

accounts. Once you have displayed the report, you can navigate through accounts to the general 

ledger, and then to individual transactions. 

The Comparative Trial Balance
 report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on 
financial reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

The report is displayed with a number of columns. All your accounts are listed on the left. The 

next column, Prior Balance, is the column that you compare to the four columns on the right 

(Unadjusted Balance, Adjusting Debits, Adjusting Credits and Adjusted Balance).

Define the time period for the report. You can either select the Reporting period and As of date, 

or select a date range to identify the report’s coverage period, but not both. If you do not specify

 Select the Prior reporting period.

you run the report.

Running a Report with Properties Separated in One File

separate tab.

traditional method for printing the Trial Balance report, and filter on one entity at a time. See 
Customizing and Running the Trial Balance Report (on page 40 ). 

Creating a Trial Balance Report 

To create a Trial Balance report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Trial balance report. 

3. 
In the Location section, click the Select button, and then choose the locations to report on. 

4. 
Select the Individual report check box. 

5. 
Click the Memorize button. 

6. 
Fill in the Name and Description fields. 

7. 
Click OK. 

Creating a Report Group and Adding Your Report to the Report Group 

To create the report group: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the More section, click the 
 Add button of Report Group. 

3. 
Name the report group. 

4. 
In the Members section, click the first blank row in the list, and then select the report that 

you created. 

5. 
Click Save. The system opens the Report Groups list.

for.

Select the Group by Location/Entity check box.

General Ledger Report

When running this report, you can:

• 
View the report in detail mode to see the transactions. 

•

By default, this report shows only accounts with balances greater than zero. However, you can 

choose to include zero-balance accounts.
