#### Displaying the Source Posting Date in the General Ledger Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 77*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Displaying the Source Posting Date in the General Ledger Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Entities > Edit > Advance Posting Date`


The Source posting date column identifies when an item was booked. When entities advance the 

posting date of their entries, it is useful to know when a journal entry was originally posted.  

To see the Source posting date column in the General Ledger report, your system must have the 

Advance posting date feature enabled.  

To enable the Advance Posting Date feature: 

1. 
Request the feature by contacting your RealPage Account Representative. RealPage enables 

this feature on the back end of your company’s system.  

2. 
Open each entity record for which you want to advance posting dates, and then select the 

Advance posting date check box.  

After enabling this feature, the Source post date field appears on journal entry records. You can 

also choose to display the date in a separate column in the General Ledger report.  

To update the entity record: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select Entities. The Entities list opens. 

3. 
For each entity that you want to see the source posting date in the General Ledger report: 

• 
Click the Edit link.  

• 
Find the Accounting section of the entity record. 

• 
Select the Advance posting date check box. 

• 
Type the End of month day. This is the date that the system uses to determine the 

next open period. 

• 
Save the entity record. 

---


<!-- Page 78 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The source posting date begins to appear in the General Ledger report for journal entries 
created after RealPage enables the feature in the back end. The source posting date data 
is not available for journal entries posted prior to enabling it. 

If you do not see the Advance posting date check box on entity records, then the feature is not 
enabled for your company. Contact your RealPage Account Representative to request the 

Advance Posting Date feature. 

Running the General Ledger Report 

1. 
Select the Show source post date option in the report settings. 

2. 
Click the View button to run the report.

##### General Ledger Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 81*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

General Ledger Report Columns 

Click any link to navigate to the details. The summary General Ledger report contains the 

following columns: 

Summary Report 

Posted dt (link) 
This is the date on which the transaction was posted to the G/L. Click the 

link to open the journal entries associated with this date. 

If you selected the Show journal transaction date check box, the name 

of this column changes to Posting period. The Posting period is the 

month and year that the transaction was posted. 

Source post date 
This is the original posting date of the entry. When your system is 

configured to advance the G/L posting date, you can refer to this field 

for the original posting date of the entry. This is a read-only field. The 

system stores the original posting date when you post the journal entry. 

This field appears only when Advance G/L posting is enabled for the 

associated entity. Contact your RealPage Support Representative to 

enable the Advance post date feature. 

Doc 
This is a document number associated with the transaction.  

When your system’s accounting method is Cash and you select the 

Show document number as invoice number option in the report’s 

settings, this column displays the invoice number instead. 

When your system’s accounting method is Accrual, the contents of this 

column is determined by the Select doc column value setting, reference 

number, or AP/AR invoice/adjustment number.  

• 
When you choose Reference number, then this column contains 

the reference number associated with the transaction. When no 

reference number is entered, the system displays the A/P invoice, 

A/R invoice, or adjustment number. 

• 
When you choose AP/AR invoice/Adjustment number, this 

column contains the A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment 

number, such as the number of the check used to pay the A/P 

invoice. If the transaction has no A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or 

adjustment number, then the column contains the reference 

number. 

---


<!-- Page 82 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Memo/Description 
If you included text in the description and line-item memo fields when 

you created a journal entry, then the description or memo text appears 

in this column. 

When you enter a description, that text is automatically included as the 

line-item memo entry, but can be overwritten. This is usually a 

description of the transaction, such as the type of invoice, date, and type 

of summary. 

Department 
This is the department number associated with the account; for example, 

900. 

Location 
This is the location associated with the account. 

Unit 
This is the unit at the location that is associated with the account. 

JNL 
This is the name of the application from which this transaction was 

derived; for example, A/P. 

Curr 
This is the currency in which the transaction was charged or paid. 

Txn amt 
This is the amount of the transaction. 

Debit (link) 
These are the charges posted to the account for the selected period. 

Click to view the journal entry associated with the charge. 

Credit (link) 
These are the payments posted to the account for the selected period. 

Click to view the journal entry associated with the payment. 

Balance 
This is the total amount of the account’s balance for the selected period. 

Total net change 
This is the total net change between the start date and end date of the 

report. 

When you select the Details option in the Show transaction presentation section, the system adds 

these columns to the report: 

Detailed Report  

Doc dt 
This is the date on the document associated with the transaction. This 

column appears only when you select the detailed version of the report. 

Payment no 
This is the payment number associated with an A/P journal transaction. 

When a payment was made in multiple payments, all payment numbers 

are included in the column and are separated by commas. This option is 

available when you select the Details option in the Show transaction 

presentation section.

##### Buttons
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 83*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods 

and to exclude specific types of data. 

The Customize button appears only after viewing a report or ledger. 

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports (on page 221) in 

the system, and then access them with the My stored reports option in 

the menu.  

Email 
Sends the report as an email message. Click to open the Email report box, 

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer. 

The file formats for exporting report data vary by report. 

Select 
Opens the multi-select box, where you can select items to filter by. 

In the multi-select box (on page 504), select the items that you want to 

include in the report.  

The option to multi-select items is not available for all reports.

apply only to the .pdf version of this report. (Click the Print button to get the .pdf version).

can leave the title as the default, or change it.  

1. 
Type over any default name that the system may have automatically supplied in this box. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page directly under your company name. 

2. 
In Report title 2, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. 

This subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report.

After you run the report, you can also either email the report to others or return to the report 

setup page to refine the results.

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods 

and to exclude specific types of data.

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports (on page 221) in 

the system, and then access them with the My stored reports option in 

the menu.  

Email

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer.

### Department Activity Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 90*

Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Department Activity Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Analytics > Department 
Activity`


Use the General Ledger Department Activity report to view a hierarchical list of department activity 

across the company. You can view data for one department or all departments, and for all 

accounts, or the data for only one account group. For example, suppose you want to know the 

liability position for the manufacturing department company wide. You would choose that 

department and account group.  

The Department Activity report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

The report is displayed by department (or by location within the department, if you have selected 

that option), date, and then account. You can print a report that contains all departments, or 

individual departments on separate report pages. You can include statistical accounts as well. 

Display options include the ability to suppress departments that have had no activity in the 

period, and detailed or summary modes.

Customizing and Running the Department Activity Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Analytics > Department 
Activity`


To customize the Department Activity report: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Financial analytics section, select Department activity. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report.  

1. 
Specify the Reporting period for which you want to run the report. 

2. 
Type the starting date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button, and then 

select the date from the calendar.  

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt when you run the report to 

ask for the reporting period. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up a filter as needed.  

1. 
To filter the report by Reporting book, select Accrual or Cash from the drop-down list. 

---


<!-- Page 92 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

2. 
To filter by adjustment or user-defined book, click the Select button, and then use the 

multi-select box to choose the books to filter by.  

3. 
Select the Combine reporting book with other books check box, as desired.  

4. 
Select the desired Account group. 

5. 
Select the Include statistical accounts in output check box as desired.  

Filling In the Dimension Filters Section 

1. 
In the Department drop-down list, select a department or department group to limit the 

scope of the activity report to one department or department group. 

2. 
Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per 

department. 

You must click the Process & Store button at the end if you select the Individual Report 
option. 

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt for a department before it 

runs the report.  

Filling In the Format Section 

1. 
To include the department or location with the activity in the report, select the Show 

department/location with activity check box. 

2. 
To arrange the report by location, select the Show by location check box. 

3. 
To arrange the report by department, select the Show by department check box. 

4. 
To create a summary report, select the Show summary only check box. To show details in 

the report, clear the check box. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Run the Report 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically in this box. 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the 

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer.

4.

What’s Next?

and to exclude specific types of data. 

The Customize button appears only after viewing a report or ledger. 

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports (on page 221) in 

the system, and then access them with the My stored reports option in 

the menu.  

Email 
Sends the report as an email message. Click to open the Email report box, 

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer. 

The file formats for exporting report data vary by report. 

Select 
Opens the multi-select box, where you can select items to filter by. 

In the multi-select box (on page 504), select the items that you want to 

include in the report.  

The option to multi-select items is not available for all reports.

Customizing and Running the Segment Activity Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Analytics > Segment Activity`


To customize the Segment Activity report: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Financial analytics section, select Segment activity. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report.  

1. 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s coverage period. Set a specific 

Start date and End date.  

You can either type the dates or click the 
 Calendar button, and then select the date 

from the calendar.  

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

2. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt for the date range before 

running the report. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up a filter as needed. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
To filter the report by Reporting book, select Accrual or Cash from the drop-down list. 

2. 
To filter the report by segments (on page 546), select one or more segments from the 

Segments drop-down list. You can also select all the values for a segment type by selecting 

the Select All check box. See Using the multi-select drop-down list (on page 505). 

---

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

3. 
To filter the report by location, select one or more locations or location group from the 

Locations drop-down list. You can also click the Select all check box to select all locations. 

4. 
To filter the report by account group, select the desired account group to include in the 

report from the Account group drop-down list. 

5. 
To show a summary report, select the Show summary only check box. To show details in 

the report, clear the check box. 

6. 
To arrange the report by segment, select the Show by segment check box. 

7. 
To arrange the report by location, select the Show by location check box. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Run the Report 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically in this box. 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the 

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to create the report.

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can also either email the report to others or return to the report 

setup page to refine the results. 

After running the report, you can: 

•

• 
Return to the main report page and refine the report further. Click the Customize button. 

You can use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want by filling in the desired 
fields and then clicking View to see the report. If after viewing the results you want to 
refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 
process until you’re satisfied. Also, for complex financial reports you plan to run regularly, 
save the report when you are done setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the 
report, change only the As of date before running the report.

### Deferred Revenue Forecast Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 115*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 115*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Deferred Revenue Forecast Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Forecast`


The Deferred Revenue Forecast report illustrates how deferred income is recognized as revenue 

over time. Use this report to forecast revenue by time period, account, customer, and more.  

The Deferred Revenue Forecast report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on 
financial reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

This report is typically used by Finance staff who need to do the following: 

• 
Budget and forecast revenue in-flows, based on prior projections. 

• 
Place revenue on hold or terminate it, or analyze revenue lost due to contract cancellations 

and terminations. 

• 
Determine how much revenue has yet to be recognized (on-hold forecasting). Running this 

report shows what the revenue would look like if the on-hold revenue were released. With 

that information, finance staff can look into the reasons why revenue is on hold. For 

instance, are there issues with collecting revenue or delivering products? Is the service team 

not turning things around as fast as it could? The report can make visible problems in excess 

deferred revenue. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option on the menu, ask your system administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the Deferred Revenue Forecast report. 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

General ledger 
Deferred Revenue Forecast 
Run 

For more information about permissions and roles, see Roles and Permissions (on page 502). If 

you don’t have permissions to access or change any of the options above, then ask your system 

administrator for assistance.

#### Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Forecast Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 116*

Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Forecast Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Forecast`


To customize the Deferred Revenue Forecast report: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Registers & Reports section, select Deferred Revenue Forecast. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can either define the report coverage by date range or by as of date and number of periods, 

but not both. 

1. 
Type the starting date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button, and then 

select the date from the calendar, and then type the number of periods to run the report. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

Use # of periods with the As of date and Forecast period fields as an alternate way to set 

the period of time you want the report to cover. For example, if you want a year of data and 

the Forecast period = Quarterly, enter 4 here; if the Forecast period = Monthly, enter 12 

here. 

The maximum number of periods allowed are: 

• 
60 for online reports 

• 
12 for PDF reports 

2. 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s coverage period. Set a specific 

Start date and End date.  

Leave the Start date blank to include all information from the earliest date you entered data 

into your company up to and including the End date. 

Leave the End date blank to include all information from the Start date up to today. The 

format must be: MM/DD/YYYY 

If you select a Start date and End date, don’t select an As of date. 

When entering a date, you can either type the dates or click the 
 Calendar button, and 

then select the date from the calendar.  

3. 
Select the Forecast period for which to run the report. 

Each column of the report will represent one period. Options are: 

• 
Monthly—displays as MMM-YY. For example, Jun-20. 

---


<!-- Page 117 -->
Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

• 
Quarterly—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Mar-20. 

• 
Semi-annually—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Jun-20. 

• 
Annually—displays as Year-YYYY. For example, Year-2020. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Use this section to set up filters that refine your report results. 

1. 
Choose the transactions to include by selecting the check boxes: 

• 
Include not started schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that have not yet started (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include in progress schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress. By default, the report will cover revenue details for 

schedules that are in progress (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include onhold schedules: Select this check box to show revenue details for schedules 

that are on hold. By default, the report will cover revenue details for schedules that are 

on hold (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include partially terminated schedule: Select this check box to show revenue details 

for schedules that are partially terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been partially terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include terminated transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been terminated. By default, the report will cover transactions 

that have been terminated (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include completed transactions: Select this check box to show the details of 

transactions that have been fully recognized. By default, the report will cover 

transactions that have been fully recognized (that is, the check box is checked). 

• 
Include open period schedules: Select this check box to show project revenue that has 

not been scheduled or posted. This filter is associated with Percent completed or 

Milestone recognition methods. 

2. 
In the Report on section, select the desired option to run the report on: 

• 
Revenue account: Select this option to limit the report to transactions for a specific 

revenue account. 

• 
Deferred revenue account: Select this option to report deferred revenue accounts 

rather than revenue accounts.  

3. 
In the Revenue account drop-down box, select the revenue account to limit the report to 

one revenue account. By default, this box is blank, which means the report will cover 

transaction details for every revenue account. 

4. 
In the Deferred revenue account drop-down list, select the desired deferred revenue 

account to limit the report to one deferred revenue account. Use this filter if you chose 

---


<!-- Page 118 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Deferred revenue account in step 2. By default, this box is blank, which means the report 

will cover transaction details for every deferred revenue account. 

5. 
In the Revenue recognition template drop-down list, select the desired template to limit 

the report to it. 

6. 
Use the Customer From and Customer To drop-down lists to select the beginning and 

ending customer in a range to include a range of customers in the report. 

In Customer From, select the first customer in a range of customers to include in the report. 

The system fills in the Customer To box with the same customer, setting it up in case you 

want to include only one customer in the report. 

In Customer To, select the last customer in a range of customers.  

Alternatively, leave the value in both fields set to the same customer if you want to report 

on only one customer. 

7. 
In the Show transactions section, select the desired option if you want to limit the report by 

whether the transactions have been posted: 

• 
Posted transactions 

• 
Unposted transactions 

• 
All 

8. 
In the Document number field, type a document number to limit the report to one 

document. 

9. 
In the Transaction Currency drop-down list, select the currency to which to limit the report. 

10. 
In the Show for drop-down list, select one of the following: 

All locations: Select to include report data for both the selected location and its child 

locations. 

This location: Select to include report data for the selected location only. 

Child locations: Select to include report data for additional locations associated with a 

location (such as secondary buildings). 

11. 
In the Department drop-down list, select a department to limit report results to one or 

more specific departments. 

• 
Select the Include subs check box to include child departments when filtering. Clear 

this check box if you don’t want the system to include children of the dimension when 

filtering. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you selected a department group. This option 

creates a separate report for the individual departments. The order of the departments 

in the groups determines the order in which the system creates individual reports.  

---


<!-- Page 119 -->
Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

You must select a Department group if you select the Individual Report option. 

12. 
In the Location drop-down list, select a location to limit report results to one or more 

specific locations. 

• 
Select the Include subs check box to include child locations when filtering. Clear this 

check box if you don’t want the system to include children of the dimension when 

filtering. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you selected a location group. This option 

creates a separate report for the individual locations. The order of the locations in the 

groups determines the order in which the system creates individual reports.  

You must select a Location group if you select the Individual Report option. 

Additional options to filter may appear, depending on the dimensions that your company’s 

system has enabled. 

Filling In the Format Section 

1. 
In the Report Type section, select the report type you want.  

Summary: Select this option for a report that condenses all account details into a single line. 

This is the default. 

Detail: Select this option for a report that displays one line per customer per account. It also 

includes additional columns of information. If you click Detail, by default the report also 

includes subtotals for each customer.  

2. 
In the Group by drop-down list, select how you want to arrange related data together. For 

example, to see all of the data for each customer, select either Customer Name or 

Customer ID. 

3. 
In the Sort by drop-down list, select how you want to sort the data in the report. The 

abbreviation “desc” after an option means “Descending order”—in this case, reverse 

alphabetical or reverse numerical order. The default sort order and number of options 

change depending on whether you want a summary report or a detail report. 

4. 
Select the desired page orientation. 

5. 
Click the Show dimension values’ Select button, and then select the dimension values that 

you want to include in the report. If a user has already selected dimension values, the Show 

dimension values box is displayed instead of a Select button. For help on using the 

multi-select box, see Using the multi-select box (on page 504).  

---


<!-- Page 120 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Filling In the Titles Section 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of this report (click Print to get the PDF version). 

The system completes the Report title 1 field with the system-assigned name of the report. This 

title appears in large type at the top of the page directly below your company name. You can 

leave the title as the default or change it.  

1. 
To change the title, type over the default name that the system automatically supplied. 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, type the text that you want to appear below the title of the report. 

This subtitle appears in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In the Footer text field, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. 

Footer text appears at the bottom of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report.

Filling In the Time Period Section 

1. 
Define the time period. You can either define the coverage by as of date and number of 

periods, or by date range, but not both. 

To define the time period by as of date: 

• 
Type the starting date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button, and 

then select the date from the calendar. 

To define the time period by date range: 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s coverage period. Set a 

specific Start date and End date.  

Leave the Start date blank to include all information from the earliest date you 

entered data into your company up to and including the End date. 

Leave the End date blank to include all information from the Start date up to today. 

The format must be: MM/DD/YYYY 

If you select a Start date and End date, don’t select an As of date. 

When entering a date, you can either type the dates or click the 
 Calendar button, 

and then select the date from the calendar.  

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

2. 
Select the Forecast period for which to run the report.  

Each column of the report will represent one period. Options are: 

• 
Monthly—displays as MMM-YY. For example, Jun-20. 

• 
Quarterly—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Mar-20. 

• 
Semi-annually—displays as MMM-YY - MMM-YY. For example, Jan-20 - Jun-20. 

• 
Annually—displays as Year-YYYY. For example, Year-2020. 

3. 
Set the length of time that you want the report to cover.  

In the # of Periods field, type the number of periods. For example, if you want a year of data 

and your Forecast Period is quarterly, type 4; if your Forecast Period is monthly, type 12. 

Limit online reports to no more than 60 periods. Limit PDF reports to no more than 12 
periods.

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports (on page 221) in

Add to dashboard

report, and then type a description of the report.

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer. 

The file formats for exporting report data vary by report. 

Select

### Deferred Revenue Details
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 133*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Deferred Revenue Details 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Details`


The Deferred Revenue Details report shows the details of customers and transactions for which 

you have deferred revenue. This report includes the transaction amount, transaction date, 

deferred amount, recognized amount, and amount paid. 

The Deferred Revenue Details report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on 
financial reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

Use this report to see the transaction detail behind those deferred numbers and to tie back to the 

deferred balance on your G/L (like an audit report). 

This report is typically used by the following users: 

• 
Auditors who need to determine what constitutes the balance on the G/L 

• 
Finance staff 

Understanding this report 

The Deferred Revenue Details report is not, by default, a cumulative report; instead, it is a report 

for a specific period. 

For example, if the current month is March and you want to see revenue recognized as of March 

31, running this report shows you any transactions processed in March along with a breakdown of 

the revenue for the transactions that were deferred, recognized, and paid. However, if you want to 

see the cumulative results as of March 31, you need to backdate your report to include older 

transactions. Because you may have revenue schedules posting in the month of March for 

transactions dated six months ago, you must select a date range that includes the oldest 

schedule.  

To ensure that you accurately display the cumulative amount deferred, recognized, and paid, 

make sure the date range you enter includes all transactions processed from inception (that is, 

from the time your company went live in the RealPage Accounting application) to date. 

This report includes only those transactions that are attached to a deferred revenue schedule 
line item. When you attach a line item to a deferred revenue recognition schedule, you begin the 
deferral process. Any line items not associated with a revenue recognition template do not go 
through a deferral process; this revenue is recognized immediately. These line items are not part 
of this report. 

You should not use this report to tie back to revenue for the period on the G/L because you may 
have a combination of revenue recognized immediately, and some deferred and then recognized in 
this period (that is, deferred from a prior quarter and recognized this quarter).

Deferred Revenue Details Columns 

Click any link to navigate into the details. The default Deferred Revenue Details report contains the 

following columns: 

Summary Report Columns 

Customer ID 
This is the unique identifier of the customer. 

Customer name 
This is the customer associated with the corresponding revenue amount. 

Base amount (CURR) This is the value of the transaction in your base currency, at the time the 

transaction took place.  

The base currency is included in parentheses. 

Amount deferred 

(CURR) 

This is the cumulative amount deferred.  

Make sure the date range you selected includes all transactions 

processed from inception to date. 

The base currency is included in parentheses. 

Amount recognized 

(CURR) 

This is the amount recognized for this period. 

The base currency is included in parentheses. 

Fx gain/loss 

recognized (CURR) 

This is the amount of gain and loss from foreign currency transactions. 

The base currency is included in parentheses. 

Amount paid (CURR) This is the amount paid in advance of being earned. 

The base currency is included in parentheses. 

The detailed version of the report displays these additional columns. 

Detailed Report Columns 

Document type 
This is the name of the sales transaction definition associated with the 

corresponding revenue amount. 

Document number 
This is the unique sales transaction identifier. 

Document line 

number 

This is the line item entry number associated with the corresponding 

item. 

Transaction date 
This is the sales transaction date. 

G/L posting date 
This is the date that the transaction posted to the General Ledger.

<!-- Page 140 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Account code ID 
This is the revenue account ID associated with the corresponding 

revenue amount. 

Account code name 
This is the revenue account associated with the corresponding revenue 

amount. 

Transaction currency  This is the currency associated with the transaction. 

Schedule status 
This is the revenue recognition schedule status associated with the 

corresponding document line number. Displays one of the following, 

depending on the schedule status filters selected when running the 

report: 

• 
Not started - all entries are still open; no revenue has been 

recognized. 

• 
In progress - at least one entry is posted. Some revenue is 

recognized but not all. 

• 
On hold - no further revenue is recognized until the transaction 

is resumed, and no modifications can be made to the schedule. 

• 
Partially terminated - a portion of the schedule has been 

terminated. The schedule includes one or more entries that are 

still Open. 

• 
Terminated - no future scheduled revenue will be recognized. 

• 
Completed - all scheduled revenue has been recognized. 

Revenue recognition 

category 

This is the revenue recognition category.  

The report includes transactions for every revenue recognition category 

unless you select a specific category. 

Revenue account ID 
This is the identifier of the revenue account. 

The report includes transaction details for every revenue account, unless 

you select a specific account. 

Revenue account title This is the name of the revenue account.  

Deferred revenue 

account number 

This is the identifier of the deferred revenue account associated with the 

deferred revenue. 

Deferred revenue 

account name 

This is the name of the deferred revenue account associated with the 

deferred revenue. 

Department ID 
This is the identifier of the department associated with the deferred 

revenue. 

Location ID 
This is the identifier of the location associated with the deferred revenue.

### Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 142*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 142*

Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Revaluation`


If your company uses multiple transaction currencies and revenue recognition, you can use the 

Deferred Revenue Revaluation report to revalue revenue recognition schedule entries. When the 

system created those entries, it used a specific exchange rate as of a certain date. You can change 

the exchange rate type and as of date, and calculate the currency gain/loss for every row of the 

revenue recognition schedule-entry table. 

You can filter the resulting data in several ways, such as by customer, customer type and 

transaction currency, and any enabled dimensions. You can generate a condensed summary 

report or a more detailed one that contains additional columns of information. You can group the 

information by customer/currency or location/currency. 

The Deferred Revenue Revaluation report is an informational source only. Revaluation reports 

don’t include information on inter-entity transactions. 

The Deferred Revenue Revaluation 
report is a standard report. Multicurrency must be enabled to 
access this report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, see Creating a Financial 
Report (on page 296 ). 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the Deferred Revenue Revaluation report.

Permissions

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 502) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 502) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

Customizing and Running the Deferred Revenue Revaluation Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Registers & Reports > Deferred 
Revenue Revaluation`


To customize the Deferred Revenue Revaluation report: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Registers & Reports section, select Deferred Revenue 

Revaluation. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
In the Revalue as of date field, type the date to use to calculate the exchange rate gains or 

losses as of a particular date. Type the Revaluation As Of Date in mm/dd/yyyy format, or 

click the 
 Calendar button, and then select the date from the calendar. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

2. 
To filter your data on a custom exchange rate type, select the custom type from the 

Revaluation Exchange Rate Types drop-down list. 

3. 
Select a customer in the From Customer drop-down list to limit the report to one customer.  

To limit the report to a set of customers, select the first customer to include in the From 

Customer drop-down list, and then, in the To Customer drop-down list, select the last 

customer to include. The report includes transactions for every customer in between. An 

unfiltered report includes every customer unless you limit the report to transactions with a 

specific customer or set of customers. 

4. 
Select a Customer type to limit the report to transactions for a specific customer type. The 

report includes transactions for every customer type unless you select a specific customer 

type. If your customers are grouped into subset types, such as Direct, Channel, and Partners, 

you can then filter the report for a specific subset, such as Direct. 

5. 
If you are a multi-currency company, you can filter transactions based on a specific currency. 

(This field does not display unless you work in a multi-currency environment.) To do this, 

use the Transaction currency drop-down list to select the currency you want the report to 

show. If you don’t select a currency, the report includes transactions in your base currency. 

6. 
In the Show for drop-down list, select an option to display transactions for certain locations 

regardless of the location you selected in the Location field.  

The Show for drop-down list appears only for multi-entity shared companies. 

• 
All Locations: Select this option to show transactions for all locations.

filtering.

### Reporting on Other Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 149*



#### Creating Financial Reports That Feature Other Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 149*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Reporting on Other Books 

You can create reporting books that are outside of your actual books, for the purpose of tracking 

and reporting on specialized accounting entries. For example, you can enter GAAP adjustments 

and then include your GAAP book as needed in reports. 

Financial reports let you choose reporting books on a column-by-column basis, enabling you to 

easily compare your data on different reporting bases. 

Other General Ledger reports give you the option to select reporting books for the entire report. 

These multi-book reporting options are available on financial reports and other General Ledger 

reports, if you’ve enabled GAAP or tax books or if you’ve set up user-defined books. 

Creating Financial Reports That Feature Other Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Reporting > Financial Reports`


In financial reports, you can specify the books to include on a column-by-column basis. You make 

your selections on the Columns tab of the financial report writer. 

For example, the following report includes columns for Accrual, a user-defined book named Real 

Estate, and GAAP. The final column combines the amounts from all selected books. 

a) Accrual book 

b) User-defined book: Real estate book 

c) GAAP book 

d) Combined: Accrual + Real Estate + GAAP books 

---


<!-- Page 150 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To select the reporting books to include in each column: 

1. 
Start by defining the financial report as usual. Go to the Financial Reports list (General 


> **Navigation Path:** `Ledger > All > Financial Reporting > Financial Reports).`


2. 
Add a new financial report or edit an existing one. 

3. 
On the Columns tab of the report definition, scroll down to the Reporting books section of 

the column. 

4. 
Verify the main reporting book that is listed. 

• 
By default, each column is set to report on the book selected on the Filters tab. 

• 
If you opted for dual-method reporting (accrual and cash), you can select a different 

main reporting book. 

5. 
Select any combination of Other books. 

• 
When you click the Edit books button, you can select one or more books to include. 

• 
At the same time, you can select whether you want to include amounts from the main 

reporting book. For example, if you include your Accrual book with your GAAP book, 

the report will show Accrual amounts with the GAAP adjustments applied. 

---



#### Creating Standard General Ledger Reports That Feature Other Books
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 151*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Including or Excluding the Main Reporting Book 

By default, amounts from the main reporting book are included to create a combined amount. 

However, there are times when you might want to clear this option. For example, suppose that 

your GAAP adjustments equal $-1,000 and the accrual amount is $10,000.00.  

What you want to see in the column determines whether to include or exclude the main reporting 

book.  

• 
To see just the GAAP adjustments, include only the GAAP book and exclude the Accrual 

book (the main reporting book).  

The resulting figure is $-1,000.  

• 
To see the GAAP and accrual amount combined, include both the GAAP and Accrual books.  

The resulting figure is $9,000. 

Creating Standard General Ledger Reports That Feature Other Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > [select a report]`


When you create a standard G/L report such as a General Ledger report, you can specify which 

books to include. Your selections are then applied to the entire report. 

To select the books to include on a standard General Ledger report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select the type of report you want to run. 

2. 
In the Filters section, verify the main Reporting book that is listed. 

If you opted for dual-method reporting (Accrual and Cash) or if your company uses multiple 
currencies and you use the Global Consolidations application to translate your currencies, 
you can select a different main reporting book. 

3. 
Select any combination of Other books. 

4. 
Decide whether to combine amounts from your main Reporting book with the Other 

books. 

By default, amounts from all books are combined together. For example, if you include your 

GAAP book with your accrual book, the report will show accrual amounts with the GAAP 

adjustments applied. 

---


<!-- Page 152 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

### Account Groups Hierarchy Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 162*

Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Account Groups Hierarchy Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Account Groups Hierarchy`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Account Groups Hierarchy`


Use the Account Group Hierarchy report to display a graphical representation of the hierarchy of 

your account groups, which includes member account groups and their accounts. The lists of 

account groups and accounts are sorted in ascending alphabetical order. If an account group has 

no members, only the accounts are displayed which helps you identify groups that have not been 

mapped to a group. 

The Account Group Hierarchy report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on 
financial reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

The main headings in this report are taken from the account name as entered in the G/L account 

group information page or the G/L account information page. This is different from other 

financial reports, which typically use the heading title, and then the name if no title is specified. 

The reason the name is used here is so that you can more easily compare the names in this report 

to the names in the Account groups list. 

The divisions in the report are differentiated by whether they are top-level groups that contain 

other member groups, and if they are groups that contain only accounts or categories. Any group 

that contains only accounts or categories is displayed after the top-level groups. The hierarchical 


> **Navigation Path:** `organization of account groups is controlled via General Ledger > All > Financial report`


structures > [member link] > Account group members. 

If your company was created with a Quick Start Financials setup template: 

• 
The report operates slightly differently for companies that use a Quick Start Financials setup 

template in that the setup template creates a set of system account groups in addition to 

your own account groups. 

• 
If your company was initially created with a setup template, a set of standard account 

groups was copied to your company. Consequently, a filter lets you choose to view the 

system account groups or the user-defined ones that your company created. You can 

navigate into user-defined account groups by clicking a link on the report, but you can’t 

navigate on system-generated account groups. 

---

Budget Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Budget`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Budget`


Use the Budget report to analyze your budget information. If you have a financial report with 

budget columns, you can also navigate into the Budget report, and from the Budget report to the 

Budget details page. There you can edit and update budget information, save, and see the 

changes reflected instantly in your financial report.  

The Budget report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, see 
Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

In this report you can: 

• 
Show total budget amounts across all periods.  

• 
Filter on location, department, and other dimensions.  

• 
Display columns for dimension values and select their display order.

#### Customizing and Running the Budget Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 170*

Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Customizing and Running the Budget Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Budget`


To customize the Budget report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Financial statements section, select Budget.  

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report using either a budget period or date range. 

To run a report for a budget period: 

• 
In the Budget period drop-down list, select the Budget period. 

To run a report for a date range: 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s period of coverage.  

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
Select the Budget type for the report. 

2. 
In the G/L account number selection section, select how you want to filter account numbers: 

• 
Range: Select this option to select a contiguous set of account numbers. Select the 

beginning and ending account numbers in the Account from and Account to 

drop-down lists. 

• 
Multiple accounts: Select this option if you want to select multiple, non-contiguous 

account numbers, and then click the Select accounts link to open the Select multiple 

accounts box. For more information, see Using the Select Multiple Accounts Box. 

• 
All accounts: Select this option to include all account numbers in the report. 

3. 
In the Account group drop-down list, select an account group to filter by. You can also click 

the Find link to search for the desired account group. 

4. 
Select the Include statistical accounts in output check box if you want to include statistical 

account data in the Budget report. Clear the check box to exclude statistical account data. 

5. 
In the Segments drop-down list, select one or more segments to include in the report. For 

more information, see Using the multi-select box (on page 505). 

6. 
In the Dimension filters section, select the dimensions that you want to use in the report. 

---


<!-- Page 171 -->
Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

7. 
To filter by dimension report structure, select the desired dimension report structure in the 

Dimension report structure drop-down list. 

The next few drop-down lists are dimensions such as Department, Location, Customer, and 

Vendor. 

8. 
Select the desired dimension or dimension group to include dimensions in the report. To 

limit the report to a selected property (location) or location group, click the Select button 

under the Property label, and then select a property or group from the Selection box. After 

choosing a couple of properties, the Select button is replaced with the list of the properties 

that you chose: 

9. 
Select the Include subs check box if you want to include data from children of the selected 

location. 

10. 
Some dimensions have a type, such as a Customer type or Vendor type. Select the type 

when you want to run the report and include only one specific type of customer or vendor.  

Customer types and vendor types vary by company. Your company has customized types. 
You can add and remove Customer types in the Accounts Receivable application’s Setup 
tab. You can add and remove Vendor types in the Accounts Payable application’s Setup 
tab.  

Filling In the Format Section 

1. 
Click the Show dimension values’ Select button, and then select the dimension values that 

you want to include in the report.  

If a user has already selected dimension values, the Show dimension values box appears 

instead of a Select button. For more information, see Using the multi-select box (on page 

504). 

2. 
In the Place total column drop-down list, choose where you want to display the Total 

column in relation to the budget period columns. Select to display it on the Right or Left of 

the budget period columns, or choose Hide. 

3. 
Select the Include notes column(s) for period(s) check box to include notes you’ve created 

for budget periods. Create notes in the Budget Account Information page. See Adding 

budget details for an account (on page 512). 

Selecting this check box also includes comments that you made to the budget model in 
OneSite. To include the comments in this Budget report, you must have exported the 

---


<!-- Page 172 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

budget model from OneSite and selected the Include Comments check box on the Manage 

Models page. 

4. 
Select the Use CSV importable format check box to enable the report to be imported as a 

CSV file. If you select this check box, all available dimension values will be exported, and 

totals will not be included. Use the filters to customize your CSV file. When exporting, select 

CSV from the Export drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the View button to run the report.

Chart of Accounts Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Chart of Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Chart of Accounts`


Use the Chart of Accounts report to view a filtered list of accounts. This report contains the same 

information as the Accounts list in General Ledger; however, you can’t edit the information in this 

report. 

The Chart of Accounts report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

To examine the way your accounts are mapped into groups, run the Account Groups Hierarchy 

report. The Account Groups Hierarchy report shows you the hierarchical structure—that is, which 

accounts are members of which groups, and which groups are members of other 

groups—whereas the Chart of Accounts report is a flat listing of all accounts.

standard chart of accounts.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Chart of 
Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > All > Reports > Chart of Accounts`


To customize the Chart of Accounts report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports section, select the Chart of accounts option. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

You can leave the filter fields blank, which is the same as specifying “All,” or you can enter values 

that limit the list, so it is more focused. You can continue to modify the filter criteria and other 

settings until you are satisfied with the results. However, you must click View or another option 

each time you change the settings. 

To set filters to refine your report results: 

1. 
Select the account type you want to include in the report: 

• 
G/L Accounts 

• 
Balance Sheet Accounts 

• 
Income Statement Accounts 

• 
Statistical Accounts 

2. 
Select the range of accounts you want in the report. Select accounts for the Account from 

and Account to from the drop-down lists. 

3. 
To include accounts for which you have required departments, select the Required 

departments check box. 

4. 
To include accounts for which you have required locations, select the Required locations 

check box. 

5. 
Select the Period end closing type from the drop-down list. 

6. 
Select the type of Normal balance for your report.  

---


<!-- Page 178 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The normal balance indicates the type of balance that this account is expected to have, 

based on how it was classified when it was set up, which is shown in the chart of accounts 

and in the accounts list. 

7. 
Select the status of the accounts to include in the report. To include both active and inactive 

accounts, select All. 

The following table describes each item in the Filters section of this report settings page: 

Account type 
Select the type of accounts to include. G/L accounts, 

Balance sheet accounts, Income Statement accounts, 

or Statistical accounts. 

Account from 

Account to 

Select the beginning and ending account numbers to 

include in the report. 

Require department 
Select this check box to include only accounts that 

require departments. 

Require location 
Select this check box to include only accounts that 

require locations. 

Period end closing type 
Select All, Closing, Non-closing, Close to accounts. 

Closing entries, or closing journal entries, are entries 

that are made at the end of an accounting period to 

zero out the accounts so that you start over in the 

next period. Some types of accounts don’t need to 

close. For example, statistical accounts are often 

non-closing. Close to accounts are those accounts 

that one account closes into. For example, a 

temporary account for petty cash might close to a 

permanent account for general expenses. 

Normal balance 
Include all normal balance accounts, or only those 

with Credit or Debit normal balances. 

The normal balance indicates the type of balance that 

this account is expected to have, based on how it was 

classified when it was set up, which is shown in the 

chart of accounts and in the accounts list. 

Status 
Include all accounts or limit the report to only active 

or inactive account.

Customizing and Running the Journals Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Financial Statements > Journals`


Before running the Journals report, you can select the time period and types of items to include as 

well as specify how you want the report to appear. 

To customize the Journals report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Reports column, in the Financial statements section, select Journals. The Journal 

report parameters page is displayed. 

Filling In the Reporting Accounts Labels Section 

You may optionally replace account labels with reporting account set’s labels.  

If you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, you can substitute the account 

labels in the Journals report with the reporting account labels. For more information, see 

Reporting account sets (on page 519). 

1. 
If you want to enable reporting accounts labels, select the Substitute with reporting 

accounts labels check box. 

2. 
If you selected the check box in step one, select the Reporting account set to use in this 

report from the drop-down list.  

3. 
If you would prefer to choose the reporting account set each time that you run the report, 

select the Prompt on run check box. When selected, the system asks you for the reporting 

account set every time that you run the report. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report. You can either select the Reporting period and As of date, 

or select a date range to identify the report’s coverage period, but not both. 

To run a report for a Reporting period: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the desired reporting period. 

2. 
In the As of date field, select the date to begin the report coverage.  

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want to be able to choose the reporting period 

and As of date when you run the report.

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

To run a report for a date range: 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s period of coverage.  

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
If your company has multiple reporting books, select the main Reporting book from the 

drop-down list. 

2. 
Select Other books that you want to use for this report. Click the Select button and then 

choose the books to use in your report. Refer to Using the multi-select box (on page 504) 

for instructions. 

The list of journals you can include in the report will be restricted to journals for those 

reporting books. 

If you opted for dual-method reporting (Accrual and Cash) or if you are using Global 

Consolidations, you can change the main Reporting Book. For Accrual-only companies, the 

Accrual book is automatically selected. 

If you enabled compliance, tax, or user-defined books, you can choose to include those 

Other Books, with or without the main reporting book. Learn more about reporting on other 

books (on page 139). 

3. 
You can combine the reporting book and other book by selecting the Combine reporting 

book with other books check box. 

4. 
In the Journal section, select an option: 

Journal: Select this option to run the report on one journal, and then select the journal from 

the drop-down list. 

Multiple journals: Select this option to run the report on multiple journals, and then click 

the Select accounts link. The Select multiple journals box opens. In the Add journal 

drop-down list, select a journal to include in the report, and then click the Add button. 

Continue to select additional journals. You can also select a range of journals in the From 

journal and To journal drop-down lists. Click Save when you have selected all journals you 

want. 

All journals: Select this option to run the report on all journals.  

5. 
Select the Include statistical journals in output check box to include statistical journals.

 Select the Individual report check box if you want each department to have its own

A/R - Multifamily Report Columns 

Delinquent and Prepaid Tie-out 

This section analyzes the delinquent and prepaid amounts in RealPage Accounting and Leasing & 

Rents, and shows when the totals agree (tie out). When they do not, the report shows the amount 

of variance with a column for you to enter the reason for the variance after the report runs. 

Summary by Charge Code 

This section summarizes prepaid and delinquent activity by transaction code. It prints only if you 

chose to include it on the report options page. Each column is totaled, with the exception of the 

first two columns. The totals consist of transaction code level balances and may not equal the 

beginning/ending prepaid or delinquent balances in the Resident Summary Balances report, which 

totals transactions by subjournal. 

Summary by General Ledger Account 

This section summarizes prepaid and delinquent activity by G/L account. It prints only if you chose 

to include it on the report options page. 

The default Accounts Receivable - Multifamily report contains the following columns: 

(Summary Section) 

Report name 
This is the name of the multifamily report, Accounts Receivable - 

Multifamily report. 

G/L account group 
This is the account group used for this report. 

Property 
This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

Period 
This is the period that the report covers. 

Delinquent and Prepaid Tie-out: [Property] 

Acct # 
This is the identifier of an account that has a delinquent or prepaid 

transaction. 

Account description 
This is the name of the account that has a delinquent or prepaid 

transaction. 

Amount per TB 
This is the amount that is delinquent or prepaid per Trial Balance. 

Subledger report 
This is the total amount for the account, as recorded in Leasing & Rents. 

Variance 
This is the variance between Amount per TB and Subledger Report 

columns. 

Variance explanation This is the explanation for the variance. 

---

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

0-30 days 
This is the amount you owe to your vendor that is up to 30 days past 

due. 

31-60 days 
This is the prepaid and delinquent amount that is at least 30 days old. 

61-90 days 
This is the prepaid and delinquent amount that is at least 60 days old. 

> 90 days 
This is the prepaid and delinquent amount that is 90 days old or over. 

Delinquent and Prepaid Details: [Property] 

Unit 
This is the identifier of the unit described in the row. 

Name 
This is the tenant name and contact information. 

• 
If you have started eviction proceedings on the tenant, an 

asterisk (*) appears beside the name. 

• 
If this is a business or corporation, an asterisk (*) or caret (^) 

appears beside the name, depending on the placeholder that 

was entered as the first name of the business. 

• 
If the business is also under eviction, the system flags the 

account with an asterisk; therefore, you may see “**” or “^*” 

beside the name of a business that is under eviction. 

Status 
This is the occupancy status, such as current tenant or applicant. 

Move-in/Out 
This is the date the tenant moved in or is scheduled to move in. If this is 

a former tenant, this is the move-out date. 

Charge code 
This is the charge code description. 

If a payment is allocated to a future charge and you chose to show 

prepaids as allocated, the code has “Future:” as a prefix. 

If there are multiple transactions, a Subtotals row appears below the 

last transaction. Separate totals are calculated for prepaid, delinquent, 

net balance, and aged amounts. 

Account 
This is the account number associated with the unit. 

Total prepaid 
This is the total amount of all open payments or credits associated with 

this charge code as of the current property date. 

---


<!-- Page 201 -->
Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Total delinquent 
This is the total of all open (or unpaid) transactions associated with this 

code as of the current property date. If a dagger symbol (†) appears 

beside an amount, the charge is delinquent due to NSF activity on the 

ledger. If a double dagger symbol (‡) appears, the charge is 120+ days 

past due. 

Net balance 
This is the net ledger balance as of the current property date. A negative 

amount is a prepaid balance; a positive amount is a delinquent balance. 

If the household has multiple transactions, the net balance prints in the 

Subtotals row and the total is: 

Total Prepaid (Subtotals) + Total Delinquent (Subtotals) 

If the subtotal has both a prepaid and delinquent balance resulting in a 
net balance of zero, the manual cash application feature is enabled in 
A/R settings, so credits (the prepaid balance) are not automatically 
applied to charges (the delinquent balance). 

0-30  
This is the prepaid or delinquent amount for this code during the 

current period. The current period is the current “Calendar” month or 

current “Fiscal” period, based on the Aging columns parameter. If aged 

by: 

• 
Calendar month, open transactions posted during the current 

calendar month are included in the total. 

• 
Fiscal period, open transactions posted in the current fiscal 

period are included in the total. 

The age is based on the original transaction date, not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

31-60  
This amount is at least 30 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted during the 

previous month is included in this total. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the previous fiscal 

period is included in this total. 

---


<!-- Page 202 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

61-90  
This amount is at least 60 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted in the calendar 

month that is two months prior to the current property date 

month is included. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the fiscal period that 

is two periods prior to the current fiscal period is included. 

The age is based on the original transaction date and not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

Over 90  
This amount is at least 90 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted in the calendar 

month that is at least three months prior to the current property 

date month is included. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the fiscal period that 

is at least three periods prior to the current fiscal period is 

included. 

The age is based on the original transaction date and not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

Total due 
This is the total amount due. 

Prorate credits 
If the tenant is moving out or transferring in the middle of the month, 

this is the prorated credit for this code. (A separate line item appears for 

the proration that covers the exact number of days the unit is occupied 

during the billing period.) 

Deposits held 
This is the total paid deposits. 

Outstanding deposit 
This is the total unpaid deposits (required deposits less deposits held). 

#Late/#NSF 
This is the number of times the tenant paid late, and the number of 

times checks were returned due to non-sufficient funds. For example, 

3/0 means the tenant paid late three times and has no NSF checks. 

Grand Totals 
This row calculates property totals. Each column from Total Prepaid 

through Deposits Held is totaled.

Standard Reports
