Summary by General Ledger Account: [Property] 

G/L account 
This is the G/L account and description. 

Charge code 
This lists each code associated with the G/L account. For cash basis 

charge codes with delinquent activity, the income account will match the 

A/R account, and the delinquency will not be reported to the general 

ledger (or accounting system) until the transaction is paid and no longer 

delinquent. Note that this scenario will be indicated with a hurricane (§) 

footnote. 

Beginning 
This shows beginning balances for the property (grand total), G/L 

account, and transaction code. The total beginning balance of all 

transaction codes listed under the G/L account will equal the G/L 

account beginning balance. Similarly, the total beginning balance of all 

G/L accounts will equal the grand total beginning balance for the 

property. 

Ending 
This shows ending balances for the property (grand total), G/L account, 

and code. The total ending balance of all codes listed under the G/L 

account will equal the G/L account ending balance. Similarly, the total 

ending balance of all G/L accounts will equal the grand total ending 

balance for the property. 

Change 
This shows the net change (beginning balance less ending balance) for 

the property, G/L account, and code. The total net change of all codes 

listed under the G/L account will equal the G/L account total net change. 

Similarly, the total net change of all G/L accounts will equal the grand 

total net change for the property. 

Grand Totals 
This row calculates the total amount by G/L account. 

When transactions payable in arrears are excluded, the report totals may not balance to other 
reports, such as the Monthly Transaction Summary report.

##### Buttons
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 205*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods 

and to exclude specific types of data. 

The Customize button appears only after viewing a report or ledger. 

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports (on page 221) in 

the system, and then access them with the My stored reports option in 

the menu.  

Email 
Sends the report as an email message. Click to open the Email report box, 

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer. 

The file formats for exporting report data vary by report. 

Select 
Opens the multi-select box, where you can select items to filter by. 

In the multi-select box (on page 504), select the items that you want to 

include in the report.  

The option to multi-select items is not available for all reports.

Customizing and Running the Security Deposits - Multifamily Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Financial Statements > Security Deposits - 
Multifamily`


To customize and run the Security Deposits - Multifamily report: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Security Deposits - Multifamily in the Financial Statements section in the Reports 

column.  

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Use this section to define the time period that you want the report to cover.  

• 
Type the date or click the 
 Calendar button to select the beginning date and ending date 

in the Opening balance date and Closing balance date fields. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

Filling In the Filters Section 

Use filters to get the specific data you want. Filters enable you to include or exclude specific types 

of data in the report, such as account group and location. These filters are required. 

1. 
In the Account group drop-down list, select the account group that you want to include in 

the report. To search for the group in a list, click the Find link at the top of the Account 

group drop-down list. 

---

Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

When you are running a report group that includes both AR-Multifamily and Security 
deposits reports, you can define separate account groups for security deposits and 
delinquencies and prepaids, which appear in the AR-Multifamily report. 

2. 
 In the Location drop-down list, select the location that you want the report to cover. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Running the Report 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of this report. (Click Print to get the PDF version). 

The system completes the Report Title 1 field with the system-assigned report name. This title 

displays in large type at the top of the page directly under your company name. 

1. 
You can leave the title as the default, or change it by typing over the default name in Report 

Title 1. 

2. 
In Report title 2, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. This 

subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. Footer text 

displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report.  

View, process, memorize, export, or customize the report or add it to the dashboard by 
clicking one of the buttons at the top of the page. You can use trial and error to get the 
precise results you want. Fill in the desired fields and then click View to see the report. To 
refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 
process until you’re satisfied. Also, for complex financial reports you plan to run regularly, 
save the report when you are done setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the 
report, change only the As of date before running the report.

Customize

View

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access.

### Rent Roll Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 221*

Chapter 2: Standard Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Rent Roll Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Rent Roll`


The Rent Roll report is a snapshot of your property’s current state of occupancy. It lists all units by 

occupancy and rental status and provides detailed unit information. You can see at a glance all of 

the units in the property that are occupied and unoccupied. 

RealPage Accounting extracts the data for the Rent Roll report from Leasing & Rents. 

You can filter the report by property, and export the report to Word, Excel, PDF, and text formats. 

The Rent Roll report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, 
see Creating a Financial Report (on page 296 ). 

---

Filling In the Titles Section 

 The system completes the Report title 1 field with the name of the report, but you can change it. 

1.

2.

3. 
In the Footer text field, type the text that you want to appear in the report footer. 

4.

Rent Roll Report Columns 

Click any link to navigate to the details. The Rent Roll report contains the following columns: 

Columns 

Resh ID 
This is the system-assigned resident ID. 

Lease ID 
This is the unique identifier of the tenant’s lease. Click the text in the 

Lease ID column to open the lease record’s Billing tab. 

Bldg/Unit 
This is the building and unit number. 

Floorplan 
This is the name of the floor plan associated with this unit. 

Unit Designation 
This is the unit’s designation code. This information is used for reporting 

purposes to identify occupied units as commercial, employee, corporate, 

conventional, affordable, or any other type of identifier that your 

company defines during the setup process. 

SQFT 
This is the total rentable SqFt of all units at the property. 

Unit/Lease Status 
This is the unit’s occupancy or lease status: Vacant, Vacant - Leased, 

Occupied, or Occupied – NTV (on notice). 

Name 
This is the head of household name for leased units, or it is blank for 

vacant units. 

Move-In 
This is the move-in date. 

Move-Out 
This is the move-out date. 

Lease Start 
This is the lease start date for the current active lease. 

Lease End 
This is the lease end date for the current active lease.

<!-- Page 224 -->
Standard Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Market + Additional 
This is market rent plus the total of non-CA type transactions scheduled 

for the floor plan or unit, and the transactions are not grouped in the 

effective rent transaction code group. 

Sub Journal 
This is the subjournal name (if applicable); otherwise, the system posts 

all billings to the default resident journal, and the report excludes this 

column. 

Required Deposit 
This is the deposit amount assigned to the floor plan or unit in setup or 

overridden on the lease application. 

Dep On Hand 
This is the total paid deposits. 

Balance 
This is the resident’s current ledger balance. 

Lease Rent 
This is the rent amount in scheduled billing. For vacant units, this is 0.00. 

Amounts associated with pending renewals, applicants, and former 

residents appear with an asterisk (*), and the report excludes them from 

totals. 

After the Lease rent column, the columns are scheduled billing codes. Each column represents a 

charge or credit code from Leasing & Rents scheduled billing. 

Scheduled Billing Codes Section 

RENT 
This billing code represents rent. 

This is a scheduled billing code. 

HAP 
This is the amount of the housing assistance payment (HAP) that a 

property with HUD contracts receives from the government. 

This is a scheduled billing code. 

RENTCONC 
This billing code typically represents rent concessions (discounts). The 

amount in the column should be a negative amount. 

This is a scheduled billing code. 

Total Billing 
This is the total scheduled billing amount for the occupied unit. 

Calculated as: 

Lease Rent + Other Charges/Credits

Setting Up Standard Report Parameters 

The first step in creating a report or chart is to define the coverage of the report. Each report has 

a different set of parameters, although most reports have these parameter types: 

• 
Period: This section lets you choose a reporting period or define a date or a date range for 

which you want data.  

• 
Filters: This section lets you define the data to include in the report. 

• 
Format: This section allows you to define how to sort and group the data. Some reports 

allow you to set the report’s page orientation. 

• 
Titles: This section allows you to define the text that appears at the top and bottom of the 

report pages. 

Refer to each report for specific instructions on configuring a report’s parameters. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Running a Report (on page 219) 

Running a Report 

After setting up a standard report’s parameters (time period, filters, format, and titles), click the 

View button to run the report.  

Examine the results. If you don’t like the results, then click the Customize button to return to the 

report’s setup page and make desired changes. 

If you do like the results, there are several things that you can do next. 

• 
To save the report’s results, click the Process & Store button to save the results.  

• 
To save the report’s settings so that you can use them again, memorize the report.

Memorized Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Memorized reports`


Use the Memorized reports page to display reports that you have saved and reports that others 

have saved and made public. From this page, you can also edit memorized reports, process large 

reports in the background using the Process & Store feature, and schedule reports to be run at a 

future date. 

To add reports to this list, display the report filter for the report to add, and then click the 

Memorize button on the report filter page. 

You can also view your memorized reports in the Reports application. 

Learn more about memorizing reports (on page 220). 

Storing Reports 

You can generate reports on demand and store them in My stored reports for later access. Use 

the Storage options page to choose the report format and where to store the report after it is 

processed. 

If you plan to process and store the same report on a recurring basis, consider scheduling it. 

Generating and Storing a Report 

To generate and store a report: 

1. 
Locate your report type and select the option to process or run it. 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Financial report: In the Financial reports list (General Ledger > All > Financial`


Reporting, then click Financial reports), locate the report, and then click the Process & 

store link. 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Report groups: In the Report groups list (Reports > More > Reports Groups), locate`


the report group, and then click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Start by displaying the report. For example, you might display a 


> **Navigation Path:** `Customer Aging report by going to Accounts Receivable > All > Reports > Customer`


Aging Report. Select report options as needed and then click the Process & store 

button. 

2. 
On the Storage options page, select the date to run the report on, where the report should 

be stored, the report name, and the format of the report. 

If you’re running a report group, you can run the report for multiple locations or entities at 

once. To ensure that the reports are collated by entity (so that each entity’s reports appear 

together), select the Grouped by Location/Entity check box. 

3. 
Follow the instructions below for selecting the report format and storage location. 

---

#### Storing a Report in My Stored Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 234*

Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Storing a Report in My Stored Reports 

You can generate reports on demand and store them in the My stored reports list for later 

access. 

To store a report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime (on page 409 ). 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand. 

3. 
In the Delivery options section, select the Store report option. 

4. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 

If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, 
then the Location ID and Name is added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for. 

5. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves a report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Saves reports in an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Saves the report as a text file. 

Only the Printable and Excel options are available for report groups. When storing report 
groups as an Excel file, each report appears on a separate tab. 

6. 
Click OK. 

---

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime (on page 409 ). 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand. 

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  

By default, you can choose from cloud-storage targets that either you ’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all cloud 
targets. 

5. 
If you want to override the default path where the report is delivered in the cloud-storage 

target, then type a different path in the Path field. 

6. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 

If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, 
then the Location ID and Name is added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for. 

7. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves a report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

---

report, you can click the 
 Print button to print the report. 

c) 
Downloads a CSV file of the report data. This is a good format to download if you 

want to import the data into another application. 

d) 
Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

e) 
Displays a text version of the report in the web browser.

report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 225).

Displays “Success” when the system has successfully stored the report in the Reporting 

Portal application.

the report. Click the link to review the error details.

offline.

### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 243*

Chapter 3: Working with Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead. 

---



### Scheduling and Delivering Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 244*



#### About Report Schedules
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 244*

Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Scheduling and Delivering Reports 

You can schedule reports to be run automatically, for instance on a weekly or monthly basis. 

When a scheduled report is generated, it can be delivered using your choice of delivery methods, 

including the option to email the report, store the report in RealPage Accounting, or send the 

report to a cloud-storage target such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, Amazon S3, or an HTTP 

address. 

Schedule Report Page 

You can use the Schedule report page to schedule a report to be run automatically, for instance 

on a weekly or monthly basis. The option to schedule a report applies to reports that you have 

previously memorized, report groups that you have created, and all financial reports. 

About Report Schedules 

When you schedule a financial, report group, or memorized report, you set some filters and a 

start date, ending date, and recurrence. There can be additional filter options that are only visible 

based on the type of report you’re scheduling, but the following selections are always used. 

You can change the settings at any time. 

When you schedule a report, it’s run based on the schedule you create, using the report filters 

and settings you provide such as the As of date, location, and any other settings. 

You can select the day of the week or the day of the month on which to run a scheduled report 

using the Start date. Daily scheduled jobs are run after midnight based on the time zone for your 

company location. Time zones are defined in your company setting. You can’t choose a specific 

time of day at which to run the scheduled report. 

Filters - the “As of date” 

When you select the schedule to run a report, setting the “As of date” tells the system to run the 

report as if it were the date that you set here. 

When you leave the “As of date” blank, the system uses the date on which the report was run as 

the current date. 

Schedule - Start, end, and recurrence 

These settings enable you to start the schedule, and tell the system how long it should be active. 

The first report will be generated on the date you select as the start date and continue at the 

selected recurrence until the “ending on” date is reached. 

• 
Start date: This date has two purposes.  

• 
First, it tells the scheduler the date on which to start running scheduled reports. 

---



#### Viewing a List of Scheduled Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 245*

Chapter 3: Working with Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

• 
Secondly, it tells the scheduler to run the report each time the start date detail recurs, 

based on the recurrence selection.  

For example, if you set the start date to the 10th of a month and the recurrence to 

Monthly, the report will run on the tenth of each month. If you select a start date on a 

Tuesday and a recurrence of every three weeks, the report will run every third week on 

the Tuesday of that week. 

• 
End date: Set the date that the scheduler stops running the report. The report runs the last 

scheduled time before the end date is reached. 

• 
Recurrence: The recurrence option tells the system how often to run the report after the 

schedule starts running: daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly. Based on the recurrence you 

choose, you’ll see further selections. For example, if you select Weeks, you can choose how 

many weeks should pass between scheduled runs, for example, every two weeks, every ten 

weeks, and so on. Selecting Month lets you choose how many months should pass between 

running the report and whether or not the schedule should run at the end of the month. 

Viewing a List of Scheduled Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Financial 
Reports > Schedule`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Reports Center > More Actions > Schedule`


To view a list of all the reports you have scheduled: 

1. 
Open the Reports Center. 

2. 
Locate the report and click the arrow for More actions. 

3. 
Select Schedule.

#### Scheduling a Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 246*

Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Scheduling a Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Financial 
Reports > Schedule`


For each report that you schedule, you can set a different schedule and choose how the report 

should be delivered. For example, you might want to email the report to yourself and selected 

people and send the report to a Dropbox folder where it can be stored and accessed by others. 

For more details about scheduling, see About Report Schedules (on page 234). 

To schedule a report: 

1. 
Locate the desired report (on page 218). You can schedule reports from the Reports center, 

the Memorized reports list, or the Financial reports list. 

To schedule a report group, see Scheduling a Report Group. 

2. 
Click the Schedule link next to the report. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups (on page 409), then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or 

more G/L account groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule Financial 

Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to schedule reports 

and reports groups to run at that time.

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save.

#### Reviewing the Schedule Status of Memorized Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 254*



#### Stopping a Scheduled Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 254*

Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reviewing the Schedule Status of Memorized Reports 

For memorized reports, you can check the status of the scheduled report (Not Scheduled, 

Scheduled, or Success) and get alerts for any reports that failed to run. 

1. 
Go to the menu for the application to which the report belongs. For example, if you 

memorized a Bills Analysis report, you would go to the All menu for Accounts Payable. 

2. 
In the Reports section, choose Memorized Reports. 

3. 
Review the information in the Status column of the Memorized Reports list. 

Learn more about schedule status information: 

The Status column advises you of the status of the scheduled execution. The possibilities are Not 

Scheduled, Scheduled, Success (and In Transit for very long reports that are being processed). If 

your report has run, the status should be Success. 

In the event of a failure, the system notifies you by displaying a Status link in this column. Click 

the Status link to display the Execution Log list, which shows all of the errors that have occurred 

and lets you display their details. 

Stopping a Scheduled Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Scheduled > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


You can change when and how often a scheduled report is delivered. If you want to keep the 

scheduled report but stop its delivery, you can set the recurrence of the report to None. 

To stop a scheduled report from running again: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu.  

2. 
Select Reports center. 

3. 
Select the Scheduled tab. 

4. 
Click More actions next to the report, and then select Edit schedule. 

5. 
In the Schedule section, set the Recurrence option to None to keep the scheduled report 

but stop its delivery. 

Alternatively, in the Ending on drop-down list, select End date, and then set the End on 

date to the current date.

Tip for Scheduling Monthly Reports 

For recurring monthly reports that include the entire month, consider the following: any report 

that includes a reporting period option can be set to Prior month. Financial, standard, and 

memorized reports have this option when creating the report. The report can then be scheduled 

to run any time during the current month. It will provide a report for the entire prior month. 

In this way, you can ensure that you won’t get additional transactions that were added between 

midnight (local time, based on your company location settings) and the time the report ran or 

missing transactions before the end of the period due to the time of day that the report was run. 

You can choose to run the report on the first (or any) day of the next month if you set the 

reporting period to Prior Month. 

Another option is to schedule the report for the last day of the month and manually add any 

transactions that occurred between the time the report ran and the end of the day.

### Custom Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 260*

Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Custom Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > Custom Reports`


In addition to standard and financial reports, you can build custom reports. Create custom reports 

to get insight and answers from the unique information stored in your system. Financial reports 

are based on account groupings such as assets and liabilities, while custom reports and 

dimension structures are based on records and fields either grouped together or separately. 

For example, you can create a custom report that displays vendor contact information. You can 

control which vendors you want to display, such as active vendors in certain regions, and select 

the details to include about the vendors. You can then sort and display the results to highlight 

what is most important to you. 

With a custom report, you can: 

• 
Report on fields from almost any record or transaction in the system, and any related data. 

• 
Customize the report for your needs. 

• 
Run the reports, export them in another format, or add them to dashboards. 

Before you can export a report or add it to a group, you need to memorize the report.  

Creating Custom Reports 

Custom reports are created with the custom report wizard, which walks you through the steps to 

create a report. Only users who have permission to Customization Services can add and edit 

reports by going to the Custom Reports list on the Customization services menu. 

You can run the custom report from the Reports application. 

Adding a Custom Report to an Application’s Menu 

If you use a custom report on a regular basis, you can add the custom report to an application’s 

menu. For example, a report with payables-related data can be added to the Accounts Payable 

menu. After adding a custom report to the A/P menu, you can run the custom report by clicking 

the Custom Reports menu option, which displays a list of all of the custom reports that you have 

added to the Accounts Payable menu. 

The Custom Reports option displays on menus only after you (or someone else) has added at 

least one custom report to the application’s menu. The Custom Reports option does not appear 

on a menu if no one has added any custom reports to the application’s menu. 

---



#### Using the Custom Report Wizard to Create Positive Pay Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 261*

Chapter 3: Working with Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Using the Custom Report Wizard to Create Positive Pay Reports 

Using the custom report wizard, you can create a report that you send to the bank for processing 

positive pay.  

Positive pay is a fraud prevention system in which you send the bank a list of checks processed by 

your company’s Accounts Payable department for a specific time frame. The bank then honors 

only the checks that appear on the list. Your report might differ slightly based on the bank’s 

requirements for the positive pay file. This example takes you step-by-step through a common 

method of creating this report. 

---



### Positive Pay Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 262*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 262*

Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Positive Pay Report 

Create positive pay reports when your company uses a positive pay system with the bank. This 

report is sent on a schedule based on when you process your checks in Accounts Payable. 

The report creates a flat list to send to the bank that includes all checks written for the time 

period, the amount, and the payee. It can contain more, but this is the minimum. The bank then 

compares the checks presented with the list and accepts only those that appear there. 

This report is created using the custom report wizard. You’ll notice that voided checks are 

included in the report. These can be removed, but are often left in the report so the bank knows 

that these check numbers aren’t valid. 

Before You Begin 

To build custom reports, you must be subscribed to Customization Services. If you do not yet 

subscribe to Customization Services, contact your RealPage representative for subscription 

information. 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to create the Positive Pay report.

Use the Financial Report Writer to create and edit financial reports. This tool can create both 

standard financial reports, such as income statements and balance sheet reports, and an infinite 

array of other reports that analyze or highlight key business metrics, such as revenue by product 

line. 

Some things you can do with a financial report include: 

• 
Selecting groups of accounts to include in your report. 

• 
Adding analysis based on your dimension data, such as items by product line, customers by 

type, or selected departments. 

• 
Expanding or collapsing sections of the report to show or hide account detail. 

• 
Selecting what you want to appear in columns, such as actual amounts, budget amounts, 

computations, and even non-financial data such as customer email addresses.

### About Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 270*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Dimensions 

A dimension is a category of data that you can organize and sort in meaningful ways. RealPage 

Accounting provides the following pre-defined dimensions: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

In addition, RealPage Accounting enables you to define new dimensions to suit your needs. These 

user-defined dimensions enable you to organize and sort categories of data unique to your 

business. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, you might create 

a user-defined dimension called Line of business. The values you could add are Direct customers, 

Channel partner, and OEM. 

Dimensions enable you to collect, sort, analyze, and report on data within one category, or 

between categories, so you can identify key factors such as: 

• 
Your most profitable or most costly customers. 

• 
The return on investment of a location or department. 

• 
Whether and to what degree a new product or product line is successful. 

• 
Which way a particular aspect of your business is trending. 

RealPage Accounting dimensions give you fine control over data definition and data hierarchy. 

With dimensions, you can customize financial reports around specific business activities, get 

greater visibility into how the business is doing, and make faster, more meaningful business 

decisions. 

Additional fees may apply for user-defined dimensions. Contact your RealPage account 

representative for more information. 

---

Dimension Structures for Financial Reports 

Dimension structures provide a flexible way for you to organize dimension data that you want to 

see on the rows or columns of a financial report. For example, instead of showing all locations on 

a report, you might want to select a Location structure that is named for a particular region and 

includes a subset of locations. 

You can add any number of structures for the dimensions you track. 

To find your dimension structures, go to the General Ledger menu and, under Report Structure, 

click Dimension Structures. There is a separate dimension structure list for each dimension you’ve 

enabled in your company. 

For multi-entity shared users: This is a master object, which can either be common (that is, 
accessible) to all entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. Learn more about dimension 
structures in a multi -entity shared environment (on page 544 ). 

Read About dimension structures (on page 264).

Dimension Structures Created from Dimension Groups 

Dimension structures are built from dimension groups, which can contain particular members 

(such as one or more locations) or members that meet certain criteria (such as customers of a 

particular type). Learn more about dimension groups. 

The following graphic shows a simple location structure named South, which contains a location 

group that includes a company’s southern offices as its members. 

a) Dimension groups are custom groupings that are meaningful to your company. 

b) Dimension report structures can contain one or more dimension groups.

#### Creating a Dimension Group and Structure Simultaneously
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 276*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension groups and dimension structures work together to provide power and flexibility in 

reporting. 

• 
Dimension groups enable you to dynamically filter data at the time you run a report, and 

can be used for standard reports, such as an A/R Ledger, as well as financial reports. 

• 
In addition to creating groups that include particular members, one of the most 

powerful ways to use dimension groups is to select members based on filter criteria. 

For example, a dimension group can filter for customers of the same type, items from 

the same product line, or locations with the same parent location. 

• 
Dimension groups are also used outside of financial reports. For example, you might 

have a dimension group that is used only to filter the A/R Ledger for customers with 

an outstanding balance greater than $500. 

• 
Dimension structures are created specifically for the purpose of adding dimensions to the 

rows or columns of financial reports. 

• 
Depending on how you assemble the groups in structures, you can achieve different 

results on reports. Groups can be assembled into structures that display dimension 

members (such as locations or customers) in a flat list or can be used to create 

multi-level hierarchical structures. 

• 
As with account groups, dimension structures enable you to choose what text you 

want to appear on heading and total lines, for example enabling you to display 

Customers by Industry in the heading row and Total Customers in the total row. 

Creating a Dimension Group and Structure Simultaneously 


> **Navigation Path:** `Reports > Setup > Dimension Groups > Location`


If you don’t already have a dimension group that contains the members you need for a dimension 

structure, you can create the dimension group and structure at the same time. 

To do this: 

1. 
Create a new dimension group, such as a new Location group. 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to Location. 

3. 
For structure type, select the Location Group option. 

4.

Create a New Dimension Structure 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the Dimension structures section, click 
 Add next to the structure you want to add. 

The system opens a blank dimension report structure information page. 

3. 
Enter a Name that indicates the function of the dimension structure. 

Based on the Name, the system suggests the name that will appear on reports (Display on 

report as) and the total line text (Display total line as). 

4. 
Review the suggested names and make changes as needed. For example, you can create a 

structure named “Eastern locations” to help you remember its function, but on reports you 

display the structure as “East Coast” with a total line of “Total East Coast.” 

5. 
In the Structure type drop-down list, select Dimension groups. For example, if you’re 

creating a location structure, select Location groups. 

The system adds the Roll Up Child Amounts check box under the Display total line as field. 

6. 
Decide whether the report should roll up child amounts for dimension members that have 

children. 

• 
By default, amounts for dimension members don’t include amounts from children. For 

example, amounts for departments don’t include any child departments, locations 

don’t include sub locations, and so on. 

• 
In some cases, rolled up reporting might make sense. For example, suppose that your 

projects are typically organized into child projects. By selecting Roll Up Child 

Amounts, you can ensure that when Project A is included on a report, the amounts 

reported all of the child projects.

Viewing or Editing a Dimension Structure 

When you edit a dimension structure, your changes will apply to all reports that use the structure. 

Before editing, it’s a good idea to review which reports and graphs will be affected. 

Dimension Structures in Your Lists 

Even if you haven’t yet created any dimension structures, you may find that you already have 

some in your lists. If you have existing dimension groups—such as location groups that represent 

different regions, we automatically create corresponding dimension structures so that you’re 

ready to use your existing groupings on reports. 

To view and edit your existing dimension structures: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Financial Statements section, select the Dimension Structures option, and then select 

the desired dimension. 

For example, to display your department structures, go to the General Ledger menu and 

select Dimension Structures > Department. 

3. 
From the Dimension report structure list, click to navigate into a structure to get more 

information about a particular structure. 

• 
The View link enables you to see how the structure is defined. 

• 
To quickly see the members within a structure, click the Members link instead. 

• 
To see which reports and graphs use the structure, click the Reports or Graphs link. 

4. 
Click the Edit link to change the dimension structure as needed. 

The dimension structure defines how the structure should be listed on reports, and what it 

should contain. 

• 
To change the title and total line, edit the fields for Display on report as and Display 

total line as. 

• 
To change the dimension members that appear when the structure is used on reports, 

edit the dimension groups that make up the structure. If the dimension structure 

contains other structures, edit those structures to review the dimension groups. 

You can also view dimension structures from within the Financial Report Writer at the time 
that you add a structure to a row or column.

To include a top or bottom match on a financial report, you must first create a dimension 

structure that contains the set of members from which you want to choose the top or bottom.

metric of your choice.

### Expanding by Dimension and the Show Option
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 289*

Chapter 4: Working with Financial Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Expanding by Dimension and the Show Option 

Since many dimensions are hierarchical (for example, a US location might be organized by state, 

with additional locations in certain cities), the Show drop-down list allows you to choose: 

• 
How many levels to show. 

• 
Whether amounts or reported individually, or with amounts “rolled up” from levels below it. 

The following table describes each option, and provides examples. 

Option 
Description 

One level down, with roll-up 
Displays rows that contain summary amounts for one level 

only. 

For example, suppose that you have locations in California, 

New York, and Florida. In addition, California has sublocations 

for Northern California and Southern California. In this case, 

the report: 

• 
Includes rows for California, New York, and Florida 

• 
Doesn’t include rows for sublocations, such as 

particular regions (like Northern California). However, 

amounts from sublocations are included in the 

summary amounts for California, New York, and 

Florida. 

All levels, with roll-up 
Displays rows that contain summary amounts for each level. 

For example, suppose that your California location has 

sublocations by city. In this case, the report: 

• 
Includes rows for California and each city in California. 

• 
Includes amounts from each city in the amount for 

California. 

---


<!-- Page 290 -->
Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

All levels, with individual balance 
Displays all levels, but with each level showing only the 

individual amounts assigned to that level. 

For example, suppose that your California location has 

sublocations by city. In this case, the report: 

• 
Includes rows for California and each city within 

California. 

• 
Doesn’t include amounts from each city in the amount 

for California. 

In the case of expenses, for instance, the row for “California” 

would include only expenses attributed directly to California 

and would not include amounts from any city in California. 

Leaf amounts, all levels 
Displays only the lowest levels of the hierarchy. 

For example, suppose you have a location in Arizona with no 

sublocations, but you also have a location in California, with 

sublocations in Los Angeles and San Jose. Choosing “Leaf 

amounts, all levels,” would include rows for: 

• 
Arizona 

• 
Los Angeles 

• 
San Jose 

Leaf amounts, one level down 
Displays only one level, but includes amounts from only the 

lowest levels. 

For example, suppose you have a location in Arizona with no 

sublocations, but you also have a location in California, with 

sublocations in Los Angeles and San Jose. Choosing “Leaf 

amounts, one level down,” would: 

• 
Include rows for Arizona and California. 

• 
California would include only amounts from Los 

Angeles and San Jose.

Creating Individual Reports by Department or Location 

For financial reports and other General Ledger reports, you can save time by: 

• 
Creating a single report for a group of departments, locations, or entities 

• 
Selecting the option to separate the data into individual reports at runtime 

For example, you might want to run a Profit & Loss report for three locations (London, Miami, and 

Boston). Instead of defining the Profit & Loss report three times (with each report filtered for a 

different location), you can create one combined report that gets split into individual reports (as 

sections) at runtime. 

This is a two-step process: 

1. 
Create a group of departments, locations, or entities 

2. 
Set up the report to create individual reports for each group member 

Running the Financial Report 

The following instructions assume that you are familiar with creating financial reports (on page 

258). 

1. 
Create or edit a financial report. 

2. 
On the Columns tab, expand each column of data by department or location. 

For example, if you have a single column that displays Actual amounts for the Prior Year, 

click in that column and use the Expand by option to expand the column by departments or 

locations. 

To do the column expansion: 

• 
Scroll down and click in the Expand by menu. 

• 
In the dialog box that appears, choose the option to expand by Departments or 

Locations. 

---


<!-- Page 292 -->
Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
On the Filters tab, select options as follows. 

• 
Select a group from the Department or Location drop-down list. 

• 
Select the Run as Individual Reports option. 

4. 
On the Format tab, select the option to display department and location titles in place of 

the company title on individual reports. 

• 
On the Format tab, switch to the Page Setup & Columns section by clicking the 

sub-tab at the top. 

• 
Select the option for Company title: Display Departments/Locations as company title 

on individual reports. 

Inactive locations aren’t included in individual reports, even if you clear the option to “Hide 
inactives.”

Using Segments in the Financial Reports Writer 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Financial 
Reports > Add/Edit > Rows`


You can filter reports using user-defined segments and units in addition to dimensions. If no 

segments are selected in filters, by default, the system displays the data for all the segments. 

• 
You can select one or more segment types and values to filter your financial data. 

• 
Locations and units are tightly coupled. When you select a Unit in Expand by, the system 

prompts you to select a location. 

• 
You can select a Location group if the individual report option is selected. 

• 
You can limit the financial report output to display only the transactions which are not tied 

to any segments by selecting the Only blank check box. 

Expanding by Segment Type on Rows 

The option to filter by segment structure appears only if you selected the option to Filter by 

segment structure on rows on the Report info tab when you created the report. 

When the option is set, it enables you to filter account groups by segment structure to include 

only certain data, such as revenue for certain product lines (user defined segments) and expenses 

for certain departments.

Tips and Tricks 

• 
When you create your report, make sure to select the option to Filter by segment structure 

on rows on the Report Info tab. 

• 
On the Rows tab, add your account groups. 

• 
Using the Filter by segment structure column, select the segment structures to filter by. 

• 
You can choose different segment structures for different account groups (as shown above) 

or click Set segment structure to apply the same one to all rows. 

• 
When you filter a row by segment structure (an option that you enable on the Report Info 

tab), your selection is used only as a filter. To show additional rows for the segment 

structure, you must set the detail level. 

• 
To limit the financial report output to display only the transactions which are not tied to any 

segments, select the Only blank check box.

Setting the Detail Level for a Segment Structure 

To set the detail level for a segment structure: 

1. 
Set the Detail Level to Summary-Hide accounts. 

2. 
Select the option to Expand by Segments. 

3. 
From the Segments drop-down list, select the type of expansion you want to perform. 

• 
Expand by segment name: This option is best for flat segment structures. It displays 

individual segment members. In the graphic below, Revenue is filtered by all “Active 

projects” and then expanded by Projects to show revenue on a project-by-project 

basis. 

• 
Expand by segment structure: This option is best for hierarchical segment structures, 

and shows summary rows for the structure. This option does not include any individual 

members. 

a) Expand by job type to show individual job types. 

b) Expand by projects to show individual projects.

Instead of displaying a single summary amount for an account group, you can create additional 

summary rows that break the data down by segment. For example, expanding a “Fixed Assets, 

Net” account group by location would display a summary amount for “Fixed Assets, Net” with 

additional rows (indented underneath) that show the amount for each location. 

The examples may refer to locations, but you can break your data down by any segment.

1. 
Set the Detail Level to Summary-Hide accounts.

Select the option to Expand by segment.

Financial Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 294) topic for a list of ways to access financial reports. 

Financial reports are available from the General Ledger, Reports, and Reporting Portal 

applications. You can create financial reports using the Financial report writer, or, if your 

company was created using a QuickStart template, you can access standard financial reports by 

clicking the Financial reports library button in the Financial reports list. 

To use one of the standard reports, you need to map your chart of accounts to the system 

categories, and the reports become live with your data. This helps speed up the otherwise 

time-consuming process of manually creating account groups that contain the appropriate G/L 

accounts and then creating financial reports and graphs using those account groups. 

Each application includes a set of standard reports that you can run to produce basic, common 

reports quickly. You can create, run, view, export, and memorize the following types of reports: 

• 
Standard reports available from the Reports section of each application menu and from the 

Reports center. 

• 
Financial reports and graphs using the Financial report writer. 

You cannot change the report structure after creating the report. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use financial reports. 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

General Ledger 
Financials 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 502) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 502) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

#### Creating a Financial Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 306*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Creating a Financial Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 294) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

The Financial report writer provides options for controlling all aspects of your financial report, 

from building your rows and columns to setting precise formatting options. 

Adding a Financial Report 

To create a report using the Financial report writer: 

1. 
In the Financial reports list, click the Add button. The Financial report writer opens. 

2. 
Name your report. 

3. 
Select your basic report structure (Report info tab (on page 326)). 

4. 
Review the options in the Report structure section of the Report info tab, using the report 

samples as a guide. After you create a report, you can’t change the report structure. 

5. 
Select either Accounts or Dimensions, depending on what you’d like to see on your report 

rows. 

6. 
Build your account rows. 

Depending on the report structure you selected on the Report info tab, you’ll either build 

rows from account groups or dimension structures. For existing reports, the headings that 

you see along the left side of the tab reflect the account groups or dimension structures 

that have already been added to the report. 

       Type of rows  
        Description 

Accounts on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the account groups 

that you want to appear on the left side of your 

report. For example, a balance sheet report might 

include “Assets” and “Liabilities and Equity.” 

Dimensions on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the dimension 

structures that you want to appear on the left side 

of your report. For example, you might want to 

show rows for customers, or certain locations or 

departments. 

---


<!-- Page 307 -->
Chapter 4: Working with Financial Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Setting Up Columns (Columns Tab) (on page 348) 

1. 
Choose the columns you want to include in the report. 

2. 
Decide what value you want to include in each column. For example, you might want to see 

the account names or dimension names on the left, followed by actual columns for different 

reporting periods. 

3. 
Column values can be based on calculations, such as summary calculations that operate on 

two or more columns (such as computing the average of a set of columns). For reports that 

feature account groups on rows, you can define more complex calculations on the 

Computations tab. 

4. 
Select the Account group purpose. This is displayed in the list and in the report. 

Filtering the Report (Filters Tab (on page 405)) 

You can set options such as the “as of date” and reporting method. You can also filter the report 

by dimension, such as filtering for a particular set of locations. 

In practice, many reports are designed to prompt the user for the “as of date” and other criteria 

when the report is run. That way you can create a single report and let the user choose the criteria 

when the report is run. 

Setting Up Headers and Footers (Format Tab (on page 416)) 

Set page header, footer, font, and other report format options. 

Row formatting options let you control the appearance and spacing of row headings and totals. 

Click the 
 Help buttons next to Row formatting and Total formatting in the Rows section to 

learn more. 

If any columns are missing when you preview the report, on the 
Filters tab choose to show zero 
balance columns to force any zero balance columns to display. 

Setting Access Restrictions for the Report (Permissions Tab (on page 433)) 

Finish the report with any optional next steps, such as adding the report to a dashboard, making 

it a favorite, or scheduling it to run automatically (Next Steps (on page 435)). 

Multi-Entity Companies: Private Reports 

By default, financial reports are set to Public. 

This means that everyone can see them. If a report is private, only the users in the entity and with 

permissions can see the report. Top-level admins can also see private reports if they check 

Include Private in the list of reports. 

To make entity-level financial reports private by default, disable the Set default permissions to 

public setting at the top-level General Ledger configuration.

#### Deleting, Inactivating, or Reactivating a Financial Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 312*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Deleting, Inactivating, or Reactivating a Financial Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 294) topic for a list of ways to access financial reports. 

If you delete a report, it can’t be restored. Making a report inactive removes it from the list but 

retains the report information in case you need to reactivate it. 

If there is chance that you’ll need to run the report at a later date—perhaps even years later— 

then we recommend that you make it inactive instead of deleting it. For example, you may need 

to make a change to a report due to an audit or generate a copy of the report for legal purposes. 

In this case, if the report is inactive, you can reactivate it and run it or make changes. If the report 

is deleted, you would have to recreate the report from scratch. 

Another reason to choose one over the other might be to keep the original report pristine while 

you incorporate changes to a copy. If the changes don’t work the way you expect, you can keep 

making changes to the copy and still make sure that you can restore the original. By inactivating 

the original, no one can use it and it doesn’t appear in lists. When you’re completely confident 

that the new report works correctly, you can go ahead and delete the original. 

Before You Begin 

Access to financial reports can vary depending on your permissions. The ability to view, add, and 

edit financial reports is controlled by separate General Ledger permissions. Working with financial 

reports can involve multiple tasks, such as running reports, editing reports, navigating into a 

report, and so on. Each of these can require a specific set of permissions, both for the General 

Ledger and for the Company. 

Make sure that you have all of the necessary permissions when working with financial reports. 

Deleting a Financial Report 

Deleting a report removes the report completely. If you are sure you never want to run the report, 

delete it. Otherwise, consider making the report inactive. 

You can configure the system to warn you when you’re about to delete a report. Click your login 

name on any page, then choose My preferences, and on the Preferences page, select the Warn 

on delete check box. 

To delete a custom report: 

1. 
Open the Financial reports list. 

2. 
Locate the report to delete, and then click the Delete link. 

3. 
Click OK to confirm. 

---


<!-- Page 313 -->
Chapter 4: Working with Financial Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Inactivating a Financial Report 

Inactivating a report removes it from lists within the system. Additionally, if you inactivate a 

custom report, it won’t appear on the Financial reports list unless you select the Include inactive 

option at the top of the list. 

To inactivate a financial report: 

1. 
Open the Financial reports list. 

2. 
Locate the report, and then click Edit. 

3. 
Go to the Next Steps step (the last step of the report writer). 

4. 
Clear the This report is active check box. 

5. 
Save the report. 

Reactivating a Financial Report 

If you inactivate a report and later want to reactivate it, you first need to be able to see the report 

in the list. 

To reactivate a financial report: 

1. 
Open the Financial reports list. 

2. 
At the top of the list, select Include inactive. Now, the inactivated report appears in the list. 

3. 
Locate the report, and then click Edit, then and select the This report is active check box on 

the Report Info tab. 

4. 
Save your changes. The report is now active again.

#### Changing the Name of The Company at the Top of a Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 314*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Changing the Name of The Company at the Top of a Report 

By default, your company name is displayed in the page header of printed reports. 

However, when you want to split a report that compares data by department or location into 

multiple individual reports, you can choose to display the department or location name in the 

report title instead of the company name. 

To display the department or location name in the report title: 

1. 
Create a financial report that shows either rows or columns expanded by department or 

location. 

2. 
For rows, go to the Rows tab and set the Detail level to Expand by dimension for 

department or location. 

3. 
For columns, go to the Columns tab and select an Expand by option for department or 

location. 

4. 
On the Filters tab, select Run as individual reports to create separate reports for each 

department or location rather than one combined report. 

5. 
On the Format tab, select Display departments/locations as company title on individual 

reports. 

6. 
Click Save & Done.

#### Creating a Comparative Income Statement Report
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 327*

Income Statement Report Columns 

By default, the Income Statement report contains the following columns: 

• 
(Accounts): This column displays a list of income and expense accounts in their account 

group hierarchy. 

• 
Month ending: This column displays account actuals for the current reporting period. 

• 
Year to date: This column displays account actuals from the beginning of the fiscal year to 

the current date. 

These are the columns that appear when you initially install the report from the System financial 

reports list. You can configure additional columns by editing the report in the Financial report 

writer. 

Creating a Comparative Income Statement Report 

When you can’t find a specific report in the system that you need, you can create a report based 

on a system-provided report. Our financial reports are the baseline reports that the system comes 

with. You can create additional reports by duplicating and changing an existing report or by 

creating your own reports using the Custom Report Writer. 

For example, if you need a comparative report that shows prior year income versus current year 

income, you can duplicate the income statement report and add columns to it that show figures 

from additional reporting periods such as Prior Month, Prior Year or any other option in the 

Reporting Periods option in the Columns tab. 

This procedure walks through the process of creating a custom comparative income statement 

report from a baseline income statement report. 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select Financial Reports. 

3. 
Type “Income” in the Name column’s search field. 

4. 
Click the Edit link of an existing income statement report that you can copy. 

5. 
Click the Duplicate button. 

---


<!-- Page 328 -->
Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
In the Duplicate report box, type a new name for the report, such as “Comparative Income.” 

7. 
Click OK to save the report as a duplicate. 

8. 
Find your new report. You may need to click Clear all filters to reset the list. 

9. 
Click the Edit link of your new report. 

10. 
Click the Columns tab. 

11. 
Click the Actual column to make it active.  

12. 
Change the Reporting period drop-down list of the Actual column to Current year to date. 

13. 
Create a second Actual column by clicking the Actual column’s heading, and selecting Add 

column right. 

14. 
Click the new column to make it active. 

15. 
Set Reporting Period to Prior year. 

16. 
If you wish to see the prior year data on the left, click the Prior Year column’s header to 

display its submenu, and then select Move column left. 

17. 
Click the Save & Done button. 

To open the report, click the link of the desired format, HTML, CSV, PDF, or Excel. 

---

Income Statement Budget Comparison Report Columns 

By default, the Income Statement Budget Comparison report contains the following columns: 

• 
(Accounts): This column displays a list of income and expense accounts in their account 

group hierarchy. 

• 
Month ending: This column section displays account actuals and budgeted amounts for the 

current reporting period. 

• 
Actual: This column displays account actuals for the current reporting period. 

• 
Budget: This column displays the amount budgeted for each account for the current 

reporting period. 

• 
Difference: This column displays the difference between the actuals and budgeted 

amounts for the current reporting period. 

• 
Variance %: This column displays the percent difference between the actuals and 

budgeted amounts for the current reporting period. 

• 
Year to date: This column section displays account actuals and budgeted amounts from the 

beginning of the fiscal year to the current date. 

• 
YTD actual: This column displays account actuals from the beginning of the fiscal year 

to the current date. 

• 
YTD budget: This column displays the amount budgeted for each account from the 

beginning of the fiscal year to the current date.  

• 
YTD difference: This column displays the difference between the year-to-date actuals 

and budgeted amounts. 

• 
YTD variance %: This column displays the percent difference between the year-to-date 

actuals and budgeted amounts. 

These are the columns that appear when you initially install the report from the System financial 

reports list. You can configure additional columns by editing the report in the Financial report 

writer.

Use the Financial report writer to create and edit financial reports. This includes both standard 

financial reports, such as income statements and balance sheet reports, and an infinite array of 

other reports that analyze or highlight key business metrics, such as revenue by product line. 

The Financial report writer guides you through the process of creating or editing a financial 

report, from adding rows and columns to deciding how your report should be formatted on page 

and in print. 

Some things you can do with a financial report include: 

• 
Selecting groups of accounts to include in your report. 

• 
Adding analysis based on your segment data, such as items by product line, customers by 

type, or selected departments. 

• 
Prompting users to set or change filter criteria at report runtime.  

• 
Expanding or collapsing sections of the report to show or hide account detail. 

• 
Selecting what you want to appear in columns, such as account data, budget data, 

computations, and even non-financial data such as customer email addresses.

Set up your columns (on page 348).

Add computations (on page 394), if applicable. 

5.

report at runtime. 

6.

7. 
Set access permissions (on page 433). 

8. 
Finish the report with any optional next steps (on page 435).
