Filtering by Location, Department, or Other Dimension 

In addition to the default dimensions for departments and locations, your company may use 

other dimensions to track transactions. These dimensions let you filter reports in multiple ways; 

for instance, by showing data from only certain locations or customers. 

If you apply more than one filter, then the report will contain the subset of data that meets all of 

the filter criteria. For example, if you choose “Sales” as the department and “Arizona” as the 

location, then the report will include data only for the Sales department at the Arizona location. 

Filter for a Specific Dimension Member 

For any dimension that you’ve enabled, you can select an individual member to filter by. For 

example, you might filter a report for a specific location, department, or customer. 

To filter for a specific location, department, or other dimension member: 

1. 
Locate the dimension filter and select the option for Specific dimension/group. 

For example, to filter for a location, go to the Location drop-down list and choose the 

Specific location/group option. 

2. 
In the drop-down list that appears, select the dimension member by which you want to 

filter. 

• 
Using location as an example, choose the name of the location by which you want to 

filter. 

• 
The drop-down lists contain all available dimension groups, followed by individual 

dimension members, sorted alphabetically by ID.

department or location, select the Run as individual reports check box. 

When the report is generated as PDF, each individual report starts on a new page. In HTML

Filter for Two or More Dimension Members Using Groups 

Use dimension groups if you want to filter for two or more dimensions. A dimension group is a

A set of locations (such as your US locations) 

•

Dimension Type 

Many dimensions can be tagged to types and groups. Customer types and vendor types can also 

have parent types for filtering. 

Categorize records according to type for filtering, sorting, and grouping opportunities. These 

types can take advantage of an additional layer of grouping by assigning a dimension type. If you 

assign a dimension type within your types, you can also get a native roll-up of any types assigned 

the dimension type during reporting. 

For example, if you set up the vendor types as Contractor and Subcontractor and make

Prompt check box.

If you want to generate the report to display only the transactions not associated with any 

dimension type, select the Only blank check box.

Prompting for Filters at Runtime 

You can prompt users for selected filters when you run the report. 

While it’s typical to prompt users for the “As of date” for a report, it’s also common to prompt for 

the location, department, or other criteria. For example, instead of creating a balance sheet report 

that is always filtered for a particular location, you can use the Prompt option to enable users to 

choose a location or location group. 

How the Prompt Option Works 

If you select the Prompt check box for a segment, the system asks for this information when you 

run the report. The user who runs the report chooses the account group or segment structure to 

filter by. 

By choosing to prompt at runtime, you can set up one report and use it multiple ways, such as 

setting up a balance sheet report and then running it for different locations on the fly. 

If you select specific segment filters and also select the Prompt check box, then the system 

automatically fills in the report prompt with your selections. However, you can override the filters. 

Example: Prompting for G/L Account Groups or Reporting Periods 

You can dynamically run financial reports on a G/L account group other than what the report was 

originally set up for (account groups are defined (on page 337) on the Rows tab of the Financial 

report writer). To do this, enable the Prompt for G/L account groups option in the financial 

report. This allows you to choose an alternate G/L account group when you run the report rather 

than duplicating a report and changing the account group(s). 

Additionally, you can enable the Prompt for reporting periods check box to dynamically run 

financial reports for a reporting period, column heading, and expand by. Columns for Actual, 

Budget, Remaining budget, Open commitments, and Pending commitments appear in the 

prompt.

When you Run, Schedule, or Process & store the report, you can select one or more account

If you do not select an account group, then the report will run based on the original account

#### Using Dimension Groups to Specify Order in Rows and Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 422*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Using Dimension Groups to Specify Order in Rows and Columns 

In financial reports, you can expand rows or columns by dimension. For example, you can expand 

an actual column into several columns by location, department, or other dimension. 

To control the order of members in rows or columns: 

Workflow 

1. 
Create a dimension group that contains the desired members. 

In the dimension group, order the members as you want them to be listed in reports. 

2. 
Filter the report by the dimension group. 

How Location and Department Filters Work 

When you make selections for Department and Location, the following rules apply: 

• 
The calculations are based on the combination of the specified department and location. 

For example, if you chose the Manufacturing department and the California location, the 

calculations are based on numbers only for Manufacturing departments that are also 

located in California. 

• 
All children of parent departments and locations are included in the calculations. 

• 
If you created a department hierarchy using a parent/child relationship, you can report on 

the parent department or the individual child department by selecting the department 

name from the drop-down list. If you choose a parent department, the system retrieves all 

the information from the child departments assigned to that parent and displays the 

information with that of the parent as a rolled-up total. 

• 
If you are a multi-entity shared user of the ownership financials and distribution feature, you 

can select a location only if the owner you select in the Report on owner field has some 

percentage ownership in the entity under which the location falls.

Running Financial Reports on Alternate G/L Account Groups 

You can dynamically run financial reports on an alternate G/L account group other than what the 

report is set up for. Instead of setting up duplicate financial reports for the same report but with 

different account groups, enable the Prompt for G/L Account Groups option in the financial 

report.  

To let the user choose the G/L account group or groups at runtime: 

1. 
Open the financial report for editing. 

2. 
Click the Filters tab. 

3. 
Select the Prompt for G/L account groups check box. 

4. 
Click Save & Done. 

When a user generates the report, the Report Prompt box opens. 

5. 
Click the Select button and then choose the account groups. 

• 
The order of the account groups that you select is the order that they will appear in 

the report. 

• 
If no account groups are selected, then the report runs based on the original account 

group.

#### Best Practices
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 424*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you choose the Process & Store option to generate the report, then the Storage Options 
box opens, where you can click the Select button and choose the account groups. 

Best Practices 

When you generate a report, the data that’s included is based on what you add to your rows and 

columns, and any filters that you apply. 

• 
All financial reports include account groups, which indicate which accounting data should 

be included in the report. For example, a balance sheet might include account groups for 

“Assets” and “Liabilities & Equity.” These account groups can include filters in their 

definitions, although this is not recommended in most cases. 

• 
Financial reports can also include segment structures that represent a set of segment data 

that you want to include on rows and columns. For example, you might want your rows or 

columns to include selected departments, customers by type, or items by product line. By 

nature, these segment structures limit the data to be displayed in the report. 

• 
Additionally, you can apply report-level filters on the Filters tab. For example, you might 

filter a report for a particular location or a location group that includes a specific set of 

locations. 

• 
In general, filters that you add to the Filters tab and filters on account groups are applied 

first, followed by any other filtering. For maximum flexibility, it’s recommended that you 

don’t use account group filters. 

---


<!-- Page 425 -->
Chapter 4: Working with Financial Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Best Practices for Filtering 

When defining reports, it’s best to keep your approach simple to avoid situations in which there’s 

a conflict between the data on rows and columns and any filtering you’ve applied. 

• 
Avoid adding filters to your account group definitions. 

Although you can define filters for an account group—for example, filtering a Cost of Goods 

Sold account group for a particular location—it’s recommended that you don’t add any 

filters to account groups. Instead of filtering your account groups: 

• 
Define your account groups without filters. 

• 
On a report-by-report basis, use the options available in the Financial Report Writer to 

select the data you want to see. 

• 
When filtering for a specific set of members (or members that meet certain criteria), define 

your filters in only one place. 

In general, avoid situations in which you select one set of segment data on rows and 

columns, and then set a report-level filter that includes a different set of data. Instead, do 

either of the following: 

• 
Apply filters on the Filters tab. To filter the entire report for a specific set of segment 

data, you can select one or more segment groups on the Filters tab. For example, you 

might filter a report for “West Coast locations.” 

• 
Select and filter data on the Rows and Columns tabs. On each tab, you can select the 

data you want to see in your rows and columns. Depending on the type of report you 

are creating, different options will be available. For example, you could add Cost of 

Goods sold to your report rows and then create columns that compare by different 

locations.

Accounts

Numbers

correctly in the report. No other formatting, such as font and font size, is allowed.

#### Showing and Hiding Zero Balance Rows and Columns

Showing and Hiding Zero Balance Rows and Columns 

The zero number options let you adjust how zero balance rows and columns are handled in the 

report. 

By default: 

• 
Sections of a report are hidden if the total or subtotal is zero and all detail rows are also 

zero. 

Regardless of the options you select for the Numbers field, the logic for including a section 

in a report is as follows: 

• 
If all rows for a section are zero, the section is hidden. For example, suppose that you 

didn’t have any charitable contributions for the reporting periods shown in a report. In 

this case, the Charitable Contributions section would be hidden. 

• 
If the total for a section is zero, but it contains some detail rows that have a balance, 

the section is included in the report. For example, a Headcount section would appear if 

there was a total of 0 headcount growth, but there was +2 headcount for one 

department and -2 headcount for another department. 

• 
Detail rows with a zero balance are hidden unless you select the option to Display zero 

balance with activity. 

• 
Columns of a report are displayed even if the total and detail rows are zero unless you clear 

the Display zero balance columns option. 

• 
Calculations are displayed by default, even if the result is 0.00, unless you select the Do not 

display zero value calculation option. 

Zero Numbers Options 

• 
Display zero balance with activity: Shows detail rows that have zero balances as long as 

there were transactions posted during the reporting period. 

This is a report-wide setting. However, you can use the Always display option on the Rows 
tab to select specific sections where you want to display the total and all detail rows, even 
if the amount is zero. 

• 
Display zero for future periods: Shows zero amounts for any column where the reporting 

period is in the future. 

This feature is useful if your report is set up for 12 months, but you only want to see actual 

amounts for the past and current periods, even if there are future transactions. If, for 

example, you have a report set up with columns for every month of the year and you run 

the report as of June 30, then even though your columns contain actual amounts, you can 

see numbers for future dates, such as for the Month Ended July. However, you can select 

this check box to zero all future numbers and clean up your report. 

---

This applies to actuals only. 

• 
Display zero balance columns: Clearing this option automatically hides any columns that 

have only zero amounts. This can be particularly useful if you sometimes compare report 

data by time period or segment and you want to automatically hide any columns that don’t 

have data. 

• 
Do not display zero value calculation: Select this option to exclude zero-value calculations 

(0.00) in the report. This setting affects the Computation on actual and Computation on 

budget column types.

and ID.

Defining Report Headers and Footers 

Page Header 

By default, printed reports start with your company name, followed by the report title, and a 

subtitle that spells out the report’s “As of date” in words. Using the options in the Page header 

and Page footer sections, you have the option to: 

• 
Change the report title. 

• 
Include additional lines of header text and optionally change how and where the date is 

displayed. 

• 
Include your company logo in the header. 

• 
Include footer text, including dynamic information that specifies the page number and 

date/time when the report was printed.

(PDF) format. As noted in the table, some header elements (such as the report title) also appear 

when the report is displayed in Excel or HTML format.

title.

As of [As_of_Date_in_Word]. This displays the words “As of” followed by the date spelled 

out in words (as in “March 31, 2012”). You can enter your own text in either Subtitle 1 or 

Subtitle 2, and you can use the following variables to dynamically include the date either 

spelled out in words or numerically. 

• 
[As_of_Date_in_Word] 

• 
[As_of_Date]

Title comment (displayed in PDF, HTML, Excel): Enter an optional comment that will display 

aligned left, above the report body. 

• 
Company title: Display departments/locations as company title in individual reports 

(displayed in PDF). By default, your company name (as entered on the Company 

information page) is displayed at the top of the page header of printed reports and reports 

exported to Excel. However, if you’re splitting a report that compares data by department or 

location into multiple individual reports, you can choose to display the department or

Page Footer 

You can enter your own footer text (400 character maximum), select the footer alignment, decide 

whether the footer should appear on all pages of the report, and add borders around the header 

and column header 1. In addition, you can automatically display the page number, date, and time 

in the footer. 

• 
Footer text (displayed in PDF, Excel): Enter the text to include in the footer, up to 400 

characters. 

• 
Align footer (displayed in PDF, Excel): The footer information that you select appears in 

both PDF and Excel output. In Excel output, the footer is always left-aligned. 

• 
Include footer text on all page (displayed in PDF, Excel): By default, the items you selected 

for the footer (page number, date, and time) and entered in the footer text field appear on 

all pages of the report. Clear this check box if you want these items to appear only on the 

first page. 

• 
Include page number (displayed in PDF, Excel): Include page numbers in the report footer. 

• 
Include report date (displayed in PDF, Excel): Include the date that the report was run in the 

footer. 

• 
Include report time (displayed in PDF, Excel): Include the time that the report was run in the 

footer. 

• 
Add border around header (displayed in PDF, Excel): Add a border around the header. 

• 
Add border around column header 1 (displayed in PDF, Excel): Add a border around the 

column header 1. 

• 
Default header height XX points (displayed in PDF, Excel): Enter a numeric value for the 

height of the header. 

If your company is linked to an outside firm (such as your CPA), that firm can add a footer to your 
financials. For example, the footer might say, “For Management Use Only.” You can’t alter or 
remove this footer as long as your companies are linked. However, the external company can 
change the footer.

Selecting Fonts 

The options in the Fonts section let you specify the combinations of font, size, color, and style 

(that is, italics and bold) you want for specific report elements. Your font selections are used for all 

output formats (HTML, PDF, and Excel), with the exception of font color, which applies only to PDF 

output. 

In the Fonts section, you can choose the fonts for: 

• 
Page header information (report title, company name, subtitle 1, and subtitle 2) 

• 
Column headings 

• 
Row headings, with separate settings for the main Headings and Totals and another for 

Subgroups and Totals 

• 
Body text (detail rows, such as those listing individual accounts) 

• 
Page footer information (page number, date, time, and footer text) 

The font size you select for column headings applies to column headings 1 and 2. The column title 
(typically, the column type such as “Actual ”) appears two points smaller than the font size you 
select. 

Other text not specified above uses the same font as the body text. For example, fonts for account 

names are the same as that for body text.

#### Setting Other Options
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 435*

Chapter 4: Working with Financial Reports

Setting Other Options 

Page Settings 

By default, your report is set up to print in Portrait orientation on letter-size paper. The system 

will determine where columns break across pages, and the report may be more than one page 

wide. However, you can choose other options that allow you to control how the report prints 

across pages. 

The choices you make in the Page settings section determine how much control you have over the 

printed page. 

• 
Default page settings: This is the default setting. If you select this option, column size and 

breaks are determined automatically. However, you can change the report from Portrait 

orientation to Landscape to fit more columns across the page. 

• 
Fit to x page(s) wide: Select this option if you want to specify how many pages wide the 

report should be (for example, fitting it to one page wide), but still have the column width 

set automatically. 

• 
Page orientation: By default, pages are set to Portrait. Select Landscape from the 

drop-down list to change the orientation of the report pages. 

• 
Measurements: If you select Custom page size you can choose to see the measurements 

for margins and column widths as points or inches. 

• 
Custom page size, column widths, and column breaks: Select this option if you want more 

control over the printed report, including the ability to select a different page size, set 

column widths, and set the page margins. 

---

Column Options and Fonts 

You can use the Column options, breaks, and fonts section to control the look of particular 

columns on reports. Available options depend on your page settings selection. Some options 

apply only when the report is output as a PDF. 

• 
Hide filter details on column titles: Hide the details of filtered columns, such as the account 

group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to all 

outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to preset the column data without showing 

all details on the report presentation of column header. to hide column filter such as 

account group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to 

all outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to pre-set the column data without 

showing all details on the report presentation of column header. 

• 
Repeat segment name/ID as 1st column on reports more than 1 page wide: When a report 

is more than one page wide, enable this feature to ensure that the first column is repeated 

on each page, making it easier to follow the column information. 

The following lists the available column options: 

• 
Width (PDF only): Width of the column on printed (PDF) reports. Not available if you chose 

the Default page settings option. 

By default, the margins and column widths are specified in points, but you can use the 

Measurement drop-down list in the Page settings section to switch to inches. 

• 
Break (PDF only): Places a page break after the selected column on printed (PDF) reports. 

Available only if you chose Custom page size, column widths, and column breaks. 

• 
Font type, Font size: Changes the font type and size for the selected column. 

• 
Color (PDF only): Changes the color of the selected column on printed (PDF) reports only. 

• 
Bold, Italic: Makes the text in the selected column bold or italic.

#### Controlling Rows and Total Lines in Printed Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 440*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Controlling Rows and Total Lines in Printed Reports 

To find these options, go to the Format tab of the Financial Report Writer and click the Rows and 

Totals section at the top of the page. 

From this section, you can control how rows and total lines appear in printed reports. 

Section Headings 

Use the Row formatting options to determine how headings should be displayed in printed 

reports. 

The following lists the available options: 

• 
Hide heading: Omits the section heading 

• 
Center heading (print only): Centers the section heading across the report 

• 
Blank lines above (print only): Inserts empty rows before the section heading 

• 
Page break after (print only): Inserts a page break after the total for the section 

Total Lines 

Using the Total formatting options, you can control how the total line appears or hide the total 

line altogether. 

The following lists the available options: 

• 
Hide totals: Hides the total title and amount line. To suppress the totals for all lines, click the 

All link at the top of the column. 

• 
Blank space above: Lets you insert up to nine blank lines before the line that contains the 

total. 

• 
Hide separator above totals: Hides the separator that appears above the line that contains 

the total. 

• 
Underline totals: Controls whether the total is underlined, and how many underlines are 

displayed. 

By default, account groups are underlined as follows: 

• 
Top-level account groups: Double underline 

• 
One level down: Single underline 

• 
Other levels: No underline

### Format Tab FAQs
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 442*

Working with Financial Reports 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Format Tab FAQs 

How do I control the width of the report? 

The width of the report is affected by the number of columns in the report, and the font sizes you 

selected. If you want to control how many pages wide your report is, you can have the system fit 

the report to a certain number of pages wide, or you can use column breaks to select how many 

columns are on each page. You can also fit more columns on a page by switching to landscape 

orientation. 

To control the width of the report, perform one of the following options: 

Fit the report to one page wide (or a selected number of pages). 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, select the Fit to x pages wide option. 

2. 
Specify how many pages wide the report should be. 

Select where page breaks fall. 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, set the custom page size, column breaks, margins, and column 

specific fonts. 

2. 
In the Column Options, Breaks, and Fonts section, locate the column after which you want 

the first column break. Any remaining columns will appear on the next page. 

If your report is more than two pages wide, set additional column breaks as needed. 

Set page orientation to landscape. 

• 
In the Page Settings section, select the Landscape option as the page orientation. 

How do I control page breaks? 

You can control where page breaks are in the report by inserting a page break at the end of a 

certain section. 

To insert a page break after a specific section: 

1. 
Go to the Rows section of the Format tab. 

2. 
Locate the section after which you want a page break. For example, if you want a page 

break after your Fixed Assets group, locate the row for that group. 

3. 
In the Row formatting column, select the check box for Page Break After.

#### Assigning Report Access
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 443*

Chapter 4: Working with Financial Reports

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Permissions Tab 

The Permissions tab identifies the report owner and specifies who can and can’t access this 

report. Users who don’t have access to a report won’t see it in the Financial reports list page, and 

it won’t appear in their Reports Center or dashboards. 

Assigning Report Access 

Depending on how your General Ledger was set up, the default permissions to financial reports 

may either grant or deny access to all users (the group called Group/Everyone). For example, if 

the default access privileges for financial reports are set up to deny access, you can selectively 

give access to users or user groups by adding them to the Access list. 

When a user or group is added to the Access list, even though the Exclusion list is set to 

Group/Everyone, the Access list takes precedence and any user or group specifically included in 

the Access list is granted access to the report. 

If access is granted to Group/Everyone but one user is added to the Exclusion list (even if that 

user is part of a group given access), that user can’t access the report. 

To set the report owner and permissions: 

1. 
If necessary, select the person who is responsible for the report as Report owner. 

By default, the person who creates the report is the report owner. However, if the report will 

be maintained by someone else, you can select that user from the list. 

2. 
Set permissions for the report by reviewing the Access list and Exclusion list. 

• 
To add a user or user group to either list, click the Add button. 

• 
To remove a user or user group from either list, select the user or group and click the 

Remove button. 

In addition to adding individual users, you can select groups of users. Learn more about adding 

user groups.

Next Steps Tab 

When you’ve finished designing your report, it’s time to start using it. 

Although you can always run your report by going to the Financial reports list page or by going 

to the Reports Center, you can do more to highlight and use your report. 

Adding a Report to a Dashboard 

Dashboards give you an at-a-glance view of the areas of your business that matter most to you. 

From the Next steps tab, you quickly add your financial report as a component on any dashboard 

that you own. 

To use the Next steps tab to add the financial report to a dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Add this report to a dashboard link. 

2. 
Select the dashboard, give it a name and location, and enter other details as needed. 

Learn more about the options for report components. 

If you see a message that you don’t have any dashboards that you can add components to, but 
you know that you have dashboards, you probably aren’t the owner of those dashboards. In this 
case, you can still edit the dashboard from the Dashboards list and then add the component. 

Can I add this report to someone else’s dashboard? 

Yes, you can add this report to any dashboard that you can see on the Dashboards list, provided 

that you have permissions to edit dashboards. However, if you’re not the owner of the dashboard, 

you’ll need access the dashboard from the Dashboards list to add the component. 

Learn more about adding a component to a dashboard. 

Scheduling a Report 

You can schedule a report to run automatically on a recurring basis, such as weekly or monthly. 

When you schedule the report, you can set it up to be delivered by email or stored. 

To schedule a report from the Financial Report Writer: 

1. 
On the Next steps tab, click Schedule this report to run periodically. 

2. 
When prompted, click the Save and schedule button to save the report and proceed. 

3. 
On the Schedule financial report page, set up a schedule for the report and select how you 

want it to be delivered. 

Learn more about the options for scheduling a report (on page 236). 

In addition to having the report emailed to you, you can also have it stored. Learn how to access 

stored reports in the Reports Center (on page 228).

A report group provides an efficient and quick way to act upon multiple reports simultaneously. 

For example, instead of having to run or schedule a set of reports one at a time, you can run a 

report group, which runs all member reports immediately or according to schedule. 

To include the report in a report group:

On the Next steps tab, click Include this report in a report group. 

2. 
When prompted, click the Save and continue button to save the report and proceed to the 

Report groups list page. 

• 
To add the report to an existing report group, click the Edit link for the report group. 

Then add the report as a member. 

• 
If you don’t have any report groups, you can add one from the Report groups list. 


> **Navigation Path:** `You can access your report groups later on by going to Reports > Setup > More > Report`


Groups.

.

or download (on page 554 ) the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide
.

#### Configuring Financial Reports for Use in Site View
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 465*

Chapter 4: Working with Financial Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Configuring Financial Reports for Use in Site View 

There are four requirements for making a report available in Site View.  

1. Assign Permissions 

• 
Enable the Financial Report in Site View permission for any user who needs to be able 

to run and view financial reports from Site View. 

• 
Assign the General Ledger and Trial Balance report permissions to any site view user 

who needs to be able to run those two reports. 

2. Access Control (Set up prompts for filters) 

Financial Suite access and exclusion rules do not apply to the Spend Management Site 

Experience (Site View). To ensure that users can access only information to which they are 

entitled, make sure that the financial report prompts for the property or location when the 

financial report is available in site view. This step is included in the Making a Financial 

Report Available in Site View (on page 456) topic. 

3. Account Group 

Financial reports that you configure for use in site view must use the Site View Financial 

Accounts account group. Be sure to add any necessary account groups as members of this 

account group to collect the report information that the report requires based on your 

business needs. By default, this group includes ISC – Income and ISC – Expenses groups but 

you can add, remove, or change them.  

This rule also applies to the General Ledger and Trial Balance reports. 

4. Show in site view setting (Financial Reports only) 

Set the Show in site view setting to make a financial report available in Site View. For 

instructions, see Making a Financial Report Available in Site View (on page 456). 

Running Financial Reports in Site View 

When you run a financial report in the Site View, the way a financial report is configured in 

RealPage Accounting determines the filters that Site View users need to define when 

running the financial report. For example, a report is likely to require the Reporting period 

and As of Date, and the Property.  

Viewing Stored Reports 

Financial reports that are stored appear in the My Stored Reports tab. You can view (on page 

228) and download any of the stored reports.

When your company is set up, you also get a library of financial graphs that you can use right 

away. In the System financial graphs list, you’ll find a set of graph templates that you can run 

as-is or install and configure to suit more specific requirements. 

The graphs in your library are designed to work with your company out of the box. By creating an 
association between G/L accounts and system -defined categories, your accounts are 
automatically assigned to account groups that are used in the graphs.

on revenue, cash balances, and profit/loss.

In the Financial graphs list, click the Graphs library button.

The Save financial graph as box opens.

Financial graphs list where you are free to run the graph or customize it to suit your needs. 

You can also run a report directly from the System financial graphs list. This version of the report 

is always the original, unmodified version of the report. 

To run a graph from the graphs library: 

1. 
In the Financial graphs list, click the Graphs library button. 

The System financial graphs page opens. 

2. 
Click the View graph link on the row of the desired graph. 

3. 
Select the chart settings: 

• 
As of date: Select the date for which to run the chart. 

• 
Graph type: Select the graph type from the charts available in the list. Learn about the 

graph types (on page 477). 

• 
Legend: Select the desired position of the legend. 

• 
Reporting method: Select whether to use accrual or cash data for the chart. 

• 
Department: To filter the chart by department, select a department. 

• 
Location: To filter the chart by location, select a location. 

• 
Show Data Table check box 

• 
Swap Data Series check box 

4. 
Click the Refresh button to apply your selections.

Selecting Data for Financial Graphs

When you create a financial graph, your choices for data series represent how you want to 

categorize the data. For example, a revenue graph can be broken down in multiple ways, such as 

by quarter, location, or customer. 

Primary vs. Compare Data Series 

Think of the Primary data series as the main way you want to categorize values, such as by 

reporting period, account group, segment, or segment structure (waterfall charts only). 

For some types of graphs, you have the option of showing a comparison within the primary data 

series. A Compare data series is available for all chart types except pie, doughnut, and waterfall. 

---


<!-- Page 481 -->
Chapter 5: Financial Charts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Data Series Options 

The way that data are displayed depends on the graph type. 

• 
Account groups: Categorizes data by one or more account groups. Example: Revenue vs. 

expense. 

• 
Reporting periods: Categorizes data by one or more reporting periods. Example: Four 

consecutive quarters. Although you can select individual reporting periods by moving them 

from Available to Selected, the quickest way to create a trend over time is to use the Period 

comparison options. 

• 
Budget comparison: Lets you compare Actual values against one or more budgets. 

This option is not available for pie, doughnut, or waterfall graphs. 

• 
Dimension: Categorizes data by the selected dimension. By default, the graph shows all 

members of each dimension. However, you can filter on a dimension group to show a 

subset of members. For example, suppose that you choose Locations as a data series. 

• 
By default, the graph shows all locations. 

• 
To restrict the list of locations, expand the Filters section. From the Location 

drop-down list, select a dimension group that represents the locations you want to 

include. 

• 
Dimension structure: In waterfall charts, categorizes data based on the substructures in a 

hierarchical dimension structure. 

This option is available only for waterfall graphs. 

Selecting a dimension structure, rather than a dimension, gives you the freedom to create 
intermediate columns based on how you want to organize and label the data. 

---

Basic Options 

As of date 
Graph data is affected by the combination of reporting period and As of 

date. For example, Current Year with an As of date of 10/12/15 is the Year 

ending 12/31/15. 

• 
In most cases, you’ll want to leave the date blank to automatically 

use the current date, at the time the graph is displayed. 

• 
You can then override the date when the report is displayed view 

the same graph data at different time periods. 

Reporting book 
Applies if multiple reporting books are enabled for your company. 

• 
Accrual vs. cash: If you have dual-method accrual and cash 

accounting enabled in General Ledger Setup, you can choose 

whether to use accrual or cash data for the graph. 

• 
Other adjustment books: If you have compliance, tax, or 

user-defined books—you can include data from those books as 

well. Select Multiple books, and then click Reporting books. 

Display Options Section 

Rounding 
The default is No Rounding, which displays all amounts to the penny. 

Alternatively, you can simplify the numbers by choosing Dollars, 

Thousands, or Millions, which rounds all amounts to the nearest unit. 

Include period in 

header 

Applies to graphs that include reporting periods as a data series. When 

displaying reporting periods, includes the period interval in the name as in 

Month ending 03/31/21 rather than just 03/31/21. 

Hide zero numbers Removes data points that have no value, such as a column or pie chart 

segment that has a $0.00 balance. 

For example, suppose that you want to compare profitability for the 

previous quarter, but you have a lot of projects. With Hide Zero Numbers, 

the graph includes only projects that had a profit (either positive or 

negative) during the reporting period. 

Show currency or 

UOM 

Applies to graphs when the primary data series is Account groups, and all 

groups use the same currency or unit of measurement (UOM). Shows or 

hides the currency symbol or UOM on the graph. This option is selected 

by default. 

For example, for G/L account groups, show the currency symbol on the 

graph, or for computational account groups, the UOM is shown. 

For statistical account groups and categories, deselect this option to show 

no currency.

Financial Charts

Filters 

The Filters section of the General Ledger Graph page lets you refine data based on dimension, 

such as by location, department, customer, or vendor. Options appear for all dimensions that are 

enabled in your company. 

Filters Section 

Dimension 

(drop-down list) 

By default, graphs show data for all dimension members. For example, a 

revenue graph would show revenue from all locations and customers. 

• 
All members (such as All Locations): The default. 

• 
Specific member or group (such as Specific Location/Group): Lets 

you filter for a specific dimension member or a dimension group 

that represents multiple members. For example, you might filter for 

a Location group that contains all your US locations. 

• 
Type (such as Customer Type): Lets you filter for dimension 

members of a specific type. Applies only to dimensions that include 

“type” as an option—Customer and Vendor. 

• 
By product line (for Items): If you categorize items by product line, 

lets you filter for a particular product line. 

For data series that are based on a dimension, filtering for a dimension 
group enables you to control the data points in the graph. For example, 
suppose that you want to show revenue by location but don’t want to 
include all locations. To do this, filter for a location group that includes 
the locations you want to see on the graph. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Display 
Displays the filter when the graph is viewed (General Ledger > All >`


Financial statements > Financial graphs > View graph), so filtering can be 

changed on the fly. 

Include subs 
Includes data from subdimensions, such as child locations or child 

customers. 

Clear this check box if you don’t want to include children of the dimension. 

For example, if you are graphing revenue by customer and some 

customers have subsidiaries that you are tracking as child customers, you 

might want to clear the Include subs check box so that revenue 

calculations aren’t skewed by the subsidiaries.

A waterfall graph helps you understand how an initial value is impacted by a series of 

intermediate positive or negative values. 

A waterfall graph:

value.

led to the total. For example, the following waterfall chart shows the contribution to revenue 

from different account groups.

Use this page to see a list of graphs created at the console level. 

Administrators that create companies from a console can add graphs to this list. This enables 

them to create a graph once and install it in any number of individual companies. 

Console financial graphs can be: 

•

• 
Installed into a company’s Financial Graphs list, where they can be edited and viewed like 

any other graph. 

The graphs in the Console Financial Graphs list are designed to work with your company

Customizing Standard Reports and Charts 

The Customize button appears after you click the View button to run the report or create the 

chart. 

Click the Customize button to return to the report’s parameters page, where you can change the 

settings for dates, filters, format, and titles. 

Each report and chart have a unique set of parameters. Refer to the report or chart type for 

information about customizing that specific report. 

Memorizing Standard Reports and Charts Parameters 

To memorize a standard report’s or chart’s parameters: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select the application, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select the report or chart that you want to customize and then memorize. The 

customization page opens. 

3. 
Customize the report or chart the way you want the system to run it in the future. 

4. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize report parameters box opens. 

5. 
In the Name field, fill in the name of the report or chart. 

6. 
In the Description field, type a description of the report or chart to remind you about its 

specific parameters. Make sure that your description distinguishes it from other memorized 

reports or charts. 

7. 
Select the Public check box to make the memorized parameters available to other system 

users. 

8. 
Click the OK button. The system adds the memorized parameters to the Memorized reports 

list.

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report page opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report page opens.

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups (on page 409), then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or 

more G/L account groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use.

<!-- Page 504 -->
Working with Charts 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save.

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

You can process and store the report or chart either before or after viewing it. 

Emailing Standard Reports and Charts 

The Email option is available after running the report. 

To email a report or a chart: 

1. 
Click the Email button. The Email report box opens. 

2. 
In the To field, type the email address of the person to whom you want to send the report. 

To enter multiple addresses, separate each address with a comma (,) or semi-colon (;). 

3. 
Click the CC me check box if you want the system to send an email to your Inbox. 

4. 
In the Subject field, type the text that you want to appear in the subject line of the email 

message. 

5. 
In the Message field, type a message to the recipient. The system completes the signature 

line and fills the From field with your email address. 

6. 
Click OK.

### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 512*



#### Assigning Permissions for a New Feature
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 512*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

Assigning Permissions for a New Feature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Subscriptions > Permissions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > Permissions`


When RealPage adds a new feature, it often comes with new permissions that you must enable 

before users can use the new feature. 

To add permissions for a new feature: 

• 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

---


<!-- Page 513 -->
Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

If using Role-based permissions 

1. 
Select Roles. 

2. 
Find the role that you want to change. 

3. 
Click the Subscriptions link.  

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions window opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions. 

Be sure to check the Reports section at the bottom of the permissions page for any new 
reports that have been added to support the new feature. 

6. 
Click the Save button on the application’s permissions page. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the Roles subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list. 

If using User-based permissions 

1. 
Select Users. 

2. 
Locate the user who needs to be able to use the new feature.  

3. 
Select the Subscriptions link. 

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions page opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions.  

Be sure to check the Reports section at the bottom of the permissions page for related 
reports. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the User application subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list. 

---

#### Adding A/P Allocation Templates
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 517*

Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Adding A/P Allocation Templates 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > 
 Templates`


A/P allocation templates allow you to tell the system how to distribute costs amongst properties 

when applied to an A/P Invoice entry. A/P allocation template provides the ability to enter line 

items on A/P invoices faster using preset lists of properties (property groups). 

To add an A/P allocation template: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add next to Templates. The Templates page opens. 

3. 
In Name, type a name for the allocation template. 

Suppose you have four offices, and you divide rental income proportionately to square 
footage, but you divide interest income equally. You create an allocation for each set of 
allocation types. Your IDs might be RENT and INTEREST along with corresponding 
descriptions. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description for the allocation to help users identify which 

allocation to use. 

5. 
In the Template type drop-down list, select Percent or Amount. 

Percent: Select this type to allocate a percentage of the A/P invoice to multiple properties. 

Amount: Select this type to allocate a specific amount to multiple properties. 

6. 
In the Memo field, type a memo that describes this allocation.  

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active to allow users to select this allocation template. 

Select Inactive to prevent users from being able to select this allocation template. It will not 

appear in selection lists. 

Select Inactive to hide unused items. When set to Inactive, the system retains the data 
but hides the inactive item on lists, drop-down lists, and so on. If you want to permanently 
remove an allocation template, you must delete it. 

If you selected Percent, the Template list contains these columns: Property, Account,

groups. You can also use a constant number as part of the calculation. Display the amount result

Additional Rules for Department and Location 

Calculations are based on the combination of account, department, and location. In other 

words, if you specify the account 6020 Freight, the department Operations and the location 

California, the calculations are based on numbers only for that account and department 

combination that is also located in California.  

All children of parent departments and locations are included in the calculations. You might 

want to budget at the child level, and not budget at the parent level, for example. This 

enables you to track costs and revenues to budget, at a very detailed level. For this reason, 

we recommend that you plan your budget before you begin entering, such as preparing 

your budget first on a separate piece of paper or Excel spreadsheet, for faster entry into the 

system.  

5.

have the segments feature enabled (on page 547 ).

date.

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime (on page 409 ). 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand. 

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  

By default, you can choose from cloud-storage targets that either you ’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all cloud 
targets. 

5. 
If you want to override the default path where the report is delivered in the cloud-storage 

target, then type a different path in the Path field. 

6. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 

If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, 
then the Location ID and Name is added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for.

### Reporting Account Sets Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 529*

Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Reporting Account Sets Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reporting Accounts`


The reporting accounts feature is an optional feature in the General Ledger that enables you to 

generate and display reports using an alternate set of accounts instead of the standard G/L chart 

of accounts. Think of each reporting account set as a separate chart of accounts that you want to 

report on.  

For example, you might define a reporting account set for a part owner named Davis Associates 

who has 70 accounts.  

Use reporting accounts to: 

• 
Define reporting account sets that represent alternate charts of accounts. Within each 

account set, you define reporting accounts and how they map to your General Ledger 

accounts. 

• 
Let yourself or others display reports using an alternate reporting account set. The option to 

select a reporting account set is available for all financial reports and some standard reports. 

• 
All existing financial reports and some standard reports can take advantage of this new 

feature without any additional setup or changes to the report. You don’t need to create 

additional reports. 

• 
Navigate from financial reports to the transaction page using reporting accounts. 

• 
(Optionally) Set a default reporting account set for users who log into your company. 

Every reporting account set is a separate chart of accounts, each of which has a unique name and 

list of reporting Accounts. For example, you might define a reporting account set for a part owner 

named Investor A who has 150 accounts. The ability to select a reporting account set is available 

for all financial reports and for selected standard reports. 

In a multi-entity environment, you must configure reporting accounts at the top level. From the 
top level, follow the instructions for enabling the feature, creating reporting account sets, 
setting up permissions, and mapping reporting accounts to G/L accounts. 
You can use reporting account sets that you define at the top level when running reports at the 
entity level.

Thresholds

variance appear. 

• 
Select the Allow a range for order to Accounts Payable invoice variance check box. 

This lets you set a variance range above or below the budgeted purchase order (PO) 

amount for the accounts payable (A/P) invoice to pass through the system without 

being flagged for approval. 

2. 
Choose whether to set the threshold at a certain Percentage or a fixed dollar Amount, and 

then type the data in the numeric field. 

3. 
To skip any invoice approval requirements if the purchase order amount is within tolerance, 

select the Bypass invoice approval if within PO/SO tolerance check box. Additional 

approval requirement settings appear: 

• 
Select the If outside of PO/SO tolerance do not allow match option to restrict a 

purchase order or service contract outside of tolerance from matching to the order. 

• 
Select the If outside of PO/SO tolerance allow match and send for approvals option 

to allow a purchase order or service contract outside of tolerance to be submitted and 

processed via the approval workflow.

### Journal Entry Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 537*

Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Journal Entry Approvals 

Journal entry (JE) approvals are specific to G/L transactions that are directly posted to a specific 

journal. Transactions that aren’t submitted directly, for example, transactions submitted to a 

subledger, aren’t approved this way. 

Journal entry approval is optional; you don’t need to require approvals for journal entries. If you 

configure a journal for approvals, every submission to post a journal entry will require approval. 

Of course, entries that are directly entered by users require approval, but approvals also affect 

journal entries from: 

• 
Recurring transactions 

• 
Memorized transactions 

• 
Transaction templates 

• 
CSV imports 

• 
Web services

### Introduction to Custom Views
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 538*

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide

Introduction to Custom Views 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Custom Views`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > [application] > All > Custom Views`


The way a list is arranged, filtered, and sorted is called a view. RealPage Accounting provides 

standard views for displaying list items or recently viewed or modified list items. In addition, you 

can create custom views to display list items the way you need to see them. 

The Custom views submenu appears in an application’s menu when someone has created a 

custom view for a list in the application. 

After you create a custom view, the system adds it to the Custom views submenu in most main 

applications: 

• 
Company 

• 
Cash Management 

• 
General Ledger 

• 
Accounts Payable 

• 
Accounts Receivable 

• 
Property Management (RealPage Commercial Property Management only) 

Exceptions 

• 
Dashboards: Custom views of the dashboard list appear on the Custom views submenu of 

the Company application. 

• 
Reports: Custom views of financial reports and graphs are available only in the Financial 

reports list and the Financial graphs list. They do not appear in the Reports menu in a 

Custom Views submenu. 

Custom Views and Exporting 

When you’ve mastered creating and deploying custom views, you may find them useful when 

exporting lists. When you export a list, the system includes the information in the current view. 

You can use views to include additional fields or exclude information as needed.

### About Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 545*

Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

About Dimensions 

A dimension is a category of data that you can organize and sort in meaningful ways. RealPage 

Accounting provides the following pre-defined dimensions: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

In addition, RealPage Accounting enables you to define new dimensions to suit your needs. These 

user-defined dimensions enable you to organize and sort categories of data unique to your 

business. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, you might create 

a user-defined dimension called Line of business. The values you could add are Direct customers, 

Channel partner, and OEM. 

Dimensions enable you to collect, sort, analyze, and report on data within one category, or 

between categories, so you can identify key factors such as: 

• 
Your most profitable or most costly customers. 

• 
The return on investment of a location or department. 

• 
Whether and to what degree a new product or product line is successful. 

• 
Which way a particular aspect of your business is trending. 

RealPage Accounting dimensions give you fine control over data definition and data hierarchy. 

With dimensions, you can customize financial reports around specific business activities, get 

greater visibility into how the business is doing, and make faster, more meaningful business 

decisions. 

Additional fees may apply for user-defined dimensions. Contact your RealPage account 

representative for more information. 

---

Dimension Report Structures 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Structures`


Dimension report structures provide a flexible way for you to organize dimension data that you 

want to see on the rows or columns of a financial report. For example, instead of showing all 

locations on a report, you might want to select a Location structure that is named for a particular 

region and includes a subset of locations. 

You can add any number of structures for the dimensions you track. 

The list of standard dimension structures may include: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

If you have additional dimension structures listed in the Dimension structure submenu, they are 

custom structures and are not discussed in this document. 

Creating a dimension structure from a group enables you to add the group to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. 

A dimension structure can only be used for filtering reports if you don’t select the Dimension 

Structure check box when you are creating a dimension group. 

Viewing the Available Dimension Report Structures 

Select a dimension structure option to view the available report structures. 

See also Dimension analysis in financial reports (on page 278) and Dimension structures for 

financial reports.

#### Multi-Entity Report Structures
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 554*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Multi-Entity Report Structures 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Subscriptions`


Multi-Entity Shared > Multi-Entity Report Structures 

You can create report structures both at the top level and at the entity level of a multi-entity 

shared company. 

In practice, many companies create and manage the majority of account groups and dimension 

structures at the top level of the company. These report structures are then automatically shared 

by all entities, and available for use in financial reports, graphs, and performance cards. 

Best Practices 

To determine whether to create a report structure at the top level or entity level, consider who 

needs to access the structure. 

• 
If a report structure should be available to all entities, create it at the top level. Account 

groups and dimension structures created at the top level automatically appear in the 

corresponding lists in each entity. 

Report structures created at the top level can be edited only at the top level. 

• 
If an entity has particular reporting needs, users can create report structures at the entity 

level. These report structures can then be used within that entity, along with any report 

structures that were inherited from the top level. 

When a user switches to an entity, the user can’t see report structures that were created 
in another entity. 

Top-Level Report Structures 

From the top level of a multi-entity shared company, you can edit and use all reporting structures, 

including those created at the entity level. 

• 
By default, lists initially display only report structures that were created at the top level. 

• 
Click the Include private check box at the top of the list to see report structures that were 

created in an entity. You can edit and use these report structures provided that you have 

access to the entities in which they were created. 

• 
You can Add new top-level report structures and Edit existing structures that were created 

at either the top level or entity level. 

---


<!-- Page 555 -->
Chapter 7: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Include Private Does Not Appear on Your Page 

The most common reason that you don’t see this feature is because you’re using a custom view. 

When you select a custom view, some options are hidden. Depending on the page you’re on, the 

Include inactive, Include one-time, Include private, and Display hierarchy options aren’t visible. 

For example, if you’re viewing from a custom view, the Financial reports list won’t provide the 

Include inactive option. 

To see the options again, switch back to View all. See Custom Views (on page 528) for more 

information. 

Entity-Level Report Structures 

When you switch to an entity, you can use report structures that were created at the top level, 

plus any report structures that were created in that entity. 

• 
You can add new report structures and edit existing structures that were created at the 

entity level. 

• 
View (but not edit) report structures that were inherited from the top level. You’ll recognize 

these by the Not owned status. This means that the entity can use these report structures, 

but they can be edited only at the top level.

### Segments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 556*

Segments Overview 

Segments are custom classifications that help you organize, sort, and report on your company 

information in meaningful ways. Think of a segment as a tag with a set of values that you can 

associate with transactions and G/L entries. For example, you might add a custom segment to 

report on your expense types, employees, or special projects. 

When you enter a new transaction, you can assign a segment to that transaction and then tag it 

with one or more segment values. Segmenting transactions is optional; however, it can be useful 

for identifying transactions and analyzing data in your reports. 

You can define up to 15 segments for your company. An additional segment, called 

Intercompany segment, is available by default. Because it’s a system segment, it cannot be 

modified. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add and manage segments. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Segments 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 502) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 502) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Enable Segments 

Before you can use segments, you must enable the segments feature in the General Ledger. See 

Enabling Segments (on page 547).

#### How to Read Paths
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 565*

Chapter 8: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

---


<!-- Page 566 -->
Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record. 

---


<!-- Page 567 -->
Chapter 8: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

#### Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 568*

Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view. 

---



##### Fields
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 569*



##### Buttons
*Source: `RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 569*

Chapter 8: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide 

Fields 

Audit Trail Columns 

Date 
This is the date and time of the change to the record, presented in the time zone 

defined in your preferences. 

Action 
This column indicates the type of update made to the record (whether it was 

created, modified, or deleted). It also indicates whether the system performed the 

action as part of a workflow, or if a user performed the action. 

Completed by This is the ID of the user who made the change. 

If the transaction is an eInvoice or oInvoice, the audit trail displays 

realpageaccounting as the user who submitted the transaction. This is because 
eInvoices and oInvoices are created electronically, either by the vendor through 
Storefront or through Invoice Processing. 

The system previously designated CPAUser as the user who submitted 
electronic invoices. 

Source 
This is the source from which the record was accessed or changed. 

Field 
This is the name of the field that was changed. 

Before 
This is the data that appeared in the field before the user saved the change. 

After 
This is the changed data that appears in the field after the user saved the change. 

Buttons 

Audit Trail Box/Audit Trail Page 

Done 
Saves any changes and opens the previous page 

Help 
Opens the Online Help page 

More actions 
Opens a drop-down list with the following options: 

• 
Export to CSV: Downloads the report as a CSV file 

• 
Export to Excel: Downloads the report as an XLS file 

• 
Export to PDF: Downloads the report as a PDF file 

• 
Table size: Allows you to select the number of rows you want to 

display per application page
