About the General Ledger Application

Use the General Ledger to create and manage accounts and
account groups, create journals and journal entries, approve
journal entries, run trial balance and general ledger reports,
open and close books, and create reporting accounts and
statistical accounts.
Use the Company application to subscribe to the General
ledger application.
Configure the General ledger and its features on the General
ledger Setup tab's Configuration command.

Create a Journal Entry

Add a journal entry to record transaction information.

1. In General Ledger, click 
 next to Journal entry.
2. Fill in the top section.
3. Fill in the Entries section.
4. Click Submit.

Debits and Credits must match to post.

View Transactions for a Journal

1. In General Ledger, select Journal Entry.
2. Find the journal to open.
3. Click the View Transactions link.

Create an Adjusting Journal Entry

Add an adjusting journal entry.

1. Open General Ledger, select Adjusting entry and then click
 next to Adjusting journal.
2. Select the Journal to which to add the entry.
3. Select the Posting date.
4. Type a Description.
5. Enter Entries.
6. Click Submit.

Create a Recurring Journal Entry

Schedule journal entries.

1. In General Ledger, select 
 next to Recurring Journal
Entries.
2. Set up the Schedules.
3. Select Transaction information.
4. Fill in the Entries information.
5. Click Save.

Create a Memorized Transaction

Create a template for Journals that can be manually posted at
any time.

1. Open the General Ledger menu, and then select Journal
Entry.
2. Select Memorized Transactions.
3. Select Header information.
4. Enter Entries information.
5. Click Save.
6. Post a memorized journal by finding the journal entry to be
reversed and clicking the check box next to the desired journals.
7. Click Post.

Create a Transaction Template

1. On the General Ledger menu, select the Setup tab, and then
click 
 next to Transaction templates.
2. In the Template ID field, type a unique identifier for the
template.
3. In the Journal drop-down list, select a journal where you want
to record the resulting transactions.
4. In the Offset account drop-down list, select the offset account.
5. In the Default description field, type a description of the
intended purpose of the template.
6. Fill in the Entries section.
7. In the Account drop-down list, select the account.
8. In the Label field, type the text that identifies the transaction
type.
9. In the Treat as drop-down list, select how you want the system
to treat the transactions created with this template, as Debit or
Credit transactions.
10. In the Department drop-down list, select the desired
department.
11. In the Department show as drop-down list, select Read-only,
Editable, or Hidden.

▪
Select Read-only to display the department as static text.
▪
Select Editable to allow users to change the Department
record.
▪
Select Hidden to hide the department.

12. In the Location show as drop-down list:

▪
Select Read-only to display the location as static text.
▪
Select Editable to allow users to change the Location
record.
▪
Select Hidden to hide the location.

13. Click Save.

Post Using a Transaction Template

1. On the General Ledger menu, select the Setup tab, and then
select Transaction templates.
2. Find the transaction template that you want to post from and
click New.
3. Type the date to post.
4. In Entries, fill in the amounts of each line item to include in the
post.
5. Click Save. The transaction is posted to the G/L.

If the transaction does not balance, the system displays an error
message.

Approve a Journal Entry

1. Open the Company menu.
2. Click Approval Workbench.
3. Select Journal entry.
4. Find the journal entry that you want to review.
5. Click View.
6. Click Approve.

Reverse a Journal Entry

Reverse a journal entry.

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Journal Entry.
2. Find the journal by Title or Symbol and click the View
Transactions link.
3. Find the journal entry to be reversed and click Edit.

The Reverse link appears only if the transaction can be
reversed.

4. Click Reverse.
5. Enter a reversing date and memo.
6. Click Reverse.
7. Click Done.

Import Data into a Journal

Import transactions into a journal.

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Journal Entry.
2. Find the journal to which to add imported transactions.
3. Click Import Transactions.
4. Click Choose File and find the file with the transactions.
5. Click Import.

Create an Account

Add an account.

1. On the General Ledger menu, select 
 next to Accounts.
2. Type an Account Number.
3. Type a name for the account in Title.
4. Select an Account Type.
5. Select the Normal Balance.
6. Select the Period End Closing Type.
7. Fill in the rest of the account record as needed and click Save.

General Ledger accounts are shown on financial statements only if
they are included in an account group. Accounts can't be added
directly to a report.

Create an Account Group

1. On the General Ledger menu, select 
 next to Account
Groups.
2. Type a Name. The name of the account group determines how
it appears on lists.
3. Specify the basic information about the account group.
4. Define the group structure.
5. Add members to the group.
6. Add filters to the group. (optional)
7. Click Save.

Create a Statistical Account

Add a statistical account.

1. On the General Ledger menu, select 
 next to Statistical
Account.
2. Enter the account number.
3. Enter the Title as it should appear on reports.
4. In Report Type, choose how per-period amounts for the
account should be reported.
5. Fill in the rest of the Statistical Account record as needed, and
then click Save.

Add a Budget

1. On the General Ledger menu, select 
 next to Budgets.
2. Fill in the Budget ID and Description.
3. Select Create a new budget.
4. Add data to the budget by either entering budget amounts
manually or by importing budget data.

Importing Budget Data

1. Download the budget template.

2. Enter budget data into the spreadsheet and save it as a CSV
file.
3. Import the budget.

Add data to the budget information manually
Fill in budget data for your accounts one by one.

1. Click Add.
2. Select an account.
3. Select a reporting period in Periods to date.
4. Type budget data for your account.
5. Click Show periods.
6. Add budget figures for each reporting period manually or by
computing budget data.

Compute budget amounts for the reporting periods

1. Specify Grow by.
2. Select Percent or Amount and then enter the Compute
amount.
3. In the list, select the Reporting periods to compute.
4. Click Compute.
5. Click Save.

Enter budget amounts for the reporting periods

1. For each of the desired Reporting periods, fill in the End of
period/budget amount.
2. Click Save.

Create an Income Statement

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Financial Reports.
2. Find CUSTOM - Income Statement.
3. Click the desired format of the report, such as PDF.
4. Fill in the report prompts as needed.
5. In Location, select a location or location group.
6. Specify the As of Date.
7. Click OK.

Create a Financial Graph

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Financial graphs.
2. Find the desired financial graph.
3. Click View graph.
4. Fill in the prompts if any and click OK. The graph opens in a
new browser tab.

Create a Financial Report

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Financial Reports.
2. Find the desired financial report.
3. Click the desired format of the report, such as PDF.
4. Fill in the report prompts as needed.
5. In Location, select a location or location group.
6. Specify the As of Date.
7. Click OK.

Print a Financial Statement

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Financial reports.
2. Find the report to print.
3. Select the link for the desired download format: HTML, CSV,
PDF, or Excel.

Select PDF for the most printable format.

Open/Close the General Ledger

To open the books:

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Open Books.
2. Select Entity/Entity group.
3. Select the To the Beginning of Period to open the General
Ledger.
4. Select the boxes of subledgers to open, Accounts payable,
Accounts receivable, and Cash management.
5. Click Open Books.

To close the books:

1. On the General Ledger menu, select Close Books.
2. Select Entity/Entity group.
3. Select the To the End of Period to close the General Ledger.
4. Select the Generate KPIs check box if Key Performance
Indicators are enabled.
5. Select Generate Work Papers.
6. Click Close Books.

RealPage Accounting 5.0 Management Fees Quick Steps 

RealPage Accounting Management Fees Quick Steps Guide 
Doc ID [197970] 
9/5/2019 

About the Management Fees Quick Steps 

Use the Fees feature to set up recurring invoices for fees 
based on percentages, total units, occupied units, or 
specify a flat fee. After setting up a fee, you can post A/P 
invoices for properties and have the system create 
corresponding A/R invoices. 
Use the Company application to subscribe to the Accounts 
Payable application and then enable the fees feature in 
Accounts Payable’s Setup tab using the Configuration 
command. Create a fee in the Accounts Payable’s Setup 
tab with the Fee Template command. 

Add a Fee Template 

Define a fee’s type, schedule, and accounting options in the 
fee template.  

1. In Accounts Payable, select the Setup tab. 
2. Select 
 Fee Template. 
3. Type a Fee ID. 
4. Select the Location. 
5. In Accounting Option, select Generate A/P Invoice 
or Journal Entry. 
6. Select Expense account. 
7. Select the Vendor. To bill fees on behalf of an entity, 
select the vendor record that represents the billing 
entity. 
8. Select the Fee type and then fill in the details for the 
type.  
• If Percentage, type the desired percentage to 
charge. 
• If Flat fee, type the Flat Fee Amount. 
• If Total Units, in Unit amount, type the amount to 
bill per unit. In Unit count, type the total number of 
units in the complex. 
• If Occupied Units, in Unit amount, type the amount 
to bill per unit. 

Fill In the Schedule Fees tab 
If you selected Occupied units, skip to the A/R tab. 

1. Click Schedule fees. 
2. Select Auto Calculate or Auto Calculate and Post.  
3. Fill in the schedule information and then specify what to 
Auto calculate and when to Auto recalculate. 

Generate an A/R invoice for the paying property 
(optional) 

1. Select the A/R tab. 
2. If billing between entity and location, select Default 
company. Or select Override Company to specify a 
different company. 
3. If you selected Default Company, select the Location. 
4. Complete the rest of the company fields. 
5. Click Save. 

Calculate Percentage Fees 

1. In Accounts Payable, select the Setup tab. 
2. Select Fee Template. 
3. Find the fee with the Percentage fee type to calculate 
and then select the check box. 
4. Based on the date in Last posted info, determine the 
next period that needs to be calculated. 
• Select the Year. 
• Select the Period. 
5. Click Calculate. 
6. In the Calculation report box, review the data to 
ensure it is correct. 
7. Set the Posting date. 
8. Click Post. 

Delete a Fee 

You can delete a fee before posting it.  

1. In Accounts payable, select the All tab. 
2. Select Fees. 
3. Find the fee that you want to delete and click the 
Details list link.  
4. Select the check box of the fee to delete and then click 
the Delete button. 

View and Print the A/P Invoice of a Fee 

1. In Accounts payable, select the All tab. 
2. Select Fees. 
3. In the Fees list, find the fee of the A/P invoice you want 
to view. 
4. Click Details list. 
5. Find the specific fee and click the A/P invoice link. 
6. Click the View link.  
7. Click Print. 

Calculate Multiple Fees 

1. In Accounts payable, select the All tab. 
2. Select Fees.  
3. Select one or more fees of the same type. The fees 
must have been posted before. (See the Last Posted 
Info column.) 
4. Click the Calculate button. 
5. Choose a year and a period or a period range and the 
click the Calculate All button. 

Recalculate a Fee 

1. In Accounts payable, select the All tab. 
2. Select Fees.  
3. Select one of more fees of the same type. The fees 
must also show that they have been posted before. 
(Refer to the Last Posted Info column.) 
4. Select Calculate. 
5. Choose a year and a period or a period range. 
6. Click Calculate All.  
7. From the Fees list, click the Details list of the 
calculated fee.  
8. From the Fee details page, click the Recalculated link. 
9. Click 
 Expand to review the list of fees, especially 
the New charged amount and the Adjustments 
columns.  
10. If an adjustment is needed, click Recalculate. 
Otherwise, click Post recalculation.  

Unpost a Fee 

1. In Accounts payable, select the All tab. 
2. Select Fees.  
3. Find the fee to unpost. 
4. Click the Details list link.  
5. Click the Details link of the item that you want to 
unpost. 
6. Click the Unpost button. 

Rerun a Posted Fee 

1. In Accounts payable, select the All tab. 
2. Select Fees.  
3. Find the fee to rerun. 
4. Click the Details list link.  
5. Click the Details link of the desired item. 
6. Click Unpost. 
7. In the Fees list, find the location with the unposted fee 
and then click Details List. 
8. Find the fee with the Unposted status. 
9. Click Details. 
10. Click Recalculate. 
11. Click Post.

### Importing Workflow

*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 12*

Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite

Importing Workflow 

Importing data into RealPage Accounting requires these four main steps: 

1. 
Downloading an Import Template (on page 6) 

2. 
Filling In Import Templates with Your Data (on page 7) 

3. 
Saving the Template as a CSV File (on page 14) 

4. 
Importing the CSV File (on page 24) 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to import data from the Import Data page:  

Application 
Activities 
Permissions 

Company 
Import Data 
Run 

You must also have specific permissions for the type of object that you are importing. For 

example, if you are importing customer data, then you must have permissions to list, view, add, 

and edit customer data. For more information about the specific permissions that you need to 

complete an import, refer to the documentation for that specific object type. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

### Preparing Data to Be Imported
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 13*



#### Downloading Import Templates
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 13*

Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Preparing Data to Be Imported 

This section describes the steps to prepare your data for import and includes tips for best success. 

Downloading Import Templates 

Each object has a unique template that you must use for importing data. There are three ways 

you can find a template for your object type: 

• 
Download the template directly from a list. 

• 
Use the Download template link in the Import box. 

• 
Download the template from the Import data page. 

Downloading directly from a list 

• 
In some lists, such as the Working budgets list, the list has a Template button that you can 

click to download the template that you need. 

Downloading from an Import box 

• 
In other lists that have an Import button, click the Import button to open the Import box, 

where a Download template link appears next to the Choose File button. 

Downloading from the Import Data Page 

If you don’t find a download button in the list or a link in the Import box, then you can download 

the template file from the Import data page. See Download a Template from the Import Data 

Page (on page 6). 

---



#### Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 14*

Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of Performance 

Analytics is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
Find the type of data that you want to import.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

A prompt opens at the bottom of the web page, asking if you want to Open, Save, or 

Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your browser’s default download folder. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Save the template to your computer, and then continue downloading templates as needed until 

you have downloaded all of the templates for data that you want to import. 

If you have a database administrator (DBA) of your other system, give the downloaded templates 

to your DBA. Ask the DBA to: 

• 
Export the data from your other system, as specified in the import template spreadsheets. 

• 
Put the applicable data into each spreadsheet. 

• 
Save the spreadsheet as a comma-delimited file (CSV). 

If you do not have a DBA, or if your DBA does not have time to complete the whole task, you can 

complete the tasks. Refer to the following topics for guidance on creating importable data. 

---



#### Filling In an Import Template with Data
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 15*



#### About CSV Templates
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 15*

Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 14). 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.  

About CSV Templates 

There are some things you should know about the CSV templates and how they behave before 

adding your data. 

Removing All Commas from Your CSV File 

RealPage recommends removing all commas from your CSV file. 

A CSV file is a Comma Separated Values file (also sometimes known as a comma delimited file). If 

there are commas in the data of your file (for example, if your numbers are formatted like 10,000 

or if you use commas between words in a field), your data will be shifted one column over 

because that is how the file is intended to work. This will either cause errors in the information or 

cause the whole import to fail. 

RealPage recommends you do not keep your actual data in a CSV file. Instead, use an Excel 
workbook to take advantage of the formatting options of Excel. When you’re ready, export your 
data as a CSV file for import into Performance Analytics. In this way, your data is formatted 
correctly for import, but you also have Excel functionality in your workbook. 

Column Order 

You can change the order of the columns as you see fit, as long as the information in the header 

cell doesn’t change. 

---


<!-- Page 16 -->
Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Do not rename or otherwise change the headers in your templates. If you change the headers, 
your import will fail. 

However, some templates require information to be imported in a specific order. For example, 

transaction data should not be imported before information about the transactions has been 

imported. Header columns containing information about the entire import need to stay to the left 

of detail columns (columns that contain the details of an account, transaction, vendor, etc.). 

RealPage recommends reviewing the column order of the original template before moving 

columns around. 

Adding Additional Columns 

If you need to keep other related information in your template document, you can add your own 

columns for this information. If you add your own columns, use a # (hashtag) symbol before the 

name of any column you add. Examples: 

#BudgetNotes 

#ClientInfo 

If by chance you use a name already in use by the system, the # (hashtag) will make sure that the 

information in your columns is not imported by accident. 

You can also use the # (hashtag) to write notes to yourself in your template. If you place the # 

(hashtag) at the start of a row, the whole row of information is ignored during import. 

You can create rows of notes by starting the row with # in the first column. 

Hiding Columns for Easy Data Entry 

When editing your file in Excel, you can hide columns you won’t be using for data entry. 

Be sure to enter required information in your file. Hiding required columns and not entering 
required information will cause your import to fail. 

Data Must Conform to the Business Logic of RealPage 

For example, the Budget ID field on the Budget Information page allows a 20-character ID to be 

entered. It follows then that the Budget import template would have the same limitation: if you 

try to import a Budget ID with more than 20 characters in your CSV file, your import fails. 

How data should be formatted is found in the header description row, under the header row. 

You can also see a field-by-field description for your specific template in this help. 

Go to Importing Data (on page 25), find the template you want to know more about, and click the 

corresponding link. 

---


<!-- Page 17 -->
Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Blank Fields Overwrite Existing Data 

A blank value in a cell is considered to be the desired value (a blank) for the field referenced by 

the column heading for the record being imported. 

In almost all cases, a blank field will overwrite existing data in RealPage to also be blank. 

Say you had the existing value 111 Elm St. as the address for a customer and you import a blank 

for this field. If you go to the normal user interface and examine the contents of that field, you will 

see that the original value 111 Elm St. is replaced by nothing, and the field is blank. 

This is not true, however, for these templates: 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Transactions 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Opening Balances 

If the value is blank in certain fields, the import does not overwrite the existing value. To remove 

the existing value in these few cases, enter the value NULL. These cases are clearly identified in 

their header descriptions. 

Budgets are an exception. Budgets can be appended with new dates, with new lines not 
previously budgeted, or they can be overwritten if same date/account combinations are used. 

Calculated Field Values 

If you used a formula to come to a value in a field, you can leave the result in place as long as you 

match the RealPage field value for decimals. 

Accounting Application Page Help 

In most cases, there is an exact match between the application pages (and the business logic with 

which they behave) and the data that you import. This includes the constraints on that data and 

any dependencies that may exist between the data in the import file and other data in the system, 

or other data that you also import. 

After you have added all of your data, you save the Excel spreadsheet as a CSV file. 

Debits and Credits Must Balance 

When importing a file that includes debits and credits, your debits and credits must balance. 

RealPage adheres to accepted accounting rules, which require debits and credits to balance. 

Likewise, if you require accounts to balance by location, then when you import location balances 

using a CSV template, the location debits and credits must also balance. 

Duplicating Records 

If an identical record already exists in the system, the import for that record typically fails because 

RealPage detects that the record exists and does not allow duplicates. 

---


<!-- Page 18 -->
Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicates are not allowed in account numbers, departments, locations, employees, customers, 

and vendors. Although you can have duplicate transactions, the transaction summary name must 

be unique per application. 

Journal entries are an exception. The system does not check for duplicate journal entries, so 
when importing journal entries, be sure to check that they have a unique ID or name.

Line Numbers 

See the Line number examples (on page 17) page for more information on how to use lines 

numbers in your CSV imports. 

Special Characters 

UTF-8 is supported in imported files, so character accents and other special characters are 

imported correctly. 

RealPage recommends that you remove commas from all numbers and do not use commas in any 

text fields. 

CSV Data Exported from Non-Excel Software 

When exporting data from other applications, the other software might use a non-standard 

approach to quoting, which could cause problems when importing into the system. 

As noted above, RealPage recommends removing all commas from text fields in a CSV file. 

However, there could be times in which removing the commas is not the ideal solution. In this 

case, CSV files do allow quotes around a value that contains a comma, and the system accepts 

this in an import. For example: 

1,2,3, “All, with exceptions” 

There may also be instances when you need to include a quote mark inside a statement with a 

comma. In this case, you would use a second set of quote marks, as follows: 

1,2,3, “All, with “inventory” exceptions” 

---



#### Preparing Your CSV File for Import
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 19*

Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Preparing Your CSV File for Import 

The Import data page is a quick way to import your information into the system. However, the 

way you prepare your CSV files directly affects the success or failure of importing your data. Learn 

the CSV import process to streamline the import process. 

This topic provides general information about preparing CSV files for import. Links to information 
about specific templates can be found in the Import data into the system, which lists all import 
topics. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 

Most imports start with getting the most recent template from the Import data page. When you 

get your templates from this list, you get templates that have been tailored to your specific 

company, including specific dimensions. 

Next you add your data, using the correct formatting as explained in the template. After you’ve 

added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

Downloading a Template 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because: 

• 
Templates in the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage at any time, especially when a new version of 

Performance Analytics is released. This means that an older template might not work. 

To download an import template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. The Import data page opens with a list of information that you can 

import into the system. 

3. 
Decide on the type of information to upload, and then click the Template link associated 

with that information. 

---


<!-- Page 20 -->
Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Other Templates 

RealPage may have additional CSV import templates that are not found on the Import data page. 

Contact your RealPage Support Representative for any templates that have been customized for 

your company. 

Adding Your Data 

After you download the appropriate template, add your data. 

The following example shows a portion of a standard CSV file for importing accounts receivable 

invoices after it has been opened in Excel, but before data has been added. The top row is the 

header row, (the data labels for all of your data), and the second row contains descriptions of the 

kinds of data to enter in the column. 

a) Some fields are not required. 

b) Some fields are required. 

c) Header row 

d) Header description row 

Each template contains a set of pre-defined headers, such as BUDGET_ID, ACCT_NO, and soon. 

You enter your data into the blank cells below the header and header description rows without 

changing the headers. 

It is important to read the description for each of the column headers. Some columns are 
required and if left blank will cause your import to fail. 

---


<!-- Page 21 -->
Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

The following illustration shows a portion of the template after the data has been added. The 

description row has been hidden for this example. 

To add your data: 

1. 
Open the template that you downloaded from the Import data page. 

2. 
Enter your information. Use the header descriptions as a guide for how to enter information 

correctly. 

• 
Do not change the headers. 

The header titles in the header row correlate to fields in UI. Incorrect header titles will 

cause an import error. When you download a template, the correct headers are in the 

template. 

• 
Read the header descriptions. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with a value not accepted by the column, it will cause an error in your import. 

• 
Enter required information. 

Some data is required, while others are not. Read the description field to determine 

which information is required. If you do not enter the required information, your 

import will fail. 

3. 
After entering your data, save the file as a comma-separated value (CSV) file. When saving 

from Excel, select the comma delimited file type. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it. 

---



#### Saving the Template as a CSV File
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 22*

Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Saving the Template as a CSV File 

In Excel: 

1. 
Click File, and then select Save As. 

2. 
Click Browse and select where you want to save the file. 

3. 
In File name, type a name that represents the data that the template contains. 

4. 
In Save as type, select CSV (Comma delimited) (*.csv). 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Some transactions have Import buttons on their lists so that you can import the transactions 
without having to leave the list. You can use this method whenever you have already downloaded 
the template that you need, filled it with the appropriate data, and saved the file in CSV format.

### Best Practices
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 23*

Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Best Practices 

The following best practices will help you prepare your CSV file for upload.  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import Data option. The Import data page opens. This is the page where you can 

find the latest templates. 

3. 
Find the object that you want to import, and then click its Template link to download a 

template.  

• 
Use the latest template, especially following a product release.  

• 
Use the correct template for the area in which you want to upload information. 

Different templates organize different types of information. Use a template specifically 

for the information you need to upload.  

4. 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to entering information.  

• 
Do not change the titles in the header row.  

The header titles correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header titles will cause an 

upload error. When you download a template from the Import data page, the correct 

headers are in the template.  

• 
Read the header descriptions in the template.  

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with an incorrect accepted value, it will cause an error in your upload.  

• 
Enter required information.  

Read the description field to determine which information is required. If you do not 

include required information, your upload will fail.  

Save the file as a comma-separated value, or CSV, file. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it. Leave the file open until your import is successful. Excel can sometimes reformat 

the file if you close it before the import is successful.

Importing Data with Line Numbers 

Some types of data have line numbers, such as G/L journal entries.

#### Line Number Examples
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 25*

Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Line Number Examples 

When you import information into Performance Analytics that uses line numbers, such as journal 

entries, invoices, or adjustments, use the following tips to ensure that your line numbers import 

correctly. 

Journal Entry Line Numbers 

When importing general ledger journal entries (including statistical journal entries), the number of 

the line item in the CSV file defines the order in which those lines are imported. There are a few 

things you can do when entering journal entry information into the CSV file that will make 

reconciliation of the journal entries easier after import: 

• 
Group debits and corresponding credits together 

• 
Enter information in the CSV template as if you were entering it in a regular journal (group 

information in a reasonable manner) 

In the G/L journal entry example below, LINE_NO 1 and 2 are entries for legal and professional 

fees and are accounted for in the DEBIT column. The corresponding CREDIT for Accounts Payable 

in line 3 equals the fees; debits match the credits. 

In line 4, a DEBIT is entered for another legal fee, with the corresponding CREDIT in line 5. Again, 

debits match the credits. 

In this example, line items in the LINE_NO start at 1 and proceed sequentially. This example also 

groups related debits and credits together, so that reconciliation is easier. The LINE_NO column 

determines the order in which the line items are imported into the system and how they will 

appear in your journal entry. RealPage recommends entering information in the CSV file as if you 

are entering it in a real journal entry. This way, when you revisit the journal entry after import, 

your entries make sense. 

Exchange Rates in Journal Entries 

When uploading G/L journal entries, the exchange rate is not required. However, if you want to 

use your own exchange rate, you must add the exchange rate to the journal entry line. The journal 

entry line number is referenced by the system. Enter journal entry line numbers as described in 

Journal entry line numbers. Line numbers are important to ensure proper line-header consistency. 

If you don’t enter a line number, or enter line numbers out of sequence, the import will fail. 

---


<!-- Page 26 -->
Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you want to use the exchange rate provided by RealPage, leave the exchange rate column blank 

in the CSV file. 

Multiple Journal Entry, Invoice, or Adjustment Line Numbers 

When you enter multiple journal entries, invoices, or adjustments, you must start the line number 

count over at 1. 

When you enter a single journal entry, invoice, or adjustment into a CSV file, you start the 

LINE_NO column at one for the line entries and continue sequentially. Below is an example of a 

single invoice entered in a CSV file. 

Figure 1: An example of an invoice, with sequential line numbers. 

a) Total Due column 

b) The AMOUNT column adds up to the TOTAL_DUE. 

c) The line numbers start at 1 and continue in sequential order. 

When you enter multiple journal entries, invoices, or adjustments into a CSV file, there are several 

things you can do to ensure your information imports correctly into the system: 

• 
Group information in a reasonable manner. 

• 
When importing invoices, make sure that the AMOUNT column and the TOTAL_DUE column 

have the same amount for each entry. 

• 
LINE_NO refers to the line item number, so when entering formation into the CSV file, start 

the LINE_NO at 1, and then list each following line item in sequential order. 

In the example below, you can see the first line item entry of a customer invoice has been marked 

as line 1 in the LINE_NO column. This invoice has line items entered in sequential order, and the 

AMOUNT column for the first invoice (in orange) and the TOTAL_DUE column equal the same 

amount. 

The second invoice (in pink) has line items that also start at 1 and continue in sequential order. 

This invoice also has the TOTAL_DUE and the AMOUNT columns equaling the same amount. 

These concepts apply to journal entries and adjustments as well: when more than one journal, 

invoice, or adjustment is added to a CSV file, you must restart the line number (LINE_NO) count at 

1 for the line items to be imported correctly. 

---


<!-- Page 27 -->
Chapter 1: Import Preparation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

When adding data for multiple line numbers in the same template file, be sure to start the line 
numbers over at one, as shown in the following image.

If your journals, invoices, or adjustments have line items and you do not enter a line number in the 
LINE_NO column, or enter line numbers out of sequence, the import will fail.

Use Row Numbers to Find Errors 

When importing A/P invoices or A/R invoices using a CSV file, if errors are found during upload, 

the entire CSV file is rejected. You can find the errors in the file if you use row numbers in the Do 

Not Import column. If your CSV file is rejected because errors are found, the error file contains the 

original row number, allowing you to quickly pinpoint where to make changes. 

a) Number the rows in the “Do not import” column. 

b) Error file contains original row numbers.

Import Preparation 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite

Order of CSV Imports 

In some cases, CSV imports must be performed in a specific order because of dependencies 

within the data. For example, if you have transactions that require locations, but you have not 

entered or imported the locations, the transaction import fails. 

It is always best to follow the order of the steps as they are presented in the Import data page 

when performing any type of import. Not all of the steps are required. For example, you may not 

use territories anywhere in your accounting data, therefore creating them is optional. 

In a few cases there are circular references. For example, an employee record can reference a 

department and vice versa. Problems that would otherwise result from such circular references 

have been eliminated for the purposes of importing by removing certain items. If you absolutely 

must have this data, you need to enter it manually. 

Importing Offline 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much processing the 

system must do to the data. If you are in doubt, select the Process offline option on the import 

utility page. 

When the offline process is complete, the system sends an email to the address you entered in 

the Import Company Information box (where you imported your file). 

RealPage recommends selecting Process offline when importing CSV files and providing your 
email address. If your import fails, you will always be notified, and the failed records are sent to 
your email. 

Automating Imports 

You may be able to automate and schedule your imports using a third-party application, such as 

Workato. 

Contact your account representative to learn more about this option.

### Import Data Page
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 30*

Import Boxes 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite

Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


Use the Import data page to: 

• 
Add accounting data to a new company. 

• 
Quickly clear some or all records from an existing company. 

• 
Choose parts of your existing accounting package you want to import, or upload long lists, 

so you don’t have to enter the data manually. 

About the Import Data Page 

If you are using the Import data page to add accounting data or other information to an 

otherwise empty company, follow the sections in their pre-defined order. The following sections 

are in the Import data page: 

• 
Set Up Company Master List: Use this section to set up your chart of accounts, statistical 

accounts, account groups, group members, departments, locations, allocations, employees, 

and territories (see Setting Up the Company Master List). 

• 
Set Up General Ledger Transactions: Use this section to set up journals, account beginning 

balances, reporting periods, and budgets (see Setting Up General Ledger Transactions). 

• 
Set Up A/P Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments: Use this section to set up the 

Accounts Payable application, A/P invoices, adjustments, and assets (see Setting Up A/P 

Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments). 

• 
Set Up A/R Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments: Use this section to set up the 

Accounts Receivable application, A/R invoices, customer lists, and adjustments (see Setting 

Up A/R Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments). 

• 
Set Up Cash Management: Use this section to set up your bank accounts, credit cards, 

credit card transactions, and other receipts (see Setting Up Cash Management). 

• 
Property Management: Use this section to set up your property, leases, locations, 

measurements, expenses, and tenant information 

This section displays if you have Commercial Property Management installed. 

• 
Condo and Co-op: Use this section to set up your property, owners, owner information, 

measurements, tasks, billing, and more. 

This section displays if you have Condo and Co-op installed. 

• 
Set Up Job Cost: Use this section to set up your jobs, draw model details, job cost history, 

job cost and replacement reserve draws, and external commitments (see Setting Up Job 

Cost). 

• 
Set Up Spend Management: Use this section to set up catalog mapping and saved items 

(see Setting Up Spend Management).

Understanding the Actions Within the Sections 

Each predefined section has one or more actions to help you customize your accounting 

application and direct you to the next step in the process flow. The following diagram describes 

the different actions in each section of the Import data page. 

These actions are per row in each section of the checklist and can differ depending on what data 
is being requested on the row. 

a) Status: A check mark in this column indicates a completed step. 

b) Type: This is accounting function or record type. 

c) Create: Click this link to add a new record. 

d) Import: Click this link to import information from a CSV file. 

e) Template: Click this link to download an XLS template that provides all standard and custom 

fields and descriptions of requirements for each field. 

f) 
View: Click this link to view a list of existing records. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

#### Importing the CSV File
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 32*

Import Boxes 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing the CSV File 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file into the system. 

To import your CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Find the information type you want to import, and then click the corresponding Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you want to import. 

5. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in mm/dd/yyyy format, select the date format that 

the data uses in the Date format field. 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
If your import box includes a Post to section, select one of the following: 

• 
Select Historical if your data is not active. 

• 
Select General Ledger to post imported invoices to the G/L. 

8. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

9. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

10. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify that all of the 

records in your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify 

them.

Importing Data During Company Setup 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


Whether you are importing data into a company for the first time or updating existing data, 

importing data into your system is a two-step process: first, you download and populate a 

template, and second, you import the data from the template. 

It’s best to complete the setup in the order listed in the Import data page. 

Download the Import Template 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information. This is important because: 

• 
Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by Performance Analytics at any time, especially when a new 

version of Performance Analytics is released. This means that an older template might not 

work. 

To download a template from the Import data page: 

1. 
Click the Template link for the data type you want to import. For example, click Template 

on the Account groups row to download a template that enables you to import or update 

account groups. 

In addition to standard columns, the system dynamically appends columns for any 
dimensions you’ve enabled and any custom fields and custom objects you’ve created so 
that you can import that information as well. 

2. 
Populate the template with your company’s information. 

3. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

4. 
Close out the CSV file. 

Import Data From the Template 

When you have populated your selected template, import the file. 

To import the table of data into your system: 

1. 
On the Import data page, locate the item for which you downloaded the template. For 

example, if you downloaded an Account Groups template, locate the Account groups row, 

and then click the corresponding Import link. The system displays an import page. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file.

Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in

6.

importing data into your system is a two-step process: first, you prepare your data for import, and 

second, you import the data from the template. 

Preparing Your Data

Close the CSV file. 

Import Data From the Template

### Introduction

## Importing Chart of Accounts Data
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 44*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Introduction 

This section includes instructions for each type of data that you can import into the system. 

Importing Chart of Accounts Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Chart of Accounts`


You can import a chart of accounts by uploading a CSV file.  

You must be at the top level to import General Ledger accounts. 

If you intend to import multiple journal entries with one file, see Importing journal entries (on 

page 292). 

Workflow 

To import a chart of accounts: 

• 
Download the template file 

• 
Fill the file with your chart of accounts data 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the file. 

Downloading the File 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data.  

3. 
Find Chart of accounts, and then select the Template link. 

4. 
Find the template file where your browser saves downloaded files. 

Filling the File with Chart of Accounts Data 

1. 
Open the template file in Excel or another spreadsheet application.  

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template with your chart of accounts data: 

---


<!-- Page 45 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the primary /sub account specification. You can find your company’s 

account specification on the Company Information page. 

• 
ACCT_NAME: Type the name of the account. 

• 
ACCT_TYPE: Type N for a balance sheet account, type I for an income statement 

account.  

• 
NORMAL_BALANCE: Type DB for a debit account; CR for a credit account. 

• 
CLOSEABLE: Type N for a non-closing account, C for a closing to account, and type R 

for a closed to account. 

• 
CLOSETOACCT_NO: Type the primary and sub account. This field is required only 

when CLOSEABLE is set to C. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. See Chart of Accounts Data Template (on 

page 38) for a full list of the available columns. 

4. 
Save the file as a CSV file. 

---

Before Importing Account Beginning Balances 

Before you can establish the beginning balances for the general ledger, create the journals that 

your company needs: 

• 
General journals 

• 
Adjustment journals 

• 
GAAP (compliance) adjustment journals 

• 
Tax adjustment journals 

• 
Statistical journals 

• 
Statistical adjustment journals 

• 
User-defined books and journals 

The options to create journals appear on the Setup tab of the General ledger menu. 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

You must have administrator-level permissions to create books and journals.  

The following permissions are required to import account data. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

General Ledger 
 Accounts 
List, View, Add, Edit 

General Ledger 
Statistical accounts 
List, View, Add, Edit 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

## Importing Account Beginning Balances
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 62*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Account Beginning Balances 

You must be at the top level to import General Ledger accounts. 

Use the Account Beginning Balances template to import beginning balances into one journal 

with one file. If you intend to import multiple journals with one file, use the steps in Importing 

General Ledger journal entries (on page 289) instead. 


> **Navigation Path:** `The Create link for both Account Beginning Balances and General Ledger Journal Entries display 
the same application page: General Ledger > All > Journals. In addition, both always contain the 
same number of records.`


To import beginning balances: 

1. 
After creating the journals, go to Company > Import data, and find the Set up general 

ledger transactions section.  

2. 
In the Account beginning balances section, choose the journal for which you want to 

establish a beginning balance from the pull-down list. This is typically the General Journal. 

3. 
Type a date for Balance as of or choose one with the 
 Calendar button.  

Typically, that date is the next day after you close your old accounting system and start a 

new set of books in Performance Analytics. However, it could be another date as well. In the 

event that you do not enter a date, the default is today. Be careful when entering the 

beginning date because the choice is important. If you choose to enter starting balances as 

of, say, two fiscal years ago because you want to be able to print comparative financial 

statements, you must then make General Journal entries for the ending G/L balances for all 

the periods between your starting balance date and the date you actually begin using 

Performance Analytics. 

If you are uploading historical transactions, be sure that your starting balances CONTAIN 

these uploaded transactions, and set the Balance As Of date to that date. 

Because G/L Transactions contain fields for both department and location, you may enter as many 

unique G/L transaction department/location combinations as you need.

## Tasks After Importing Beginning Balances
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 63*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Tasks After Importing Beginning Balances 

After importing account beginning balances, you should: 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Populate your account group ranges from the General Ledger > Account Groups page.`



> **Navigation Path:** `2. 
Create a financial report to test your data from the General Ledger > Financial Reports`


page. 


> **Navigation Path:** `3. 
Create a Trial Balance from the General Ledger > Trial Balance page to make certain that`


your starting balances have been set up correctly. 

Be sure to properly format your Trial Balance so that it includes all relevant accounts. You can 
make sure the relevant accounts are included on Account Groups page. If the correct accounts 
are not included, this can throw off your Balance Sheet artificially. 

Importing G/L Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Chart of Accounts`


This import allows you to add new accounts and to update existing G/L account records. 

Workflow for Importing G/L Accounts 

• 
Download the chart of accounts template. 

• 
Fill the template with account data. 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the file. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Chart of Accounts row, and then click the Template link in the row. The system 

either downloads the template to your browser’s default download folder, or prompts you 

to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template  

To fill in the template with your data: 

1. 
Open the template file in your spreadsheet application. 

2. 
For each G/L account, add the required information: 

• 
ACCT_NO: Account number. The account number must conform to the primary/sub 


> **Navigation Path:** `account specification as it is defined in Company > Setup.`


• 
ACCT_NAME: Type the account name. It can be up to 80 characters long. 

---


<!-- Page 64 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
ACCT_TYPE: Type N for Balance Sheet, I for Income Statement 

• 
NORMAL_BALANCE: Type DB if the account has a debit normal balance, type CR for a 

credit normal balance. 

• 
CLOSEABLE: Type N for non-closing, type C for closing to, type R for closed to. 

• 
CLOSETOACCT_NO: Type the account number that this G/L account closes to. This 

field is required if you set CLOSEABLE to C. The account number that you specify must 


> **Navigation Path:** `conform to the primary/sub account specification as it is defined in Company > Setup.`


3. 
Optionally, add data in any of the remaining columns. 

• 
REQ_DEPT: This is the Require Department field. Type T for true or F for false. 

• 
REQ_LOC: This is the Require Location field. Type T for true or F for false. 

• 
CATEGORY: Type any value that appears in the drop-down list. In the General Ledger 

GL account list, click any cell in this column to view the drop-down list. Do not type in 

a value. You must select the General setup template during company setup to tag a 

category. Otherwise, importing the chart of account with a category tagged will cause 

an error during the upload process. 

• 
ACTIVE: Specify if the G/L account should be active. Type T for true or F for false. 

• 
REQUIREPROJECT: This is the Require Project field. Type T for true or F for false. 

• 
REQUIRECUSTOMER: This is the Require Customer field. Type T for true or F for false.

• 
REQUIREITEM: This is the Require Item field. Type T for true or F for false. 

• 
REQUIRECLASS: This is the Require Class field. Type T for true or F for false. 

• 
ALTERNATIVE_ACCOUNT: This is the G/L account alternative field. Type None, Payables 

account, or Receivables account. 

• 
REQ_UNIT: This is the Require Unit field. Type T for true or F for false. 

• 
CHART_TYPES: This is the Chart types field. Type the desired chart type to assign to the 

account. 

• 
SUBLEDGERCONTROLON: This is the Disallow direct posting field. Type T for true or F 

for false.

JPM_ACCT_NO: This is the Custom account field.

IMPORT_DESCRIPTION_DEBIT: This is the Import Description-Debit field. Type the

ALLOW_AS_ELIMINATION_ACCOUNT: This is the Allow as Elimination Account field.

## Importing Account Beginning Balances
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 70*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite

Importing Account Beginning Balances 

You must be at the top level to import General Ledger accounts. 

Use the Account Beginning Balances template to import beginning balances into one journal 

with one file. If you intend to import multiple journals with one file, use the steps in Importing 

General Ledger journal entries (on page 289) instead. 


> **Navigation Path:** `The Create link for both Account Beginning Balances and General Ledger Journal Entries display 
the same application page: General Ledger > All > Journals. In addition, both always contain the 
same number of records.`


To import beginning balances: 

1. 
After creating the journals, go to Company > Import data, and find the Set up general 

ledger transactions section.  

2. 
In the Account beginning balances section, choose the journal for which you want to 

establish a beginning balance from the pull-down list. This is typically the General Journal. 

3. 
Type a date for Balance as of or choose one with the 
 Calendar button.  

Typically, that date is the next day after you close your old accounting system and start a 

new set of books in Performance Analytics. However, it could be another date as well. In the 

event that you do not enter a date, the default is today. Be careful when entering the 

beginning date because the choice is important. If you choose to enter starting balances as 

of, say, two fiscal years ago because you want to be able to print comparative financial 

statements, you must then make General Journal entries for the ending G/L balances for all 

the periods between your starting balance date and the date you actually begin using 

Performance Analytics. 

If you are uploading historical transactions, be sure that your starting balances CONTAIN 

these uploaded transactions, and set the Balance As Of date to that date. 

Because G/L Transactions contain fields for both department and location, you may enter as many 

unique G/L transaction department/location combinations as you need.

## Importing Account Groups
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 71*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Account Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Account Groups`


You can import and export account group data and group member data. Each type of data has its 

own template file. Note that the account group template is different from account group member 

template. 

This procedure describes importing account group data. You must import account groups first 

and then import account group members second, because the account groups must exist before 

you can import the account group members (on page 72). 

If this is the first time that you are creating account groups, then follow the instructions in First 

Time Account Group Imports. Otherwise, follow the instruction in Importing Account Groups to 

Update the System. 

First Time Account Group Imports 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Set Up Company Master List section, and then find the Account groups row. 

4. 
Click the Default template link. The system downloads the file to your browser’s default 

location.  

5. 
Go to Step 2, Preparing the Data. 

Importing Account Groups to Update the System 

Step 1: Exporting from the Account Groups List  

You can export account group information from the Account Groups list.  


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to the Account Groups list (General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Account groups).`


2. 
Click the Export button. A box appears with two choices, Account Groups or Member 

Groups.  

3. 
Select Account Groups. 

---


<!-- Page 72 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Step 2: Preparing the Data 

When you download a template from the Import data list, the correct headers are in the template 

already. Fill in the columns with your data, save it as a CSV file, and then upload the file. The 

header titles in the template that you download correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header 

titles will cause an upload error.  

For more information about the CSV upload process, including best practices, common errors, 

and how to upload your CSV file, see Preparing Your CSV File for Import (on page 11).  

1. 
Open the file with Microsoft Excel. 

2. 
Add information about account groups to the template. 

3. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
GROUP_NAME: Type a name for the account group that is unique. This name is case 

sensitive. 

• 
NORMAL_BALANCE: Type DB for debit, CR for credit. 

• 
MEMBER_TYPE: Type G for Groups, A for G/L accounts, S for statistical accounts, 

COMP for Computation, C for Category, and SC for Stat Category. 

• 
F_DEPARTMENT: Type the department. This field is required when 

F_DEPARTMENT_TYPE is set to H or T. 

• 
F_LOCATION: Type the location. This field is required when F_LOCATION_TYPE is set to 

H or T. 

4. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns.  

5. 
Save the file as a CSV file type (on page 14). If you are saving from Excel, choose the 

comma-delimited file type.  

The file will have the file extension .csv after you save it. Leave the file open until your 

import is successful. Excel can sometimes reformat the file if you close it before the import is 

successful.  

Step 3: Importing the Account Group Data 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Click Account groups. 

3. 
Click the Import button.  

If the link says Default Import, click the link to have the system automatically create a list of 

default account groups.  

4. 
Select Account groups. The Account groups import box opens. 

5. 
Click the Choose file button.  

---

7.

8.

9.

11.

complete.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

You must have Administrator privileges to import account groups. The following permissions are 

required to import account group data. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

General Ledger 
 Account group 
List, View, Add, Edit 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

To download a template, you must have permission to access the Company application and to 

access the Import Data page.

## Importing Account Group Members
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 80*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Account Group Members 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Account Groups > Import > 
Group Members`


You can import and export account group members. Before you import group members, you 

must import account groups first, because the groups must exist before you can update the 

members. See Importing account groups (on page 63). 

Downloading the Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import Data. 

3. 
Find the Set Up Company Master List section, and then find the Group Members row. 

4. 
Click the Template link. The system downloads the file to your browser’s default location. In 

this CSV file, each account group is mapped to a list of group members.  

Preparing the Data 

When you download a template from the Import data list, the correct headers are in the template 

already. Fill in the columns with your data, and then save it as a CSV file. The header titles in the 

template that you download correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header titles will cause an 

upload error.  

For more information about the CSV upload process, including best practices, common errors, 

and how to upload your CSV file, see Preparing your CSV file for import (on page 11).  

1. 
Open the file with Microsoft Excel. 

2. 
Add information about an account group’s members to the template. 

3. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
GROUP_NAME: Type a name for the account group member that is unique. This name 

is case sensitive. 

• 
CALC_AMOUNT: Type the code for the calculated amount: type F for For Period, S for 

Start of Period, and E for End of Period. 

• 
APPLY_BUDGET: This column fills the Apply calculation to budget field. Type T for 

true, F for false. This column is required when MEMBER_TYPE is set to A or S. 

• 
LEFT_OPERAND_CALC_AMT: Type F for For Period, S for Start of Period, or E for End of 

Period. This column is required when the MEMBER_TYPE is set to COMP and 

LEFT_OPERAND_ACCOUNT is not blank. 

• 
RIGHT_OPERAND_CALC_AMT: Type F for For Period, S for Start of Period, or E for End 

of Period. This column is required when the MEMBER_TYPE is set to COMP, and 

RIGHT_OPERAND_ACCOUNT is not blank.

## Importing Account Group Purpose Data
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 87*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Account Group Purpose Data 

This procedure helps you add Account group purposes information to an account group. 

If your system does not have account groups, then you must add account group data first, before 

you can import account group purposes.  

Workflow 

1. 
Download the template for Account group purposes. 

2. 
Fill the template with data. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

4. 
Import the file.  

Downloading the template 

To download the import template file for account group purposes: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. The Import data page opens. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Account group purposes row, and then 

click Template. The system downloads the file to your browser’s default download location. 

Filling the Template with Data 

1. 
Open the template file in Excel, and fill in the required column. 

• 
NAME: Type the account group purpose. The name must be unique, and it is 

case-sensitive. 

2. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining column: 

• 
STATUS: Type ACTIVE or INACTIVE.  

3. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 14). 

Importing the File 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the More section of the Setup menu, click Account group purposes. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Account group purpose box opens. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button. 

5. 
Find and select the file with the data that you saved as a CSV file.  

6. 
Click Open. 

7. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format, select the date format 

that the data uses in the Date format field. 

---


<!-- Page 88 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

8. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

9. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

10. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

11. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify all the records in 

your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify them. 

---



## Importing Account Label Data
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 89*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Account Label Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Account Label > Template/Import`


Before you can import account label data, the Account label feature must be enabled. See 

Configuring A/R Functionality. 

To download the account labels template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Locate the Set up A/R master list, open invoices and adjustments section. 

4. 
In the Account label row, click Template. The system either downloads the Account label.xls 

file or prompts you to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template with Account Label Data 

1. 
Open the Account label.xls file in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
ACCOUNTLABEL: Type the account label identifier. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type the description of the account label. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the account number associated with the account label. 

3. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining columns. 

• 
OFFSETGLACCOUNTNO: Type the offset account number. 

• 
USEFORPM: Type true when this account label is used with Commercial Property 

Management. Type false when this account label is only used by RealPage Accounting. 

• 
USEFORRENT: Type true when this account label is used with Commercial Property 

Management and the account label is associated with rent. Otherwise, type false. 

• 
PAYMENTPRIORITY: Type U for Urgent, H for High, N for Normal, and L for Low. The 

default is N. 

• 
SLRACCTNO: Type an account number for the straight line rent income account. 

• 
SLROFFSETACCTNO: Type an account number for the straight line rent offset account. 

• 
STATUS: Type ACTIVE or INACTIVE. 

4. 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 14). 

---


<!-- Page 90 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing the Account Label Data 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Locate the Set up A/R master list, open invoices and adjustments section. 

4. 
In the Account label row, click the Import link. The Accounts Receivable Labels box opens. 

5. 
Click the Choose File button. 

6. 
Select and open the CSV file that contains the account label data. 

7. 
In the Date format field, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, select a date 

format that you want to use. The system supports 24 date formats.  

8. 
In the File encoding list, leave the setting auto detect unless you are unable to import your 

file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

9. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. This method allows the system to process the data when system activity is lighter. If 

you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, clear the Process offline check box. 

10. 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. When the system 

completes the import process, it sends an email to the address with either a message about 

the success or failure of the import, including any errors that occurred in the process. 

11. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row in the file that starts with a # symbol.

## Importing Account Tax Return Codes
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 91*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Account Tax Return Codes 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Master List > Account Tax 
Return Codes > Template/Import`


Account tax return codes are used with the UK’s value added tax (VAT).  

The Import Process 

1. 
Download a template. 

2. 
Fill the template with account tax return code data. 

3. 
Prepare a CSV file for import (on page 11). 

4. 
Import the CSV file. 

5. 
Resolve errors. 

Downloading the Template 

To download a template, you must have permission to access the Company application and to 

access the Import Data page. 

To download a template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import Data.  

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Account tax return codes row. 

4. 
Click the Template link. 

Filling in the Template 

1. 
Open the downloaded file in Excel. 

2. 
Fill the file with the following required data: 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the account number to use for tax return codes. The account must 

conform to your system’s primary/sub account specification.  

This is defined in the Company information record on the Accounting tab. Open the 

Company menu, Setup tab, Company option, and then click the Accounting tab. 

3. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns:  

• 
TAXCODE: Type the tax return code. 

• 
MRCCODE: Type the M-3 return code. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format.
