## Importing Account Title by Entity
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 94*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Account Title by Entity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Account Titles by Entity > Import`


The template for account titles by entity data is available by clicking the Import button on the 

Account title by entity list. 

RealPage recommends that you download a new blank template whenever you import 

information into the system. This is important because: 

• 
Templates on the Import Data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of the system is 

released. This means that an older template might not work. 

However, some templates are not available from the Import data list. The account titles by entity 

template is one of those. 

To download the account title by entity template: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Account title by entity. The Account Title by Entity list opens. 

3. 
Click the Import button.  

4. 
Click the Download link to download the template file.  

The header titles in the template you download correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect 

header titles will cause an upload error. 

---


<!-- Page 95 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Filling In the Template File 

1. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
LOCATIONID: This is the unique identifier of the entity/location associated with the 

account title. 

• 
ACCOUNTNO: This is the account number associated with the account title.  

• 
TITLE: This is the account title that you want to assign.  

2. 
Save the file as a CSV file. The file that you import must be in CSV format. 

For more information about the CSV upload process and how to prepare a CSV file, see 

Preparing Your CSV File for Import (on page 11). 

To import the account titles by entity file with data in it: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the More section, select Account Titles by Entity. The Account Titles by Entity list with 

your accounts opens. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Account title by entity box opens. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you created. 

5. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format, select the date format 

that the data uses in the Date format field. 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
If you want the system to generate and store these records offline while you continue to 

work, select the Process offline check box. 

8. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

9. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported.

## Importing Accruals
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 96*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Accruals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Accrual Template > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up General Ledger Transactions > 
Accruals > Import`


To download the accruals template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Import Data option. 

3. 
In the Set Up General Ledger Transactions section of the Import Data page, find the Accruals 

row, and then click the Template link. The Accruals template downloads to your browser’s 

default download location. 

4. 
Open the template and add the accrual data that you want to import. Take care to exactly 

match the template’s data structure as you do this.  

Do not use leading zeros in ID fields. If you MUST use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

5. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
ACCRUAL_ID: Type the unique identifier associated with the accrual. 

• 
FLOCATIONS: Type the name of a location. The location must be defined in the 

system. 

• 
BOOK: Type the name of a book, including: All books, Accrual, GAAP, Tax, and 

User-defined.

## Importing Adjusting Journal Entries
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 104*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Adjusting Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Template`


Downloading the Template 

To download the adjusting journal entries template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Import data option, and then download the template for General Ledger Journal 

Entries. 

Filling In the Template 

Dates 

Typically, the Date is the next day after you close your old accounting system and start a new set 

of books in the system. In the event that you do not enter a date, the default is today. The choice 

of date is important: for example, if you choose to enter a date of two fiscal years ago because 

you want to be able to print comparative financial statements, you must then make Journal 

entries for the ending G/L balances for all of the periods between your starting balance date and 

the date you actually begin using Performance Analytics. 

If you are uploading historical transactions, make sure that your starting balances contain these 

uploaded transactions, and set the date to that date. 

If you find you have set the wrong starting date for your G/L balances, you can clear the 

transactions from the Import data page, and then start again. 

Line Items 

The uploaded file must contain a number in either the DEBIT or CREDIT field. One or the other is 

required. For example, if you do not have a debit amount, you must have a credit amount. You 

can import negative numbers for either, in which case a negative debit amount is treated as a 

credit, and a negative credit is treated as a debit. 

---


<!-- Page 105 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

The LINE_NO must be unique per journal entry and per journal. For example, Summary 1 might 

contain line numbers 1-20, Summary 2 1-44 and so on. For more information on line numbers, 

see Importing Data with Line Numbers (on page 16). 

1. 
Minimally, add the required journal entry data to the template. 

• 
JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DATE: Type the date of the journal entry. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of up to 80 characters. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number, starting with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DEBIT: Type the debit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

CREDIT field. 

• 
CREDIT: Type the credit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

DEBIT field. 

• 
SOURCEENTITY: Type the name of the entity. This value is required when the option to 

automatically create inter-entity transactions is enabled for journal entries and the 

journal entry is not balanced by location. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date. This field is required unless you provide a value in 

the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

2. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

---


<!-- Page 106 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing the Data 

To import the data: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu.  

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section, click the Adjusting Entry option, and then select the type of 

adjusting entry that you want to import. 

3. 
Click the Import transactions button. 

4. 
Click the Choose files button, find the CSV file with the data that you want to import, and 

double-click it. 

5. 
If the data in the CSV file includes dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format, select the date 

format used in the data that you are importing.  

6. 
Leave the File encoding setting set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
Select the Process offline check box if you want to process the import offline. Select this 

option for large files.  

8. 
In the Email results to this address field, type the email address where you want the system 

to send import results and error data. 

9. 
Click the Import button.

## Importing A/P Invoices
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 107*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Accounts Payable Invoices > Template/Import`


You can import A/P invoice data by filling in an A/P invoice template with data, saving the file in 

CSV format, and uploading the CSV file into the system. The actual import process occurs offline.  

• 
Each CSV file can contain up to 5,000 transactions. 

• 
The A/P invoice transactions should be open transactions only. Do not include paid or 

partially paid transactions. 

If an error occurs, the system rolls back the transaction. 

To upload historical invoices, be sure to select the Historical option. 

To import A/P invoices: 

1. 
Download the template. 

2. 
Fill in the template. 

3. 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 14). 

4. 
Importing the A/P invoice data.  

You can upload A/P invoices using the Import data option. You can also upload the A/P 
invoices in the A/P invoices list. 

Downloading the Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of Performance 

Analytics is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

Templates 

As long as you have appropriate permissions, you can download any template, fill it with data, 

and then import the data. 

Follow these steps to prepare the data. Alternatively, give these instructions to your database 

administrator, who can help you with this step. 

---


<!-- Page 108 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Each template has detailed information about one type of data. An item can be a thing, such as 

an entity, location, vendor, or contact; or a transaction type, such as invoices, fees, or adjustments. 

When you fill a template, make sure the data matches the template. For example, do not fill a Unit 

template with Location data. 

You can download the templates and import the data from the Import data page. 

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Accounts 

Payable Invoices option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the A/P invoices import template. You can find the file 

in your browser’s default download location.  

Filling In the Template 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor associated with the invoice. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date of the invoice. 

• 
DUE_DATE: Type the date that the payment is due. 

• 
BASECURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or EUR for the 

base currency. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. This field is 

required for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. Locations in 

line items must use the same base currency. 

• 
CURRENCY: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code for the currency used for 

this transaction.  

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the unique invoice number.  

---


<!-- Page 109 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type a G/L account number to associate this A/P invoice with it.  

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique number of the location associated with the A/P 

invoice. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number of the invoice item. The line number appears in the 

Entries list on the A/P invoice page. 

5. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns:  

• 
BATCH_TITLE: Type the title of the batch of transactions to which this invoice belongs. 

• 
PAID_DATE: If the invoice has been paid, type the date that the invoice was paid.  

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the A/P invoice.  

• 
PO_NO: Type a reference number that is associated with the invoice. 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor that is associated with this 

invoice. 

• 
TOTAL_DUE: Type the total amount due. 

• 
TOTAL_PAID: If the invoice has been paid, type the amount paid. 

• 
POSTING_DATE: Type the date that this invoice is to be posted to the general ledger. 

• 
TERM_NAME: Type the name of the terms of payment. 

• 
SUPDOCID: Type the attachment ID of the document that you want to attach to this 

transaction. You must have uploaded the documents prior to filling in this 

spreadsheet. 

• 
PAYMENTPRIORITY: Type the priority of the payment. The default is Normal. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date for the exchange rate. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_TYPE_ID: Type the exchange rate type. 

• 
EXCHANGE_RATE: Type the exchange rate used for this transaction. 

• 
PAYTO: Type the name of a contact who is designated to receive the payments for the 

vendor. The contact must be defined in the system. 

• 
RETURNTO: Type the name of a contact who is designated to receive returned goods 

for the vendor. The contact must be defined in the system. 

• 
ACTION:  

• 
INCLUSIVETAX: Type “T” if this is inclusive of taxes. Otherwise, type “F.” 

• 
SEPARATE_VENDOR_PYMT: Type “T” if you want the system to cut a separate check 

for this vendor. Otherwise, type “F.” 

• 
INVOICE_ON_HOLD: Type “True” to place the invoice on hold. Otherwise, type “False.” 

The default value is “false.” 

• 
SOURCEENTITY: Type the name of the source entity. The source entity is the entity 

that is the source of the money in a transaction between two or more entities.

BANKENTITY: Type the name of the bank.

8. 
Select the mode for importing in the Post to field: 

• 
Select the Historical option for imported transactions to have no effect on the general 

ledger. 

• 
Select the General Ledger option for imported transactions to post live to the general 

ledger. 

9. 
If you select Historical as the import mode, you can select the Process Offline check box. 

This is useful when your import file is large. 

10. 
To have the system send an email when the import is complete or if errors occur, type your 

email address into the Email results to this address field. 

11. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row that starts with a # symbol.

## Importing A/P Adjustments
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 131*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing A/P Adjustments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Accounts Payable Adjustments > Template/Import`


Use the import template that is designed for accounts payable adjustments. 

Adjustments that are imported from a CSV file are not posted to the General ledger. 

To import A/P adjustments: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Accounts 

Payable Adjustments option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the A/P adjustments import template. You can find the 

file in your browser’s default download location. 

5. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

Filling the Template 

1. 
Open the template using a spreadsheet application. By default, the file opens in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required fields for each A/P adjustment that you want to import: 

• 
ADJUSTMENT_NO (Recommended): Type a unique number to assign to the 

adjustment. 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the vendor’s unique identifier. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date that the adjustment was created. 

• 
BASECURR: Identify the base currency by typing a three letter ISO currency code, like 

USD or EUR.  

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date. This field is required unless you provide the 

EXCHANGE_RATE. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number. Start with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the account number associated with the line item.  

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the line item. 

3. 
Optionally, fill in any of the other columns in the template as needed. 

4. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV). 

---


<!-- Page 132 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing the CSV File 

To import the CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Accounts 

Payable Adjustments row, and then select the Import link.  

4. 
In the import box, click the Choose file button, and then find the CSV file. 

5. 
Select the Accounts Payable Adjustments CSV file to import, and then click Open. 

6. 
Click the Import button. The system loads the data into the system. 

---



## Importing A/R Adjustments
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 133*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing A/R Adjustments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Accounts Receivable Adjustments > Template/Import`


Use the import template that is designed for Accounts Receivable Adjustments.  

Adjustments that are imported from a CSV file are not posted to the General Ledger. 

To import A/R adjustments: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Accounts 

Receivable Adjustments option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the A/R adjustments import template. You can find the 

file in your browser’s default download location.  

5. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

Filling the Template 

1. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
ADJUSTMENT_NO (Recommended): Type a unique number to assign to the 

adjustment. 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID: Type the unique identifier of the customer associated with the 

adjustment. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date of the adjustment. 

• 
BASECURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or EUR for the 

base currency. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. This field is 

required for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. Locations in 

line items must use the same base currency. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date for the exchange rate. This field is required unless 

you provide the exchange rate in the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number of the adjusting entry. These numbers appear on the 

left side of the Entries list on the A/R Adjustment page. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type a G/L account number. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the adjustment. Designate negative numbers with a 

leading dash. 

2. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns:  

• 
BATCH_TITLE: Type the title of the batch of transactions to which this adjustment 

belongs. 

---


<!-- Page 134 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the invoice number associated with this adjustment. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the adjustment transaction. 

• 
CURRENCY: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code for the currency used for 

this transaction. Use this field only in multi-currency companies. This field defines the 

transaction currency. If no field is defined here, the system uses the base currency. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_TYPE_ID: Type the exchange rate type. 

• 
EXCHANGE_RATE: Type the exchange rate used for this transaction. 

• 
MEMO: Type a note about the adjustment. 

• 
ACCT_LABEL: Type the account label to associate with the adjustment.  

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique number of the location associated with the 

adjustment. In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, 

LOCATION_ID must be in an entity that uses the same base currency as BASECURR. 

• 
DEPT_ID: Type the unique number of the department associated with the adjustment. 

The department must be defined in the system. 

• 
ARADJUSTMENTITEM_ARACCOUNT: Type the A/R account number. It must conform 

to the defined primary/sub account, must be a valid account number, and must be 

balancing as a receivable account. 

• 
ACTION: Type the transaction status. 

• 
SUPDOCID: Import any documents that are attachments to transactions before you 

import the transactions themselves. Use the Attachments list’s Add option to import 

documents into the system. (Company > All > Storage > Attachments > Add). After 

importing the attachments, consult the Attachments list to find a document’s unique 

identifier. Type the document’s ID in the SUPDOCID field to associate the document 

with the transaction. 

• 
BILLTO: Type the name of a contact who is designated to receive the bills. The contact 

must be defined in the system. 

• 
SHIPTO: Type the name of the contact who receives shipments. The contact must be 

defined in the system. 

• 
UNITNUM: Type the number of the unit associated with the adjustment. 

• 
GLDIMPARTNER: Type the partner. 

• 
ARADJUSTMENTITEM_VENDORID: Type the vendor name. The vendor must have a 

record defined in the system. 

• 
ARADJUSTMENTITEM_CUSTOMERID: Type the customer name. The customer must 

have a record defined in the system. 

• 
(Segment Type): Type the two-character code for the segment type to associate with 

the transaction.  

• 
(Segment Value): Type the value of the segment to associate with the transaction. 

---



### Accounts Receivable Adjustments Data Template
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 135*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

You can include up to four segment types and values in the import file. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

To import adjustment data: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, select the Adjustments option. 

3. 
Click the Import button. 

4. 
Check that the box’s title and on-screen instructions above the Choose file button reflect 

the type of data that you are importing. 

5. 
Click the Choose files button, and then select the file that you want to import. 

6. 
Click Open. 

The file you import must be in CSV format. 

7. 
If your data contains dates, then in the Date format field select the date format used by the 

data that you are importing. 

8. 
Leave the File encoding field set to the default status, auto detect. 

9. 
Select the Process offline check box to have the system import the data with the least 

impact to system processing speed. 

10. 
To have the system send an email when an offline import is finished or when errors occur, 

type your email address in the Email results to this address field. You can enter multiple 

email addresses; separate each address by a semi-colon or comma. 

11. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row that starts with a # symbol. 

Accounts Receivable Adjustments Data Template 

Best Practices 

• 
Export the data from your other system, including as much of the data as is available. 

• 
Mark any row you want the import to ignore with a # symbol. The system ignores any row 

starting with a # during import. 

• 
Be sure to format the data to match the template precisely. 

Your template’s columns may differ from this documentation, as your template is designed 
around your company’s business needs. Your template may also differ from the documentation if 
your company has chosen not to enable certain features. 

---

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Required Fields 

Each column of the template represents a field in which you can import data. The required fields 

of the template must be filled in before you can import the data. 

• 
ADJUSTMENT_NO (Recommended) 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID 

• 
CREATED_DATE 

• 
BASECURR: Required for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies.  

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Required unless you provide the exchange rate in the EXCHANGE_RATE 

column. 

• 
LINE_NO 

• 
ACCT_NO 

• 
AMOUNT

## Importing A/R Invoices
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 146*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing A/R Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Accounts Receivable Invoices > Template/Import`


To import A/R invoices: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Accounts 

Receivable Invoices option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the A/R invoices import template. You can find the file 

in your browser’s default download location.  

5. 
Open the template file in Excel.  

Filling the Template 

1. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID: Type the unique identifier of the customer associated with the invoice. 

This field is the customer dimension. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date of the invoice. 

• 
DUE_DATE: Type the date that the payment is due. 

• 
TOTAL_DUE: Type the total amount due. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number of the invoice item. The line number appears in the 

Entries list on the A/R invoice page. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type a G/L account number. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the invoice. 

• 
BASECURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or EUR for the 

base currency. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. This field is 

required for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. Locations in 

line items must use the same base currency. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date for the exchange rate. This field is required unless 

you provide the exchange rate in the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

These fields are required if the line is to be deferred: 

• 
REVREC_TEMPLATE: Type the revenue recognition template to use. 

DEFERREDREV_ACCOUNT: Type the account number. The account number must exist 

in the system.  

• 
REVREC_JOURNAL: Type the name of the revenue recognition journal. This journal 

must exist before you can use the journal name in an import. 

---


<!-- Page 147 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
REVREC_SCHEDULE_LINE_NO: Type the line number. Line numbers are the 

incrementing numbers on the left side of the transaction in the Entries list. 

• 
REVENUE_ACCOUNT: Type the revenue account that you see when you navigate into 

the Rev rec schedule link from the A/R Invoice. This is the account to which the sales 

amount is posted to G/L when revenue is recognized.  

• 
REVREC_POSTINGDATE: Type the posting date.  

• 
REVREC_AMOUNT: Type the amount.  

2. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns:  

• 
BATCH_TITLE: Type the title of the batch of transactions to which this invoice belongs. 

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the invoice number. 

• 
PO_NO: Type a reference number. 

• 
POSTING_DATE: Type the G/L posting date. 

• 
TOTAL_PAID: If the invoice has been paid, type the amount paid. 

• 
PAID_DATE: If the invoice has been paid, type the date that the invoice was paid.  

• 
TERM_NAME: Type the name of the terms of payment. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the A/R invoice.  

• 
CURRENCY: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code for the currency used for 

this transaction.  

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date for the exchange rate. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_TYPE_ID: Type the exchange rate type. 

• 
EXCHANGE_RATE: Type the exchange rate used for this transaction. 

• 
MEMO: Type a note about the A/R invoice. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type a G/L account number to associate this A/R invoice with it. 

• 
ACCT_LABEL: Type the account label to associate with this A/R invoice. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique number of the location associated with the A/R 

invoice. 

• 
DEPT_ID: Type the unique number of the department associated with the A/R invoice. 

• 
ALLOCATION_ID: Type the allocation to use. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount expressed in the base currency. 

• 
SUBTOTAL: Type the subtotal of the amount before tax is added. 

• 
REVREC_STARTDATE: Type the start date for revenue recognition. 

• 
ARINVOICEITEM_ARACCOUNT: Type the A/R account number. 

• 
ACTION: Type the transaction status. Valid statuses include “Draft” and “Submit.” 

• 
SUPDOCID: Import any documents that are attachments to transactions before you 

import the transactions themselves. Use the Attachments list’s Add option to import 

documents into the system. (Company > All > Storage > Attachments > Add). After 

---


<!-- Page 148 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

importing the attachments, consult the Attachments list to find a document’s unique 

identifier. Type the document’s ID in the SUPDOCID field to associate the document 

with the transaction. 

• 
BILLTO: Type the name of a contact who is designated to receive the bills. The contact 

must be defined in the system. 

• 
SHIPTO: Type the name of the contact who receives shipments. The contact must be 

defined in the system. 

• 
SOURCEENTITY: Type the name of the source entity. The source entity is the entity 

that is the source of the money in a transaction between two or more entities. 

• 
BANKENTITY: Type the name of the bank. 

• 
BANKGLACCOUNT: Type the bank G/L account to associate with this A/R invoice. 

• 
UNITNUM: Type the unit number associated with the A/R invoice. 

• 
REVREC_ENDDATE: Type the end date for revenue recognition. 

• 
TAX_LINE_NO: Type the line number for the tax charge. 

• 
TAX_AMOUNT: Type the amount of the tax. 

• 
TAX_DETAILID: Type the unique identifier of the tax detail. Tax details are only used 

with VAT taxes. 

• 
VAT_RETURN_OVERRIDE_DATE: Type the override date of the VAT tax return. 

• 
REXTERNAL_PAYMENT_HEADER: Type the text in the external payment header. 

• 
ARINVOICEITEM_CUSTOMERID: Type the customer identifier associated with the 

invoiced item.  

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_1: Type the two-character code for the segment type to associate with 

the transaction.  

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_1: Type the value of the segment to associate with the transaction. 

You can include up to five segment types and values in the import file. 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues 

imports can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.  

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing A/R Invoices 

To import invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & find section, select A/R Invoices. 

3. 
Click the Import button.  

4. 
Click the Choose file button and find the file you want to import. 

---



### A/R Invoice Data
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 149*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

The file you import must be in CSV format. 

5. 
In the Date format field, if your csv file contains dates, you can set the date format to match 

the format in the csv file. 

6. 
To allow the system to auto detect the type of csv file that you are uploading, skip the File 

encoding check box. You can also select a specific csv file format, such as Mac OSx, 

Windows-1252, and more if needed. 

7. 
In the Post to section, select the mode for importing: 

• 
Historical: imported transactions have no effect on the general ledger. 

• 
General ledger: imported transactions are posted live to the general ledger. 

Note the rules listed on the page for importing to the general ledger. 

If you select Historical, the system imports the file while offline. This is useful when your 

import file is large. 

8. 
If you want to be notified by email when an offline import is finished, or if errors occur in 

the import process, type your email address in the Email results to this address field. When 

the import is finished, the system sends an email to the address you specify. 

9. 
Click Import. 

A/R Invoice Data 

Best Practices 

• 
Export the data from your other system, including as much of the data as is available. 

• 
Mark any row you want the import to ignore with a # symbol. The system ignores any row 

starting with a # during import. 

• 
Be sure to format the data to match the template precisely. 

Your template’s columns may differ from this documentation, as your template is designed 
around your company’s business needs. Your template may also differ from the documentation if 
your company has chosen not to enable certain features. 

Required Fields 

Each column of the template represents a field in which you can import data. The required fields 

of the template must be filled in before you can import the data. 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID 

• 
CREATED_DATE  

• 
DUE_DATE 

• 
TOTAL_DUE 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE  

• 
LINE_NO

## Importing Assets
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 165*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Assets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Assets > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Assets > Assets > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Fixed Assets > All > Assets / Draft Assets > Import Assets`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Importing asset information into RealPage Accounting adds a new asset record to RealPage 

Accounting’s Accounts Payable and Fixed Assets, and to the Facilities application. 

Importing Historical Assets Information From Facilities into RealPage Accounting 

For every asset record that you want to import into Accounting, fill in the FACILITIES_ASSET_ID 

column with the asset ID from the Facilities application. This tells the system that the asset already 

exists in Facilities, and that it is creating historical asset information. The system will not create a 

new asset record in Facilities. Without the FACILITIES_ASSET_ID column filled in, the system will 

create duplicate records in Facilities. 

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the import template for assets: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Import data menu option. The Import data 

page opens. 

2. 
In the Set up A/P master list, open invoices, and adjustments section, click the Template link 

next to Assets. 

The system either downloads the Assets.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the Assets.xls file and fill in the required asset information: 

• 
ASSET_NAME: Type a descriptive name to identify the asset. 

• 
CATEGORY: Type the name of the asset class or asset category to associate with the 

asset. 

• 
TYPE: Type what kind of asset the asset is; for example, “Air conditioner,” “Ceiling fan,” 

“Clothes washer,” etc. 

---


<!-- Page 166 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

See the Asset types list in Accounts Payable to add and manage asset types. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the ID of the property where the asset is located. 

• 
ASSET_COST: Type the original cost of the asset. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number associated with the invoice. 

• 
FACILITIES_ASSET_ID: If the asset information that you are importing is from the 

Facilities application, type the asset ID from the Facilities application in this field. When 

there is an ID in this field, this tells the system that you are importing historical asset 

information into Accounting.  

4. 
Optionally, fill in additional information and invoice details associated with each asset: 

• 
SERIAL_NUMBER: Type the asset’s serial number. 

• 
MODEL_NUMBER: Type the asset’s model number. 

• 
WARRANTY_NUMBER: Type the asset’s warranty number. 

• 
IN_SERVICE_DATE: Type the date that the asset was placed in service. Typically, this is 

the date the asset began being used; it does not have to be the same as the purchase 

date. 

• 
WARRANTY_START_DATE: Type the date the asset’s warranty coverage begins. 

• 
WARRANTY_END_DATE: Type the date the asset’s warranty coverage expires. 

• 
OUT_OF_SERVICE_DATE: Type the date that the asset was disposed or taken out of 

service. 

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the invoice number associated with the asset, if any. 

• 
INVOICE_DATE: Type the invoice date. 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the ID of the vendor from which the asset was purchased. 

• 
UNIT: Type the unit number where the asset is located. 

• 
DEPARTMENT_ID: Type the ID of the department associated with the asset.  

• 
SALVAGE_VALUE: Type the amount that the asset is estimated to be worth at the end 

of its useful life, when all depreciation is expensed. 

• 
DEPRECIATION_CONVENTION: Type when to start the asset’s depreciation schedule. 

Valid values include: 

• 
P: Start depreciating the asset the month that the asset is placed in service. If you 

leave this field blank, the schedule defaults to this option. 

• 
N: If the asset was placed in service between the 1st and the 15th of the month, 

then start depreciating the asset on the first day of that month. If the asset was 

placed in service between the 15th and the 31st of the month, then start 

depreciating the asset on the first day of the next month. 

• 
M: Always treat the asset as if it started in the middle of the quarter (the quarter 

is determined by the date it was placed in service). Mid-quarter depreciation 

---


<!-- Page 167 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

prevents the asset from exceeding its maximum depreciation for the year. This 

option is applicable only to assets whose asset book is set to depreciate assets on 

a Quarterly basis. Asset books are defined in the asset class. 

• 
QUANTITY: Type the quantity of assets on the invoice. 

• 
CONDITION: Type the condition of the asset. Valid values include: 

• 
N: New 

• 
UG: Used/Good 

• 
UF: Used/Fair 

• 
UP: Used/Poor 

• 
DEPARTMENT: Type the name of the department associated with the asset. 

5. 
Optionally, fill in the opening balances for the financial and tax books associated with the 

asset: 

You can import only the books that match the asset class . If you enter a date and amount 
for the Tax book but the asset class does not support the Tax book, then it will be ignored. 
Likewise, if you do not enter both the opening balance and the thru date, it will be ignored.  

• 
GENERAL_OPENING_BALANCE: Type the opening balance for the “General” asset 

book. 

• 
GENERAL_THRU_DATE: Type the date through which to set the opening balance for 

the “General” asset book. 

• 
TAX_OPENING BALANCE: Type the opening balance for the “Tax” asset book. 

• 
TAX_THRU_DATE: Type the date through which to set the opening balance for the 

“Tax” asset book. 

• 
OTHER1_OPENING_BALANCE: Type the opening balance for the “Other 1” asset book. 

• 
OTHER1_THRU_DATE: Type the date through which to set the opening balance for the 

“Other 1” asset book. 

• 
OTHER2_OPENING_BALANCE: Type the opening balance for the “Other 2” asset book. 

• 
OTHER2_THRU_DATE: Type the date through which to set the opening balance for the 

“Other 2” asset book. 

6. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

---


<!-- Page 168 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Data from the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
On the Import data page, find the Set up A/P master list, open invoices, and adjustments 

section, and then click the Import link next to Assets. 

You can also click the Import assets button in the Asset information list. 

The Import box opens. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button.

## Importing Bank Accounts
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 169*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Bank Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Cash Management > Bank 
Account > Template/Import`


Use the import template that is designed for bank accounts. 

To import bank account data: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Cash Management section, find the Bank Account option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the bank account import template. You can find the file 

in your browser’s default download location. 

5. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

Filling the Template 

1. 
Open the template using a spreadsheet application. By default, the file opens in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in your bank account details. When you are importing new bank accounts, you must 

provide at least the bank name and account ID. If you are updating existing bank account 

information, then you only need to fill in the bank account ID and the fields that you want 

to update. Bank account updates via import apply to both top-level and entity-level 

accounts. 

Some fields in the template may or may not apply depending on whether the account is a 
checking or savings account. Check the information below the column names to see which 
types of accounts each field applies to. 

• 
ACCOUNT_TYPE: Type “Checking” if the bank account is a checking account or 

“Savings” if the bank account is a savings account. 

• 
ACCOUNT_ID: Type the unique identifier for the bank account. 

• 
ACCOUNT_NUMBER: Type the 10-digit bank account number found at the bottom of 

the check. 

• 
BANK_NAME: Type the name of the bank. If you have more than one account at this 

bank, include a description for the account in the name. 

• 
ROUTING_NUMBER: Type the routing number. 

• 
BRANCH_ID: Type the bank branch ID. This is the number found at the top of the 

check, above the date field. 

• 
ADDRESS1, ADDRESS2, CITY, STATE, ZIP, COUNTRY: Type the bank’s address. 

• 
PHONE_NUMBER: Type the bank branch’s phone number. 

---


<!-- Page 170 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
CURRENCY: Type the ISO-4217 currency code that corresponds with the bank 

account’s transaction currency. This column applies only to companies with 

multi-currency enabled. 

• 
GL_ACCOUNT: Type the default bank G/L account number. 

• 
DEFAULT_PAYABLE_JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal in which to record 

payments and transfers out of the account. The default journal is the same as the one 

used for A/P payments. 

• 
DEFAULT_RECEIVABLE_JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal in which to record 

deposits and transfers into the account. The default journal is the same as the one 

used for A/P payments. 

• 
SERVICE_CHARGE_ACCOUNT_LABEL: Type the service charge account label. 

• 
SERVICE_CHARGE_GLACCOUNT: Type the default service charge G/L account for 

reconciliations. During reconciliation, you can enter service charges (and other fees). 

• 
INTEREST_EARNED_ACCOUNT_LABEL: Type the interest-earned account label. 

• 
INTEREST_EARNED_GLACCOUNT: Type the interest-earned G/L account for 

reconciliation. During reconciliation, you can enter interest earned. 

• 
DEPARTMENT_ID: Type the default department ID for G/L posting. If your company 

does not use departments, then this field won’t be in the import template. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the default location ID for G/L posting. Depending on your 

company, a location may be required to enforce balancing associated journal entries. 

• 
ENABLE_FOR_RPVPAYMENTS: Type “T” (true) to allow the bank account to be used for 

RealPage payments or third-party payments. Otherwise, type “F” (false). 

• 
ENABLE_FOR_RPDEBIT_CARD: Type “T” (true) to allow the bank account to be used for 

RealPage Debit Card payments or petty cash (PC) reimbursements. Otherwise, type “F” 

(false). This field is required to process payments and reimbursements. 

• 
DEBIT_CARD_BANK_ACCOUNT_TYPE: Type the bank account type that should be 

refunded for utility reimbursement payments and petty cash (PC) card payments 

through RealPage Debit Cards. Valid values include “Settlement Account”, “Return 

Account”, and “Deposit Account”. 

• 
ACTIVE: Type “T” (true) if the bank account is active or “F” (false) if the bank account is 

inactive. 

• 
COMPANY_NAME: Type the company name to print on checks. 

• 
COMPANY_ADDRESS1, COMPANY_ADDRESS2, COMPANY_CITY, COMPANY_STATE, 

COMPANY_ZIP, COMPANY_COUNTRY: Type the company address to print on checks. 

• 
COMPANY_PHONE: Type the company phone number to print on checks. 

• 
DONT_PRINT_COMPANY_ADDRESS: Type “T” (true) if you want to print the company 

address on checks or “F” (false) if you don’t want to print the company address on 

checks. 

---


<!-- Page 171 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
CHECK_PRINTING_FORMAT: Type the check printing format. Valid values include 

“standard”, “business”, “high security”, and “custom”. 

• 
NEXT_CHECK_NO: Type a starting number for the next check. For each succeeding 

check that you print the number increments by one. 

• 
CHECK_PAPER_FORMAT: Type whether you want to print the check on the top, 

middle, or bottom panel. Valid values include “top”, “middle”, and “bottom”. 

• 
PRINT_DETAIL: Type “T” (true) if you want to add fields to the non-remittance panel of 

the check; otherwise, type “F” (false). These fields include columns for the account, 

department, and location of each line item. You can generate up to 18 line items per 

page in either summary or detail mode. 

• 
DISPLAY_LOCATION: Type whether to print the location ID, location name, or both the 

location ID and the location name in the location column on the check stub. Valid 

values include “id”, “name”, or “both”. 

• 
ADDITIONAL_TEXT: Type the text that you want to appear under the signature line of 

the check. For example, “Void after 60 days.” You can type up to 40 characters. 

• 
PRINT_VENDOR_STUB_DETAIL: Type “T” (true) if you want to add vendor stub 

information when printing checks. Otherwise, type “F” (false). 

• 
ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ALIGNMENT: Type “left” to align the account number on the left 

side of the check, or type “right” to align the account number on the right side of the 

check. 

• 
ACCOUNT_NUMBER_POSITIONING: Type the number of spaces required to position 

the account number on your check if you still need additional adjustment. This is the 

number of spaces to append before or after the bank account portion of the MICR. 

You can enter up to five spaces. 

• 
CHECK_NUMBER_LENGTH: Type the length of the check number in the MICR. This 

determines the number of zeros required to pad the check number. 

• 
REGIONAL_SETTINGS_US_ON_US_SYMBOL: Type “T” (true) if your bank requires the 

ON-US symbol to appear on the MICR line in front of the account number. Otherwise, 

type “F” (false). 

•

the check amount box for CPA member banks. Otherwise, type “F” (false).

## Importing a Budget
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 177*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing a Budget 

It’s often easiest to create a budget using Microsoft Excel or other spreadsheet program. Creating 

a budget in spreadsheet form allows you to upload large volumes of data. The spreadsheet can 

include all account and dimension combinations. 

For consolidated budgets, Performance Analytics does not translate your budget from the 
entity base currency to the consolidated currency. You need to run a global consolidation to do 
the translation for the budget, and then upload the amount into Performance Analytics.  

Permissions 

In general, the ability to import data requires permission to access the Import data option of the 

Company application’s Setup tab. This permission is required even if the import is performed 

outside of the Import data page. 

Workflow 

Uploading a budget from a spreadsheet is a multi-step process:  

1. 
Create a new budget (on page 170) in Performance Analytics and give it a unique Budget 

ID. 

2. 
Download the budget template (on page 170) from the Import data page. 

3. 
Enter your budget data (on page 171) in the spreadsheet. 

The rows in your spreadsheet will refer to the Budget ID that you created in Step 1. 

4. 
Import the spreadsheet (on page 173). 

If you are uploading amounts for a consolidated budget, make sure the amounts are already 
converted into the consolidated currency using your company’s own exchange rate.  

---



### Creating a New Budget and Giving It a Unique Budget ID
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 178*

Creating a New Budget and Giving It a Unique Budget ID 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Budgets`


Before you can upload a budget spreadsheet, you must first create the budget. Clicking Add in 

the Budgets list lets you create a new budget and give it a budget ID. 

1. 
In the Budget ID field, type a unique ID for the budget, such as “Board-approved” or 

“Current Budget.” The budget ID identifies the budget when you are adding budget data or 

including a budget in a report. Before naming your budgets, review the information in Plan 

Your Budgets. 

A best practice is to give the budget an ID that doesn’t reference a particular fiscal year or 

date. Then you can append new time periods to your existing budget. 

2. 
Type a description for the budget to indicate the budget’s purpose in the Description field. 

3. 
Choose whether this is a new budget or if you are copying an existing budget. 

• 
If this is your first budget, select the Create a new budget option. 

• 
If you are using an existing budget as a basis for a new budget, select the Create a 

budget from existing budget and reporting period range option, and then choose 

the budget from the drop-down list. 

4. 
Select the Default Budget check box if this budget will be the default for financial reports. 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Downloading the Budget Template 

Preparing a budget for upload requires that you download the Budget template from the Import 

Data page.  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. You may have to scroll the menu to see this option. 

3. 
Find the Set up General Ledger Transactions section, and then click the Template link in the 

Budgets row. 

The asterisk (*) next to Budgets means that importing budget data updates existing budget 

records. 

4. 
Open the budget template in a spreadsheet application.  

About the Template 

The header line displays information about each field and the data that can be entered in it. 

Each horizontal row in the spreadsheet represents budget detail that combines a G/L account, 

optional dimension-level detail, and the budget amount for each reporting period. You will add a

### Entering Your Budget Data in the Spreadsheet
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 179*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

row for every account and dimension combination that will be budgeted. Budget amounts are 

entered in the Reporting Period columns. 

You can use the budget template to add new budget detail or update existing details. If you 

already have a budget for an Account-Department-Location combination, and if you have the 

same combination in the file you import, the imported data overwrites the existing budget. 

Before you use the Budget template to upload budget data, create a new budget in the RealPage 

Accounting system to which you want to add data. The budget ID must exist before you can add 

it to the template. See Creating a New Budget and Giving It a Unique Budget ID (on page 170). 

Tips for Filling the Budget Template 

• 
BUDGET_ID must already exist in the system.  

• 
ACCT_NO is mandatory and refers to the account being budgeted. 

• 
DEPT_ID and LOCATION_ID are optional and can be empty. If you do use them, they must 

conform to valid IDs in Performance Analytics. 

• 
Other dimensions are also optional. However, if a G/L account is defined as requiring a 

dimension, then the dimension must be used in the budget. 

• 
You can add any number of period columns for which you want budgets. To do so, those 

periods must already exist in the Performance Analytics system and be budgetable periods, 

and the column headers must contain the names of those periods exactly as they appear in 

Performance Analytics. In the field definitions that follow, this field is labeled (BUDGETABLE 

PERIOD 1...n). However, in your upload it would be something like “Month ended January 

2023.” If the period does not exist, the entire file is rejected, and the system sends you an 

email with the errors. 

Entering Your Budget Data in the Spreadsheet 

You can create a large matrix of budget data in a spreadsheet, and then upload it.  

• 
The Budget ID and Account ID are always required.  

• 
You can create detailed budgets using dimensions.  

• 
Each account and dimension combination can have budget data for the selected reporting 

periods.  

• 
Your budget planning determines the level of detail that you should include. 

Sample 

The sample below shows budget data for a company that is including dimensions in its current 

budget. 

The column headings show the field names indicating the data to be entered. Note that fields for 
dimensions are included.

budgeted. 

In this example, there’s a revenue account 4010, and two operating expense accounts, 6005 

and 6010.

Enter any dimension detail that you want to include for this line. 

•

including department, location, project, and item.

Importing Charge Cards 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All> Import Data > Set Up Cash Management > Charge 
Card > Template/Import`


Use the import template that is designed for credit cards. 

To import credit card data: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2.

4.

downloaded file in your browser’s default download location. 

Filling the Template 

1. 
Open the template using a spreadsheet application. By default, the file opens in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required fields for each credit card that you want to import: 

• 
CARD_ID: Type the card number. 

• 
LAST_FOUR_DIGITS_CARD_NUMBER: Type the last four digits of the card number. 

• 
CARD_TYPE: Type the card type. Valid values are: Visa, Mastercard, Discover, American 

Express, Diners Club, Other Charge Card. 

• 
PAYMENT_TYPE: Type Credit or Debit. 

• 
EXPIRATION_MONTH: Type the month that the card expires. Valid values are: January, 

February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, 

December. 

• 
EXPIRATION_YEAR: Type the year that the card expires.  

• 
CREDIT_CARD_OFFSET_ACCOUNT: Type a credit card offset G/L account. The account 

must be defined in the system and conform to primary/sub account specification in 

Company > Company Info. 

• 
DEBIT_CARD_CHECKING_ACCOUNT: Type the checking account ID to use with the 

debit card.  

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the vendor’s unique identifier. 

3. 
Optionally, fill in any of the other columns in the template as needed. 

4. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV).

## Importing Charge Card Transactions
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 186*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Charge Card Transactions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Cash Management > 
Charge-Card Transactions > Template/Import`


Use the import template that is designed for credit card transactions. 

To import credit card transaction data: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Cash Management section, find the Charge-Card Transactions row. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the charge card transaction import template. You can 

find the file in your browser’s default download location. 

5. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

Filling the Template 

1. 
Open the template using a spreadsheet application. By default, the file opens in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required fields for each credit card transaction that you want to import: 

• 
CARD: Type the name of the credit card. The name must match a charge card that is 

defined in Cash Management.  

• 
DATE: Type the transaction date. 

• 
PAYEE_NAME: Type the name of the person being paid.  

• 
TRANSACTION CURRENCY: Type the 3-character abbreviation for the currency in 

which the transaction was conduction, such as USD or CAD. This field is required only 

in multi-currency companies.  

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date of the transaction. This field is required unless you 

provide the exchange rate in the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number. Start with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number associated with the transaction. The account 

number must conform to the primary/sub account specification in Company > 

Company Info. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the transaction. 

• 
PAYOFF_DATE: Type the date that the card will be paid off. This field is required when 

the Payoff field is set to True, (T). 

3. 
Optionally, fill in any of the other columns in the template as needed. 

4. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV).

Importing the Contacts 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Contacts row. 

4. 
Click the Import link. 

5. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the file with your contact data. 

6. 
In the Date format field, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, select a date 

format that you want to use. The system supports 24 date formats.  

7. 
In the File encoding field, leave the setting as auto detect unless you are unable to import 

your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of 

file encoding. 

8. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. The Process offline feature allows the system to process the data when system activity 

is lighter. If you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, do not select the 

Process offline check box.

Importing Contracts

In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, click the Template link 

in the Contracts row. 

The system downloads the template to your local drive. 

Filling the Template File with Your Data 

Open the template using a spreadsheet application and then enter the information. By default, 

the file opens in Excel.

Fill in the required fields for each contract that you want to import:

CONTRACT_ID:  Type the unique identifier of the contract.  

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique location identifier of the entity.

VENDOR_ID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor. 

• 
TOTAL_AMOUNT: Type the amount of the contract.

Open the Company menu.

Select Import data.

In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Contracts row, 

and then select the Import link.  

4. 
In the import box, click the Choose file button, and then find the CSV file. 

5.

## Importing Customer Records
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 195*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Customer Records 

You can quickly update information for multiple customers at once by exporting customer data in 

CSV for Import format, editing the resulting spreadsheet, and then importing your changes.  

A CSV import works well for:  

• 
Updating information for multiple customers at once: Using a CSV import, you can update 

selected data for multiple customers. For example, you can export the Customers list with 

the Email Address field included, add or modify the email addresses in a spreadsheet 

application, and then import your changes.  

• 
Adding new customers to your existing Customers list: Using a CSV import, you quickly add 

new customers without having to create the customers one at a time. Any spreadsheet row 

that contains a unique  

Don’t overwrite existing data with blank data, unless you intend to remove that data from 
your Customers list. For example, if you export the Email Address field and then clear the 
data in the Email Address column of your spreadsheet, existing customer email addresses 
will be deleted when you import the file.  

Using the import and export features on the Customers list, you can: 

• 
Export your Customers list in one of several standard formats (CSV, Excel, Word, PDF) so 

that you can print or use the information in another application. 

• 
Quickly update your Customers list by exporting selected data, making changes, and then 

importing your changes. 

Importing Customers 

You can import new customer information at the top level by uploading a CSV file. Follow these 

steps to import new customer information from an external source. 

1. 
Download a template from the Import Data page (on page 6) 

2. 
Fill the customer template with data 

3. 
Save the template file as a CSV file (on page 14) 

4. 
Import the CSV File 

Downloading the Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Customers > Template`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

---


<!-- Page 196 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of Performance 

Analytics is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
In the Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Customers row.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

Filling In the Customer Template with Data 

You can update information for existing customers. For example, you might correct customer 

addresses or add email addresses for selected customers. You can also add new customers. If the 

Customer ID that you specify doesn’t already exist in the system, a new customer record will be 

created. 

You can include sets of fields for a Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact. The template contains fields for 

this information, but it is not required. 

The Bill-to contact fields have a B_ prefix and the Ship-to contact fields have an S_ prefix. 

If the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact fields are not included, the primary contact information is 

used for the customer. This means that the COMPANY_NAME field, when used for the Bill-to 

contact, would be B_COMPANY_NAME, and the shipping contact would be S_COMPANY_NAME. 

To fill the customer template: 

1. 
Open the file in Excel.  

2. 
Fill the required columns in the customer template: 

• 
CUSTOMER_ID: Type a unique identifier for the customer. If customer sequence 

auto-numbering is enabled, the system completes the Customer ID if you do not 

supply one. (Company > Services: Subscriptions: A/R Preferences). 

• 
CUST_NAME: Type the name of the customer. 

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type the primary contact name. If the contact name already exists, 

you must create the customer manually in the system, or enter a new contact name in 

this file. 

• 
PRINTAS: Type the name of the company as you want it to appear on payments and 

notices. This field is used with the Customer ID field to create the suggested contact 

name, which is the unique contact ID used throughout the system that can’t be edited 

after creation. This is also the name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists. 

---


<!-- Page 197 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the rest of the columns. Refer to the Customers Data Structure (on 

page 191) for a full list of columns. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV (on page 14) format. 

Importing Order of Precedence 

When importing customer records, child records must be imported after parent records. Child 

records that incorrectly reference a parent record can cause your import to fail. For example, if the 

parent record does not exist, or if the parent record references a child record as if it were a parent, 

your import can fail. 

If you include an ACCT_LABEL, the system creates an account label on-the-fly when you import 

your file. 

This means you can’t re-use the same ACCT_LABEL for another customer. 

If you include an ACCT_LABEL, you must also include: 

• 
a GL_ACCTNO that conforms to a primary/sub account specification in Company > 

Setup: Company Info. 

• 
the GL_ACCTNO must point to valid account. 

• 
DELIVERYOPTIONS can be set to online, only if the company subscribes to online 

delivery. 

Customer lists have optional sets of Contact fields for the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact. The fields 

are identical to the required set of primary contact fields, except they have B- and S- prefixes. If 

either the Bill-to and/or Ship-to contact fields are not included, the primary contact information is 

used instead. 

The Don’t Include On Company’s Contact List and G/L Group fields found in the Customer 

Information page are not represented in the template. 

Importing the Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Customers > Import`


1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Customers row in the Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section. 

4. 
Click Import. 

5. 
Click the Choose file button, and then find the CSV file with the customer data. 

6. 
In the Date format field, select the date format that you are using if the CSV file includes 

dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format. 

---

#### Updating Multiple Customer Visibility Records

Updating Multiple Customer Visibility Records 

Performance Analytics allows you to update multiple customer visibility records as a group. 

By exporting the existing customer visibility list to a CSV file, you can quickly update all 

customer’s restrictions in your favorite spreadsheet application. After updating the data, just save 

the file in CSV format again, and import the file right from the Customer visibility list.  

By default, visibility is set to Unrestricted. To restrict customer visibility, you will need a list of 

locations and departments that are allowed to see the customer records you want to restrict.  

The following procedures walk you through each step of the process in detail. 

Exporting the Customer Restrictions List 

To prepare for export: 

1. 
If you haven’t already done so, choose the list view that includes the data you want to 

export.  

2. 
At the top of the Customer visibility list, click the All drop-down menu and then choose the 

name of the view that you previously created.  

If you don’t select a view before exporting the Customer visibility list, your export file will 

include the list of customers and columns that you currently see in the Customer visibility 

list.  

To export the list: 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Choose an export format from the drop-down menu. These are the standard export formats 

available in Performance Analytics: 

---



#### Using CSV Import to Mass Update Customer Restrictions
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 221*



#### Creating the List View that Includes the Data You Want to Export
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 221*

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in Performance Analytics do not have the CSV for import option. 

If the current view of the Customer visibility list contains any fields that can ’t be 
updated through an import process, those fields won’t be included in the export file. 

Using CSV Import to Mass Update Customer Restrictions 

Click each step of the workflow to view the detailed instructions.  

Workflow 

1. 
Create a list view that includes the data you want to export (on page 213). 

2. 
Export the customer restrictions list in CSV for Import format (on page 214). 

3. 
Update the CSV file (on page 215). 

4. 
Import your changes (on page 216). 

Creating the List View that Includes the Data You Want to Export 

To control what gets exported, you can create a custom view of the Customer visibility list that 

includes just the data you want to see.  

To customize a view before exporting: 

1. 
Locate the Manage views drop-down menu at the top of the Customer visibility list, and 

then choose Create New View.  

2. 
On Step 1 of the Create New View wizard, select the columns of data you want to include.  

You can choose from standard customer fields (such as name and ID) and any custom fields 

that you’ve created for your company.  

3. 
Make other changes as needed.  

---

Using the wizard, you can:  

• 
Choose the order in which columns appear.  

• 
Filter the list of customer restrictions, such as filtering for customers who are 

unrestricted, or customers who can be viewed by top level only.  

• 
Choose the sort order for columns, for example, sorting customers by ID or Visibility.  

Exporting the Customer Restrictions List in “CSV for Import” Format 

Before starting this process, we recommend that you create a custom view (on page 213) of your 

Customer visibility list that includes the customers and columns you want to update. That way, 

when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet that’s tailored to the information you want to 

change.  

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Visibility. 

3. 
Choose the list view that includes the data you want to export.  

• 
At the top of the Customer visibility list, click the All drop-down menu and then 

choose the name of the view that you previously created.  

• 
If you don’t select a view before exporting the Customers list, your export file will 

include the list of customers and columns that you currently see in the Customers list.  

If the current view of the Customer visibility list contains any fields that can ’t be updated 
through an import process, those fields won’t be included in the export file.

4. 
Export the Customers list in CSV for Import format.  

The system exports the data to a predefined CSV import template, which you can then open 

and update. 

What’s Next? 

Updating the CSV Template File (on page 215) 

Updating the CSV Template File 

To update the template file: 

1. 
Open the CSV file in a spreadsheet application.  

2. 
Update the data.  

• 
You can update overall restrictions for existing customers as follows:  

Unrestricted customer: As well as the top level, all entities within the multi-entity 

structure can view this customer and post transactions to it.  

Restricted to top-level only: Only the top level of the multi-entity structure can view 

this customer and post transactions to it.  

Restricted customer: Only the chosen locations, location groups, departments or 

department groups within the multi-entity structure can view this customer and post 

transaction to it.  

• 
You can change which locations or departments within the multi-entity structure can 

view selected customers.  

Example 

To set restrictions: 

1. 
Open the CSV file in Excel. 

2. 
To restrict a customer from being fully accessible, change the Visibility column to Restricted. 

3. 
Type the names of the locations and departments that are allowed to see the customer 

record, as follows: 

---

Add the first location or location group to the Location_1 column.  

• 
Add a new column for each location, sequentially numbering the column names: 

Location_1, Location_2, Location_3 

• 
Add the first department or department group to the Department_1 column. 

• 
Add a new column for each additional department as you did for location, sequentially

4.

Importing Your Customer Visibility Changes 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Visibility > Import`


To import customer visibility data: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Visibility. 

3. 
Click the Import button at the top right of the list.  

4. 
Click the Browse button and locate the CSV file you created to import.  

Be sure to specify the email address where results should be sent. If any records fail to 
import, you’ll be notified by email. 

5. 
Select other options as needed.
