#### Importing Departments
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 225*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Departments 

You can import departments by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Departments > Template`


1. 
Download the most recent Departments template from the Import data list. When you get 

your templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been tailored to your 

specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses. See Downloading a 

Template from the Import Data Page (on page 6). 

2. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

3. 
Fill in the import template (on page 7) starting with the required columns in the template: 

• 
DEPT_ID: Type a unique identifier for the department. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
DEPT_NAME: Type a department name of up to 40 characters. 

4. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. 

After you’ve added your data, review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common errors (on page 487) and 

Best practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format. File > Export > CSV (Comma delimited file) 

6. 
In the Set Up Company Master List section, find the Departments row, and then click the 

Import link.  

Importing the Data 

To import the CSV file with department data: 

• 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file you want to import. 

• 
In the Date format field, select the desired date format. 

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the 

selected date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, 

---



#### Departments Data Template
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 226*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

it attempts to discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that 

date format. 

• 
In the File encoding drop-down list, leave this option set to Auto detect unless you’re 

unable to import your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to 

select a different type of file encoding. 

• 
Select the Process Offline check box to import offline. 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much 

processing the system must do on the uploaded data. If you’re not sure how much 

time your upload will take, select Process Offline. When the system completes the 

process, it sends an email to the address you provide in the Email results to this 

address field. The system also sends you any errors that may have occurred in the 

process. If you prefer to wait until the upload process is complete, do not select the 

Process Offline check box. 

• 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. 

• 
This is the email address where the system sends import results and errors. You can 

enter multiple email addresses, separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). RealPage 

highly recommends entering an email address. 

• 
Click the Import button. 

• 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

#### Importing Dimension Relationships
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 228*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Dimension Relationships 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Dimension Relationship`


You can’t export or import an application package that contains standard-to-standard dimension 

relationships. Import or export the package first, then manually create the dimension 

relationships. 

Edit the base dimension to enable autofilling of related objects before you create the 

relationships between the two dimensions. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the import template file for dimension relationships: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. The Import Data page opens. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, click the Template link next to Dimension 

relationships. The system either downloads the Dimension relationship.xls file or prompts 

you to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling In the Dimension Relationship Data 

1. 
Open the Dimension relationship.xls file in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the columns in the template: 

• 
RELATION: Type the desired relationship type. Valid values include:  

• 
Positive Pay Detail: Type this option to associate one vendor to many check 

range details. 

• 
Payment Detail: Type this option to associate one vendor to many payment 

details records. 

• 
Vendor Document: Type this option to associate one vendor to many vendor 

documents. 

• 
Vendor Request: Type this option to associate one vendor to many Vendor 

Requests. 

• 
Payment Format: Type this option to associate many vendors to one payment 

format. 

• 
Vendor: Type this option to associate many vendors to one vendor. 

• 
Contact. Type this option to associate many contacts to one vendor. The contacts 

can be pay-to contacts, return to contacts, 1099 contacts, display contacts, and 

primary contacts. 

• 
DIMENSION1: Type the name of the base dimension. 

• 
DIMENSION1_VALUE: Type the value for the base dimension. 

---


<!-- Page 229 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
DIMENSION2: Type the name of the secondary dimension that is based on the first 

dimension. 

• 
DIMENSION2_VALUE: Type the value for the secondary dimension. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

Importing the Dimension Relationships 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Dimension relationship row. 

4. 
Click the Import link. 

5. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the file with your dimension relationship data. 

6. 
In the Date format field, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, select a date 

format that you want to use. The system supports 24 date formats.  

7. 
In the File encoding field, leave the setting as auto detect unless you are unable to import 

your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of 

file encoding. 

8. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. The Process offline feature allows the system to process the data when system activity 

is lighter. If you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, do not select the 

Process offline check box. 

9. 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. When the system 

completes the import process, it sends an email to the address with either a message about 

the success or failure of the import, including any errors that occurred in the process. 

10. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row in the file that starts with a # symbol.

#### Importing Updated Employee Transaction Data
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 230*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Updated Employee Transaction Data 

You can import employee 1099 transactions into the system by uploading a CSV file with the 1099 

data. You can also update the information manually by selecting the 1099 form type and box for 

the transaction, the employee default, and the 1099 name for the employee. 

Workflow 

• 
Download the Employee 1099 Transaction Update template 

• 
Fill in the template 

• 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 14) 

• 
Import the employee1099 CSV file 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Import Employee Expenses > Employee 
1099 Transaction Update > Template`


To download the Employee 1099 Transaction Update template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Import Employee Expenses section, find the Employee 1099 Transaction Update row, 

and click Template.  

The system either downloads the template file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Employee 1099 Template 

The system ignores a blank in the NAME1099, DEFAULT1099TYPE, and DEFAULT1099BOX fields, 

and does not change the existing data. To delete data, enter the value NULL. 

This upload is different from most others because you are not creating new records. Instead, you 

are updating existing records. 

The upload can retroactively mark existing transactions as eligible for a 1099 for employees you 

specify and for a given time period. Additional fields update the 1099 form type and box, as well 

as the 1099 name. You may update any combination of these fields in a single upload. For 

example, you could update the form type and box, but not the 1099 name and transactions. You 

must include the form type and box as well as the date range for a transaction update. 

The following chart illustrates these variations. For example, say you only want to update the 1099 

name. The first line shows how you enter the NAME1099 field for a given employee. 

You explicitly state that the transactions are not to be flagged as 1099-able by placing an N in the 

UPDATETRANS field. 

---


<!-- Page 231 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

To fill in the employee 1099 template: 

1. 
Open the file in Excel.  

2. 
Fill the required columns in the employee template: 

• 
EMPLOYEEID: Type the unique identifier associated with the employee. 

• 
DEFAULT1099TYPE: Type the 1099 type. Use one of the following values: DIV, INT, 

MISC, R, S, PATR, G  If this field is blank, the system leaves the existing value in place. 

To remove the existing value, type the value NULL. 

This field is required when FORM1099BOX is selected or UPDATETRANS is ‘Y. 

• 
DEFAULT 1099BOX: Type the 1099 box name. It must be a box that is valid for the 

form type. If this field is blank, the system leaves the existing value in place. To remove 

the existing value, type the value NULL. 

This field is required when FORM1099BOX is selected or UPDATETRANS is ‘Y. 

• 
UPDATETRANS: Type Y or N. If you type Y, it retroactively marks the employee’s 

transactions as 1099-able based on date range and Form 1099 Type and Box listed in 

this upload. For CSV-imported bills, you can mark bills as 1099-able if you imported 

them as unpaid or partially paid, but not if you imported them as paid. 

• 
FROMDATE: Type the beginning date of the range to start updating transactions 

beyond that point. Use the format MM/DD/YYYY 

This field is required if transactions are to be updated.  

• 
TODATE: Type the end date of the range to stop updating transactions beyond that 

point. Use the format MM/DD/YYYY. 

This field is required if transactions are to be updated.  

3. 
Add any other optional data to the additional fields in the import template.  

• 
EMPLOYEENAME: Type the name of the employee for reference to help you identify 

correct employees in the list. 

• 
NAME1099: Type the  value to update the field.  

This field is updated only if a value is present. If the value is blank, the system leaves 
the existing value in the system. To remove the existing value, type NULL. 

4. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV).

Importing Employees 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Employees`


You can import employees’ data by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file containing 

data. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Employees > Template`


1. 
Download the most recent Employees template from the Import data list (on page 6). When 

you get your templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been tailored 

to your specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses.  

2. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

3. 
Fill in the required columns in the template using the correct formatting as explained in the 

template. See Filling in Import Templates (on page 7). 

• 
EMPLOYEE_ID: Type a unique identifier for the employee. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type the employee’s contact name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
PRINT_AS: Type the employee name as you want it to appear on documents. 

4. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. Refer to the Employees Data Template (on 

page 230) for a full list of columns. 

After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 

mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common Errors 

(on page 487) and Best Practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

6. 
On the Company menu, click Import data. 

7. 
In the Set Up Company Master List section, find the Employees row, and then click the 

Import link. The Employees import box opens. 

8. 
To import the CSV file with employee data: 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 237*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file you want to import. 

• 
In the Date format field, select the desired date format. 

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the 

selected date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, 

it attempts to discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that 

date format. 

• 
In the File encoding drop-down list, leave this option set to Auto detect unless you’re 

unable to import your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to 

select a different type of file encoding. 

• 
Select the Process Offline check box to import offline. 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much 

processing the system must do on the uploaded data. If you’re not sure how much 

time your upload will take, select Process Offline. When the system completes the 

process, it sends an email to the address you provide in the Email results to this 

address field. The system also sends you any errors that may have occurred in the 

process. If you prefer to wait until the upload process is complete, do not select the 

Process Offline check box. 

• 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. 

This is the email address where the system sends import results and errors. You can 

enter multiple email addresses, separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). RealPage 

highly recommends entering an email address. 

9. 
Click the Import button. 

10. 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

Importing Entities 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > Entities 
> Template/Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Import`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Prerequisites 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. If 

your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

The following permissions are required to import entity data. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Company 
Entities 
List, View, Edit, Add 

You must have permission for each tab that you want to import information into. If you do not 

have permission for a tab, but you do have permissions to view and edit entities, then the tab is 

read-only. 

Application

Downloading the Entities Template 

You must have individual permissions for each tab in the entity record to add or edit information 

on that tab. If you don’t have permission for the tab—but you do have permissions for 

entities—then the information on the tab will be read-only. These tab permissions apply when 

adding entities, importing entities, editing entities, or updating entities via import. 

To download the import template file for entities: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Import data menu option. The Import data page opens. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, click the Template link next to Entities. 

The system either downloads the Entities.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

4. 
Open the Entities.xls file and fill in the required columns in the entity template. 

• 
ENTITY_ID: Type a unique identifier for the entity. The identifier can be alphanumeric 

and up to 20 characters. 

• 
ENTITY_NAME: Type an entity name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
PRINT_AS: Type the name as you want it to appear on documents related to the entity. 

• 
S_PRINT_AS: Type the entity name as you want it to appear on documents related to 

shipping. 

5. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining columns. Refer to the Entities Data Template (on page 

242) for the complete list of columns. 

If the property name on your invoices is slightly different than your entity name in 
Performance Analytics, make sure that you fill in the PROPERTY_NAME column with the 
name that appears on your invoices. During the AI invoice process, the system checks to 
see if the name on the invoice is the same as either the entity name or the property name. 

6. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the Entities 

To import the entity data: 

1. 
On the Import data page, find the Set up company master list section, and then click the 

Import link next to Entities. The Entities import box opens. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file.

#### Updating Entity Information in Bulk via Import
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 267*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Updating Entity Information in Bulk via Import 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > Entities 
> Template / Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Import`


You can update entity information in bulk using the Import feature. The only field that is required 

when updating information in bulk is the Entity ID. Any additional information that you enter into 

the CSV file either adds to or updates existing information. Fields that are left blank do not 

change or overwrite existing information in the entity record. 

You must have individual permissions for each tab in the entity record to add or edit information 
on that tab. If you don’t have permission for the tab—but you do have permissions for 
entities —then the information on the tab will be read-only. These tab permissions apply when 
adding entities, importing entities, editing entities, or updating entities via import. 

Download the Entities Template from the Import Data Page 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information. This is important because: 

• 
Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by Performance Analytics at any time, especially when a new 

version of Performance Analytics is released. This means that an older template might not 

work. 

To download the Entities template from the Import data page: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import data menu option. The Import data page opens. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the row labeled Entities, and then click the 

Template link. 

In addition to standard columns, the system dynamically appends columns for any 
dimensions you’ve enabled and any custom fields and custom objects you’ve created so 
that you can import that information as well. 

4. 
Populate the template with any entity information that you want to add or update. Leave 

the cell blank if you do not want to update that field in the existing entity record. 

You must enter the Entity ID; all other fields are optional. 

5. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

6. 
Close the CSV file. 

---


<!-- Page 268 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Import Updated Data from the Template 

When you have populated the Entities template, import the file back into the system to update 

the entity records. 

To import the CSV file: 

1. 
On the Import data page, click the Import link in the row labeled Entities. The Entities box 

opens. 

You can also import directly from the Entities list itself. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button. 

---



#### Importing Approved Staff Expenses
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 269*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Approved Staff Expenses 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > Staff 
Expenses > Import`


When you import expenses that have already been approved, the system marks the expenses with 

an Approved status. The system creates invoices for the posted expenses. After importing the CSV 

file, these expenses appear in users’ My expenses lists, and posted expense reports appear in the 

Staff expenses list.  

When importing approved expenses, the system automatically posts expenses because expenses 

from P-card vendors have already been approved once. 

To import expenses from the Import data page: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Expense Reports - 

Approved row, and then select Template. The template for approved expenses (on page 

404) downloads to your browser’s default download location.  

Preparing the Data for Importing 

1. 
Export the approved expenses data from your other system. 

2. 
Open the downloaded template (on page 7) in Microsoft Excel or your favorite spreadsheet 

application. 

3. 
Fill in the template with the approved expense data that you want to import. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.  

Do not use leading zeros in ID fields. If you MUST use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
USER_ID: Type the ID of the user who the expense is being submitted for. 

• 
EXP_REPORT_NAME: Type the expense report name. 

• 
DATE_FILED: Type the date that the expenses were filed. The default value is today’s 

date. 

• 
DATE: Type the date. The default value is today’s date. 

• 
EXPENSE_CATEGORY: Type the category of the expense.  

• 
REIMBURSEMENT_TYPE: Type who or what will be reimbursed: Employees, Property, 

or P-card vendor. 

---


<!-- Page 270 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the approved expense. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique identifier of the location associated with the expense.  

5. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns. Many of the valid values differ by company 

because your company configures expenses in your system depending on your business 

needs. See Configuring Expense Reports. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the expense. 

• 
MEMO: Type a description of the expense. 

• 
UNIT: Type the unit number associated with this expense.  

• 
CORPORATE_EXP_REPORT: Type “true” if this is a corporate expense report or type 

“false” if not. Corporate expense reports do not appear in Site View. 

• 
DEPARTMENTID: Type the unique identifier of the department that is associated with 

the expense.  

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_1: Type the segment type associated with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_1: Type the segment value of segment 1 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_2: Type a second segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_2: Type the segment value of segment 2 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_3: Type the third segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_3: Type the segment value of segment 3 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_4: Type the fourth segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_4: Type the segment value of segment 4 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_5: Type the fifth segment type to associate with the expense. 

You can include up to five segment types and values in the import file. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_5: Type the segment value of segment 5 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_CUSTOMERID: Type the unique identifier of the customer that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_VENDORID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_EMPLOYEEID: Type the unique identifier of the employee that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_PROJECTID: Type the unique identifier of the project that is 

associated with the expense report item.

*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 272*

Importing Draft Expenses 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > Staff 
Expenses > Import`


You can import expenses from the Staff expenses page or from the Import data page. This 

procedure describes importing from the Import data page.  

When you add expense data to the import file, add the User ID of the user who incurred the 

expense and the amount. You can also specify the expense report name to associate an expense 

with a specific expense report.  

After importing the CSV file, these expenses appear in users’ My expenses lists. The system sends 

an email message to each user who had expenses in the imported file. The user must add 

additional information, attach any required receipts and invoices, and then submit the expenses 

for approval. 

To import expenses: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Expense Reports - 

Draft row, and then select Template. The template (on page 399) for draft expenses 

downloads to your browser’s default download location.  

Preparing the Data for Importing 

1. 
Export the unapproved, draft expenses data from your other system. 

2. 
Open the downloaded template (on page 7) in Microsoft Excel or your favorite spreadsheet 

application. 

3. 
Fill in the template with the unapproved expense data that you want to import. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.  

Do not use leading zeros in ID fields. If you MUST use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
USER_ID: Type the ID of the user who the expense is being submitted for. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the draft expense. 

5. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns. Many of the valid values differ by company 

because your company configures expenses in your system depending on your business 

needs. See Configuring Expense Reports.

*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 275*

Importing External Commitments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Job Cost > External 
Commitment > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Periodic Tasks > External Commitments > 
Import External Commitments`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Downloading and Filling In the Template 

To download the import template for external commitments: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Import data menu option. 

The Import data page opens. 

2. 
In the Set up job cost section, click the Template link next to External commitment. 

The system either downloads the External Commitment.xls file or prompts you to open or 

save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the External Commitment.xls file and fill in the required information: 

• 
Job name: Type the name of the job to which the commitment applies. Make sure to 

type the job name exactly as it appears in the Jobs list. 

• 
Cost code: Type the cost code to assign to the external commitment. Make sure to 

type the cost code exactly as it appears in the Cost codes list. 

• 
Commitment date: Type the date on which to commit the costs. 

• 
Amount: Type the amount of the cost commitment. 

4. 
Optionally, fill in the following fields: 

• 
Description: Type a brief description for the external commitment. 

• 
PO number: Type the purchase order number associated with the external 

commitment. 

5. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

---


<!-- Page 276 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Data From the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
On the Import data page, find the Set up job cost section, and then click the Import link next 

to External commitment. 

You can also click the Import external commitments button in the Job cost external 

commitments list. 

The Import box opens. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button.

Importing Fees 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set up AP Master List, Open Invoices, 
and Adjustments > Template/Import`


You can import fee data by uploading a CSV file. 

Download the Fees Import Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data.

In the Set up AP master list, open invoices, and adjustments section, find Fees, and then click 

the Template link. The system downloads the fees.xls file to your browser’s default 

download location. 

Fill the Fees File with your Fees Data 

By default, the file opens in Excel.  

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each fee that you want to import: 

• 
FEEID: Type a valid fee identifier. 

• 
FLOCATIONS: Type a location. The location must be defined in the system. 

• 
ENTRYTYPE: Type B if you want the system to create an A/P invoice (bill) or J if you 

want to record a Journal Entry. 

• 
DRACCTID: Type a G/L account that is defined in the system. 

• 
FEETYPE: Type one of these options: P (Percentage), F (Flat Fee), or U (Unit). 

• 
FLATFEEAMOUNT: Type the amount to invoice for a flat fee. 

• 
UNITAMOUNT: Type the amount of the fee to charge per unit. 

• 
UNITCOUNT: Type the number of units at this location. 

• 
AUTOCALCULATE: Type one of the options: C for current month, M for prior month, Q 

for prior quarter, or Y for year-to-date. 

• 
POSTINGDATEAUTO: Type C for current month, or type M for prior month. 

• 
CREATE_AR_INVOICE: Type I to use the default company or type E to use an external 

company. 

2. 
Add any other optional data to the additional fields in the import template. 

3. 
Save the fee import template file as comma delimited (CSV).

The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add

#### Importing Initial Open Items
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 281*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Initial Open Items 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank`


There are three ways to reconcile a checking account: 

• 
Reconcile manually 

• 
Import a file with bank transactions  

• 
Use bank feeds 

Whether you have a BAI file obtained from the bank, or if you have downloaded the bank 

template and filled it with transactions to reconcile, then you can import the file and have the 

system automatically match transactions against the transactions in the system. After the system 

completes automatic matching, you may need to match any remaining transactions that were not 

matched. You may also need to create additional transactions in the system to match what is in 

the bank. 

The system uses two attributes to match checks to transactions entered in the system: check 

number and amount. You can adjust your matches by changing the matching attributes. See 

Defining Matching Attributes. 

After you import a file, you see two tabs on the account reconciliation page: RealPage and Bank. 

You can match transactions from either tab. 

You can upload multiple files for daily or weekly imports. However, make sure you only upload the 
delta (the new transactions) to avoid duplicate bank transactions appearing in the system. 

Downloading the Initial Open Items Template 

RealPage recommends that you download a new blank template from the Import data list 

whenever you import information into the system. However, some templates are not available 

from the Import data list. The Initial open items template is one of these. 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
Select Bank.  

3. 
In the Account to reconcile drop-down list, select an account to reconcile that requires 

initial open items. 

4. 
Select the Initial open items button. 

5. 
Click the Import button. 

6. 
Click the Upload template for initial open items link. The system either downloads the 

InitOpenItems.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s 

settings. 

---

DATE: Type the date of the transaction. The date should be less than beginning 

balance cut off date for the bank account ID provided. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the transaction.  

3. 
Optionally, fill in additional information associated with each transaction: 

• 
Doc No: Type the unique identifier associated with the transaction. 

• 
TYPE: Type the type of transaction. Use one of the following values: 

• 
checkdebit (for bank accounts) 

• 
depositcredit (for bank accounts) 

• 
charge (for credit card accounts) 

• 
payment (for credit card accounts) 

• 
PAYEE: Type the name of the payee. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the transaction. 

4. 
Save the file as a CSV formatted file.

2.

to the Choose File button.

importing.

Leave the File encoding drop-down list set to Auto detect.

You can import intercompany billing data as transaction and line entry data or you can create the 

intercompany billing record and then import line entry data separately.  

This topic describes how to import data for the intercompany billing record that includes both the 

transaction’s header information and the line entry data. For instructions on importing only the 

line entry data, see Importing Intercompany Billing Entries Only (on page 283). 

If the Job cost columns contain data in the import file but the Include job cost option is not 
selected, then the Job name and Cost code columns will not be imported. When the Include job 

cost option is enabled, then the JOB and JOB_COST_DETAIL columns are required. 

To prepare the data for import: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Import data option.  

3. 
Find the Set Up AR Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section. 

4. 
Find the Intercompany Billing row, and then click the Template link. The template 

downloads to the default browser download location.  

5. 
Fill the template with intercompany billing data.  

The required fields include: 

• 
DATE 

• 
TOTAL_AMOUNT 

• 
BILLING_ENTITY 

• 
REVENUE_ACCOUNT 

• 
CURRENCY 

• 
DUE_DATE 

6. 
Optionally, fill in the rest of the intercompany billing data (on page 277). 

7. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

8. 
Import the data. You can import the data from either the Intercompany Billing list or from 

the Import Data page. 

For information on importing intercompany bill entries, see Importing Intercompany Billing 

Records and Entries (on page 283).

Use this procedure to import journal entries when you are using the Data Import wizard to

To create journal entries manually: 

1.

check box blank.

Legacy account associated with the journal entry. If you did not select the Use map check

Continue adding rows as needed.

## About Importing Journal Entries
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 297*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

To import journal entries in bulk using a template: 

1. 
Click the Download journals template link to download the journals CSV template. 

2. 
Populate data into the spreadsheet. 

3. 
Save the spreadsheet in CSV format. 

4. 
In the wizard, click the Choose file button to upload the CSV file back into the system. 

5. 
Click the Create journal entries button to import the journal entries. 

About Importing Journal Entries 

Importing historical G/L data in the form of journal entries allows you to bring past accounting 

activity—typically from a prior system—into your current accounting environment.  

When you bring journal entries from another system into the RealPage Financial Suite, those 

entries represent: 

• 
Past accounting activity 

• 
Closed or prior periods 

• 
Legacy balances 

• 
Historical adjustments 

All of this is, by definition, historical data. 

Imported journal entries are considered historical data when they are loaded from a prior 
system or prior period to preserve accounting history. They are not automatically historical just 
because they were imported. 

Importing historical journal entries ensures that your general ledger reflects a complete financial 

history, supports comparative reporting, and maintains a full audit trail. 

Historical journal entry imports are most commonly used during system migrations or when you 

need to load prior-period activity for reference, reporting, or compliance. 

You can import any external or historical journal entry data into the general ledger. 

Prerequisites 

Before you import journal entries, confirm the following: 

• 
You must have permissions to import data into the General Ledger application. 

• 
The property/entity structure must be already set up. 

• 
The chart of accounts must be configured. 

• 
Create the journals in the General Ledger application that your system needs to 

accommodate the journal entries that you are importing.  

• 
Accounting periods and books must be open or available for posting. 

---


<!-- Page 298 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
A final trial balance or legacy journal detail must have been approved. 

• 
Performance Analytics recognizes debits as positive numbers and credits as negative 

numbers. Each journal entry must net to zero in order to balance. The system does not 

include accounts with zero (0) balances. 

• 
Save a backup copy of the source data. 

Best Practices 

• 
Test in a non-production environment first. 

• 
Import a small sample batch before the full load. 

• 
Separate historical conversion data from live operational entries. 

• 
Use clear batch naming conventions, such as HIST-CONV-YYYYMM. 

• 
Keep a detailed mapping and reconciliation workbook. 

Order of Precedence 

Import parent records before you import child records. Child records that incorrectly reference a 

parent ID fail to import. For example, when you try to import a child record and its parent record 

does not exist, the child record import will fail. 

Import into Any Journal 

You can import journal entries into any of these journals: 

• 
G/L journals 

• 
GAAP (Compliance) 

• 
Tax 

• 
User-defined books 

• 
Adjustment journals 

• 
Statistical adjusting entries 

• 
Any custom journal 

Where to Import 

You can import journal entries from three places in the system: 

1. 
From your Journal Entries list in the General Ledger application. 

2. 
With the Data Import wizard in the Company application. 

3. 
From the Import Data page of the Company application. 

From the Import Data page, you can:  

• 
Import account beginning balances into multiple journals 

Use the G/L Journal Entries upload to import account beginning balances into multiple 

journals with one uploaded file.  

• 
Import Account Beginning Balances  

---


<!-- Page 299 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Import into only one journal with one file. 

The Create link for both General Ledger Journal Entries and Account Beginning Balances 

display the same application page, General Ledger: Transaction. In addition, both always 

contain the same number of records. 

Importing Manually Versus Using the Data Import Wizard 

You can either import the journal entries using the Data Import wizard or you can import the 

journal entries manually. Follow the instructions based on whether you are using the Data Import 

wizard or not: 

• 
Use the Data Import wizard to import journal entry data (on page 288) 

• 
Import journal entries manually 

Importing Offline 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much processing the 

system must do to the data. When in doubt, select the Process offline option on the import utility 

page. 

When the offline process is complete, the system sends an email to the address you entered in 

the Import Company Information dialog (where you imported your file). 

RealPage recommends selecting Process offline when importing CSV files, and then provide your 
email address. If your import fails, the system notifies you, and sends the failed records to your 
email. 

---



## Importing Journal Entries
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 300*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up General Ledger Transactions > 
General Ledger Journal Entries > Template/Import`


Use this procedure to import historical journal entries from an external accounting system into 

RealPage Accounting and you are not using the Data Import wizard. If you are using the Data 

Import wizard, see Importing External and Historical Journal Entries (on page 288). 

Downloading the Template 

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
In the Set Up General Ledger Transactions section, find the General Ledger Journal Entries 

option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

Filling In the Template 

Dates 

Typically, the Date is the next day after you close your old accounting system and start a new set 

of books in the system. In the event that you do not enter a date, the default is today. The choice 

of date is important: for example, if you choose to enter a date of two fiscal years ago because 

you want to be able to print comparative financial statements, you must then make Journal 

entries for the ending G/L balances for all of the periods between your starting balance date and 

the date you actually begin using Performance Analytics. 

If you are uploading historical transactions, make sure that your starting balances contain these 

uploaded transactions, and set the date to that date. 

If you find you have set the wrong starting date for your G/L balances, you can clear the 

transactions from the Import data page, and then start again. 

Department and Location 

Because G/L Transactions contain fields for both department and location, you can enter as many 

unique G/L transaction department/location combinations as you need. DEPT_ID and 

LOCATION_ID must refer to a valid department and location. 

Line Items 

The uploaded file must contain a number in either the DEBIT or CREDIT field. One or the other is 

required. For example, if you do not have a debit amount, you must have a credit amount. You 

---


<!-- Page 301 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

can import negative numbers for either, in which case a negative debit amount is treated as a 

credit, and a negative credit is treated as a debit. 

The LINE_NO must be unique per journal entry and per journal. For example, Summary 1 might 

contain line numbers 1-20, Summary 2 1-44 and so on. For more information on line numbers, 

see Importing Data with Line Numbers (on page 16). 

To fill in the template: 

1. 
Open the template in a spreadsheet application. 

2. 
Fill in the required fields in the template: 

• 
JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DATE: Type the date of the journal entry. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of up to 80 characters. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number, starting with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number to associate it with the journal entry. 

• 
DEBIT: Type the debit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

CREDIT field. 

• 
CREDIT: Type the credit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

DEBIT field. 

• 
SOURCEENTITY: Type the name of the entity. This value is required when the option to 

automatically create inter-entity transactions is enabled for journal entries and the 

journal entry is not balanced by location. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date. This field is required unless you provide a value in 

the EXCHANGE_RATE column. 

3. 
Optionally, fill in any of the remaining columns. Refer to the template itself for more 

information about the additional data that you can import. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

5. 
After you’ve entered your data, look through the file for any of the common issues (on page 

487) that imports can have. 

---

VALIDATION STEPS 

 Validate source data 

•

• 
Remove duplicate, incomplete, or unapproved entries. 

• 
Confirm debits equal credits for each batch or journal. 

• 
Standardize date formats, account numbers, and property codes. 

• 
Verify all referenced accounts and segments already exist in RealPage. 

Map legacy data to RealPage fields 

• 
Compare each source column to the required RealPage import fields. 

• 
Document any field transformations. 

• 
Convert legacy account numbers or business units where needed. 

• 
Confirm whether amounts should be imported as detail journals, monthly summaries, 

or beginning balances. 

Perform pre-import checks 

Review a sample of entries for accuracy. 

Confirm: 

• 
Valid posting dates 

• 
Open periods 

• 
Balanced entries 

• 
Valid account combinations 

• 
Correct sign conventions 

• 
Have accounting leadership or the conversion lead approve the file before loading it. 

You are ready to import your file to your system.

### Importing Data with Line Numbers
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 306*



### Journal Entries Template
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 306*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Data with Line Numbers 

Some types of data have line numbers, such as G/L journal entries. 

In the following example, note how the line numbers (LINE_NO) are constructed. While this 

example is taken from a G/L Journal Entry import, it is illustrative of any import that requires line 

numbers. 

Notice that both Batch1 and Batch2 have four line numbers, and the numbering for each batch 

starts over at 1. 

Journal Entries Template 

Required Fields 

The required fields of the template must be filled in before you can import the data. 

• 
JOURNAL 

• 
DATE 

• 
DESCRIPTION 

• 
LINE_NO 

• 
ACCT_NO 

• 
DEBIT - Required if a credit amount is not present. 

• 
CREDIT - Required if a debit amount is not present. 

• 
SOURCEENTITY - Required only when the option to auto-create inter-entity transactions is 

enabled for journal entries and the journal entry is not balanced by location. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE - Required unless you provide the EXCHANGE_RATE. 

Below is an explanation of available columns: 

• 
JOURNAL: Required. This is a code of up to four characters that represents the journal. 

• 
DATE: Required. This is the date of the journal entry. It defaults to the current date. 

---


<!-- Page 307 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
REVERSEDATE: This is the date on which to reverse the transaction. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Required. This is a description of the transaction. You can use up to 80 

characters including alphanumeric characters and the underscore. 

• 
REFERENCE_NO: This column contains a reference number. You may not have duplicate 

numbers within any company. In MEGA companies, two entity companies may use the same 

number. 

• 
LINE_NO: Required. These are the line numbers on the left side of the transaction area. Start 

with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Required. This column fills in the Account field. You can enter any values, but 

they must conform to primary/sub account specification that is defined in Company > 

Setup: Company Info.  

• 
LOCATION_ID: This is the unique identifier of a location. The ID must correspond to a valid 

location in the system. 

• 
DEPT_ID: This is the unique identifier of a department. The ID must correspond to a valid 

department in the system. 

• 
DOCUMENT: This is a document name. The name can have up to 30 characters. 

• 
MEMO: This is a note associated with the journal entry. The note can have up to 1,000 

characters. 

• 
DEBIT: Required if a credit amount is not present. This column contains the debit amount. 

The amount can have up to 38 digits, with 2 decimal places. A negative number is treated as 

a credit. 

• 
CREDIT: Required if a debit amount is not present. This column contains the credit amount. 

The amount can have up to 38 digits, with 2 decimal places. A negative number is treated as 

a debit. 

• 
SOURCEENTITY: Required only when the option to auto-create inter-entity transactions is 

enabled for journal entries and the journal entry is not balanced by location. This column 

fills in the Source entity field. It must correspond to a valid location in the system. 

• 
CURRENCY: This column contains the currency abbreviation, such as USD or EUR. Leave the 

column blank to default to the base currency of the entity. Fill in this column only in 

multi-currency companies. This field defines the transaction currency. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Required unless you provide the EXCHANGE_RATE. Fill in this column 

only in multi-currency companies. This column determines the exchange rate as of this date. 

The value defaults to todays date. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_TYPE_ID: This column defaults to the RealPage Daily Rate. Fill in this column 

only in multi-currency companies.  

• 
EXCHANGE_RATE: This column defaults to the exchange rate of the CURRENCY on the 

EXCH_RATE_DATE for the EXCH_RATE_TYPE. Fill in this column only in multi-currency 

companies. This value overrides the default exchange rate, which is the product of the 

CURRENCY, EXCH_RATE_DATE and EXCH_RATE_TYPE. 

---


<!-- Page 308 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
STATE: This column contains Draft or Posted. You can edit the value only when the state is 

set to Draft. If left blank, the state will be set to Posted. 

• 
ALLOCATION_ID: This column must contain a valid allocation. After importing, this value 

cannot be changed. 

• 
BILLABLE: This column contains T or F. The default value is F.  

Dependencies are CUSTOMER and ITEM. 

• 
UNITNUM: This column contains the unit key value. The value must be a number from 0 to 9 

digits.  

• 
JOB_NAME: This column contains a job name. The job name field is associated with the job 

cost application.  

• 
COST_CODE: This column contains a cost code. This field is associated with the job cost 

application.  

• 
CF_GLENTRY_WSTOKEN: This column contains a web service token. 

• 
CF_GLENTRY_PMCID: This column contains a PMC ID. 

• 
CF_GLENTRY_SITEID: This column contains a site ID. 

• 
CF_GLENTRY_SUMID: This column contains a summary ID. 

•

to import job cost history data into the Job Cost Activity list. 

Download the Job Cost History Import Template

Select Import data.

In the Set up Job Cost section, find Job Cost History, and then click the Template link. The 

system downloads the Job Cost History.xls file to your browser’s default download location. 

Fill the Job Cost History File with Your Data

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each historical job cost record that you want to import: 

• 
JOB NAME: Type the name of the job. 

• 
COST CODE: Type the cost code associated with the job. 

• 
INVOICE NUMBER: Type the invoice number associated with the job. 

• 
DATE: Type the date of the job. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount allocated for the job. 

• 
VENDORID: Type the unique identified associated with the vendor doing the job. 

• 
VENDOR NAME: Type the name of the vendor that is doing the job. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the job. 

2. 
Save the template file as comma delimited (CSV). 

Importing Historical Job Cost Data

## Importing a Job Budget
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 325*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing a Job Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Budgets by Job`


When you add a new job, the system automatically creates empty budgets for each job cost code. 

You can export the list of budgets to a CSV file and then re-import the file with the budget details 

instead of entering each cost code budget manually. 

You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 
status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 
information, see Adding a Budget Change Order. 

To import a cost code budget: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, select the Budgets by job link next to the desired job. 

The (Job Name) - Budgets page opens with a list of budget details for each of the job’s cost 

codes. 

2. 
On the Budgets page, click Export budgets template. 

• 
If the job type includes segments, click Budget to start the download process. 

• 
If the job type does not include segments, the system immediately starts the 

download process. 

The system either downloads the chartexport-(job name).csv or prompts you to open or 

save the chartexport-(job name).csv file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the chartexport-(job name).csv file. 

The file automatically provides information for some fields: 

• 
JOB NAME: This is the name of the job. 

• 
COST CODE: This is the code of the cost code. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: This is a description of the cost code. 

4. 
In the BUDGET column for each budgeted cost code, enter the budget amount of that cost 

code. 

For all cost codes that do not have a budget for the job, leave the BUDGET column as “0”. 

The example below shows a cost code budget import list. 

---


<!-- Page 326 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as.  

6. 
In the Save as box, use the Save as type drop-down list to select “CSV (comma delimited) 

(*.csv).” 

7. 
Change the File name or location as needed, and then click Save. 

8. 
On the (Job Name) - Budgets page, click Import. The system opens the Import budget 

information box. 

9. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

10. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

11. 
Click Done. 

12. 
If you are adding unit- or segment-level budgets, you must add those budgets separately. 

For more information, see Importing a Job Segment Budget (on page 323). If you are not 

tracking segment-level budgets for the job, you can skip this step. 

---



## Importing Job Budgets by Month
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 327*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Job Budgets by Month 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Jobs > Budgets by Month`


Use this process to import job budgets on a monthly basis to provide more granular reporting. 

You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 
status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 
information, see Adding a Budget Change Order. 

To import a monthly job budget: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, select the Budgets by month link next to the desired job. 

The Budget by month page opens. 

2. 
In the Select job drop-down list, select the job for which you are importing a budget. 

The Begin date and Completion date - required fields must be defined for the job before 
you can continue. 

3. 
Click the Download budgets by month template link. 

The system either downloads the CSV file or prompts you to open or save the CSV file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

4. 
Open the (Job Name) Monthly Budget.csv file. 

The template automatically populates data for some of the fields based on the job you 

selected: 

• 
Cost code: This is the cost code number and description. 

• 
CO#: This is the change order number for the corresponding cost code. If a budget 

change order was submitted, then an additional row appears for the cost code with 

the budget changes. Change orders are listed sequentially under the cost code’s 

original budget. For example, if you have three change orders, then three rows will 

appear under the original budget as CO# 1, 2, and 3. 

You do not need to make changes to this column in the template. 

• 
BUDGET: This is either the total amount originally budgeted for the cost code or the 

budget change amount. 

A positive amount in the BUDGET column is added to the original budget. A negative 
amount is subtracted from the original budget. 

5. 
In the monthly reporting period columns, fill in the monthly budget amounts for each cost 

code as needed. 

---


<!-- Page 328 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The columns correspond with the Begin date and Completion date - required fields in the 
job record. For example, if the job begins on 2/15 and ends on 5/31, then a column appears 
for each month during that time period (February, March, April, May). 

6. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

7. 
On the Budget by month page, click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file to 

import it back into the system. 

A table appears with the imported budget information. Header accounts (cost codes that 

did not have a WIP account) do not appear in the table. 

8. 
Click Done. 

After you’ve imported a job’s budget, you can return to the Budget by month page to 

manually edit or update budget amounts. If the budget is locked, then you have to submit a 

change order to edit the budget. 

---



## Importing Job Cost or Replacement Reserve Draws
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 329*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Job Cost or Replacement Reserve Draws 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > All > Search & Find > 
Draw Workbench > Import Draws`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the import template for job cost and replacement reserve draws: 

1. 
In the Company application, click the All tab, and then click the Import data menu option. 

The Company setup checklist page opens. 

2. 
In the Set up Job Cost section, click the Template link next to Draw. 

The system either downloads the Draw.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the Draw.xls file and populate the draw information: 

• 
Job/Reserve name: Type the name of the job or replacement reserve to which the 

draw applies. Make sure it matches the name of the job or reserve as it appears in the 

Jobs list or Reserves list, respectively. 

• 
Funding source: This field applies only to job cost draws. Type the primary funding 

source of the draw. Make sure it matches the name of the funding source as it appears 

in the Funding source list for job cost. 

This also determines the draw model of the draw.  

• 
Funding source option: This field applies only to job cost draws. Type one of the 

following values: 

• 
Single source: This option allocates the full draw to one funding source. 

• 
Multiple sources: This option allocates the draw to funding sources by line item 

or applies individual line items to multiple funding sources. 

• 
Multiple sources allocated by percent: This option allocates the draw to funding 

sources based on the percentages entered on the Job information page. 

---


<!-- Page 330 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Multiple sources allocated by amount: This option allocates the draw to funding 

sources based on specific amounts. 

• 
Draw name: Type the draw name. 

• 
Draw number: Type the draw number. 

• 
Draw date: Type the date of the draw. 

• 
Additional jobs: This field applies only to job cost draws. Type the names of any 

additional jobs in the draw, separated by commas. Make sure each job matches the 

name of the job as it appears in the Jobs list. 

4. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

Importing Data From the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
On the Company setup checklist page, find the Set up Job Cost section, and then click the 

Import link next to Draw. 

You can also click the Import draws button on the Draw workbench page. 

The Import box opens. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button. 

---

Importing a Job Segment Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves > All > Search & Find > Job Segment Budgets > 
Import Job Segment Budgets`


Before you can import or add segment budgets: 

• 
The job type of the job must use a cost structure with at least four levels of definition. For 

more information, see Adding, Duplicating, or Editing a Cost Structure. 

• 
The cost code(s) must allow segment-level tracking. For more information, see Adding a 

Cost Code. 

• 
You must assign units to the job. For more information, see Editing a Job. 

• 
You must add cost code budgets. For more information, see Importing a Cost Code Budget 

(on page 317). 

• 
You can add, import, or edit budgets only for jobs in the Pending or Active status. If the job 

status is Active (budget locked), you must instead add a budget change order. For more 

information, see Adding a Budget Change Order. 

• 
On the import spreadsheet and Job segment budget page, the system provides the cost 

code levels, but not cost code descriptions. As a reference, you can export the cost code list 

for the job type of the job whose budgets you plan to enter. 

To import a segment budget: 

1. 
In the Jobs list, select the Budgets link next to the desired job. 

The (Job Name) - Budgets page opens with a list of budget details for each of the job’s cost 

codes. 

2. 
Click the Export budgets template button, and then select the Units budget link.  

The system either downloads the chartexport-(job name)-segment.csv or prompts you to 

open or save the chartexport-(job name)-segment.csv file, depending on your browser’s 

settings. 

The Units budget template allows you to upload budgets for individual job segments or 
units. However, we recommend that you use the Budgets template to import a job budget 
(on page 317 ) first, and then when you add units to the job, the system will automatically 
create a budget per cost code per unit in the Job segment budgets list. 

3. 
Open the chartexport-(job name)-segment.csv file. 

The file automatically provides information for some fields: 

• 
JOB NAME: This is the name of the job. 

• 
COST CODE: This is the code of the cost code.  

---


<!-- Page 332 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The file provides one set of all cost codes available for the job. To import cost codes 

for multiple units at a time, copy this list for each unit you are entering budgets for. 

4. 
For each segment-level budget, enter the required information: 

• 
UNIT: Enter the unit Number. 

• 
BUDGET: Enter the budget amount of that cost code for that specific unit. You can 

enter one budget per cost code for each unit. 

For all cost codes that do not have a budget for the job, enter a budget of “0”. 

The example below shows a segment budget import list. 

5. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as.  

6. 
In the Save as box, use the Save as type drop-down list to select “CSV (comma delimited) 

(*.csv).” 

7. 
Change the File name or location as needed, and then click Save. 

8. 
In the Applications menu, select Job Cost, and then select the All tab. 

9. 
In the Search & find section, click Job segment budgets. 

10. 
On the Job segment budgets page, click Import job segment budgets.  

The Import job segment budgets box opens. 

11. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

12. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

13. 
Click Done.

## Importing Journals
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 333*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Journals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


The system can automatically import default journals based on your company’s accounting 

method. 

Importing Default Journals 

To import default journals: 

1. 
Open the Company application. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set up General Ledger transactions section, find Journal, and then click the Default 

link. 

The Create default journals box opens. Journals will be imported based on the accounting 

method you have selected  

4. 
Click the Create button. 

The system begins importing the default journals. The journals that are imported depend on 

which accounting method your company uses: single-book (either Accrual or Cash) or 

dual-book (Accrual and cash). See below for a list of journals imported for each method.  

• 
If the import is successful, then the Import success notification box will appear with a 

confirmation message. 

• 
If the import is unsuccessful, then the Import error notification box will appear with 

an error message. You will receive an email notification with an explanation of the 

error(s). There will also be a link to download a CSV file with the error details. 

5. 
Click Done to close the box. 

Default Journals for Single-Book Companies 

If your company uses the Accrual or Cash accounting method, then the system will import the 

following default journals: 

• 
ARJ—Accounts Receivable Journal 

• 
APJ—Accounts Payable Journal 

• 
CDJ—Cash Disbursements Journal 

• 
GJ—General Journal 

• 
PYRJ—Payroll Journal 

• 
CRJ—Cash Receipts Journal 

• 
OBJ—Opening Balance Journal 

---


<!-- Page 334 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Default Journals for Dual-Book Companies 

If your company uses the Accrual and cash accounting method, then the system will import the 

following default journals: 

• 
ARJA—Accounts Receivable Journal (Accrual) 

• 
ARJC--Accounts Receivable Journal (Cash) 

• 
APJA—Accounts Payable Journal (Accrual) 

• 
APJC—Accounts Payable Journal (Cash) 

• 
CDJ—Cash Disbursements Journal 

• 
GJ—General Journal 

•

•

•

indicators. The system opens the Key Performance Indicators box.

Import your file into the system. See Importing the CSV file (on page 24) for more

## Importing Loan Schedules
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 339*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Loan Schedules 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Debt Maintenance`


To import loan records into the Debt Maintenance list: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select Debt Maintenance. 

3. 
Download the template by clicking the Template button. 

4. 
Open the downloaded file in Excel.  

5. 
Fill the template with the loan data that you want to import. 

• 
Loan_ID: This field must contain a unique loan identifier. 

• 
PAYMENT_NO: Type the unique number associated with the payment, up to 4 

characters. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date that the loan payment was made. 

• 
GL_DATE: Type the date that the payment was posted to the general ledger. 

• 
DUE_DATE: Type the date that the payment was due.  

• 
Line item #1 on the bill: Type a non-zero number. Type the number with a leading 

dash to a designate negative number. 

• 
Status: Type H for Historical or P for Pending. 

6. 
Optionally, fill in any of the non-required columns of the template.  

7. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 14). 

8. 
Import the file (on page 24). 

9. 
Click the Import button. The Loan Schedule box opens. 

10. 
Click the Choose File button, find the CSV file with the data that you want to import, and 

double-click it. 

11. 
If the data in the CSV file includes dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format, select the date 

format used in the data that you are importing. 

12. 
Leave the File Encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

13. 
If your import box has a Process offline check box, you can select it to process the import 

offline. Select this option for large files. 

14. 
In the Email results to this address field, type the email address where you want the system 

to send import results and error data. 

---

To understand the import process, it’s important to understand the columns in the loan schedule 

template. Below is an explanation of available columns and the impact they have in the automatic 

A/P invoice creation process. 

LOAN_ID: 
This is the unique identifier of the loan. The system uses the ID to link 

the payment to the loan. 

Required: Yes 

PAYMENT_NO 
The value must be unique for each loan payment. 

Four characters maximum 

Required: Yes

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

BILL_NO 
The system uses this value to populate the Invoice number field on 

the system-created A/P invoice. If the BILL_NO is blank, the system 

automatically creates an invoice number upon creating the 

system-created A/P invoice. The system-generated invoice number is 

created in the following format: <Payment number - Loan number>. 

Optional.  

30 characters maximum. 

CREATED_DATE 
The scheduler uses this value to determine if the system should create 

an A/P invoice or not. The scheduler creates A/P invoices for payments 

containing a CREATED_DATE less than or equal to the current date. It 

also uses this value to populate the Date field on the A/P invoice. 

Required: Yes 

GL_DATE 
The system uses this value to populate the G/L posting date field on 

the system created A/P invoice.  

If your system does not have the G/L posting date field enabled, the 
GL_DATE in the loan schedule template should equal the 
CREATED_DATE. 

Required: Yes 

DUE_DATE 
The system uses this value to populate the Due date field on the 

system-created A/P invoice. 

Required: Yes 

PRINCIPAL 
The system uses this value to populate the principal line item on the 

system-created A/P invoice. 

Required: Yes 

INTEREST 

ESCROW 

OTHER 1-7 

The system uses these values to populate the Amount fields on the 

line items for the system-created A/P invoice.  

You must, at a minimum, have a G/L account for the desired line items 
if you are importing amounts for their corresponding columns. 

Required: No

STATUS 
The scheduler uses this value to determine if the system should create 

an A/P invoice or not. Applicable statuses include: 

• 
Historical: The system does not create A/P invoices for 

payments with a Historical status. These payments appear on 

the Loan schedule list only. 

• 
Pending: The system creates A/P invoices for payments with a 

Pending status on the CREATED_DATE specified for the 

payment.
