Importing Location Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Location Groups`


This import allows you to add new location groups. 

Workflow for Importing Location Groups 

• 
Download the location groups template. 

• 
Fill the template with location group data. 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the file. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Location group row, and then click the Template link on the row. The system either 

downloads the template to your browser’s default download folder, or prompts you to open 

or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template  

To fill in the template with your data: 

1. 
Open the template file in your spreadsheet application. 

2. 
For each location group, add the required information: 

• 
LOC_GROUP_ID: Type a unique identifier for the location group. 

• 
LOC_GROUP_NAME: Type a name for the location group. 

• 
MEMBERS: Type the names of entities that are members of the location group. 

3. 
Optionally, add data in any of the remaining columns. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the location group. 

• 
LOC_GROUP_CONTACT: Type the name of an existing valid contact name. 

• 
PRIVATE: Type true if you want the location group to be private. Otherwise, type false. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the CSV File 

1. 
Return to the Import Data list, and then click the Import button on the Location groups 

row. 

2. 
In the Import box, click the Choose file button, and select the CSV file that you updated 

with location group data.

## Importing Locations
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 346*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Locations 

You can import locations by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file containing 

data. 

Downloading the Template 

When you download templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been 

tailored to your specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses.  

1. 
Open the Company menu.  

2. 
Click the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Locations row, and then click the 

Template link. 

The system either downloads the Locations.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling In the Locations Template 

Add your data using the correct formatting as explained in the template.  

1. 
Open the template in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type a unique identifier for the location. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
LOCATION_NAME: Type a location name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
START_DATE: Type the start date related to the location.  

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type a contact name. This column is required if the contact is 

specified. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. 

4. 
After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 

mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common errors 

(on page 487), Best practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

---

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format [File > Export > CSV (Comma delimited file)]. 

6. 
Import the location data’s CSV file (Company > All > Import Data > Locations > Import). 

7. 
In the Date format field, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, select a date 

format that you want to use. The system supports 24 date formats.  

8. 
In the File encoding field, leave the setting as auto detect unless you are unable to import 

your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of 

file encoding. 

9. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. The Process offline feature allows the system to process the data when system activity 

is lighter. If you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, do not select the 

Process offline check box. 

10. 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. When the system 

completes the import process, it sends an email to the address with either a message about 

the success or failure of the import, including any errors that occurred in the process. 

11. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row in the file that starts with a # symbol. 

12. 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

## Importing Manual Payments
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 357*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Manual Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Manual Payments > Import`


You can import manual payments at the entity level or the top level. When you import manual 

payments for entity-level bank accounts at the top level, the system creates entity-level payment 

records. 

To import manual payments: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, select the Manual Payments option. 

3. 
Click the Import button. 

4. 
Download the import template by clicking the Download template link. 

Filling the Template 

The system does not import the data of any row that starts with a # symbol. 

1. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
PAYMENT_METHOD: Type one of the following: Check, Record Transfer, Cash, or 

Credit Card. 

• 
BANK_ACCT_ID: Type a valid bank account number. This field is required when the 

Payment Method is set to “Printed Check,” “EFT,” or “Cash.” 

• 
CONFIRMED_CHECK: Type “TRUE” if you want the system to import the payments as 

confirmed checks. Otherwise, type “FALSE.” This field is required when the Payment 

Method is set to “Printed Check.” 

• 
PAID_DATE: Type the date of payment. 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor that was paid. 

• 
DOC_NO: Type the reference number associated with the payment, such as the check 

number. This field is required when the Payment Method is set to “Printed Check.” 

• 
CREDIT_CARD_ID: Type the credit card number. This field is required when the 

Payment Method is set to “Credit Card.” 

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the A/P invoice number associated with this payment. 

• 
TOTAL_TRX_AMOUNT: Type the total amount of the transaction. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number of the item being paid for. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type a G/L account number. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount expressed in the base currency. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique number of the location associated with the payment. 

2. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns:  

---


<!-- Page 358 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
BANK_GLACCOUNT_NO: Type a bank G/L account to associate with this transaction. 

• 
PAY_TO: Type the name of a contact. The contact must be defined in the system. 

• 
MEMO: Type a note about the payment. 

• 
DEPT_ID: Type the unique number of the department associated with the payment. 

• 
UNIT_NUM: Type the number of the unit associated with the payment. 

• 
BASECURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or EUR for the 

base currency. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. This field is 

required for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. Locations in 

line items must use the same base currency. 

• 
CURRENCY: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code for the currency used for 

this transaction.  

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date for the exchange rate. 

• 
EXCH_RATE_TYPE_ID: Type the exchange rate type. 

• 
EXCHANGE_RATE: Type the exchange rate used for this transaction. 

• 
AP_SEGMENTTYPE_1: Type the segment type to associate with the transaction. 

• 
AP_SEGMENTVALUE_1: Type the value of the segment to associate with the 

transaction. 

You can include up to four segment types and values in the import file. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the Data 

1. 
Click the Import button on the Manual Payment page. 

2. 
Click the Choose files button, and then select the file that you want to import. 

3. 
Click Open. 

The file you import must be in CSV format. 

4. 
If your data contains dates, then in the Date format field, select the date format used by the 

data that you are importing. 

5. 
Leave the File encoding field set to the default status, Auto detect. 

6. 
Select the Process offline check box to have the system import the data with the least 

impact to system processing speed. 

7. 
To have the system send an email when an offline import is finished or when errors occur, 

type your email address in the Email results to this address field. You can enter multiple 

email addresses; separate each address by a semicolon or comma. 

8. 
Click the Import button. 

9. 
Repeat the process for each bank account/payment type combination. 

---

## Importing Other Receipts
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 362*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

You can include up to ten segment types and values in the import file. 

Importing Other Receipts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Cash Management > Other 
Receipts > Template/Import`


Use the import template that is designed for other receipts. 

To import other receipts data: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Cash Management section, find the Other Receipts row. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the other receipts import template. You can find the 

file in your browser’s default download location. 

5. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

Filling the Template 

1. 
Open the template using a spreadsheet application. By default, the file opens in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required fields for each receipt that you want to import: 

• 
RECEIPT_DATE: Type the date on the receipt. 

• 
PAYMETHOD: Type one of the payment methods: Printed Check, Credit Card, EFT, and 

Cash. 

• 
DOCDATE: Type the date on the document. This value is editable if the transaction 

isn’t linked to a deposit, hasn’t been reconciled, and the period is open. 

• 
DEPOSITTO: Type where the receipt is deposited, Bank account or Undeposited funds. 

• 
BANKACCOUNTID: Type the checking or savings account number. The account 

number must be defined in the system.  

• 
DEPOSITDATE: Type the date the payment was deposited. This value is required when 

you select Bank account in DEPOSITTO. 

• 
UNDEPACCTNO: Type the G/L account used for undeposited funds. This value must 

confirm to the primary/sub account specification in Company > Company Info.  

• 
CURRENCY: Identify the currency used by typing the three letter ISO currency code, 

like USD or EUR.  

• 
EXCH_RATE_DATE: Type the date when the exchange rate takes effect. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number. Start with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account based on your deposit method. This value must 

confirm to the primary/sub account specification in Company > Company Info. The

• 
TRX_AMOUNT: Type the amount of the line item. This field applies only to 

multi-currency companies. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the line item. 

• 
PAYER_NAME: Type the name of the payer.  

3. 
Optionally, fill in any of the other columns in the template as needed. 

4.

Importing the CSV File 

To import the CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Cash Management section, find the Other Receipts row, and then select the 

Import link.  

4. 
In the import box, click the Choose file button, and then find the CSV file. 

5. 
Select the Other Receipts CSV file to import, and then click Open. 

6. 
Click the Import button. The system loads the data into the Other Receipts list. 

Importing Payment Data 

You can import A/P payments and manual payments.  

You can import only one bank account and payment type combination at a time. 

You can choose whether you want imported payments to go through the approval process in 

Approval configuration in the A/P payments section. The Enable A/P payment approval against 

each selected entry creation from CSV import option applies to A/P payments and not to 

manual payments.

## Importing A/P Payments
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 364*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing A/P Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay AP Invoices > Import`


See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can expedite your payment process by importing payment data. You can also import manual 

payments, payments that you made outside of the system. 

If an entity is marked Do not pay, then invoices for that entity cannot be processed by importing 
them. 

To import records of payments that need to be made: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, select the Pay A/P invoices option. 

3. 
Select the Import button. 

4. 
Click the Download template link. You can find the file in your browser’s default download 

location, typically your Downloads folder.  

5. 
Open the AP Payments.xls file in Excel and fill it with your data.  

You can import only one bank account and payment type at a time. 

6. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor to pay. 

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the unique identifier of the invoice to pay. 

• 
PAYMENT_DATE: Type the date that you want to record as the date that the payment 

is made. 

• 
AMOUNT_TO_PAY: Type the amount that you want to pay towards the invoice. 

• 
PAYMENT_METHOD: Type one of the following: Printed Check, ACH or Electronic 

payment (if EFT or BACS), Cash, or Credit Card. 

• 
BANK_ACCT_ID: Type the bank account number to use for the payment. 

• 
INVOICE_CURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code for the currency to use 

for the payment. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. Examples: 

USD (US dollars), BPS (UK), CAD (Canadian). 

7. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns:  

• 
CREDITS_APPLIED: Type the amount of credits available to apply to the payment. 

• 
SEP_VENDOR_PAYMENT: Type “T” if you want separate payments. Otherwise, type “F.” 

• 
PYMT_REQUEST_METHOD:  

Type “1” for Use vendor preference.

## Importing Petty Cash Cards
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 367*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Petty Cash Cards 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Cash Management > Petty Cash 
Cards > Template/Import`


You can import Petty Cash Card data by uploading a CSV file. 

Download the Petty Cash Cards Import Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Cash Management section, find Petty Cash Cards and then click the Template 

link. The system downloads the Petty Cash Cards.xls file to your browser’s default download 

location. 

Fill the File with Your Data 

By default, the file opens in Excel.  

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each item that you want to import: 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique identifier of the location that is associated with the 

petty cash card. 

• 
ADDRESS_1: Type the street address of the location that is associated with the petty 

cash card. 

• 
CITY: Type the city of the location that is associated with the petty cash card. 

• 
STATE: Type the state of the location that is associated with the petty cash card. 

• 
ZIP: Type the ZIP Code of the location that is associated with the petty cash card. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount on the petty cash card. 

• 
PETTY_CASH_ACCT: Type the G/L account number of that is associated with the petty 

cash card. 

• 
FIRST_NAME: Type the first name of the person who is issued the petty cash card. 

• 
Last_NAME: Type the last name of the person who is issued the petty cash card. 

• 
AUTHORIZED_USERS: Type the unique identifier of the user who is authorized to use 

the petty cash card. 

This field is required when the card is issued to a property. 

2. 
Add any other optional data to the additional fields in the import template. 

• 
ADDRESS_2: If the address has a second line, type the line in this column. 

3. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV). 

---

## Importing Prepaids
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 371*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Prepaids 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Periodic Tasks > Prepaids > Import`


Before You Begin 

• 
Download the template and fill it with your prepaids data. 

• 
Save the template as a CSV file.  

To download the prepaids template: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Prepaids in the Periodic Tasks section of the menu. 

3. 
in the Prepaid Journal Entries list, click the Import button. 

4. 
In the Prepaids Import box, click the Download template link. 

Filling the Template File with Your Data 

Open the template using a spreadsheet application and then enter the information. By default, 

the file opens in Excel. 

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each prepaid journal entry that you want to import: 

• 
START_DATE: Type the date that payments are scheduled to begin. Prepaids post 

monthly. 

• 
END_DATE: Type the date that payments are scheduled to end.  

• 
POSTING: Type one of the following to determine when you want to post the prepaid: 

Based on start date, Beginning of month, End of month 

• 
TOTAL_AMOUNT: Type the total. The amount must be equal to the total amount of 

the posted prepaid. 

• 
ROUNDING_ACCT: Type a G/L account. This value is required when Round is set to 

True. 

• 
DATE_STARTING_PREV_EXP: Type the date that the amount for prepaid journal entries 

were accounted for outside of RealPage Accounting. A value is required when a 

previously expensed amount is defined. 

• 
EXP_PAID_DATE: Type the date when the expense was paid if the date was before the 

date that the payments are scheduled to begin. 

• 
BOOK: Type the name of the book that you want the prepaid journal entry to appear 

in. 

• 
JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal for prepaid journal entries. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description that identifies the prepaid entry. 

• 
SOURCE_ENTITY: Type the paying entity’s name. 

---


<!-- Page 372 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number, starting with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number to associate the journal entry. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the location.  

• 
DEBIT: Type the debit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

CREDIT field. A negative number is treated as a credit. 

• 
CREDIT: Type the credit amount. This field is required if no value is supplied in the 

DEBIT field. A negative number is treated as a debit. 

2. 
Optionally, fill in any of the remaining columns. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

4. 
After you’ve entered your data, look through the file for any of the common issues (on page 

487) that imports can have. 

You are ready to import your file to your system. 

Importing the Data 

To import prepaids data: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Prepaids in the Periodic Tasks section of the menu. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Import box appears. The box’s title and on-screen instructions 

above the Choose file button reflect the type of data that you are importing. 

4. 
Select the file that you want to import and click the Open button. 

The file you import must be in CSV format. 

5. 
If your data contains dates, then in the Date format field, select the date format used by the 

data that you are importing. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding field set to the default status auto detect. 

7. 
Select the Process offline check box to have the system import the data with the least 

impact to system processing speed. 

8. 
To have the system send an email when the import is finished, type your email address in 

the Email results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses; separate 

each address by a semi-colon or comma. The system sends an email when an offline import 

is finished and when errors occur. 

9. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row that starts with a # symbol.

## Importing Purchase Orders
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 381*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Purchase Orders 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data >Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Purchase Orders > Template`


To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select Import Data. 

The Import data page opens. 

2. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, click the Template link 

in the Purchase Orders row. 

The system downloads the template to your local drive. 

Filling the Template File with Your Data 

Open the template using a spreadsheet application and then enter the information. By default, 

the file opens in Excel. 

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each purchase order that you want to import: 

• 
PO_DATE: Type the date of the purchase order.  

• 
PO_NO: Type the unique number associated with the purchase order. This field is 

required if Document sequencing is not enabled.  

• 
ENCUMBRANCE_DATE: Type the date of encumbrance of the funds for this purchase 

order.  

• 
VENDOR_ID:  Type the vendor’s unique identifier. This vendor must already be 

defined in the system.  

• 
BILLTO_CONTACTNAME: Type the name of the person to bill for the purchase order. 

This field is required if USE_COMPANYADDR is true.  

• 
BLANKET_PO_TYPE: If the purchase order is a long-term agreement between a buyer 

and a vendor for recurring purchases of goods or services at predetermined prices 

over a specified period, then this field is required, Type either QTY for quantity or AMT 

for amount.  

• 
EXPIRY_DATE: If this purchase order is a blanket purchase order, then this field is 

required. Type the date that the blanket purchase order expires. 

• 
LINE_ENTRY_TYPE: Type Standard or Job Cost. This field indicates whether the item is 

associated with a standard purchase order or a purchase order associated with a job 

cost project.  

• 
LINE_NO:  Type the line number. Start with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the location identifier of the entity.  

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the account number associated with the line item.

ITEM_DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the item in the purchase order.  

•

purchase order.  

•

•

Importing the CSV File 

To import the CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Purchase 

Orders row, and then select the Import link.  

4. 
In the import box, click the Choose file button, and then find the CSV file. 

5. 
Select the Purchase Orders CSV file to import and click Open. 

6. 
Click the Import button. The system loads the purchase order data into the system. 

Reasons Budgets Won’t Import 

Budgets can fail to import for a number of reasons. Some of the most common reasons are: 

• 
A budget ID has not been created for the budget you’re importing. 

• 
Reporting periods haven’t been created for the budget you’re importing. 

• 
The reporting periods haven’t been set as budgetable. 

• 
The budget contains duplicate line items. 

• 
Budgets won’t import if they contain duplicate line items. 

• 
The budget import template hasn’t been correctly formatted. 

Before you import a budget 

Before you import your budget, make sure that you have done the following. 

---


<!-- Page 383 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Create a Budget ID 

Before importing a budget, use the General Ledger to create a Budget ID for the budget you plan 

to import. If you do not create the budget ID before an import, an error message occurs 

referencing an invalid Budget ID. After the new Budget ID has been created, you can then import 

your Budget Details. For more information, see Adding a budget. 

Create reporting periods 

Create reporting periods before importing a budget. Reporting periods used in a budget must be 

marked as Use for Budgeting and can’t overlap with another reporting period. 

If the reporting period already exists, and you receive an error message when attempting to 

import, check your reporting period dates and the reporting period in your import file. The 

budgetable periods may be overlapping and causing an import error. 

Budgetable periods 

There can only be one budgetable reporting period per time frame. To mark a reporting period as 

budgetable or to verify that time frames are not overlapping, view the Reporting periods list and 

make changes as necessary. 

To make a reporting period budgetable: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the More section, select the Reporting periods option. 

3. 
Click Edit next to the appropriate period in the list. 

4. 
Select the Use for budgeting box. 

5. 
Adjust the Start and End dates if needed. 

6. 
Click Save. 

Remove duplicate line items 

Line items that have the same dimensional values, but different budget amounts cannot be 

imported. 

For example, if you have two line items that have the same ACCT_NO, DEPT_ID, PROJECTID, and 

EMPLOYEEID, but different budget amounts, when the file is imported, you get Error BL05000161 

Performance Analytics has no way of knowing which line contains the correct budget information. 

To avoid this error, delete duplicate line items, or ensure that all line items have different 

dimensional values. 

---


<!-- Page 384 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Best practices 

The following best practices will help you prepare your CSV file for upload. 

1. 
From the Import data page, download a template. 

• 
Use the latest template, especially following a product release. 

• 
Use the correct template for the area in which you want to upload information. 

Different templates organize different types of information. Use a template specifically 

for the information that you need to upload. 

2. 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to entering information. 

• 
Read the header descriptions in the template. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format 

or with an incorrect accepted value, it will cause an error in your upload. 

• 
Enter required information. 

Some data are required, while other data are not. Read the description field to 

determine which information is required. If you do not enter required information, 

your upload will fail. 

3. 
Save the file as a comma-separated value (CSV) file. If you are saving from Excel, you could 

choose the comma delimited file type. 

The file will have the file extension .csv after you save it. 

Leave the file open until your import is successful. Excel might reformat the file if you close 

it before the import is successful.

## Importing Replacement Reserve Draw Model Details
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 387*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Replacement Reserve Draw Model Details 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost & Reserves or Replacement Reserves > Setup > Draw Models 
> Replacement Reserves > Draw Model Details > Template/Import`


Add draw model details to define how replacement reserve costs are structured and displayed on 

a draw. Each detail represents a line on the draw—such as a section header, cost line, or 

total—and controls how costs are grouped, ordered, and rolled up into totals. 

This topic explains how to import draw model details in bulk. To add lines one at a time, see 
Adding Replacement Reserve Draw Model Details. 

To import draw model details: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Job Cost & Reserves application, and then click the 

Setup tab. 

If you do not have a subscription to Job Cost, select the standalone Replacement Reserves 
application instead. 

2. 
In the Draw models section, select the Replacement reserves menu option. 

The Draw models list opens. 

3. 
Click the Draw model details link next to the desired draw model. 

The Draw model details list opens. 

4. 
Click the Template button. 

The system either downloads the drawmodeldetail.xls file or prompts you to open or save 

the drawmodeldetail.xls file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

5. 
Open the drawmodeldetail.xls file.  

6. 
For each draw model you want to add, enter the required information: 

• 
DRAWMODELNAME: Enter the draw model Name, including any spaces. 

• 
DRAWMODELDETAILNAME: Enter the name of the draw model detail. 

• 
RECORDTYPE: Complete this field based on the draw model detail level: 

• 
For detail-level draw model details, leave this field blank. 

• 
For title-level draw model details, enter “title”. 

• 
For total-level draw model details, enter “total”. 

• 
TOTALLEVEL: Enter the level number (0–5) of the draw model detail. 

• 
SEQUENCE: Enter the sequence number of the draw model detail.  

• 
STATUS: Complete this field based on the draw model detail status: 

• 
For active draw model details, leave this field blank. 

---


<!-- Page 388 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
For inactive draw model details, enter “inactive”. 

The example below shows a draw model detail list. 

7. 
When your changes are complete, click Save as.  

8. 
In the Save as box, use the Save as type drop-down list to select “CSV (comma delimited) 

(*.csv).” 

9. 
Change the File name or location as needed, and then click Save. 

10. 
On the Draw model details page, click Import. The system opens the Import draw model 

detail information box. 

11. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

12. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

13. 
Click Done.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Accounts > Add/Edit/View > 
Import Reporting Accounts`


There are two places where you can import reporting accounts.  

• 
From the Reporting Account Sets list. Use this method to import a new chart of accounts 

(COA). 

• 
From the Reporting Account Set page. Use this method to import reporting accounts into a 

reporting account set. 

A reporting account set must already exist before you can import reporting accounts or 
mappings.  

Workflow for Importing Reporting Accounts 

• 
Download the reporting account template. 

• 
Fill the template with reporting account data. 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the file. 

If the reporting accounts and/or mappings are created in a CSV file outside the application, 

import it by clicking the Import button on the Reporting account sets page. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data.  

3. 
Find Reporting Accounts and Mappings row, and then click the Template link on the row. 

The system either downloads the template to your browser’s default download folder, or 

prompts you to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template with Reporting Account Data 

To fill the template with your data: 

1. 
Open the file in your spreadsheet application. 

2. 
For each account that you want to be able to use in reports, add the following information 

in the required columns: 

• 
NAME: Type the name of the reporting account set to add this data to. 

---


<!-- Page 392 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
GL_ACCT_TYPE: Type the code for the account type. When importing into a statistical 

account, type N for Cumulative, or type I for For period. Otherwise, type N for Balance 

sheet or type I for Income statement. 

• 
REPORTING_ACCT_TYPE: Type the code for the reporting account type. When 

importing into a statistical account, type N for Cumulative, or type I for For period. 

Otherwise, type N for Balance sheet or type I for Income statement. 

3. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining columns. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the purpose of the account. 

• 
GL_ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number 

• 
GL_ACCT_NAME: Type the name of the G/L account that is mapped to the reporting 

account. 

• 
REPORTING_ACCT_NO: Add the account number to map to the G/L account. 

• 
REPORTING_ACCT_NAME: Type the desired name of the reporting account. 

• 
STATISTICAL: Type T (True) if the account is a statistical account type. Type F (False) if 

the account is not a statistical account. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the CSV File 

1. 
Return to the Reporting Account Sets list, and then click the Import button. 

2. 
In the Import box, click the Choose file button, and select the CSV file that you just 

updated. 

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select the date format used in the file that you are 

importing. 

4. 
Type your email address in the Email results to this address field. 

5. 
Click the Import button.

## Importing Reporting Periods
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 393*

Importing Reporting Periods 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up General Ledger Transactions > 
Reporting Periods > Template`


You can use the Import option to add multiple reporting periods in bulk. 

Downloading the Reporting Periods Template 

To export and fill out the reporting periods template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select Import Data. 

The Import data page opens. 

2. 
In the Setup General Ledger Transactions section, click the Template link in the Reporting 

Periods row. 

The system downloads the template to your local drive. 

Filling the Template File with Your Data 

Open the template using a spreadsheet application and then enter the required information. By 

default, the file opens in Excel. 

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each reporting period that you want to import: 

• 
NAME: Type the name of the reporting period that you want to import. The name can 

be up to 80 characters long, and can be composed of alphanumeric characters and the 

underscore. 

• 
HEADER1: Type the first line to show on the report. This field can be up to 40 

characters, contain alphanumeric characters and the underscore. This field is required. 

• 
HEADER2: Type a second line to show on the report. This field is optional. 

• 
START_DATE: Type the beginning date of the reporting period. The date must be 

composed of numbers and the slash (/) character. This field is required. 

• 
END_DATE: Type the ending date of the reporting period. The date must be 

composed of numbers and the slash (/) character. This field is required. 

• 
BUDGETABLE: Type T to display this reporting period in the list of available reporting 

periods for inclusion in a budget. This is a true/false field. The default value is F. This 

field is required. 

• 
STATUS: Type T to display this reporting period in lists. Type F to hide the reporting 

period in lists but keep it in the system for later use. The default value is T. 

2. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV). 

---

1. 
Open the Company menu.

Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up General Ledger Transactions section, find the Reporting periods row and then 

select the Default Import link. The Reporting Periods box opens. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button and browse for the CSV file. 

5. 
Select the CSV file to import and click Open. 

6. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select the date format that you used in the file. 

7. 
Click the Import button. The system loads the data into the Reporting Periods list.

Importing Segments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Segments > Template/Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Segments > Import`


Downloading the Template 

1. 
On the Import data page, find the Segments row, and click the Template link. 

2. 
Open the downloaded file and fill it with segment data: 

• 
Type: Type a two-character alphabetical code for the segment. 

• 
Name: Type a name that describes the segment. This name appears in reports. 

• 
Segment value: Leave this column blank. 

• 
Status: Type the status of the segment, either “Active” or “Inactive.” 

You can include up to 15 segment types and values in the import file. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the Segments 

1. 
In the Segments list, click the Import link. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button.

Importing Segment Rules 

When you import segment rules, the system overwrites your existing set of segment rules. To 
preserve the existing rules, be sure to include them in your data.

Download the segment rules template (on page 393). 

2. 
Fill the spreadsheet with your data. 

3. 
Save the spreadsheet in CSV format. 

4. 
Upload the segment rule data (on page 395). 

Downloading and Filling the Segment Rules Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > More > Segment Rule Set > Download Entries 
Form`

Form`

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Click the Segment rule set option. 

Alternatively, in the Company application, click the Ledger sentry option. 

3. 
Click the Download entries form link. The system downloads the template to your browser’s 

default location. 

To fill in the template: 

1. 
Open the template in your favorite spreadsheet application. 

2. 
In the TYPE column, fill in either Account or Property.

## Importing Draft Expenses
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 404*

Import Instructions by Type of Data

Importing Staff Expenses 

• 
Importing Draft Staff Expenses (on page 264) 

• 
Importing Approved Staff Expenses (on page 261) 

Staff Expenses Import Box 

Use this box to prepare for importing staff expense data into Performance Analytics. This is a 

standard import function with one difference. When you import expenses, you must specify 

whether the expenses are draft or approved. 

To use this import box: 

1. 
Download the desired staff expenses template. 

• 
If you want to import staff expenses before they have been approved, then click the 

Staff Expenses - Draft template link. 

• 
If you want to import staff expenses that have been approved, select the Staff 

Expenses - Approved template link. 

2. 
Prepare your data for importing. 

3. 
Import the expense data.  

For details, refer to Importing staff expenses (on page 396). 

Importing Draft Expenses 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > Staff 
Expenses > Import`


You can import expenses from the Staff expenses page or from the Import data page. This 

procedure describes importing from the Import data page.  

When you add expense data to the import file, add the User ID of the user who incurred the 

expense and the amount. You can also specify the expense report name to associate an expense 

with a specific expense report.  

After importing the CSV file, these expenses appear in users’ My expenses lists. The system sends 

an email message to each user who had expenses in the imported file. The user must add 

additional information, attach any required receipts and invoices, and then submit the expenses 

for approval. 

To import expenses: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

---


<!-- Page 405 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

3. 
In the Set Up Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Expense Reports - 

Draft row, and then select Template. The template (on page 399) for draft expenses 

downloads to your browser’s default download location.  

Preparing the Data for Importing 

1. 
Export the unapproved, draft expenses data from your other system. 

2. 
Open the downloaded template (on page 7) in Microsoft Excel or your favorite spreadsheet 

application. 

3. 
Fill in the template with the unapproved expense data that you want to import. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.  

Do not use leading zeros in ID fields. If you MUST use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
USER_ID: Type the ID of the user who the expense is being submitted for. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the draft expense. 

5. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns. Many of the valid values differ by company 

because your company configures expenses in your system depending on your business 

needs. See Configuring Expense Reports. 

• 
EXP_REPORT_NAME: Type the expense report name. 

• 
DATE_FILED: Type the date that the expenses were filed. The default value is today’s 

date. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the expense. 

• 
DATE: Type the date. The default value is today’s date. 

• 
EXPENSE_CATEGORY: Type the category of the expense.  

• 
REIMBURSEMENT_TYPE: Type who or what will be reimbursed: Employees, Property, 

or P-card vendor. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique identifier of the location associated with the expense.  

• 
MEMO: Type a note about the expense.  

• 
UNIT: Type the unit number associated with this expense.  

• 
CORPORATE_EXP_REPORT: Type “true” if this is a corporate expense report or type 

“false” if not. Corporate expense reports do not appear in Site View. 

• 
DEPARTMENTID: Type the unique identifier of the department that is associated with 

the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_1: Type the segment type associated with the expense. 

---


<!-- Page 406 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_1: Type the segment value of segment 1 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_2: Type a second segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_2: Type the segment value of segment 2 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_3: Type the third segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_3: Type the segment value of segment 3 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_4: Type the fourth segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_4: Type the segment value of segment 4 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_5: Type the fifth segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_5: Type the segment value of segment 5 associated with the 

expense. 

You can include up to five segment types and values in the import file. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_CUSTOMERID: Type the unique identifier of the customer that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_VENDORID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_EMPLOYEEID: Type the unique identifier of the employee that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_PROJECTID: Type the unique identifier of the project that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_CLASSID: Type the unique identifier of the class that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

6. 
Save the file as a CSV-formatted file (on page 14). 

Importing the File 

1. 
When you are ready to import the file, click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV 

formatted file. 

2. 
In the Date format field, type the date format that you used for the expenses in the CSV file. 

3. 
Leave the File encoding field as auto detect. 

4. 
In the Import as section, select Draft if the staff expenses have not been approved. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box if your file contains such a large number of expenses 

that you want the system to process the data offline so as not to degrade system 

performance.

SEGMENTVALUE_1: Type the segment value of segment 1 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_2: Type a second segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_2: Type the segment value of segment 2 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_3: Type the third segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_3: Type the segment value of segment 3 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_4: Type the fourth segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_4: Type the segment value of segment 4 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_5: Type the fifth segment type to associate with the expense. 

You can include up to five segment types and values in the import file. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_5: Type the segment value of segment 5 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_CUSTOMERID: Type the unique identifier of the customer that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_VENDORID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_EMPLOYEEID: Type the unique identifier of the employee that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_PROJECTID: Type the unique identifier of the project that is 

associated with the expense report item.

Importing Standard Vendors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Standard Vendors > Template/Import`


You can import standard vendor data by uploading a CSV file with the standard vendor data in it. 

Download the Standard Vendors Import Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find Standard vendors, 

and then click the Template link. The system downloads the Standard Vendors.xls file to 

your browser’s default download location. 

Fill the File with Your Data 

By default, the file opens in Excel.  

1. 
Fill in the required columns for each vendor that you want to import: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type a unique identifier of the vendor. 

• 
ENTITY_ID: Type a unique identifier of the entity associated with the vendor. 

2. 
Add any other optional data to the additional columns in the import template. 

• 
VENDOR_NAME: Type the name of the vendor. 

• 
ENTITY_NAME: Type the name of the entity associated with the vendor.  

3. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV). 

Importing the Standard Vendor Data 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find Standard Vendors, 

and then click the Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button and browse for the CSV file. 

5. 
Select the CSV file to import and click Open. 

6. 
Click Import.

## Importing Statistical Accounts
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 417*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Statistical Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Statistical Accounts`


This import allows you to add new statistical accounts. 

Workflow for Importing Statistical Accounts 

• 
Download the statistical accounts template. 

• 
Fill the template with statistical account data. 

• 
Save the file in CSV format. 

• 
Import the file. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Statistical Accounts row, and then click the Template link on the row. The system 

either downloads the template to your browser’s default download folder, or prompts you 

to open or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Template  

To fill in the template with your data: 

1. 
Open the template file in your spreadsheet application. 

2. 
For each statistical account, add the required information: 

• 
ACCT_NO: Account number. The account number must conform to the primary/sub 


> **Navigation Path:** `account specification as it is defined in Company > Setup: Company Info.`


• 
ACCT_NAME: Type the account name. It can be up to 80 characters long. 

• 
REQ_DEPT: Type T if you want to require the selection of a department. Otherwise, 

type F. The default is false. 

• 
REQ_LOC: Type T if you want to require the selection of a location. Otherwise, type F. 

The default is false. 

• 
TAXABLE: Type T if the statistical account is taxable. Otherwise, type F. The default is 

false. 

3. 
Optionally, add data in any of the remaining columns. 

• 
ACTIVE: Type T if you want the statistical account to be visible in lists. Otherwise, type 

F. When set to F, the statistical account is not visible in lists, but it remains in system 

for later use. 

---


<!-- Page 418 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
REPORT_TYPE: Type N to set the account to a cumulative balance, type the letter I for 

the balance for the period, showing only the change from the previous period.. 

• 
CHART_TYPES: Type the chart type. The Chart types field is available only when the 

chart type feature is enabled. 

• 
CATEGORY: If your company was created with a Quick Start template, you can assign 

the account to a predefined account category. Type the desired category. 

• 
REQUIREPROJECT: Type T if you want to require the selection of a project. Otherwise, 

type F. The default is false. 

• 
REQUIRECUSTOMER: Type T if you want to require the selection of a customer. 

Otherwise, type F. The default is false. 

• 
REQUIREVENDOR: Type T if you want to require the selection of a vendor. Otherwise, 

type F. The default is false. 

• 
REQUIREEMPLOYEE: Type T if you want to require the selection of an employee. 

Otherwise, type F. The default is false. 

• 
REQUIREITEM: Type T if you want to require the selection of an item. Otherwise, type F. 

The default is false. 

• 
REQUIRECLASS: Type T if you want to require the selection of a class. Otherwise, type 

F. The default is false. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the CSV File 

1. 
Return to the Import Data list, and then click the Import button on the Statistical accounts 

row. 

2. 
In the Import box, click the Choose file button, and select the CSV file that you updated 

with statistical account data. 

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select the date format used in the file that you are 

importing. 

4. 
Type your email address in the Email results to this address field. 

5. 
Click the Import button.

## Importing Statistical Journal Entries
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 424*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Statistical Journal Entries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All Import Data > Set Up General Ledger Transactions 
>Statistical Journal Entries > Template`


You can import statistical journal entries into multiple journals with one upload. When you do so, 

the transactions are contained within a summary that is kept in the system. If you navigate into 

the journal to edit or view one of these transactions, a list with the entire summary opens. For 

other G/L transactions, the Transaction edit page opens. 

Downloading the Template 

To download the template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import Data. The Import data page opens. 

3. 
In the Setup General Ledger Transactions section, click the Template link in the Statistical 

Journal Entries row. 

The system downloads the template to your local drive. 

Filling the Template File with Your Data 

Open the template using a spreadsheet application and then enter the required information. By 

default, the file opens in Excel. 

1. 
Fill in the required fields for each statistical journal entry that you want to import: 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type the description of the statistical journal entry that you want to 

import. The description can be up to 80 characters long, and can be composed of 

alphanumeric characters and the underscore.  

• 
JOURNAL: Type the name of the journal for the statistical journal entry that you want 

to import. The journal name is four characters long.  

• 
DATE: Type the date of the statistical journal entry. The date defaults to todays date. 

• 
LINE_NO: Type the line number. Start with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and 

increase by one for each subsequent line. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the account number to associate with the statistical journal entry. The 

account number must conform to the primary/sub account specification that is 

defined in Company > Company Info. 

• 
STATE: Type the status of the statistical journal entry. Valid values are Draft and 

Posted.  

2. 
Optionally, fill in any of the other columns in the template as needed. 

3. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV). 

---


<!-- Page 425 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing the CSV File 

To import the statistical journal entries CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up General Ledger Transactions section, find the Statistical journal entries row, 

and then select the Import link.  

4. 
In the import box, click the Choose file button, and then find the CSV file. 

5. 
Select the Statistical journal entries CSV file to import and click Open. 

6. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select the date format that you used in the file. 

7. 
Click the Import button. The system loads the data into the statistical journals that are 

specified in the spreadsheet.

Importing Summaries 

If you have a collection of transactions saved in CSV (comma separated values) file format, you 

can upload the data to the system: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Locate the transaction type.  

For example, if you have a file with A/R invoice data, look in the Set Up A/R Master List, Open 

Invoices and Adjustments section to find the Accounts receivable invoices. 

If you have a file with A/R adjustments data, look in the Set Up A/R Master List, Open 

Invoices and Adjustments section to find the Accounts receivable adjustments. 

4. 
In the Summary type drop-down list: 

• 
Select Monthly to import a batch of monthly summaries. 

• 
Select Summary name in file if you want the system to use the summary name in the 

Batch_TITLE column of the file’s data.  

If you are importing daily summaries, this is the default. 

5. 
Click the Import link. The Import company information box opens. 

6. 
Select the date format. 

7. 
In Post to, select General ledger. 

8. 
In Email results to this address, type an email address where you want the system to send a 

report with the results of this upload. 

9. 
Click the Import button.

## Importing Transactions into a Summary
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 427*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Transactions into a Summary 

(Summary Title) > Import 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access the Summaries list. 

You can import transactions into a summary in Accounting and Commercial Property 

Management.  

You can choose whether to post the imported transactions to the G/L or to mark them as 

historical. The system does not post historical transactions to the G/L. 

Transactions that you import and post to the general ledger must follow these guidelines: 

• 
The CSV file can include a maximum of 5,000 transactions per file. 

• 
Import open transactions only. Do not include paid or partially paid transactions. 

• 
The file you import must be in CSV format. If your csv file contains dates, you can set the 

date format to match the format in the CSV file. 

To import transactions: 

1. 
Open the Summaries list. 

2. 
Find the summary into which you want to import transactions, and then click the link in the 

Summary title column. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Import company information page opens. 

4. 
Click the Browse button and click the file with the transaction data to import. 

5. 
Click the Open button to choose the file. 

6. 
In File encoding, you can allow the system to auto detect the type of CSV file that you are 

uploading, or you can select a specific CSV file format, such as Mac OSx, Windows-1252, 

and more. 

7. 
In Post to, select the mode for importing: 

• 
Historical: imported transactions have no effect on the general ledger. 

• 
General ledger: imported transactions are posted live to the general ledger. 

When importing to the General ledger, the system processes the import offline and posts 

the transactions using daily batching. 

Errors cause the system to roll back the import immediately. 

8. 
If you select Historical, you can choose to process the import offline. This is useful if your 

import file is large. 

---

9. 
If you want to be notified by email when an offline import is finished or if errors occur in the 

import process, type your email address in the Email results to this address field. When the 

import is finished, the system sends an email to the address you specified. 

10. 
Click the Import button. 

The system’s data format setting is located in the General information section of the Company 

application, Setup tab, Company option.

## Importing Transaction Allocations
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 429*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Transaction Allocations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


Workflow 

1. 
Download the transaction allocations template. 

2. 
Fill the template with transaction allocations data. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format 

4. 
Import the file. 

Downloading the Transaction Allocations Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu.  

2. 
Click the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Transaction allocations row, and then 

click the Template link. 

The system either downloads the Transaction Allocations.xls file or prompts you to open or 

save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling In the Template with Transaction Allocation Data 

Add your data using the correct formatting as explained in the template.  

1. 
Open the template in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
ALLOCATION_ID: Type a unique name for the allocation. 

• 
ALLOCATE_BY: Type P for Percentage, A for Absolute or F for Fixed amount with 

over/under logic. 

• 
ALLOCATE_TO: Type B for both, D for department or L for location. 

• 
LINE_NO: Start with 1 for the first line of a transaction, and increase by one for each 

subsequent line. 

• 
VALUETYPE: Type Amount or Percent. 

• 
VALUE: Type the amount or percentage to allocate. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. Refer to the Transaction Allocations Data 

(on page 422) topic for a full list of columns. 

After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 
mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common Errors 
(on page 487 ) and Best Practices . 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

---

## Importing Unit Data (Commercial and Condo and Co-op)
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 436*

Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Unit Data (Commercial and Condo and Co-op) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Property Management > Unit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Condo and Co-op > Unit`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Use this procedure to import new unit records into Property Management or Condo and Co-op. 

You can upload unit data for only one application at a time. Do not intermix unit records for 

Commercial Property Management and Condo and Co-op applications. 

Importing units data into Accounting requires a different template. If you want to import units 

data into Accounting, see Importing Accounting Units Data (on page 431). 

If you mistakenly import the units through Accounting first, and then try to import units through 

Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-op, the system rejects the second attempt 

to import the units as duplicates. 

Download a Template 

To download the unit template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Unit row in either the Property Management section or the Condo and Co-op 

section, depending on the application that you want to import units into. 

4. 
Click the Template button. The Save As box opens. 

5. 
Save the Unit.xls file to your computer. 

6. 
Open the template in Excel. 

7. 
Fill in the required columns of the unit template with your data.  

• 
PROPERTY: This is the unique identifier of the location associated with the unit. 

• 
UNIT: This is the unique identifier of the unit. 

• 
CONDO_PERCENTAGE: Type the percentage of ownership interest in the common 

elements allocated to each unit. This value is typically determined by the developer 

when the condo is created and recorded in the condo’s governing documents such as 

---


<!-- Page 437 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

the declaration or master deed. This field is required only when the property type is 

condominium. 

8. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining columns: 

• 
FLOOR: Type the floor on which the unit is located. 

• 
UNIT_DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the unit. 

• 
UNIT_TYPE: Type a valid unit type. Unit types are customized in each system, so check 

the unit types available in your system to find out the valid values.  

• 
STATUS: This is the status of the unit. Type ACTIVE or INACTIVE. 

• 
MARKET_RENT_PER_SQUARE_AREA: Type the market rent per square area.  

• 
ADDRESS1: Type the street address of the unit. 

• 
ADDRESS2: Type the second line of the street address where the unit is located.  

• 
CITY: Type the city where the unit is located.  

• 
STATE: Type the state where the unit is located.  

• 
ZIP: Type the ZIP Code of where the unit is located.  

• 
COUNTRY: Type the country where the unit is located.  

• 
REPORTING_CODE_LABEL: Type the label of the unit’s MR code. 

• 
REPORTING_CODE: Type the MR code of the unit.  

9. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

10. 
Close the CSV file. 

Import Data From the Template 

When you have populated your selected template, import the file. 

To import the data: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Units row in the Property Management or Condo and Co-op sections, and then click 

the Import link. The Import Unit Information box opens. 

It is important to import the unit data in the Property Management or Condo and Co-op 
sections, and not the Set Up Master List section. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button and locate the CSV file that contains the unit data. 

5. 
In the Date format drop-down list, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, 

select a date format that you want to use. The RealPage Commercial Property Management 

system supports 24 date formats. 

---


<!-- Page 438 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
In the File encoding drop-down list, leave the setting as Auto detect unless you are unable 

to import your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different 

type of file encoding. 

7. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. The process offline feature allows the system to process the data when system activity 

is lighter. 

If you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, do not select the Process offline 

check box. 

8. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address. When the system 

completes the import process, it sends an email to the email address in this field. The 

system also sends any errors that may have occurred in the process. 

9. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row that starts with a # symbol. 

Click the Help button for additional information about this subject in the RealPage 
Accounting help system. 

To import the table of data into the Import data page: 

1. 
On the Import data page, locate the item for which you downloaded the template. For 

example, if you downloaded an Account Groups template, locate the Account groups row, 

and then click the corresponding Import link. The system displays an import page. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button to select your populated template file. 

3. 
In Date format, select a format that matches the format in your CSV file. 

4. 
In File encoding, you can allow the system to auto detect the type of CSV file format you 

are uploading, or you can select a specific type from the list. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In Email results to this address, enter your email address to receive a message with a list of 

data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button. 

---



## Importing Accounting Units Data
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 439*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Accounting Units Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Units > Template/Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Template/Import`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

This procedure assists you with importing units data to use with the core RealPage Accounting 

applications. You can use import template to create new unit records, update existing units, or 

both. When importing, the system does not remove existing data when a column is blank in the 

import template. 

Importing unit data for use with Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-op requires 
the use of different templates and import links. To import data into unit records for one of these 
applications, see Importing Unit Data (on page 431 ). 

Download a Template 

To download the RealPage Accounting units template: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
Select the Units menu option. 

The Units list opens. 

3. 
Click the Template button. 

4. 
Save the Units_.xls file to your computer. 

5. 
Open the file in Excel. 

6. 
Fill in the required columns of the template with your data.  

• 
LOCATION: This is the unique identifier of the location associated with the unit. 

• 
UNITNUM: This is the unique identifier of the unit. 

7. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining column: 

• 
STATUS: This is the status of the unit. Type ACTIVE or INACTIVE. 

• 
ADDRESS1: This is the main street address of the unit. 

• 
ADDRESS2: This is the second line of the street address of the unit. 

• 
CITY: This is the city where the unit is located. 

---


<!-- Page 440 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
STATE: This is the state where the unit is located. 

• 
ZIP: This is the ZIP Code where the unit is located. 

• 
COUNTRY: This is the country where the unit is located. 

• 
FLOORPLANNAME: This is the name of the floor plan of the unit.  

• 
RENTABLESQFT: This is the rentable square footage of the unit.  

8. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

9. 
Close the CSV file. 

Import Data From the Template 

When you have populated your selected template, import the file. 

To import the data back into RealPage Accounting: 

1. 
Return to the Units list. 

2. 
Click the Import button in the upper-right corner. 

The Import unit information box opens. 

3. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

4. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

5. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

6. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

7. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

8. 
Click the Import button. 

---



## Importing Vendors
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 441*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Vendors 

Workflow for importing vendor and vendor-related data: 

1. 
Download the vendors template. 

2. 
Fill the template file with vendor data. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 14). 

4. 
Import the vendor file. 

• 
If you plan on importing vendor 1099 transactions, follow the instructions in Importing 

Vendor 1099 Transactions (on page 467). 

• 
If you plan to import vendor ACH information, follow the instructions in Importing 

Vendor Electronic Payment Information (on page 479). 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Vendor > Template`


To download the vendor template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Vendors row, 

and click Template.  

The system either downloads the template file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Templates, Matching the Provided Data in the Structure 

Do not use leading zeros in ID fields. If you MUST use leading zeros in IDs, convert the column of 

ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does not remove the 

leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you use a template to 

import information that requires IDs. 

1. 
Export the vendor data from your other system. 

2. 
Open the file in Excel. and copy the exported vendor data of each object into the vendor 

template file. Take care to exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.  

You can specify the vendor’s preferred payment method in the Vendor template. Download 
the latest vendor template to add preferred payment method to vendor records when you 
import vendors. 

3. 
Fill the required columns in the vendor template: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type a unique ID for the vendor. 

---


<!-- Page 442 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
NAME: Type the vendor name. 

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type the name of the contact associated with the vendor. 

• 
PRINT_AS: Type the name of the vendor as you want it to appear on official 

documents. 

• 
R_PRINT_AS: Type the name of the contact to use for returns to the vendor as you 

want it to appear on official documents. 

• 
P_PRINT_AS: Type the name of the contact to use when paying the vendor as you 

want it to appear on checks and documents. 

4. 
Optionally, fill in any additional columns as needed. Refer to the Vendor Data Template (on 

page 435) for a full list of columns. 

The Do not itemize vendor field is available to import only when your company has enabled 
AI invoice scanning. 

5. 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 14). 

Importing the Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Vendors > Import`


To import vendor data: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Click Vendors. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Import box appears. The box’s title and on-screen instructions 

above the Choose file button reflect the type of data that you are importing. 

4. 
Select the file that you want to import and click the Open button. 

The file you import must be in CSV format. 

5. 
If your data contains dates, then in the Date format field, select the date format used by the 

data that you are importing. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding field set to the default status auto detect. 

7. 
Select the Process offline check box to have the system import the data with the least 

impact to system processing speed. 

8. 
To have the system send an email when the import is finished, type your email address in 

the Email results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses; separate 

each address by a semi-colon or comma. The system sends an email when an offline import 

is finished and when errors occur. 

9. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row that starts with a # symbol. 

---
