## Importing Vendor 1099 Transaction Update
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 475*

Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

Importing Vendor 1099 Transaction Update 

You can import vendor 1099 transactions into the system by uploading a CSV file with the 1099 

data. You can also update the information manually by selecting the 1099 form type and box for 

the transaction, the vendor default, and the 1099 name for the vendor. 

Workflow 

• 
Download the Vendor 1099 Transaction Template 

• 
Fill in the template 

• 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 14) 

• 
Import the vendor 1099 CSV file 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Vendor 1099 Transaction Update > Template`


To download the Vendor 1099 Transaction Update template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Vendor 1099 

Transaction Update row, and click Template.  

The system either downloads the template file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling the Vendor 1099 Template 

The system ignores a blank in the NAME1099, DEFAULT1099TYPE, and DEFAULT1099BOX fields, 

and does not change the existing data. To delete data, enter the value NULL. 

This upload is different from most others because you are not creating new records. Instead, you 

are updating existing records. 

The upload can retroactively mark existing transactions as eligible for a 1099 for vendors you 

specify and for a given time period. Additional fields update the 1099 form type and box, as well 

as the 1099 name. You may update any combination of these fields in a single upload. For 

example, you could update the form type and box, but not the 1099 name and transactions. You 

must include the form type and box as well as the date range for a transaction update. 

The following chart illustrates these variations. For example, say you only want to update the 1099 

name. The first line shows how you enter the NAME1099 field for a given vendor. 

---


<!-- Page 476 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

You explicitly state that the transactions are not to be flagged as 1099
-able by placing an N in 
the UPDATETRANS field. 

To fill in the vendor 1099 template: 

1. 
Open the file in Excel.  

2. 
Fill the required columns in the vendor template: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the vendor’s ID. The data must refer to a vendor ID that is already in 

the system. The system uses this field as the matching key, and not to update data. It 

must match an existing vendor ID. 

• 
DEFAULT1099TYPE: This field specifies the form type for the transaction, and changes 

the default form type for transactions going forward. You specify various 1099 forms 

here using the values DIV, INT, MISC, R, S, PATR and G. This field is updated if a value 

is present. If the value is blank, the system leaves the existing value in the system. To 

remove the existing value, enter the value NULL. Data in this column is required when 

FORM1099BOX is true or when UPDATETRANS is set to Y.  

In the normal user interface, you access this information on the Form 1099 Information 


> **Navigation Path:** `page (Accounts Payable > All > Vendors). Click the Edit link for an existing vendor`


and go to the Additional information tab. At the bottom, click the Form 1099 link.) 

• 
DEFAULT 1099BOX: Data in this column is required when FORM1099BOX is true or 

UPDATETRANS is set to Y. Type a positive integer followed by an optional alpha 

character. The data in this column must refer to a box that is valid for the form type. 

This field specifies the box for the transaction, and changes the default box for 

transactions going forward. You specify the box for a given 1099 form type with 

positive integers followed by an optional alpha character as applicable. Example: 2A. 

This field is updated if a value is present. If the value is blank, the system leaves the 

existing value in the system. To remove the existing value, enter the value NULL. You 

access the default box in the normal UI at the same location as DEFAULT1099TYPE 

above. 

---


<!-- Page 477 -->
Chapter 3: Import Instructions by Type of Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 

• 
UPDATETRANS: If you enter a Y, the system flags all the transactions for the given 

date range as 1099-able. An N instructs the system not to flag the transactions. If you 

enter a Y, then you must also supply data for type and box, as well as the date range. 

For CSV-imported A/P invoices, you can mark A/P invoices as 1099-able if you 

imported them as unpaid or partially paid, but not if you imported them as paid. 

• 
The system retroactively marks the vendor’s transactions as 1099-able based on date 

range and Form 1099 Type and Box listed in this upload.  

• 
FROMDATE: Type the start of the date range for transactions to be updated. Use the 

format MM/DD/YYYY. Data in this column is required when UPDATETRANS is set to Y. 

• 
TODATE: Type the end of the date range for transactions to be updated. Use the 

format MM/DD/YYYY. Data in this column is required when UPDATETRANS is set to Y. 

3. 
Optionally, fill in any additional columns as needed. Refer to the Vendor 1099 Transaction 

Data Template (on page 470) for a full list of columns. 

• 
VENDOR NAME is optional and helps you identify that you included the correct 

vendor because their IDs can be cryptic. It is not required for the upload. In fact, the 

system ignores this field. 

• 
NAME1099 supplies the information for the Recipient’s Name box on the 1099 form. 

In the normal user interface, this field is title 1099 Name and is found on the Vendor 


> **Navigation Path:** `Information page, Additional Information tab (Accounts Payable > All > Vendors). On`


the 1099 form, the system places the 1099 name first in the “Recipients name” box if 

the 1099 name exists, and the print as name (which is usually a copy of the vendor 

name) second. The print as name found on the Vendor tab. If the 1099 name does not 

exist, the system places the print as name as the only name. 

This field is updated if a value is present. If the value is blank, the system leaves the 

existing value already in the system. To remove the existing value, enter the value 

NULL. In a multi-entity shared structure of multiple companies, the system performs 

this at the top level, irrespective of entity. In other words, the top level changes this 

field for the entity. If you are in an entity that has private vendors not accessible to the 

top level, coordinate with your system administrator. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 14)

*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 487*

Importing Vendor Electronic Payment Information (ACH, EFT, BACS) 

If you want to pay vendors electronically, you can save time by importing electronic payment 

information for your vendors. In the import file, you can enable electronic payment as a payment 

method for selected vendors and specify the routing number and other information required for 

depositing the payment in the vendor’s account. 

Downloading the Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Import Data option. 

2. 
On the Import data page, look for the Set Up Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments 

section and find the Update vendors for electronic payments or Update vendors for ACH 

row.  

3. 
Click the Template link to download the template.  

Filling In the Columns 

1. 
Open the downloaded file in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required fields. 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the unique vendor ID. 

• 
ELECTRONIC_PAYMENT_ENABLE: Type “True” or “T” to enable electronic payments. 

Type “False” or “F” to disable electronic payments. 

• 
BANKFORMAT: Type your electronic format: ACH, EFT, or BACS. This field is required if 

ELECTRONIC_PAYMENT_ENABLE is set to “T” or “True.” 

• 
ACH_BANK_ROUTING_NUMBER: Type the financial institution’s routing number. This 

field is required when BANKFORMAT is set to “ACH.” 

• 
ACH_ACCOUNT_NUMBER: Type the account number. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “ACH.” 

• 
ACH_ACCOUNT_TYPE: Type “Checking Account” or “Savings Account.” This field is 

required when BANKFORMAT is set to “ACH.” 

• 
ACH_SEC_CODE: Type “CCD,” “CTX,” or “PPD.” This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “ACH.” The default value is “CCD.” 

• 
EFTBRANCHID: Type the financial institution’s branch ID. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “EFT.” 

---


<!-- Page 488 -->
Import Instructions by Type of Data 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
EFTACCOUNTNUMBER: Type the account number. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “EFT.” 

• 
BACSACCOUNTNAME: Type the name of the account. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “BACS.” 

• 
BACSACCOUNTNUMBER: They the account number. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “BACS.” 

• 
BACSSORTCODE: Type the BACS sort code. This field is required when BANKFORMAT 

is set to “BACS.” 

3. 
Optionally, fill in any of the non-required columns of the template.  

• 
PAYMENT_METHOD: Type one of the following: Cash, Check, Charge Card, Record 

Transfer, Paymode-X, RealPage Payments. If you have ACH enabled, then the valid 

value is “ACH.” If you have foreign electronic payments enabled, then the valid value is 

“Electronic Payment.”  

• 
BACSACCOUNTTYPE: Type the character related to the destination BACS account 

type. The valid values are 0 and 1. The default is 0. When the data comes from 

Barclay’s bank, use the value provided by Barclay’s bank. 

• 
PAYMENT_NOTIFICATION: This column controls whether the system sends an 

automatic payment notification. Type “True,” “False,” “T,” or “F.” 

4. 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 14). 

5. 
Import the CSV file (on page 24).

Importing Vendor Visibility Information

You can import vendor visibility information by uploading a CSV file. 

When you’re adding new vendors, you must include at least the following columns: 

• 
Vendor ID 

• 
Visibility

Required custom fields: If you’ve created any custom fields that are required, you must also 

include these columns. 

To import vendor visibility into your company:

Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab.

impact to system processing speed. 

8. 
To have the system send an email when the import is finished, type your email address in 

the Email results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses; separate

Resolving Import Errors 

This chapter describes how to resolve errors when your data fails to import properly.

### Introduction

### Import Error Notification
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 492*

Resolving Import Errors 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Introduction 

When an import process fails, the system sends an email containing a list of errors and how to 

correct the problems.  

This section details the email notification, common errors associated with importing data, and 

how to handle them. 

Import Error Notification 

There are a number of reasons imported records fail, such as duplicated entries or invalid field 

content. RealPage provides information about the failed records in an attempt to help you fix the 

import error. 

Finding the Error Message 

The Import confirmation page indicates how many records failed. This page also contains a link 

to download a CSV file, which contains only the failed records. 

Records that are successfully imported are not returned in the CSV file. 

Click the link and download the CSV file. 

If you entered your email address into the Import Company Information box, an email is sent 

that contains the error messages for your attempted import. The email lists the error code, and 

then each unique instance of that error in the file you attempted to import. 

The error message email is sent to the email address associated with the user ID logged in at the 

time of the file upload; otherwise, the email address for the company contact is used. 

The import pages also allow another email address to be explicitly entered in the Email results to 

this address field. 

If you did not enter your email in the Import Company Information box, and you do not click the 
link in the Import confirmation page, there is no way to retrieve the CSV error report file for the 
import you just did. 

Best practice: Enter your email in the Import Company Information box at the beginning of every 
import. 

The reason you are sent a separate email with the error messages is because a record could fail 

for more than one reason. Displaying all of the text for each record in the CSV file could become 

quite cumbersome and hard to read. Furthermore, it is often the case that thousands of records 

are uploaded. If thousands of errors fail, the CSV file could become quite bloated.

Read the Error Message Email 

The error messages for your failed upload file can be challenging to read. RealPage recommends 

the following strategy: 

• 
Start at the top of the email and look at each error message section. 

• 
In each section, start reading from the bottom up. The error at the bottom of the section is 

the first error encountered during import. 

a) Start here. 

b) Read from the bottom up. 

c) In each section, the specific error is listed at the top.

Start at the Top of the Email 

Error messages are presented in sections, and the sections are listed in the order that the errors 

are encountered in your file. 

Example: 

=================================================== 
Error BL01001973 
=================================================== 
BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number.  
The account number ‘4150’ already exists. 
BL01001973-1 Correction: Enter unique account number. 
BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record Could not create  
GL Account record! 
=================================================== 

When you read the error messages such as the one above, start with the error number. 

The error codes, such as BL01001973 above, are internal codes. These internal codes can help 
RealPage locate the source of a systemic issue if one is identified. 

=================================================== 
Error BL03000019 
=================================================== 
BL03000019-1 Description: Invalid contact data entered. 
TRANSACTION TYPE is a required field and cannot be empty 
BL03000019-1 Correction: Some of the fields you have entered 
are invalid. Please correct them with proper values. 
=================================================== 

Read from the Bottom of the Error Message Up 

In the example, the error code is BL01001973-2. 

Description: Unable to create record Could not create G/L Account record! first. 

This identifies the first error that occurred during import. It’s not informative, however, so look at 

the next error message for more information. 

The next error message in the list (as read from the bottom up), BL01001973-1 Correction: 

Enter unique account number, identifies the reason the G/L account record couldn’t be 

created, but it’s not yet clear what to do to fix the problem. 

The final error message in the example above (as read from the bottom up) describes more fully 

the cause of the error and suggests a fix: find and delete the duplicate account number.

It is possible to have several errors for a single failed record. You must resolve all of the errors in a

Always review which fields are required for the template you are working in. In the template file, 
the description row underneath the header row indicates whether or not a field is required, 
among other information.

### Handling Import Errors
*Source: `Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite.pdf`, Page 498*

Resolving Import Errors 

Importing Data into the RealPage Financial Suite 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Handling Import Errors 

If you experience import errors, review the tips in About CSV Templates (on page 7) and review 

the common errors (on page 487).  

Import errors occur when you try to import information that does not match the requirements of 

the template. Each template has a set of required information that you must enter to successfully 

import the file, and formats to follow for certain kinds of information. Read the descriptions in the 

template to determine the most accurate way to enter your data.  

If individual transactions are in error, the rows in the transaction that are in error are saved in a 

CSV file for you along with an error code for each row. The system sends an email with 

information about specific errors (on page 484).
